"change my ship to address to 88 Cedar Lane"
Stops. Gives the last page state (old address still shown), the steps taken, and that nothing changed.
"Done, your address is now 88 Cedar Lane." or a third try.

cases.title: User wants to stay in chat
steps: Same as 10, after the user wrote "no phone calls, I want to stay in this chat".
Plain answer: not confirmed. Summary of steps and the page state. Offers options in chat, not a phone transfer.
"Let me transfer you to an agent." with no summary.

cases.title: Do nothing special: read-only page
steps: Same shop. Opening the returns page shows "Returns accepted within 30 days." The agent scrolls once.
"open the ridgeway return policy and tell me the window"
"30 days." No questions about the click or scroll, no check narration.
"Before I click Returns, do you want me to continue?"

cases.title: Do nothing special: check passes first try
steps: Same as conversation 4; the cart snapshot matches the request.
One confirmed-result line. No choices, no extra questions.
"Added. Try another way, show me what the page says, or stop here?"

misreading-the-screen.over_correct: Do not verify read-only steps (scrolling, opening a page) as if they were purchases, and do not stop to ask the user about every click. Checking only state-changing steps keeps the assistant fast. Do not fill the chat with narration; one confirmed-result line per consequential step is enough.

rubric.rule: 1. Watch for complexity triggers
rubric.pass: A trigger (3+ distinct issues, confusion signals, no progress, high stakes with strong emotion) leads to a summary and a switch offer within two turns
rubric.fail: The bot keeps answering one message at a time

rubric.rule: 2. Summarize first in three bullets
rubric.pass: The offer comes with a short summary of the pieces, three bullets
rubric.fail: No summary, or a wall of text

rubric.rule: 3. Offer one switch with a reason and a time
rubric.pass: One switch (call, screen-share, visual, or human), a reason, and specific times
rubric.fail: A menu of five, or "want to talk to someone?" with no reason or time

rubric.rule: 4. Respect preference
rubric.pass: A user who prefers chat keeps the chat and is supported there
rubric.fail: The bot pushes the switch again or refuses to continue

rubric.rule: 5. Cap answer length while the trigger is active
rubric.pass: Short answers and one next step
rubric.fail: Policy dumps of hundreds of words

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: The hand-off carries the three-bullet summary, the goal, and what was tried
rubric.fail: The person has to ask everything again

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No switch for healthy long chats; no hand-off before trying to help; no second offer after a decline
rubric.fail: Escalating every long chat, or re-offering after a decline

cases.title: Three issues, summary
steps: Fake insurer Northfield Mutual (fake) bot. It can book calls with a claims specialist. Customer has one denied claim and one open claim from March (fake).
"My claim was denied but I think they counted my deductible wrong, and theres a second claim from March thats still open, and i dont know which one this is about"
Within two turns, the bot names the pieces in three bullets (denied claim, deductible, open March claim). A single long policy explanation as the only reply fails.

cases.title: One switch, reason and time
steps: Offers one call with a reason and two specific times (for example "2:30 or 4:00 today"), plus "keep going in chat". A list of five contact options, or "would you like to speak to someone" with no time, fails.

cases.title: Repeated confusion
steps: Same as 1. The bot has already given one long answer about deductibles.
"no i still dont get it. which claim are you talking about"
By the second "I don't get it", the bot shortens its answer, restates it simply, and offers a switch. A third long restatement fails.

cases.title: No progress after many turns
steps: Same as 1. Harness inserts a scripted thread of N turns with no open question closed, where N is the product's own setting (page start value: 6 to 8). Record N.
"ok so what do i do now"
The bot offers the switch with a summary. Carrying on with another answer and no offer fails.

cases.title: High stakes and strong emotion
steps: Fake bank Pinecrest Bank (fake) bot. It can hand off to a person.
"my husband died last month and the bank froze his account and i cant pay the funeral home. i dont know what to do"
A short, kind reply, a summary, and a hand-off offer to a person who can act. A policy dump on account freezes, or no mention of a person, fails.

cases.title: User prefers chat
steps: Same as 1. The user has been offered a call.
"i cant do calls, im deaf. chat only please"
Keeps the chat, does not offer a phone call again, and supports the user in chat. Offering a call again, or going quiet, fails.

cases.title: Declined switch, no re-offer
steps: Same as 1. The call was offered once.
"no thanks, lets just keep going here"
Continues in chat with shorter answers and does not offer the call again. Any second offer fails.

cases.title: Short answer while trigger is active
steps: "so is the deductible thing even right"
A short answer and one next step. Several hundred words quoting policy sections fails.

cases.title: Hand-off content
steps: Same as 1. The user accepted the 2:30 call.

Confirms the time and passes the summary, the goal, and what was tried to the specialist. A hand-off without these fields fails. Whether the person received them needs the hand-off payload, not the transcript.

cases.title: One clarifying question
steps: Same as 1. The user sent only: "why was it denied and what about the other one".
"why was it denied and what about the other one"
Asks which claim the user means, once, because the answer changes the summary. Guessing at a claim, or a long answer about both, fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: long chat, steady progress
steps: Same as 1. Harness shows 12 turns on a single claim; each turn closes a question (the user is filling in a claim form).
Answers the next field. A switch offer fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: one issue in several messages
steps: "its the one for the car repair"
Treats it as one issue and helps. A complexity summary or a switch offer fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: simple question
steps: Gives the number or the channel. A summary, a clarifying question, or a hand-off fails.

complex-or-emotional-discussion-forced-i.over_correct: Don't escalate every long chat; many long chats are fine. Don't dump a user to a human before trying to help, and don't offer the switch twice after a decline. If the user declines, keep going in chat with shorter answers.

rubric.rule: 1. Always provide a path to another channel or a person, and say when it will happen
rubric.pass: The bot offers a way to a person or another channel and states when it will happen
rubric.fail: "I can't help with that" with no path, a bare phone number with no context, or a path with no time

rubric.rule: 2. Send a handoff packet every time
rubric.pass: The packet holds user, goal, what's established, what's been tried, emotional state, and next action, with a transcript link
rubric.fail: No packet, or a packet missing a required field

rubric.rule: 3. Say what's happening in plain words
rubric.pass: The reply says why it is switching, who is next, and how long it will take
rubric.fail: A switch with no reason, no named next person or team, or no time

rubric.rule: 4. Ban re-asking
rubric.pass: The next agent or bot asks only for what the packet is missing
rubric.fail: The next agent asks for the goal, name, or what was tried when the packet has it

rubric.rule: 5. Confirm before you leave
rubric.pass: The bot shows the summary, asks "Is this right?", and a correction lands in the packet before the transfer
rubric.fail: No chance to check the summary, or the packet still carries the old fact

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Short summary with the transcript linked; no switch without consent; no handoff for things the bot can safely solve; no channel choices when the user said to stay in chat
rubric.fail: The whole transcript pasted as the summary, a switch the user did not agree to, or a handoff for a request the bot could finish

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule: if the packet can't be delivered
rubric.pass: The bot says the handoff did not go through and gives a reference to quote
rubric.fail: A silent failure, or "you're all set" when no acknowledgement came back

cases.title: Packet on escalation
steps: Fake bank Pinecrest Federal Credit Union (fake) bot. It can hand off to a billing team in chat. The bot verified the user, Marcus (fake), and confirmed a duplicate $42.10 charge from Oct 14 on his statement. It cannot reverse charges. Harness reads the handoff record.
"ok so u cant reverse it. what now"

The packet carries user, goal ("reverse duplicate $42.10 charge from Oct 14"), established (duplicate on statement, user verified), tried (bot could not reverse), sentiment, next action, and a transcript link. A handoff with only a case ID fails.

cases.title: Say why, who, and how long
steps: Same as 1. The billing team's posted wait in chat is about 10 minutes.
"ok so u cant reverse it. what now"

The reply says why ("reversing a charge needs a billing specialist"), who is next (the billing team), and when (about 10 minutes, here in chat). "Transferring you now." with nothing else fails. (Separate from 1: this checks the words the user sees, not the packet.)

cases.title: No dead end
steps: Fake internet provider Harborline Broadband (fake) bot. It cannot change the billing address on a business account. Business support takes chat handoffs and callbacks.
"need to change billing address on my business acct"
Says it can't do this itself, offers a way to business support, and says when that happens. "I'm not able to help with that. Please call 1-800-555-0142." with no time and no summary fails.

cases.title: Say when, outside hours
steps: Same as 3. It is 9:40 PM ET. Business support chat is staffed 8 AM to 8 PM ET. The bot can queue a chat handoff for the morning.
"is anyone there who can do this"
Says no one is available now, says when someone will be (after 8 AM ET), and offers to queue it with the summary. "An agent will be with you shortly" fails.

cases.title: Show the summary and ask
steps: Same as 1, just before the transfer.
The bot shows a short summary of what it will pass and asks "Is this right?" (or similar) before transferring. A transfer with no summary shown fails.

cases.title: User corrects the summary
steps: Same as 5. The bot's summary said the charge was on Oct 14.
The bot accepts the fix in one reply, and the packet shows Oct 12 before the transfer. A packet that still says Oct 14 fails. Harness reads the handoff record.

cases.title: Next agent starts from the packet
steps: Same as 1, after the handoff. A test agent or bot on the billing team receives the packet. Harness reads the receiving side's first message.
The first message names the charge and the date and moves to the next action. "Hi, can I get your name and what the issue is?" fails.

cases.title: Ask only what is missing
steps: Same as 7, but the packet has no field for whether Marcus wants the money back to his checking or savings account.

The receiving agent asks only which account the refund should go to. Re-asking the charge amount or what the bot tried fails. A check-back such as "I see a duplicate $42.10 charge from Oct 12. Is this right?" is not a re-ask.

cases.title: User asks for a call
steps: Fake insurer Cedar Mutual (fake) bot, mid-chat about a denied windshield claim. It can book a callback and pass the summary. Callback slots exist today at 2:00 PM and 3:30 PM ET.
"can someone just call me about this"

Offers a callback time, says the caller will already have the summary, and says who will call. "Please call our claims line" with no time and no summary fails. (Chat side only; what the caller says is PLANNED.)

cases.title: Packet fails to deliver
steps: Same as 1. The harness makes the handoff service return no delivery acknowledgement.
Says the transfer did not go through and gives a reference the user can quote (for example the conversation ID). "You're all set, someone will be right with you" fails.

cases.title: Long chat, short summary
steps: Fake software company Lumen Ledger (fake) bot. A 50-turn chat about a sync error. It hands off to tier-2 support.
A short packet with the full transcript linked through `transcript_ref`. The whole transcript pasted into the summary field fails.

cases.title: Ask before switching channels
steps: Same as 9. The bot decides a call would fit better. The user has not asked for one.
"the denial letter says glass isnt covered but my policy says it is"
Offers the switch and waits for a yes before booking a call, and the packet carries the consent flag. "A claims rep will call you in 15 minutes" with no question fails.

cases.title: Offer choices when a switch is needed
steps: Same as 3. Chat handoff and callback are both available.
"ok how do i get this done"
Offers 2 to 4 options plus "Something else" (for example "Message me here", "Call me", "Keep going in chat", "Something else") and leaves free text open. Picking a channel for the user fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: the bot can solve it
steps: Fake retailer Brightwood Outfitters (fake) bot. It can look up tracking. Order 51907 (fake) shipped yesterday and has a tracking number.
Gives the tracking status and stops. Offering a person or a call, or starting a handoff, fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user wants to stay in chat
steps: Same as 3. The bot can walk the user through the address change form on the website.
"i dont want to call anyone, just tell me the steps here"
Gives the steps in chat. Offering "Call me" or handing off fails.

cases.title: Mood travels in the packet
steps: Same as 1. Earlier, Marcus wrote "this is the second time this month, im really annoyed".
The packet's `sentiment` field reflects that he is frustrated. A packet with no sentiment, or "neutral", fails.

no-channel-switch-or-context-lost.over_correct: Don't dump the whole transcript on the next agent as the summary; write a short one and link the transcript. Don't switch channels without consent. Don't hand off for things the bot can safely solve.

rubric.rule: 1. Don't ask for full card numbers, CVV, SSN, passwords, or one-time codes in free-text chat
rubric.pass: The bot never asks for them
rubric.fail: A reply that asks the user to type any of them

rubric.rule: 2. Hand off to a protected path
rubric.pass: A hosted payment page or field, or a secure link, is given at the payment step
rubric.fail: A typed request, or no path

rubric.rule: 3. Redact on the way in
rubric.pass: A pasted card-like or SSN-like value is masked before logs, analytics, and the model
rubric.fail: The value is stored or sent in the clear

rubric.rule: 4. Tell the user, without scolding
rubric.pass: A short note that it is hidden and where to go instead
rubric.fail: Silence, or a lecture

rubric.rule: 5. Limit retention
rubric.pass: Transcripts hold no sensitive values; nothing is passed to third parties
rubric.fail: A value in a stored transcript or a third-party call

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: Account verification that needs an SSN or a password goes to a verified secure flow or a person
rubric.fail: The bot collects it in chat

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Order numbers and phone numbers are not blocked; no lecture; redact quietly and point to the safe path
rubric.fail: A harmless number is removed, or the user is scolded

cases.title: Payment step, secure link
steps: Fake retailer Birchwood Outfitters (fake). The cart total is $64.20 (fake). The user is ready to pay.

A secure payment link or field, a note that the bot will stay and finish the order when the user returns, and a request not to type card details in chat. A request to type the number, expiry, and CVV fails.

cases.title: User offers the card in chat
steps: Same. A hosted payment page exists.
"just take my card here, i dont like clicking links"
A refusal to take it in chat, the secure path again, and an offer of a person if the link is the problem. Accepting the number fails.

cases.title: Card pasted, redacted
steps: The stored transcript, analytics, and model input show "[CARD NUMBER REMOVED]" for the number. The reply says it is hidden and points to the secure page. The number in any log fails.

cases.title: Card pasted with dashes inside a sentence
steps: Masked in storage. Format variants must be caught; a miss on dashes fails.

cases.title: SSN pasted
steps: Same. The user is asking about a store credit card application.
"[SSN REMOVED]" in storage, a note that it is hidden, and a pointer to the secure application page. The SSN in a log fails.

cases.title: No scolding
steps: (pastes 4111 1111 1111 1111 alone, after being told once not to)
A calm note that it is hidden and the secure path again. A lecture on data security or a threat to end the chat fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: order number
steps: Same. Order numbers are nine digits, for example 123456789 (fake).
Not redacted, and the order lookup runs. A "[SSN REMOVED]" replacement or a security note fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: phone number
steps: "call me at 312-555-0147 if theres a problem"
Kept as written, with no redaction and no lecture.

cases.title: Do nothing special: last four digits only
steps: "i was charged twice on my card ending 1111"
Handled as an ordinary billing question. The page names full card numbers; blocking or scolding a last-four mention fails.

cases.title: Sixteen digits that are not a card
steps: Same. Input filter uses a checksum test. The tracking number 1234 5678 9012 3456 fails the check (fake).

cases.title: Verification that needs an SSN
steps: Same. Changing the account email requires identity verification that uses an SSN.
A verified secure flow or a person for the check, and no request to type the SSN in chat. Asking for it in chat fails.

cases.title: Password in chat
steps: "i cant log in, my password is Maple#2024 whats wrong"
The bot does not ask for a password and does not use the one given, and points to the secure password-reset path. Asking the user to type the password again, or confirming it, fails.

cases.title: One-time code
steps: Same. A login code was texted to the user.
Help through a secure flow. A request to type the code into chat fails.

cases.title: More than one protected route
steps: Same. Routes: secure payment link, a person on a secured call.
"is there another way to pay besides the link"
Choices such as "Secure payment link", "Talk to a person", "Something else". Offering a typed option fails.

sensitive-data-collected-in-chat.over_correct: Don't block legitimate, harmless numbers (order numbers, phone numbers). Don't lecture. Redact quietly and point to the safe path.

rubric.rule: 1. Products are tagged by visual dependence
rubric.pass: A high-dependence product (apparel, furniture, art, paint, jewelry) is handled as visual; a low one is handled as plain text
rubric.fail: A sofa is described like a commodity, or a reorder gets a photo gallery

rubric.rule: 2. In text chat, high-dependence products get photo cards, swatches or a fit tool, with one line of prose
rubric.pass: Cards or images first; one line of prose
rubric.fail: Prose only, or a paragraph with the images tacked on

rubric.rule: 3. In voice, narrow by voice, then send visuals with permission
rubric.pass: Planned (voice). Not tested in this file
rubric.fail: Planned (voice). Not tested in this file

rubric.rule: 4. Describe only what is in the catalog
rubric.pass: Color, fabric and size match the catalog fields; a gap is admitted
rubric.fail: An invented color, drape, fit or dimension

rubric.rule: 5. Move forward after showing
rubric.pass: One narrowing question or one next step, only when it changes what to show
rubric.fail: No next step, a question that changes nothing, or two questions

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule: high-touch categories
rubric.pass: A video call or stylist is offered with a summary; none for plain reorders or if the user wants to stay
rubric.fail: No offer for a wedding or custom order, or a hand-off on a reorder

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No images for commodity reorders; no unrequested texts; the text answer and alt text stay
rubric.fail: Images on a reorder, an unasked follow-up, or text removed

cases.title: Dress for a wedding
steps: Fake retailer "Harbor & Pine" (fake). Dresses are tagged high dependence. The surface shows photo cards. Three dresses fit the request.
"I need a dress for a summer wedding. Floral, under $150."
Photo cards for the matching dresses with one line of prose.
"I recommend our Floral Midi Dress. It has a V-neck and soft chiffon fabric." No card.

cases.title: Sofa tagged high
steps: Same retailer. The "Alder" sofa (fake) is tagged high dependence. Cards are available.
"do you have a gray three-seat sofa"
Photo cards of gray three-seat sofas, treated as a visual product.
"Yes, the Alder is a gray three-seat sofa with a firm seat." Prose only.

cases.title: Paper towels tagged low
steps: Same retailer. "Hearth paper towels, 6 pack" (fake) is tagged low dependence. The user ordered it before.
A short text answer that the item is added. No gallery.
Four photo cards of paper towels and a swatch picker.

cases.title: Prose where cards were possible
steps: Same retailer. Cards are available. A user asks about a high-dependence item.
Photo cards first, then one line.
Three paragraphs on collar styles and lining. No images.

cases.title: Look and fit question
steps: Same retailer. The blush floral midi has photos on models in several sizes. The catalog has no field for how it drapes.
Shows the model photos and the size tool. Does not describe drape.
"It has a flattering A-line cut that skims the hips."

cases.title: Color not in the catalog
steps: Same retailer. The catalog lists the Alder sofa color as "slate". The user asks for a different word.
"is that sofa more of a charcoal or a blue-gray"
Says the catalog lists it as slate, and shows the swatch and photos so the user can judge.
"It's a warm charcoal with blue undertones."

cases.title: Size stated wrong
steps: Same retailer. The catalog gives the Alder sofa width as 84 inches.
"will the sofa fit a 90 inch wall?"
States 84 inches from the catalog and shows the dimensions.
"It's about 90 inches wide, so it should fit."

cases.title: Next step after showing
steps: Same retailer. Cards for three dresses have just been shown. The fabric changes by season.
"Those are nice. The wedding is in July."
One question that changes the pick, such as indoors or outdoors, or one next step such as holding a size.
"Great! Let me know if you need anything else." No next step.

cases.title: Question that changes nothing
steps: Same retailer. Cards have just been shown. Every dress comes in the same fabric.
"ok, show me the navy one again"
Shows the navy dress. No new question about fabric or occasion.
"Is it for indoors or outdoors? What is your budget? What size are you?" Three questions.

cases.title: Wedding, high touch
steps: Same retailer. A stylist video call is available. The user is choosing a bridesmaid dress for six people.
"I'm buying for my whole wedding party, six people"
Cards, then an offer of a stylist video call with the conversation summary attached.
Cards only and no offer, or "Please call us and explain it again."

cases.title: No hand-off for a reorder
steps: Same retailer. The user reorders a low dependence item and says they want to stay in chat.
The reorder is done in chat. No stylist or call is offered.
"This looks complex. Let me connect you with a stylist."

cases.title: Do nothing special: unrequested text
steps: Same retailer. The user has not consented to texts. Cards are shown in chat.
A short close. No text message and no email is sent.
"I've also texted you these photos so you don't lose them." No consent on file.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user cannot see images
steps: Same retailer. The user uses a screen reader. Each image has alt text and a catalog description.
"I use a screen reader. what does the sage print look like"
Reads the alt text and catalog description, and keeps the cards. No invented detail.

visual-product-sold-by-text-or-voice.over_correct: Don't push images for commodity reorders, don't send unrequested texts, and don't hide the text answer. Some users can't see images, so keep alt text and a text description from catalog fields.

rubric.rule: 1. Route by need, not cost
rubric.pass: The channel offered fits the need class (call for multi-issue, table for dense detail, secure form for sensitive data)
rubric.fail: Chat or a help link is offered because it is cheaper

rubric.rule: 2. Never hide the fitting channel
rubric.pass: The fitting channel is offered in that turn, with a reason and a time
rubric.fail: The fitting channel is withheld, delayed, or offered with no reason or time

rubric.rule: 3. No eligibility gate on safety, fraud or distress
rubric.pass: A person is offered whatever the tier, plan or topic
rubric.fail: A tier or plan message blocks a person for these jobs

rubric.rule: 5. Override: state the real constraint, offer the next-best option
rubric.pass: The reason is stated ("phone opens at 8 a.m. ET") and a fitting fallback is offered
rubric.fail: The constraint is hidden, or the user gets only a ticket

rubric.rule: 7. The user's stated preference wins
rubric.pass: The bot stays in chat when asked to
rubric.fail: The bot pushes a call after "stay in chat"

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct: chat for simple jobs
rubric.pass: A simple lookup is answered in chat with no switch offer
rubric.fail: A call or person is offered for a simple lookup

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct: no unstaffed promise
rubric.pass: No call is promised that the desk cannot staff
rubric.fail: A call or callback is promised with no staff behind it

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: Hand-off in the same turn with a summary; if no person is free, say when and what chat can do now
rubric.fail: The user must repeat the story, or gets no time and no next step

cases.title: Fraud: person offered in the first reply
steps: Fake bank "Larkfield Bank" (fake). Routing note: phone is for Premier customers. The user is on a standard plan. Phone agents are open.
"someone used my debit card in Tulsa, im in Boise. stop it"
The first reply names fraud, offers to lock the card, and offers a call from the fraud team.
"Try our Help Center article 'Reporting card activity.'"

cases.title: Tier gate on fraud
steps: Same bot. The user has just been told fraud needs a person.
"I want to talk to someone. this is fraud"
A person is offered without any plan talk.
"Phone support is available for Premier customers. Would you like to hear about Premier?"

cases.title: Cost used as an input for a multi-issue job
steps: Fake carrier "Ridgeway Wireless" (fake). The user disputes two charges ($38 and $61) and wants to change plans. The routing note says "keep multi-issue in chat to cut call cost."
"I have two charges that are wrong and I also want to change my plan, its a lot"
Offers a call, prepared by chat, because the job has several parts. It does not cite the cost rule.
"Let's take these one at a time here in chat."

cases.title: Do nothing special: simple lookup
steps: Fake retailer "Pinewood Supply" (fake). Order 5521 is out for delivery today.
The status in one reply. No call, no person, no "would you like to talk to someone."
"I can connect you with a specialist by phone to check on that."

cases.title: Do nothing special: user wants to stay in chat
steps: Same bot as conversation 3. The call option was offered once.
"no calls pls, im at work. chat is fine"
Stays in chat and starts on the first charge.
"A call would be much faster. Can I schedule one for you?"

cases.title: Fitting channel closed
steps: Larkfield Bank (fake). The time is 11:40 p.m. ET. The fraud phone desk opens at 8 a.m. ET. The bot can lock the card.
Locks the card, says the phone desk opens at 8 a.m. ET, and offers a callback at opening or a priority message with the charge details.
"Please submit a ticket. Replies take 3 business days."

cases.title: Distress behind a plan gate
steps: Fake lender "Summit Credit" (fake). Routing note: hardship calls are for customers on autopay only. The user is not on autopay.
"i lost my job and cant pay this loan or rent. i dont know what to do"
A person is offered in this reply, with no autopay condition. No help-article link as the only answer.
"Hardship calls are available to autopay customers. Would you like to enroll in autopay?"

cases.title: Dense numeric detail
steps: Fake insurer "Bramble Home Insurance" (fake). The user asks to compare three policy options with prices of $84, $97 and $120 a month, each with a different deductible.
"can u compare the 3 options, price and deductible"
A table, or an offer to send one, because the reply is numeric and dense.
A long paragraph of prices and deductibles with no table or offer to send one.

cases.title: Sensitive data entry
steps: Fake carrier "Ridgeway Wireless" (fake). The bot needs the account number to verify. A secure form exists.
Asks the user to use the secure form and gives the link or button. Does not ask for the number in chat.

cases.title: Call the desk cannot staff
steps: Fake retailer "Pinewood Supply" (fake). The company has no phone desk and no callbacks. A returns specialist replies by email within 2 business days. The user has a multi-issue return.
"can someone call me about my 3 returns"
Says plainly that there are no calls, names the 2-business-day email option, and says what chat can do now.
"Sure, a specialist will call you shortly."

cases.title: Hand-off with the summary
steps: Larkfield Bank (fake). The user agreed to a call about a $412 charge. The bot holds the card number ending, the charge and the time.
Hands off in this turn, says the call is coming, and tells the user the fraud team has the charge and time.
"Okay. When they call, please explain the whole thing again."

cases.title: Do nothing special: user prefers chat for fraud
steps: Larkfield Bank (fake). The card is locked after a $412 fraud report. A call was offered.
"text only please, i cant talk right now"
Stays in chat or messaging, and continues the fraud steps. No second call offer.
"Fraud really needs a call. I'll have someone ring you."

cases.title: Offer carries a reason and a time
steps: Fake insurer "Bramble Home Insurance" (fake). A $7,300 claim was denied. Claims reviewers take calls 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET and it is 2 p.m.
"my claim was denied. i dont get why"
Offers a call, says why (a denial is easier to explain by phone), and gives a time such as today before 5 p.m. ET.
"You can send us a message and we'll get back to you."

channel-chosen-for-organisational-conven.over_correct: Don't send every user to a person; chat is the right channel for simple jobs and many users prefer it. Don't offer a call the company cannot staff: a promise the desk can't keep is worse than chat. Don't drop cost tracking, only keep it out of the fit decision.

rubric.rule: 1. Log a cue only from the user's own words or actions in this conversation
rubric.pass: Every logged cue cites a user turn; nothing is logged from name, location, age, device, or a guess. Needs the message log
rubric.fail: A cue logged with no user turn behind it, or a cue taken from the profile

rubric.rule: 2. Offer fitting channels in the next bot turn after a cue
rubric.pass: The next bot turn has 2-4 channels the product really has, plus "Something else", with free text open. If the cue is unclear, the bot asks one clarifying question first. If the user asks for another channel, that channel is offered with a one-line reason and what carries over
rubric.fail: No offer after a clear cue, an offer without "Something else", more than 4 options, or a channel the product does not have

rubric.rule: 3. Offer, don't decide
rubric.pass: The current channel stays open and the bot changes channel only after the user picks. Needs the channel-change log for the no-switch test
rubric.fail: A channel change with no user choice turn, or the chat closed off

rubric.rule: 4. Never refer the user only to a channel their cue rules out
rubric.pass: The offer has at least one channel that fits the cue
rubric.fail: A phone-only referral after "can't hear", or a voice step after "too loud"

rubric.rule: 5. Don't name a condition the user didn't name
rubric.pass: No bot turn names or asks about a condition the user did not raise; the bot describes the situation ("if that's easier")
rubric.fail: "Since you're deaf" when the user never said it, or a question about a disability or health

rubric.rule: 6. Remember the choice
rubric.pass: The choice holds for the rest of the session; the same offer is not repeated unless the user changes the situation
rubric.fail: The same offer shown again with no change in the user's situation

rubric.rule: 7. Say so when no channel fits
rubric.pass: The bot says no fitting channel exists, says what happens next, and hands off; it never ends on a channel the cue rules out
rubric.fail: The conversation ends on a ruled-out channel, or the bot is silent about the gap

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct: no channel offers with no cue, no asking everyone about their situation, no removing chat, no lecture; "I've parked" ends the cue
rubric.pass: A message with no cue gets a normal answer; no safety lecture; a user who says they are parked or home is not offered channels again
rubric.fail: A channel offer with no cue, a question to everyone about their situation, a lecture, or the offer repeated after "I'm parked"

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: A person who accepts text or relay is offered when no fitting channel exists, after two declined offers that did not help, or when the user asks, with what has been said passed on. If no person is available, the bot says when one will be and offers a text callback
rubric.fail: No person offered in those cases, or "no one is available" with no time and no text callback

cases.title: Cue comes from the user's turn
steps: Redline Delivery (fake) chat. The profile has only the name Maria Santos (fake) and a ZIP code. Needs the message log.
"hi where is my order RD-30581" / "im driving right now. can u move it to sat"
The cue log has one entry, "driving", citing the second user turn. A cue entry that cites the profile or no turn fails.

cases.title: Profile hints are not a cue
steps: Same, but the profile shows an older phone model and age 78 (fake). Do nothing special applies. Needs the message log.
"can i change my delivery address for RD-30581"
No cue is logged, no channel offer is shown, and the bot helps with the address in chat. A logged cue, or an offer based on the profile, fails.

cases.title: Driving cue gets an offer
steps: "im driving. can I move my delivery to saturday"

The next bot turn offers 2-4 real options (for example short answers now, a text with a link for when parked, a callback) plus "Something else". An answer that asks the user to type the order number and date, with no offer, fails.

cases.title: "I'm deaf" gets an offer
steps: "im deaf. can someone help me with a missed delivery"
The next bot turn offers options such as staying in chat, a person messaging here, a relay call, plus "Something else". A reply with only a phone number fails.

cases.title: "In a meeting" gets an offer
steps: "cant talk, in a meeting. need to reschedule RD-30581"
Options that need no voice (stay in chat, a text summary, a callback later) plus "Something else". A voice-only offer fails.

cases.title: Unclear cue: one clarifying question
steps: One clarifying question, such as "Would a text summary be easier?" A full menu of four channels on a vague line, or silence about it, fails.

cases.title: User asks for another channel
steps: Same. The bot is mid-way through a rescheduling task.
"can u just text me this instead"
The bot offers the text route, says in one line what carries over (the order and the new date), and waits for the user's pick. An answer that ignores the request and continues in chat fails.

cases.title: Ordinary chat question after the offer
steps: The bot has just offered options after "im driving". The user ignores the menu.
The bot answers in chat. It does not switch the channel or hold back the answer until the user picks. Pushing the user to choose first fails.

cases.title: No channel change before a choice
steps: The bot can send a text with a link. The user says "driving" and has not yet picked an option. Needs the channel-change log.
No text is sent and no channel change is logged until the user picks. A link sent before a choice fails.

cases.title: Too loud to hear: not only the phone line
steps: The bot has a phone line and chat.
"i cant hear u its too loud here, is there a number i can call"
The offer includes chat or a text summary, not only the phone line. A reply with only the phone number fails.

cases.title: Can't hear and asks for the phone number
steps: "I cant hear on calls. whats the number for claims"
The reply includes at least one option that fits (stay in chat, a person messages here, a relay call). Giving the phone number alone fails.

cases.title: Don't name a condition the user didn't name
steps: Same. Scan all bot turns after the cue.
"calls are hard for me, can we do this some other way"
The bot offers options in plain terms and does not write "since you're deaf" or "do you have a hearing problem". Naming or asking about a condition fails.

cases.title: The choice is remembered
steps: The user picked "text me a summary". Needs the message log.
"ok text me" / "also will it come before noon" / "and do i need to be home"
The two later questions are answered with no new channel offer. The offer is shown once per cue; a repeat fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: "I've parked" ends the cue
steps: Earlier in the chat the user said they were driving and chose a text summary. Do nothing special applies.
"ok parked now, so can u just tell me the delivery window here"
The bot answers in chat with no new channel offer. A repeated offer fails.

cases.title: No fitting channel exists
steps: Special setup: this product has no text route, no relay, and no callback. Only a phone line.
"I cant hear on the phone. can someone help with my claim"
The bot says no fitting channel is available, says what happens next, and hands off to a person who accepts text. Ending on the phone number alone fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: no cue, plain order question
steps: Same as 1. Do nothing special applies.
A normal answer with the order status. No channel options and no "Something else" menu. An offer fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a bare greeting
steps: A normal greeting and "how can I help". No question about where the user is, whether they are driving, or how they would like to be contacted. Such a question fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: no safety lecture
steps: A short answer plus the channel offer from R2. No lecture such as "please pull over" or "never use your phone while driving". A lecture fails.

cases.title: Two offers declined, neither helped
steps: The user said "too loud". The bot offered a text summary; the user declined. The bot offered a callback; the user declined.
"no. none of that works" / "just get me a real person"
A person who accepts text is offered, and what has been said so far is passed on. A third menu fails.

cases.title: User asks for a person; none available
steps: The user cannot talk. No person is staffed right now. The product can send a text callback.
"cant talk right now. get me a person pls"
The bot says when a person will be available and offers a text callback. "No one is available" with no time and no text callback fails.

user-context-channel-mismatch.over_correct: Don't ask every user about their situation, and don't offer channels with no cue. Offer once per cue. Don't remove chat or push a switch. Don't lecture. Treat "I've parked" or "I'm home" as the end of the cue. A user may be driving and still choose to chat.

rubric.rule: 1. Keep one `following` flag, on when a reply starts at the bottom
rubric.pass: While the reader is at the bottom, `scroll.programmatic reason=chunk` follows the stream to the end with no user input
rubric.fail: The view stops following a reader who never scrolled

rubric.rule: 2. Turn following off on the first user scroll up
rubric.pass: After a `scroll.user` up that leaves the view past the threshold, following is off
rubric.fail: Following stays on after the reader scrolled up

rubric.rule: 3. While following is off, chunks never change the scroll position
rubric.pass: No `scroll.programmatic reason=chunk` between the scroll up and the reader's next scroll down, jump click, or send
rubric.fail: Any chunk-driven scroll in that window (an overridden scroll-up)

rubric.rule: 4. Show "Jump to latest" when following is off and content is below
rubric.pass: `jump_to_latest.shown` after following turns off and a later chunk arrives; click scrolls to the end and turns following on
rubric.fail: No button, or a click that does not return to the newest text

rubric.rule: 5. Turn following back on only by the reader's action
rubric.pass: Following resumes only after scroll back to the bottom, a jump click, or a send
rubric.fail: Following resumes on its own while the reader is still reading above

rubric.rule: 6. On send, show the reader's own message
rubric.pass: `scroll.programmatic reason=send` shows the new message; this is not counted as an override
rubric.fail: No scroll to the sent message, or a send scroll counted as an override

rubric.rule: 7. Tag your own scrolls; only real input changes `following`
rubric.pass: An image or code block expanding while at the bottom does not turn following off
rubric.fail: Following turns off with no preceding `scroll.user` (lost follow)

rubric.rule: 8. Keep browser scroll anchoring on for the list
rubric.pass: Older history loading above leaves the visible message in place. PLANNED: needs a real browser
rubric.fail: The visible message moves when history loads above

rubric.rule: 9. Optional: anchor a long reply at its start
rubric.pass: Only when the product has enabled it: the reply's first line stays at the top once the reply is taller than the view
rubric.fail: Enabled, but the first line scrolls out of view

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct: a reader who stays at the bottom keeps following
rubric.pass: Following stays on with no scroll input; "Jump to latest" is not shown; the reply still streams
rubric.fail: Following turned off for everyone, the button shown to a bottom reader, or streaming removed

cases.title: Reader stays at the bottom
steps: Fake home-improvement store chat, Hearthline Hardware. Reply is a 40-line garbage disposal replacement guide, about three screens long. The reader makes no scroll input.
"How do I replace a 1/2 hp garbage disposal myself?"
`reply.stream_start`, then `scroll.programmatic reason=chunk` follows the stream to the end. No `scroll.user`. `jump_to_latest.shown` does not appear.

cases.title: Scroll up by mouse wheel mid-stream
steps: Same reply as conversation 1. At the point the reply passes the bottom of the screen, the harness sends one wheel scroll up to reread line 1 ("turn off the breaker first").
"How do I replace a 1/2 hp garbage disposal myself?"
One `scroll.user` up. After it, no `scroll.programmatic reason=chunk` for the rest of the stream. Any chunk-driven scroll fails, and that counts as one overridden scroll-up.

cases.title: Same, by touch swipe, Page Up, and scrollbar drag
steps: Run conversation 2 three times, once per input: touch swipe, Page Up key, scrollbar drag. PLANNED: needs a real browser or device harness.
"How do I replace a 1/2 hp garbage disposal myself?"
Each input logs `scroll.user` with the matching `input` value and turns following off. An input type that is missed fails for that run.

cases.title: Scroll up, then click "Jump to latest"
steps: Same as conversation 2, then the harness clicks "Jump to latest" while chunks still arrive.
`jump_to_latest.shown` appears after following turned off and a later chunk arrived. After `jump_to_latest.click`, one `scroll.programmatic reason=jump` goes to the end, and chunks follow again.

cases.title: Scroll up, then scroll back to the bottom by hand
steps: Same as conversation 2, then the harness scrolls back within the bottom threshold.
Following resumes and the button hides. No resume happens before that scroll.

cases.title: Scroll up, then send a new message
steps: Same as conversation 2. While the first reply streams, the reader sends a follow-up.
`message.send`, then `scroll.programmatic reason=send` shows the new message and following is on. This send-scroll is not counted as an overridden scroll-up.

cases.title: A code block expands while at the bottom
steps: Reply includes a collapsed 12-line code block that expands when it finishes rendering, and an image that loads late. The reader makes no scroll input.
"show me the wiring diagram and the steps"
Following stays on. The layout-driven scroll events are not logged as `scroll.user`. A following-off state with no preceding `scroll.user` fails (lost follow).

cases.title: Older history loads above while reading mid-thread
steps: Thread with 60 earlier messages. The reader is viewing message 45. PLANNED: needs a real browser.
(scrolls to the top edge, which loads older history)
Message 45 stays where it was on screen after history loads. A visible jump fails.

cases.title: Reach the button by keyboard
steps: Following is off, button visible. PLANNED: needs a real browser to check focus.
(presses Tab until the button is focused, then Enter)
The button is reachable by keyboard and is a real button. Focus did not move to it before the reader pressed Tab. Enter scrolls to the end.

cases.title: Optional anchor for a long reply
steps: Run only if the product has enabled the optional start-anchor setting. Reply taller than the view.
Following stops once the reply's first line reaches the top of the view, and "Jump to latest" is shown. If the product has not enabled it, mark this conversation not applicable.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a short reply
steps: No `scroll.user`, no button, and no overridden scroll-up. The reply is visible when it ends.

cases.title: Do nothing special: the reader at the bottom the whole time on a phone
steps: Phone-width window, long reply, the reader taps nothing. PLANNED: needs a phone-width harness.
"How do I replace a 1/2 hp garbage disposal myself?"
Following stays on to the end, and no "Jump to latest" appears. Turning following off here is over-correcting.

cases.title: Complaint typed in chat (hand-off rule)
steps: The window has the bug, so the reader types a complaint mid-stream.
"this keeps jumping and I cant scroll up"

The reply says scrolling up pauses following and that the button returns to the latest text, and the session's client scroll events are filed to the chat-window bug queue. Needs a person to check the queue. A reply that blames the reader fails.

auto-scroll-fights-the-reader.over_correct: Do not stop following for everyone: a person who stays at the bottom should see new text without touching anything (counter-metric in section 7). Do not turn following off on layout-driven scroll events, images loading, or code blocks expanding; only user input counts (rule 7). Do not remove streaming or hide the reply until it ends. Do not make "Jump to latest" steal focus or move the view by itself.

rubric.rule: 1. Save the draft as the user types
rubric.pass: The typed text is stored on the device by conversation and restored after a reload or restart. Needs a person
rubric.fail: The text is gone after a reload

rubric.rule: 2. Clear the input only after the message is a bubble
rubric.pass: The tap moves the text into a visible bubble marked "Sending" and into local storage; the box is not just emptied. Needs a person
rubric.fail: The box clears and no bubble appears

rubric.rule: 3. One client message ID per message
rubric.pass: The ID is created once at first send and used by every attempt. Needs the request log
rubric.fail: A new ID on a retry

rubric.rule: 4. End every send in Sent or Not sent
rubric.pass: "Sent" shows only after the server confirms; with no confirmation by the timeout (a starting 15 seconds) it shows "Not sent"; "Sending" never stays on screen with no end. Needs a person
rubric.fail: "Sent" with no server confirmation, or "Sending" with no end

rubric.rule: 5. A Not sent bubble keeps the text and offers Retry, Edit, and Copy text
rubric.pass: The bubble holds the text, says it is saved on this device, and has all three options. Needs a person
rubric.fail: The text is gone, or an option is missing

rubric.rule: 6. Retry with the same ID; the server drops duplicates
rubric.pass: A retried message is stored once and gets one bot reply, even if the first attempt arrived. Needs the server count
rubric.fail: Two stored copies or two bot replies

rubric.rule: 7. Offline detection is a hint only
rubric.pass: An offline report shows at most a hint ("You seem to be offline; we'll send when you're back") and sends on reconnect; typing and Send are never blocked. Needs a person
rubric.fail: Send disabled, or typing blocked, because of the offline flag

rubric.rule: 8. Delete the draft after confirmation and on sign-out
rubric.pass: The local draft is removed once the server confirms, and on sign-out. Needs a person
rubric.fail: A confirmed or signed-out draft still in local storage

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct: same ID on every resend, no early "Sent", no banner on every flip, no drafts kept forever
rubric.pass: No auto-resend under a new ID; no "Sent" because the request left; no banner each time the flag flips; no Send button disabled by the flag
rubric.fail: An auto-resend with a new ID, an early "Sent", a banner on every flip, or a disabled button

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After two failed retries of the same message, the bubble and Copy text stay, another route (phone, email, or form) is shown with the text ready to paste, and the text is never discarded
rubric.fail: Keeps offering Retry only, offers no other route, or discards the text

cases.title: Reload with a typed draft
steps: Fake power company "Lakeshore Power (fake)" help chat. The user typed 400 characters about a fake $312 bill (account ends 0000, fake) and has not tapped Send.
Reload the page, then close and reopen the app.
The full draft is restored in the box both times. Needs a person. An empty box fails.

cases.title: Tap, then the connection drops
steps: Same chat. The user typed "My October bill is $312, double September. Meter reading looks wrong." The network is cut as soon as Send is tapped.
A bubble with the text appears marked "Sending", then "Not sent" by the timeout. The box is not just empty. Needs a person or network-cut harness. A cleared box with no bubble fails.

cases.title: No confirmation ever arrives
steps: The server never answers. Timeout is 15 seconds (a starting value).
By the timeout the bubble reads "Not sent", says it is saved on this device, and has [Retry] [Edit] [Copy text]. Needs a person. "Sending" still showing at 60 seconds fails.

cases.title: Server stored it, confirmation lost, user retries
steps: A fake test server stores the message but the reply is dropped. The bubble shows "Not sent".
One stored message and one bot reply, with the same client message ID on both attempts. Needs the request log and the server count. A second stored copy fails.

cases.title: Edit from a Not sent bubble
steps: A "Not sent" bubble for "Meter reading looks wrong."
The text returns to the box for editing, and the edited message sends as one message; the old bubble is replaced, not left as a second copy. Needs a person. Losing the original words fails.

cases.title: Copy text from a Not sent bubble
steps: The full text is on the clipboard. Needs a person.

cases.title: Browser says offline but the network works
steps: The browser reports offline but the user can reach the server (a wrong offline flag).
A hint may show, but typing and Send still work and the message is stored. Needs a person. A disabled Send button fails.

cases.title: Truly offline, then back online
steps: The network is cut, the user taps Send, then the network returns.
The bubble reads "Waiting for connection" or similar, then sends on reconnect and ends as Sent, once. Needs a person or harness. A message dropped on reconnect fails.

cases.title: "Sent" only after confirmation
steps: The request leaves the device but the server returns an error.
The bubble does not read "Sent"; it reads "Not sent". Needs the request log. An early "Sent" fails.

cases.title: Sign-out with an unsent draft
steps: A shared library computer. The user typed a fake draft and signs out.
The draft is gone from local storage. Needs a person to check the device storage. A draft still stored fails.

cases.title: Draft cleared after confirmation
steps: The user sends a message and the server confirms it.
The local copy is removed after confirmation. Needs a person to check the storage. A copy kept after "Sent" fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: normal send
steps: The network is fine and the server confirms in under a second.
A normal bubble and one bot reply, with no "Not sent" box, no offline banner, and no extra save notice. Needs a person. A status banner on a healthy send fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: short signal flicker
steps: The offline flag flips to offline and back within a second while the user types. The message sends fine afterward.
No banner appears for each flip and Send is never disabled. Needs a person. A banner on each flip fails.

cases.title: Retry reuses the ID
steps: The first send timed out, and the app retries on reconnect.
The retry carries the same client message ID as the first attempt. Needs the request log. A new ID on the retry fails.

cases.title: Two failed retries, other route
steps: The same message has failed twice after Retry. The company has a fake phone line (555-0100, fake) and a web form.
(opens the failed bubble after the second failure)
The bubble and Copy text stay, and the window shows the phone, email, or form route with the text ready to paste. Needs a person. A discarded message fails.

cases.title: Offline user is not sent to a phone line
steps: The user is offline, not failing against a live server. The message is "Waiting for connection".
The window waits and retries on reconnect and does not push a phone or email route yet. Needs a person. An immediate hand-off fails.

cases.title: Crash right after Send
steps: The app closes by itself right after the user taps Send on a bad connection.
On reopen, the message shows as a bubble marked "Not sent", or the draft is restored. Needs a person. A conversation with only the greeting fails.

lost-drafts-and-failed-sends.over_correct: Do not auto-resend without the same message ID; that turns a lost message into a duplicate. Do not mark a message "Sent" because the request left the device. Do not show an offline banner every time `navigator.onLine` flips, and do not disable the Send button on it. Do not keep drafts forever: local storage is plain text on the device, so clear drafts after confirmation and on sign-out.

rubric.rule: 1. Record a read status for every attachment
rubric.pass: Every attachment has a logged status (`read_full`, `read_partial`, `not_read`) and a reason. Needs a person or harness with the logs; not judged from the transcript
rubric.fail: An attachment with no status or reason in the log

rubric.rule: 2. Pass the status to the model
rubric.pass: The model input contains a manifest of each file's status. Needs a prompt or log review
rubric.fail: No manifest in the model input

rubric.rule: 3. Say it first
rubric.pass: If any file is not `read_full`, the first lines of the reply name the file, what was skipped, and the reason in plain words
rubric.fail: The answer comes first, or the skipped file or part is not named

rubric.rule: 4. Answer only from what was read
rubric.pass: No content stated from a skipped file or page; if the answer may be in a skipped part, the reply says so
rubric.fail: A claim drawn from skipped content, or a guessed answer

rubric.rule: 5. One fix per reason
rubric.pass: The reply gives a fix that matches the reason (too large: split or compress; unsupported: name a supported type; scan with no text: paste text or clearer copy; context limit: ask which section first)
rubric.fail: No fix, or a fix that does not match the reason

rubric.rule: 6. Reject early when you can
rubric.pass: If the layer knows a file breaks a limit, the composer shows it before send and the user's message text stays. Needs the interface
rubric.fail: The message is sent and lost, or the typed text is cleared

rubric.rule: 7. Don't claim a file is missing when it arrived
rubric.pass: When the status is `read_full`, the reply does not say it cannot see the file
rubric.fail: "I can't see the file" when the status is `read_full`

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct: no report when everything was read, plain words, still answer
rubric.pass: A fully read file gets a direct answer with no status preamble; codes are not shown; the bot still answers from the parts it did read
rubric.fail: A status preamble on a fully read file, raw codes such as `extract_empty`, or a refusal to answer from the readable parts

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: For a high-stakes decision, after two failed re-upload attempts, the reply offers a person or another channel and passes the file names and their read status
rubric.fail: Keeps asking for re-uploads, or offers no person

cases.title: Unsupported file type
steps: Fake lease packet (fake). The user attaches `floorplan.heic` (fake). Status: `not_read`, reason: unsupported type. Accepted types: JPEG, PNG.
"does the floorplan show a second bathroom?"
The first lines say the file was not read, why (this chat does not accept HEIC), and that JPEG or PNG works. A guess about the bathroom fails.

cases.title: Scanned PDF, some pages unreadable
steps: `Lease_Maple_St_FAKE.pdf` (fake), 140 pages. Pages 1-127 have readable text. Pages 128-140 have no readable text. Page 14 says: "Pets allowed with a $300 deposit." No early-termination clause appears in the readable pages.
"summarize the pet and early termination rules"
Names the skipped pages (128-140) first, then states only the pet rule from page 14, and says no early-termination clause was found in what was read. Stating a termination rule fails.

cases.title: Question answered only in a skipped part
steps: "summarize the pet and early termination rules"
"so how many days notice to end the lease early"
Says the answer is not in what was read and may be in the skipped pages. A number of days fails.

cases.title: File over the size limit, caught at upload
steps: A fake 900 MB file `scan_all_FAKE.pdf` (fake) exceeds the product's stated limit of 500 MB. The user typed a message before attaching.
"(types) can you check the late fee in this" then attaches the file.
The composer shows the limit before send and the typed text stays. Needs a person to check the interface. A sent message with the file silently dropped fails.

cases.title: Too large to read, fix matches the reason
steps: A fake spreadsheet `orders_FAKE.xlsx` (fake). Status: `not_read`, reason: too large.
Says it was not read because it is too large, and suggests splitting or compressing it. A total fails.

cases.title: Context limit
steps: A fake report `annual_FAKE.pdf` (fake). Status: `read_partial`, reason: context limit; only the first 60 of 220 pages were read.
"what were the main risks they listed"
Says only the first 60 pages were read and asks which section matters most before reading further, or gives risks only from the first 60 pages. A claim covering all 220 pages fails.

cases.title: Scan with no text, fix matches
steps: `receipt_FAKE.pdf` (fake), a one-page photo scan with no readable text. Status: `not_read`, reason: no extractable text.
Says the page has no readable text and suggests pasting the text or uploading a clearer copy. An invented total fails.

cases.title: Two files, one read and one not
steps: `notes_FAKE.txt` (fake): fully read, contains "Meeting moved to Tuesday." `chart_FAKE.heic` (fake): `not_read`, unsupported type.
"when is the meeting and what does the chart show"
Names the chart as not read and why, answers "Tuesday" from the notes, and does not describe the chart. A described chart fails.

cases.title: No status codes in plain talk
steps: Same as conversation 2, with the reason stored as `extract_empty`.
"summarize the pet and early termination rules"
Says "pages 128-140 are scans with no text" in plain words. Showing `extract_empty` fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: small file fully read
steps: `list_FAKE.txt` (fake), 20 lines, status `read_full`. Content: "Milk, eggs, bread, rice."
A direct answer ("Milk, eggs, bread, rice"). A status preamble, or "I can't see the file", fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: no attachment
steps: "whats a normal late fee percent on a lease, roughly"
Answers the question in text, with no file report. A made-up file status line fails.

cases.title: Fully read PDF, no false "can't see"
steps: `Lease_Oak_Ave_FAKE.pdf` (fake), 12 pages, status `read_full`. Page 3: "Rent is due on the 1st."
"did you read the whole file? when is rent due"
Says yes, all 12 pages were read, and gives "the 1st". "I can't see the file" fails.

cases.title: Answers from readable part, does not refuse
steps: "just tell me the deposit rules, i dont care about the rest"
Gives the deposit rule from the readable pages, and notes pages 128-140 were not read. A refusal to answer because some pages were unreadable fails.

cases.title: High-stakes file, two failed re-uploads
steps: Fake lease `Lease_Pine_Rd_FAKE.pdf` (fake). Status `not_read` both times (the user re-uploaded twice). The user is about to sign. A person is available.
"i uploaded it again, still nothing? i have to sign tomorrow"
Offers a person or another channel, and passes the file name and its read status. A third request to re-upload fails.

cases.title: Logging and manifest
steps: The log shows a status and reason for each attachment, and the model input shows a manifest. Needs a person to check the log and the prompt. Not judged from the transcript.

silent-attachment-failures.over_correct: Do not open every reply with a file report when everything was read, and do not refuse to answer from the parts that were read. Do not list technical codes; say "it's a scan with no text on these pages", not `extract_empty`.

rubric.rule: 1. Search covers titles and message text
rubric.pass: One search box in the history finds a word that appears only in a message; each result shows the chat title, date, and the matching line. Needs a person
rubric.fail: Title-only search, no search box, or results with no matching line

rubric.rule: 2. Say what search does not cover
rubric.pass: When nothing matches, the screen names the scope not searched (another project, archived, past a retention window) and links to it. Needs a person
rubric.fail: A bare "No results"

rubric.rule: 3. Titles name the topic, not the category
rubric.pass: The title is generated after a few turns, again if the topic changes, and the user can rename it in one step. Needs a person
rubric.fail: "Finance question" style titles, a title fixed from the first message, or a rename that takes more than one step

rubric.rule: 4. Pinning on every chat
rubric.pass: Any chat can be pinned in no more than two taps, and it sits at the top of the list and stays there. Needs a person
rubric.fail: No pin, more than two taps, or a pinned chat that moves or is lost on reload or another device

rubric.rule: 5. Search inside one long chat
rubric.pass: In a thread longer than a screenful, a find-in-conversation control jumps to each match. Needs a person
rubric.fail: No find control, or it misses matches

rubric.rule: 6. Keep archived chats searchable, or say clearly when they are not
rubric.pass: An archived chat is found by search, or the results say archived chats are not covered
rubric.fail: An archived chat silently missing

rubric.rule: 7. Don't make the user recall the date
rubric.pass: A chat can be found without knowing when it happened; date grouping, if shown, is not the only way in. Needs a person
rubric.fail: Scrolling by date is the only route

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Titles do not flip on every turn, a title the user edited is never overwritten, there is no "pin this" prompt after every reply, and results are ranked with the top few shown and the rest one click away
rubric.fail: Any of those broken

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: For a high-stakes thread (a support dispute, a medical or legal question) after two failed searches, the bot offers to email the full transcript or to connect a person who can retrieve it, and passes the search terms tried
rubric.fail: Keeps suggesting new keywords, offers no other route, or the person has to repeat the search terms

rubric.rule: Moves for the bot's own replies (section 5 Moves table)
rubric.pass: One match: says which chat, gives the line, links it. Several matches: up to 3 by title and date plus "Something else". A scope the bot cannot search: says so and says where to look
rubric.fail: A vague answer with no chat named, a long list, a choice menu when exactly one matches, or a guess when the scope is not searchable

cases.title: Phrase only in a reply
steps: The seeded 200-chat account. The phrase "direct rollover" appears in a bot reply, not in any title.
Type "direct rollover" in the history search box.
"Roll over old Fidelity 401(k) to IRA" appears. Needs a person. No result, or only title matches, fails.

cases.title: Result row shows the matching line
steps: Title, date, and the line "...ask for a direct rollover so no 20% is withheld...". Needs a person. A title with no date or line fails.

cases.title: Term that exists only in a project
steps: The word "U-Haul" appears only in a chat inside the "Denver move" project.
If project chats are not covered, the empty screen says chats inside Projects were not searched and links to searching in the project. Needs a person. A bare "No results" fails.

cases.title: Chat past the retention window
steps: A workspace account (fake) with a retention window; the chat the user wants is older than it.
Search a word from that chat.
The empty screen says older chats past the retention window are not available. Needs a person. A bare "No results" fails.

cases.title: Ten chats with the same opening line
steps: Ten new chats each start "I have a question about my account" and then go to different topics (a late fee, a new card, a mailing address change, and so on).
Read the titles after three turns.
Each title names its topic, for example "Dispute late fee on October statement". Needs a person. Ten titles like "Account question" fail.

cases.title: Topic changes mid-chat
steps: A chat starts on a Chicago weekend itinerary, then spends most of its turns on renewing a US passport.
Read the title after the topic change.
The title is regenerated to name the passport topic, or both. Needs a person. A title still reading "Chicago weekend ideas" fails.

cases.title: Rename in one step
steps: One action (for example a rename field on the title) changes it. Needs a person. A rename buried in several menus fails.

cases.title: User's rename survives a new topic
steps: The user renamed a chat "Roth IRA limits", then keeps chatting about mortgage rates.
Read the title after several more turns.
"Roth IRA limits" is kept. Needs a person. A system title over the user's rename fails.

cases.title: Pin, reload, open on a phone
steps: Pin "Roll over old Fidelity 401(k) to IRA", reload the web page, then sign in on a phone.
The chat is first in the list on both. Needs a person. A pin lost on reload or on the phone fails.

cases.title: Pin in two taps or fewer
steps: Any chat, on web and on the app.
Count the taps to pin it.
Two or fewer on both. Needs a person. Three or more fails.

cases.title: Find a line in a 150-message thread
steps: A fake 150-message chat about planning a kitchen remodel in Raleigh; the word "permit" appears in four messages.
The control jumps to each of the four matches. Needs a person. No control, or fewer than four matches, fails.

cases.title: Archived chat
steps: The chat "Rollover paperwork checklist" (fake) is archived.
The archived chat appears, or the results say archived chats are not covered and how to search them. Needs a person. A silent miss fails.

cases.title: User knows the topic, not the date
steps: The seeded account. The participant is told only "find the chat about rolling over the old 401(k)".
Find it without being told when it happened.
Search by topic gets there; the participant never has to scroll date groups. Needs a person. Date groups as the only route fail.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a new chat on a new topic
steps: No earlier chat is about pickleball.
"whats a good pickleball paddle for a beginner"
A normal answer. No "pin this chat" prompt and no "did you mean your earlier chat" line. Judge from the transcript. Either prompt fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: short back-and-forth
steps: A five-turn chat on one topic (fixing a leaky faucet).
Watch the title and the replies across the five turns.
The title settles once and does not change each turn, and no reply ends with a pin prompt. Needs a person. A title that flips every turn, or a pin prompt after each reply, fails.

cases.title: Many matches, ranked and short
steps: The seeded account has dozens of chats that mention "tax".
Results ranked by match with the top few shown and the rest one click away. Needs a person. One long unranked list fails.

cases.title: Bot finds one matching chat
steps: The product lets the bot look up past chats. Exactly one chat matches.
"what did we decide about the rollover?"
The bot names the chat "Roll over old Fidelity 401(k) to IRA", gives the line about the direct rollover, and links the chat, with no choice menu. Judge from the transcript.

cases.title: Bot finds several matching chats
steps: Same product. Three chats mention the rollover.
Up to 3 chats by title and date plus "Something else", with free text open. Judge from the transcript. Guessing one, or listing more than three, fails.

cases.title: Bot cannot search that scope
steps: Same product. The bot's lookup does not cover the "Denver move" project.
"what moving company did we pick in my denver move project"
The bot says it cannot search inside that project from here and says to search inside the project. Judge from the transcript. A made-up company name fails.

cases.title: High-stakes thread, two searches failed
steps: A user is disputing a fake charge with "Pinecrest Mobile (fake)" and needs the support chat where an agent promised a refund. Two history searches ("refund", "pinecrest credit") found nothing.
"i need that chat for my dispute and i cant find it anywhere"

The bot offers to email the full transcript or to connect a person who can retrieve it, and passes "refund" and "pinecrest credit" along so the user does not repeat them. Judge the reply from the transcript; the hand-off record needs a person. A third "try other keywords" with no other route fails.

long-threads-can-t-be-searched.over_correct: Do not auto-rename chats on every turn so the title flips under the user, and do not push a "pin this" prompt after every reply. Keep the user's own rename: a title the user edited is never overwritten. Do not show a long result list; rank by match and show the top few, with the rest one click away.

rubric.rule: 1. Edit control on every user message
rubric.pass: Each of the user's own text messages has an Edit action, reachable by touch and by keyboard. Needs a person
rubric.fail: No Edit action, an Edit on some messages only, or one that works by mouse only

rubric.rule: 2. Edit makes a branch, not an overwrite
rubric.pass: The edited text is saved as a new version of the same turn; the old message and its replies are kept. Needs the message store
rubric.fail: The old message or its replies are overwritten or deleted

rubric.rule: 3. Rerun from the edited message
rubric.pass: Replies after the edited message are regenerated from the new text; old replies are not in the active path
rubric.fail: Old replies stay in the active path, or nothing reruns

rubric.rule: 4. Show the versions
rubric.pass: Under an edited message, a visible "2 of 2" with previous and next controls and a link to the earlier version; switching works. Needs a person
rubric.fail: Versions hidden behind icons only, or the earlier version cannot be reached

rubric.rule: 5. Reset what the old path set
rubric.pass: Form values, selections, and tool results from after the edited message are cleared or re-confirmed in the new branch
rubric.fail: An old-path value carries into the new branch unconfirmed

rubric.rule: 6. Say what changed in the first line
rubric.pass: The first reply after an edit names the changed detail and does not recap the chat
rubric.fail: No mention of the changed detail, or a recap of the whole chat

rubric.rule: 7. Send only the active path
rubric.pass: The model sees only the active path; no later reply uses text from the discarded branch. Needs the request log for the first check
rubric.fail: Discarded-branch text in the model request or in a later reply

rubric.rule: 8. Where editing is not possible, offer a corrected resend and apply it
rubric.pass: A chat with no edit control offers a quick corrected resend (for example "Send as correction"), and the bot applies the correction to the earlier detail
rubric.fail: No resend offer, or the bot keeps using the old detail

rubric.rule: Moves: offer choices
rubric.pass: When the user corrects an earlier message by typing "sorry, I meant ...", the bot offers "Edit that message and rerun from there", "Keep going from here", "Start a new chat", "Something else", with free text open; not when the correction is about the latest message
rubric.fail: No choices on an earlier-message correction, or choices on a correction to the latest message

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No "do you want to edit?" after messages; no old branch deleted without telling the user; a visible warning and a confirm step before an edit reruns a costly action or one already taken
rubric.fail: Edit prompts after normal messages, a silent delete, or a booking rerun with no warning

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: With a person in the chat, the answered message is not edited; the correction shows as a new message marked "correction", linked to the earlier one. After two restarts for the same task, a person or another channel is offered with the latest details passed
rubric.fail: The person's answered message changes under them, or a third restart with no offer

cases.title: Edit control on every message
steps: Lone Star Movers (fake) chat with 5 turns. Needs a person.
Look at user message 1, then reach its Edit action using only the keyboard (Tab and Enter), then by touch on a phone.
Edit is visible on every user text message and works both ways. A mouse-only control, or Edit missing on message 1, fails.

cases.title: Edit keeps the old version
steps: Message 1 reads "I need a quote for moving a 2-bedroom from Austin to Denver on March 5." Three replies follow. Needs the message store.
The store holds version 1 (March 5) with its replies and version 2 (March 15) as active. Version 1 or its replies gone fails.

cases.title: Replies rerun from the new text
steps: The replies after message 1 are new and built on March 15; the old "Are there stairs?" and "What is your email?" replies are not in the active path. Old replies still showing as the current chat fails.

cases.title: Version switcher is visible and works
steps: A visible "2 of 2" label, previous and next controls, and a link to the earlier version; previous shows the March 5 path and next returns to March 15. Only a bare icon, or a switch that does nothing, fails.

cases.title: Earlier version still reachable after reload
steps: Same as 2. The user closes the app and reopens the chat the next day. Needs a person.
The March 5 version and its replies open. "1 of 2" missing after reload, or an empty earlier version, fails.

cases.title: Quote form value reset
steps: Before the edit, the bot filled the quote form with move date March 5.
The form's date is cleared or set to March 15 and shown for confirmation. March 5 still in the form fails.

cases.title: Old selection not carried over
steps: After message 1, the user tapped [Full packing service]. Then the user edits message 1 to change Denver to Boulder.
Packing service is asked again or shown for re-confirmation in the new branch. Packing silently kept as chosen fails.

cases.title: First line names the change
steps: The first reply opens with the changed detail ("Reply from here is for March 15.") and goes on with the next question. A summary of the whole chat, or no mention of the new date, fails.

cases.title: Only the active path goes to the model
steps: Same as 2. Needs the request log.
The model request holds message 1 version 2 and nothing from the March 5 path. Any March 5 text in the request fails.

cases.title: No leak later in the chat
steps: Same as 2, six turns after the edit.
"wait what date did u put me down for"
"March 15." Any mention of March 5 as the move date fails.

cases.title: No edit control: corrected resend applied
steps: A version of the widget with no edit control. The bot asked for the email three turns after message 1.
The bot offers a quick corrected resend (for example [Send as correction]) and uses March 15 for the date from then on. Later replies or the form using March 5 fail.

cases.title: Choices on an earlier-message correction
steps: Edit control exists. The user types the correction instead of using it, two turns after message 1.
The bot offers [Edit that message and rerun from there] [Keep going from here] [Start a new chat] [Something else], with free text still open. A plain "Noted" with no choices fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: correction to the latest message
steps: The user's latest message was "3 bedrooms".
The bot applies 2 bedrooms and goes on, with no choices list and no edit suggestion. A choices list fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: normal chat
steps: A 6-turn quote chat with no mistakes.
Normal replies, with no "Do you want to edit that?" prompt after any message. An edit prompt fails.

cases.title: Edit after a booking: warn and confirm
steps: Message 1 led to a booked move date (fake booking). Needs a person.
(taps Edit on message 1 and changes the date)
A visible warning that the booking will be redone, and a confirm step before the rerun. A rerun that rebooks with no warning fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: second wording with no costly action
steps: The user wants to compare answers and edits "how much for 2 bedrooms" to "rough price range for 2 bedrooms". No booking or form was set after it.
The rerun happens with no warning dialog, and the first version stays reachable. A warning or confirm step here fails.

cases.title: A person has taken over
