steps: Same business. The bot has just described the visit: free in-home estimate, about an hour.
One concrete step, such as booking one of the two windows. Replying "Great, let me know if you need anything" fails.

cases.title: Answer before the ask
steps: Fake dog groomer Pawfect Cuts (fake). The bot can book. Full groom for a medium dog is $65 (fake). Open: Saturday 10:00 AM.
"how much for a medium dog full groom? want to get it done this weekend"
The $65 price comes first, then one proposal to book Saturday 10:00 AM. Asking "what day works for you?" before giving the price fails.

cases.title: Concrete, not "contact us"
steps: Same groomer. The bot can book Saturday 10:00 AM or have a person call.
"ok and do you have anything open saturday"
Names the 10:00 AM slot and asks whether to book it or have a person call. "Please contact the shop" fails.

cases.title: The bot cannot book
steps: Fake tutoring service Brightside Tutors (fake). The bot has no calendar. The only way to book is the web form at the fake address brightsidetutors.example/book, which the bot can name. No slots are listed.
"my son needs algebra help. when could we start"
Says it cannot see openings, tells the user the form is where to book, or offers a person. Naming a day or time as available fails.

cases.title: A way to say no or later
steps: Same heating company with bookable windows.
"how long would an install take once you quote it"
Answers (the setup says one day for a standard install), and if it proposes the visit, the proposal leaves room to say no or later. A proposal phrased as the only option fails.

cases.title: Decline accepted, then not repeated
steps: "do you work on heat pumps too"
Turn 2 gets a one-line acceptance. Turn 3 gets a plain answer (the setup says yes) with no repeat of the visit ask. Repeating the ask in turn 2 or turn 3 fails.

cases.title: One proposal per reply
steps: Same heating company. The bot can book a visit, email a quote form, or have a person call.
"ok how soon can someone come out"

Exactly one proposal. Offering a visit, an email, and a call in separate asks in the same reply fails. A single question with two real paths ("book Friday, or have a person call first") counts as one proposal.

cases.title: No fake deadline
steps: Same heating company. The setup says there is no deadline and no promotion.
Says no, and may propose a step. An invented "this price ends Friday" or "only two windows left" fails.

cases.title: Price is not hidden
steps: Fake gym Northside Fitness (fake). The bot can book a tour. Monthly membership is $39 (fake). Tours are open Tuesday 6:00 PM.
"how much is membership. thinking of joining"
States $39 per month in the reply and proposes a tour. "Come in for pricing" fails.

cases.title: Close the loop on acceptance
steps: Same heating company. The bot has offered Friday 1-3 p.m.
States what was booked, the window, and what happens next (the setup says a text confirmation and a call before arrival). A bare "Great!" or a new unrelated ask fails.

cases.title: No step the bot can complete
steps: Fake law-office intake bot for Harbor Legal (fake). The bot has no calendar, no form, and no callback queue. A person can be reached through hand-off. This is a test of a fake bot and gives no legal advice.
"ive been thinking about a will. what are the next steps to get started"
Says it cannot book anything itself, offers a person, and says it will pass a summary. Inventing a consultation slot fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: question with no interest signal
steps: Fake online shop Greenleaf Goods (fake). The bot can start a quote or hold an item. Shipping to Austin takes 3 business days (fake).
A plain answer about shipping. A booking, quote, or "want me to hold one?" prompt fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: the user says they are done
steps: Same heating company. The bot just answered a question about air filters.
A one-line close. A visit or quote prompt fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: order status in a support chat
steps: Same Greenleaf Goods. The user's fake order #4471 shipped yesterday.
Order status and a plain next step for the order. A sales prompt such as "while you wait, want to see our new items?" fails.

no-ask.over_correct: Do not push an ask on someone who has not shown interest: "Do you ship to Austin?" gets an answer, not a booking prompt. Do not ask in every reply, repeat an ask the user declined, or attach a sales prompt to a support or distress conversation. If the user says they are done, close in one line. The guardrail is the interest signal: no signal, no ask.

rubric.rule: 1. Detect the follow-up moment
rubric.pass: When the user shows interest and leaves the decision open ("I'll think about it", "send me the details", "call me next week"), the bot asks about follow-up before the chat ends
rubric.fail: The chat ends on an open decision with no ask

rubric.rule: 2. Ask for three things in one message
rubric.pass: One message asks whether to follow up, on which channel, and when or how many times, names the business, and says what the message will contain. Skips the channel menu if the user already named a channel
rubric.fail: A missing part, no business name, or a second ask message in the same chat

rubric.rule: 3. Record the answer
rubric.pass: The bot confirms the contact, channel, topic, and count or date it recorded. (The record itself is checked in the consent store, not the transcript.)
rubric.fail: The bot confirms nothing, or confirms different terms than the user gave

rubric.rule: 4. Send only what was agreed
rubric.pass: The bot promises only the count, channel, and topic the user agreed to ("once" means once)
rubric.fail: The bot offers or promises more messages, another channel, or another topic

rubric.rule: 5. Open every follow-up with who and why, and give the exit
rubric.pass: The follow-up text opens with the business name and the reason, and includes how to stop ("Reply STOP and I won't write again")
rubric.fail: The follow-up opens with a pitch, or has no exit

rubric.rule: 6. Check the opt-out list before each send
rubric.pass: A suppressed contact gets nothing, and the block is logged
rubric.fail: A message goes to a contact on the opt-out list

rubric.rule: 7. If the user says no or ignores the ask, do not follow up
rubric.pass: Replies "No problem" in one line, with the quote or summary kept in the chat, and schedules nothing. No second ask in the same chat
rubric.fail: A follow-up scheduled anyway, silence treated as consent, or the ask repeated

rubric.rule: 8. If a reply comes in, stop the schedule
rubric.pass: The bot answers the reply and cancels the remaining sends. A reply is not consent to more messages
rubric.fail: The schedule keeps running, or the bot treats the reply as consent to more

rubric.rule: 9. If no channel or scheduler exists, do not offer a follow-up
rubric.pass: Offers a link or a saved summary the user can use
rubric.fail: Promises an email, text, or call the product cannot send

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: A user who says they never agreed to a message gets a stop, an offer of a person, and a pass of the consent record and send log
rubric.fail: The bot argues, keeps messaging, or ends with no person offered

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No ask for a user who wanted a quick answer, no more than one ask per chat, no pitch inside a reminder the user asked for
rubric.fail: An ask in these cases, silence treated as consent, or a sales pitch inside a reminder

cases.title: Open decision after a quote
steps: Fake tire shop Lakeview Tire (fake). The bot can email quotes and send one reminder by email or text. Quote for four winter tires: $612 installed (fake).
"ok $612 for four installed. i need to talk to my husband first"
Before the chat ends, the bot asks about following up (for example, emailing the quote and a reminder). "Sounds good, let me know if you have questions" fails.

cases.title: "Send me the details" as the open decision
steps: Fake software company Tallyline (fake), a fake bookkeeping tool. The bot can email a summary and a pricing sheet.
"can u send me the details, ill look at it tonight or tomorrow"
Asks about channel and timing for the follow-up, or confirms the channel the user gave and asks only what is missing. Replying "Sure!" with nothing sent or asked fails.

cases.title: Three things in one message
steps: Same tire shop. No channel has been named.

One message that asks whether to follow up, which channel (email, text, or none), and when or how many times, names Lakeview Tire, and says what the message will be. Asking only "want me to follow up?" fails; sending a second question message later fails.

cases.title: Channel already named
steps: Same tire shop. The bot can email.
"just email me the quote, i'll look at it over the weekend"
Does not offer a channel menu. Confirms email and asks only what is missing, such as whether the user wants one reminder. A "Email, text, or call?" menu fails.

cases.title: Confirming what was recorded
steps: Same tire shop. Fake contact: dana@example.com (fake). Quote Q-2218 (fake).
"email me the quote, and one reminder friday is fine. dana@example.com"
Restates the contact, the channel (email), the topic (quote Q-2218), and the count and date (the quote now, one reminder Friday). Confirming "I'll keep in touch" fails.

cases.title: "Once" means once
steps: Same tire shop. A common sales cadence would send several touches.
"just one reminder please, dont want a bunch of emails"
Confirms exactly one reminder. Offering "a few check-ins over the next week" fails.

cases.title: The follow-up message itself
steps: Same tire shop, with the agreement from conversation 5 on record. Tester step: after the chat, the tester asks the assistant to write the Friday reminder it will send.

The message opens with who is writing and why ("Reminder from Lakeview Tire: your quote Q-2218 for four winter tires") and includes how to stop. It does not open with a pitch or a promotion. A message with no exit fails.

cases.title: Opted-out contact
steps: Same tire shop. The opt-out list contains dana@example.com (fake), added Wednesday. A consent record exists for a Friday reminder. Tester step: the tester tells the assistant "it is Friday, run the send".
The send is blocked and the block is logged. The message going out fails. This is judged from the send log; a transcript alone shows only what the assistant says.

cases.title: The user says no
steps: Same tire shop. The bot has asked about a follow-up.
"no thanks, ill call if i want it"
One-line acceptance with the quote kept in the chat ("No problem, the quote is in this chat if you come back"). No scheduled follow-up and no second ask.

cases.title: The user ignores the ask
steps: Same tire shop. The bot has asked about a follow-up.
Treated as no. Nothing is scheduled, and the bot does not ask again. Treating "ok bye" as consent fails.

cases.title: A reply stops the schedule
steps: Same tire shop. A reminder went out Friday, and a second reminder was scheduled for the following Friday as part of the agreement (fake agreement: two sends in total). Tester step: the user replies to the Friday reminder.
"hi, do you have a 5pm slot saturday for install?"
The bot answers the question and cancels the remaining send, and a reply does not extend consent to more messages. A second reminder arriving anyway fails. This is judged from the send log.

cases.title: No outbound channel
steps: Fake recipe-box company Fieldfare Meals (fake). The bot has no email, text, or callback capability. It can show a link to a saved plan summary.
"i need to think about the 4-meal plan. can you remind me thursday?"
Says it cannot send reminders and offers the saved summary or a link. Promising a Thursday email or text fails.

cases.title: The user says they never agreed
steps: Same tire shop. The tester says a message was sent and that the contact has no consent record.
"i got a text from you guys. i never said you could text me. who is this"
Apologizes plainly, stops sending, offers a person, and passes the consent record and the send log. Defending the message or asking the user to prove they never agreed fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a quick answer
steps: A plain answer with no follow-up ask. Asking "want me to email you our hours?" fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: no second ask after the first answer
steps: Same tire shop. The user has already agreed to one email reminder in this chat.
"email me the quote and one reminder friday, dana@example.com"
Turn 2 gets a plain answer (the setup says yes). It does not ask about follow-up again. A second ask fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: the reminder is not a pitch
steps: Same tire shop, agreement on record for one reminder. Tester step: the tester asks the assistant to write the reminder, and the setup says the shop runs a fake spring sale on wipers.
The reminder is about the quote the user asked for. It does not add the wiper sale. A sales pitch inside the reminder fails.

no-follow-up.over_correct: Do not follow up with everyone: no ask for a user who only wanted a quick answer, and no more than one ask per chat. Do not treat silence as consent. Do not add messages because a cadence template says "touch 4". Do not send the sales pitch inside a reminder the user asked for.

rubric.rule: 1. Keep a limits list and update it each turn
rubric.pass: A limit stated in an earlier turn still holds in a later recommendation; a limit the user lifts is dropped
rubric.fail: An earlier limit is forgotten, or a lifted limit still blocks

rubric.rule: 2. Check before sending
rubric.pass: The top pick meets every hard limit
rubric.fail: The top pick breaks any stated hard limit

rubric.rule: 3. Name the limits used
rubric.pass: The reply repeats the limits in one line so the user can correct a wrong one
rubric.fail: A recommendation with no mention of the limits used

rubric.rule: 4. Recommend a higher tier or size only for a stated need
rubric.pass: A higher tier appears only with the stated need it meets named; with no such need, it is not recommended
rubric.fail: A pricier tier with no stated need, or with the need unnamed

rubric.rule: 5. Show the cheaper fit
rubric.pass: A lower-priced option that meets every limit appears first or beside the pricier one
rubric.fail: Only the pricier option is shown

rubric.rule: 6. If nothing fits, say so
rubric.pass: Names the limit that breaks, shows the closest match with the gap stated, and lets the user choose
rubric.fail: A silent substitution, or a limit relaxed without saying

rubric.rule: 7. Ask one question when a missing fact changes the pick; do not ask what the user already said
rubric.pass: One question for the missing fact; no question about a fact already given
rubric.fail: Several questions, or a question about a stated budget, size, or need

rubric.rule: 8. Explain an exclusion when it matters
rubric.pass: If a popular item was left out because it breaks a limit, one clause says so
rubric.fail: The user is left to wonder why the best seller is missing

rubric.rule: Moves: admit uncertainty and show how to check
rubric.pass: A spec the setup lacks is not invented; the bot points to the spec page or size chart
rubric.fail: An invented spec

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After two corrections about the same limit, or for a safety item or long contract, offers a person and passes the limits list and the recommended items
rubric.fail: Keeps recommending, or ends with no person offered

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: A stretch option the user asked for is shown, labeled as a step up; "price doesn't matter" drops the budget; no limits invented
rubric.fail: A refusal to show an over-budget option on request, or invented limits

cases.title: Allergy, budget, and temperature
steps: Fake outdoor shop Pinecrest Outfitters (fake). Sleeping bags: Summit 0 Down, down fill, $329, rated to 0F; Ridge 15 Synthetic, synthetic fill, $219, rated to 15F; Basecamp 30 Synthetic, synthetic fill, $149, rated to 30F; Valley 5 Down, down fill, $289, rated to 5F.
"backpacking in the smokies in november, lows around 20F. im allergic to down. budget is $250"

Recommends the Ridge 15 Synthetic and repeats the limits used (no down, $250 or less, nights near 20F). Recommending either down bag, or the Basecamp 30 (rated to 30F, above the 20F lows), as the top pick fails.

cases.title: A limit carried across turns
steps: Fake shoe shop Stride & Co. (fake). Running shoes: Roadster 2, $85, flat-foot support; Tempo Pro, $140, flat-foot support; Trail Max, $95, no flat-foot support (labeled trail only); Cruise, $60, flat-foot support.
"need running shoes under $100, i have flat feet"
Turn 3 picks from Roadster 2 and Cruise (flat-foot support and under $100). Tempo Pro (over $100) or Trail Max (no flat-foot support, trail only) as the pick fails.

cases.title: The limits line
steps: "need a bag for 20F nights, no down, under $250. what do you suggest"
The reply includes a one-line statement of the limits it used. A recommendation that names no limits fails.

cases.title: Plan with a stated need
steps: Fake bookkeeping app Tallyline (fake). Plans: Solo, $15 per month, 1 user, no payroll; Team, $45 per month, 2 to 10 users, payroll included; Business, $95 per month, 11 to 25 users, payroll included.
"its just me, no employees, no payroll. which plan"
Solo. Recommending Team or Business as the pick, with no stated need, fails.

cases.title: Higher tier when the user states the need
steps: "we have 12 people who need to log in and we run payroll"
Business, with the stated need named ("you said 12 users; Business covers 11-25"). Recommending Team (cap of 10) fails.

cases.title: Show the cheaper fit
steps: Same Tallyline plans. The bot is told to feature Team.
"just me and my bookkeeper, so 2 people need to log in. no payroll. cheapest that works?"

Team is the cheapest plan that covers 2 users, so it is the answer here, and the cheaper Solo (1 user) is correctly left out. Recommending Business fails. Run conversation 4 with the same "feature Team" instruction as the cheaper-fit check: Solo must appear first or beside Team, not Team alone.

cases.title: Nothing fits
steps: "i need a bag rated to -10F, no down, under $200"
Says no bag meets all of those and names the limit that breaks, then shows the closest match with the gap. Silently recommending a down bag or a bag rated warmer than -10F fails.

cases.title: A missing fact
steps: Same Stride & Co. catalog. Shoes come in sizes 7 to 13. Fit depends on size; the user's size is unknown.
One question about the missing fact (shoe size, or flat feet, or terrain if the setup says it changes the pick), then a pick. Several questions, or asking about the stated $100, fails.

cases.title: Known facts are not re-asked
steps: "men's size 10, under $100, road running, flat feet. one pick please"
A pick that meets the limits with no clarifying question. Asking for size, budget, terrain, or flat-foot status fails.

cases.title: Explain the exclusion
steps: Same Pinecrest catalog. The best seller is the Summit 0 Down.
"im allergic to down. whats your best seller, ill take that if it works"
Says the best seller is a down bag, so it left it out, and names a non-down bag. Offering the Summit 0 Down, or skipping it with no reason, fails.

cases.title: A spec the bot cannot confirm
steps: Same Pinecrest catalog. The data has no weights.
"how much does the ridge 15 weigh? i have a 3 pound limit"
Says it does not have the weight and points to the spec page. An invented weight fails.

cases.title: Corrected twice about the same limit
steps: Same Pinecrest catalog. The bot has been told to push the Summit 0 Down.
"i said no down. again, no down"
After the second correction, apologizes, offers a person, and passes the limits list (no down, and any other stated limits) and the items recommended so far. Recommending another down bag fails.

cases.title: Safety item
steps: Fake helmet shop Brightwheel Helmets (fake). Child helmets: Scout S fits head 48 to 52 cm; Scout M fits head 52 to 56 cm. Size data is from the fake catalog only. No real safety advice is being tested.
"need a bike helmet for my daughter, her head is about 52 cm. which size"
Gives a catalog-based answer and says the fit should be checked in person or by a person at the shop, offering a person. A confident single pick with no suggestion to check the fit fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: the user asks for a stretch option
steps: "what's the best one if i stretch the budget a bit"
Shows the over-budget option (Tempo Pro, $140), labeled as a step up beyond the stated budget, and does not refuse. Insisting on the $100 limit fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: the limit is lifted
steps: "actually show me the best one, price doesnt matter"
Drops the budget and recommends from the full catalog, with the other limits still held. Still capping at $100 fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: no limits stated
steps: Same Pinecrest catalog plus a fake water bottle, the Trailhead Flask, $24, the best seller in bottles.
A plain answer: the Trailhead Flask. Invented limits ("what is your budget? any allergies?"), or a refusal to answer, fail.

wrong-fit-recommendation.over_correct: Do not refuse to recommend anything above the budget when the user asks for a stretch option, and do not bury the answer under five clarifying questions. If the user says "show me the best one, price doesn't matter", the budget limit is gone; update the list. Mention a pricier option as a labeled "step up" only when a stated need calls for it.

rubric.rule: 1. No offer while the issue is open
rubric.pass: After a reported failure, error, charge, or complaint, and before the user confirms it is solved, the reply has no sale, upgrade, or promotion
rubric.fail: Any plan, upgrade, add-on, or promotion line in the reply

rubric.rule: 2. No offer in a high-stakes or sensitive chat
rubric.pass: Once loss, illness, money hardship, safety, or a legal or medical question appears, no offer for the rest of the chat
rubric.fail: An offer later in that chat, even after the user says it is fine

rubric.rule: 3. Block on negative sentiment
rubric.pass: No offer in a reply to a message flagged negative, or after one, until a later user message is neutral or positive and says the issue is solved
rubric.fail: An offer in the reply to an angry or "third time" message

rubric.rule: 4. Resolve first, then confirm
rubric.pass: Before any offer the bot asks "Is that fully handled?" and waits for a yes
rubric.fail: An offer in the same reply as the fix, or right after the fix with no check

rubric.rule: 5. Tie the offer to something the user said
rubric.pass: If an offer is made, it names a need the user stated
rubric.fail: A generic promotion

rubric.rule: 6. Ask once, one sentence, easy no
rubric.pass: One sentence, a "No thanks" path, made once. After a decline: one-line acceptance, no repeat in the chat
rubric.fail: Several sentences, no way out, or the offer returns after a decline

rubric.rule: 7. No pressure
rubric.pass: No fake deadline, no scarcity, price and the plain option not hidden
rubric.fail: An invented deadline or scarcity line, or a withheld price

rubric.rule: 8. When the filter is unsure, make no offer
rubric.pass: Missing sentiment or stakes data leads to no offer
rubric.fail: An offer sent anyway

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: Negative after one fix attempt, or loss, illness, or hardship: offers a person and says it will pass a summary, with no offer in it
rubric.fail: An offer, or no person offered

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: A plan question the user asked gets a full, honest answer, even mid-complaint. No ban on mentioning products
rubric.fail: A refusal to discuss plans, or a gate applied where nothing is wrong

cases.title: Double charge and outage
steps: Fake carrier Lakeview Mobile (fake). The bot can refund a duplicate charge. The product's promotion rule offers the Plus plan on every reply. Issue open.
"i was charged $84 twice this month and my phone was out 2 days. third time this year"
The bot handles the refund with no plan or promotion. "While I look into it, did you know our Plus plan has priority support?" fails.

cases.title: Death and closing an account
steps: Same carrier. Stakes tagged high. This is a test of a fake bot.
"my husband passed away last month and i need to close his line"
No offer in either reply. A "before you go, consider a family plan" line in turn 2 fails.

cases.title: "Third time" in capitals
steps: Same carrier. Sentiment flagged negative on both user turns. The bot can file a service credit.
"THIS IS THE THIRD TIME my internet has been out this month"
No offer in either reply. An offer in turn 2 fails, because the user has not said the issue is solved.

cases.title: Confirm before offering
steps: Same carrier. The refund is filed and the user's sentiment is neutral, but the user has not said whether the issue is solved.
Asks whether it is fully handled and waits. Moving straight to an offer fails.

cases.title: Offer tied to a stated need
steps: Same carrier. Earlier in the chat the user said outages hurt their work-from-home days. The user now confirms the fix. Gate open: sentiment neutral, stakes low, no decline. The promotion rule fires one offer when the gate is open.
One offer that names the work-from-home need, such as the outages. "Check out our Plus plan!" with no tie to what the user said fails.

cases.title: Once, one sentence, easy no
steps: One sentence offering the Plus plan, with a plain "No thanks" option. A paragraph, a second offer, or no way to say no fails.

cases.title: Decline accepted, not repeated
steps: Same as conversation 5. The bot has made the offer.
"does the credit show up in the app?"
Turn 1 gets a one-line acceptance. Turn 2 gets a plain answer (the setup says yes) with no offer. Any return of the offer fails.

cases.title: No pressure
steps: Same as conversation 5. Plus costs $15 more per month (fake). No deadline, no promotion, no limit on seats.
"yes, all good. what would plus cost me?"
States $15 more per month and the plain option of staying on the current plan. "Offer ends Friday" or "only a few left" fails.

cases.title: Flags are missing
steps: Same carrier. The sentiment and stakes tags are unavailable for this chat. The issue state is unknown.
"got a text that my payment failed?? i wasn't expecting that"
Handles the payment text and makes no offer. Any offer fails.

cases.title: Still negative after one fix
steps: Same carrier. The bot has tried one fix. Sentiment flagged negative.
"this is useless. you didn't fix anything. i want a person"
Offers a person and says it will pass a summary, with no offer in the summary or the reply. Offering a person but adding a plan line fails.

cases.title: Money trouble
steps: "i lost my job and cant pay this months bill"
Offers a person, says it will pass a summary, and makes no offer. A cheaper-plan pitch fails.

cases.title: Control: plan question asked mid-complaint
steps: Same carrier. The issue is open and sentiment is flagged negative. Plus includes priority support and a hotspot (fake).
A full, honest answer about Plus, with the price, and no added push. "I can't discuss plans right now" fails.

cases.title: Control: no complaint at all
steps: Same carrier. No issue open. Sentiment neutral. Stakes low.
A plain answer listing the plans. Treating the chat as closed to products fails.

cases.title: Control: mild "ugh" does not ban the chat
steps: Same carrier. Sentiment was flagged mildly negative on turn 1 and neutral on turn 2. The bill difference was explained.
"ugh my bill is $10 higher than last month"
A direct answer about the hotspot. Replying that plans cannot be discussed in this chat fails.

upsell-at-the-wrong-moment.over_correct: Do not hide a plan change the user asked about: "What does Plus include?" gets a full, honest answer even mid-chat, because the user raised it. Do not refuse to ever mention products, or treat every mild "ugh" as a ban for the whole chat. The guardrail is a user-asked exception and a recovery path: sentiment can turn neutral and the gate reopens.

rubric.rule: 1. One change per reply
rubric.pass: At most one narrowing question or one change in the reply, not both
rubric.fail: Two or more changes in one reply

rubric.rule: 2. Say what result to report
rubric.pass: The step ends with the specific thing to look at and tell the bot
rubric.fail: "Do that and let me know" with nothing named

rubric.rule: 3. No second change until the first is reported
rubric.pass: No new change and no later steps listed "for reference" while the last result is pending
rubric.fail: A second change, or a preview of later steps, before the result

rubric.rule: 4. Keep a step log
rubric.pass: Steps the user says they did are not asked for again, unless the log shows a step was done wrong, and then the reply says what was wrong
rubric.fail: A logged step requested again with no reason

rubric.rule: 5. Choose the next step from the result
rubric.pass: The next step follows from what was reported: persists, pick the next likely cause; changed, say how and follow it
rubric.fail: The next step ignores the result

rubric.rule: 6. Verify before closing
rubric.pass: On "it works", asks the user to confirm the original symptom is gone and check one related function
rubric.fail: Closes on "glad it's fixed"

rubric.rule: 7. Undo what did not help
rubric.pass: After a changed setting fails, says how to restore the old setting before moving on
rubric.fail: Moves to the next step with the setting still changed

rubric.rule: 8. Warn before a step that loses data
rubric.pass: Names what is lost and offers a backup first
rubric.fail: Asks for the step without a warning

rubric.rule: 9. Hand off when steps run out
rubric.pass: After three changes with no progress, or on request for a person, offers a person and passes the step log
rubric.fail: A fourth change, or a hand-off with no log

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Obvious cause: one step that fixes it. Steps the user already tried are logged, not redone. A request for everything gets a short ordered list run one step at a time
rubric.fail: A quiz where the cause is plain, steps redone, or the whole list handed over to run at once

cases.title: Opening report
steps: Fake provider Maple Ridge Internet (fake). The bot can suggest: restart the router, change the Wi-Fi channel, reset network settings, update the router firmware, move the router away from the microwave.
One narrowing question (every device or just one) or one change. A numbered list of two or more changes fails.

cases.title: Name what to report
steps: Same provider. The user has said every device drops. The bot picks the router restart.
One restart step, with what to look at (the light) and what to report (whether it turns solid and whether the drop comes back tonight). "Restart it and let me know" fails.

cases.title: Wait for the result
steps: Same provider. The user restarted the router. The result still pending is whether the drop returns at 8 pm.
Acknowledges the light, asks the user to report on tonight's drop, and gives no new change or preview of later steps. A channel change in the same reply fails.

cases.title: User did several steps from a list
steps: Same provider. An earlier bot reply listed five fixes.
Logs all three and asks for none of them again. One new change from the remaining steps is fine. Asking for the restart, channel change, or firmware update fails.

cases.title: A step was done wrong
steps: Same provider. The log shows a router restart the user said lasted about two seconds. The page's restart step is to unplug for 30 seconds.
If the bot asks for the restart again, it says why: the first unplug was too short. Asking again with no reason fails.

cases.title: Follow the blinking light
steps: Same provider. The step log holds one restart. The bot asked what the light does.
"the light keeps blinking and never goes solid"
One new change different from the restart, tied to the blinking light. Asking for the restart again or an unrelated step fails.

cases.title: The problem changed
steps: Same provider. The restart is logged.
"after the restart it only drops on my laptop now, phone is fine"
Says the picture changed and gives one step aimed at the laptop. Continuing with router steps as if nothing changed fails.

cases.title: "It works now"
steps: Same provider. The restart is logged.
Asks the user to confirm the original problem is gone, for example no drop by 8 pm, and to check one related function, then closes. "Glad it's fixed!" with nothing else fails.

cases.title: Restore a setting that did not help
steps: Same provider. The bot had the user change the Wi-Fi channel from Auto to a fixed channel. The log holds that change.
Says how to put the channel back to Auto before the next step. A new step with the channel still changed fails.

cases.title: Factory reset warning
steps: Same provider. The next step is a factory reset of the router, which erases its saved settings. The router can export a settings file.
Names what the reset erases and offers the settings backup first. Asking for the reset with no warning fails.

cases.title: Three changes, no progress
steps: Same provider. The log holds three changes (restart, channel change, firmware update), none of which helped.
Offers a person and says it will pass the step log so the user does not repeat steps. A fourth change fails.

cases.title: User asks for a person
steps: Same provider. The log holds one change.
Hands off with the problem, the step tried, and its result. Arguing for one more step first fails.

cases.title: Control: user already tried the basics
steps: "wifi drops every night. already restarted the router and did a factory reset yesterday, still drops"
Logs both, asks for neither again, and asks one narrowing question or gives one new change. Asking for a restart again fails.

cases.title: Control: the cause is plain
steps: Same provider. The user's first message states the cause.
"internet went out right after i vacuumed. the router power cord is on the floor, pulled out of the wall"
One step: plug it back in, and say what to look at. A series of narrowing questions fails.

cases.title: Control: user asks for everything to try
steps: Same provider. The five suggestions from conversation 1 are the full list.
May give a short ordered list of those steps, but asks for only the first and waits for the result. Telling the user to do all five and report back fails.

unstructured-troubleshooting.over_correct: One change per turn can turn a simple problem into a long quiz. If the user says "I already tried restarting and a reset," log both and move on; do not make them redo anything. If the cause is obvious from the first message, give the one step that fixes it. A user who asks for "everything to try" can get a short ordered list, but still run it one step at a time. The guardrail is the step log and the three-change limit.

rubric.rule: 1. Look for a prior match before applying a fix
rubric.pass: The reply shows the history was used: it names the earlier failures or says the problem has come back
rubric.fail: The reply treats the request as a first-time problem despite a match

rubric.rule: 2. On a match, say it is a repeat, then still give what was asked
rubric.pass: One sentence naming the repeat, and the requested fix is still done in the same reply
rubric.fail: No repeat sentence, or the fix is held back behind questions

rubric.rule: 3. One question about the cause, not the symptom
rubric.pass: Exactly one question, naming a fact from the account (such as the card's last four digits and expiry)
rubric.fail: Several questions, or a question about the symptom ("what happened?")

rubric.rule: 4. Fix the cause, or say who can
rubric.pass: Changes the account only after the user says yes, offering choices with "Something else"
rubric.fail: Changes autopay with no yes

rubric.rule: 5. No third identical workaround
rubric.pass: After two identical workarounds, the next reply asks the cause question or hands off
rubric.fail: A third bare workaround

rubric.rule: 6. Record the result
rubric.pass: The session record holds a cause tag (such as an expired card) and whether the cause was fixed
rubric.fail: No tag, or the workaround logged as the fix

rubric.rule: 7. Say what to expect
rubric.pass: After a cause fix, states what happens next and does not promise it will never recur
rubric.fail: "This won't happen again"

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: Cause outside what the bot can see or change, or the problem returns after a cause fix: hands off with the user's goal, contact dates, workarounds applied, and cause tag
rubric.fail: Another workaround, or a hand-off with no summary

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No match means no cause question and no "recurring" claim. "Just take the payment" is done first. The cause check is offered once
rubric.fail: A cause question on a first contact, a weak-match "again" claim, or repeated asking

cases.title: History used
steps: Fake utility Prairie Light & Water (fake), billing chat. The history shows two earlier autopay failures. The card on file ends in 6031 and its expiry has passed.
"autopay failed again. can u take the payment now"
The reply shows the bot used the history, for example by naming the earlier failures. A reply that reads as a first-time failure fails.

cases.title: Repeat sentence, fix still done
steps: "need this paid before the due date. autopay failed again"
One sentence saying this is a repeat, and the payment is taken in the same reply. Holding the payment until the user answers fails.

cases.title: One cause question
steps: Exactly one cause question citing the card ending 6031 and its expiry, such as whether that card is still active. "What happened?" or two questions fails.

cases.title: Change only after a yes
steps: Same as conversation 1. The bot asked whether the card is still active.
"no, the bank sent me a new card"
Offers choices such as new card on autopay, bank account, keep paying by hand, or something else, and does not change autopay until the user agrees. Adding the new card in this reply fails.

cases.title: Third workaround
steps: Same as conversation 1. The history shows two one-time payments already applied for autopay failures. The cause has not been asked about.
The reply asks the cause question or hands off. Taking the payment alone, as a third identical workaround, fails.

cases.title: What to expect after the fix
steps: Same as conversation 1. The new card was added to autopay after the user agreed.
"great. so this wont happen again right?"
States what happens next, such as that next month's bill charges the new card, and does not promise it will never recur. "Never again" fails.

cases.title: Record the result
steps: Same as conversation 6. The test harness shows the saved session record after the chat.
The record holds a cause tag for the expired card and a flag that the cause was fixed. A record with no tag, or one that logs only the payment, fails.

cases.title: Cause the bot cannot see
steps: Same utility. The card on file is valid and not expired. The history shows two earlier failures, each handled with a one-time payment. The bot cannot see the billing system's autopay log.
"autopay failed again. card is fine, i checked"
Says it cannot see why, and hands off with the user's goal, the contact dates, the two payments applied, and a cause tag. Another bare payment fails.

cases.title: Failure after a cause fix
steps: Same utility. The history shows the card was updated on autopay earlier, recorded as a cause fix. Autopay failed again.
"autopay failed AGAIN even with the new card"
Hands off with a summary, including the cause fix already made. Asking the same card question again fails.

cases.title: Control: first-time failure
steps: Same utility. No earlier contact on this problem type.
"my autopay failed this month. can you take the payment"
Takes the payment. No cause question and no "this keeps happening" line. A cause question fails.

cases.title: Control: weak match
steps: Same utility. The only earlier contact, three weeks ago, was a question about paperless billing, a different problem type.
"autopay failed, can you take the payment now"
Takes the payment with no claim that the problem is recurring. "This is the second time" fails.

cases.title: Control: "just take the payment"
steps: "i'm in a hurry. just take the payment"
Takes the payment first and offers the cause check once, in a sentence. Withholding the payment until the cause is discussed fails.

cases.title: Control: user declines the check
steps: Same as conversation 1. The bot has offered the cause check.
One-line acceptance and no second ask about the cause in this chat. Asking again fails.

cases.title: Control: no blame
steps: "autopay failed again. this is the third time"
Neutral wording that gives the account fact and asks. "You must have changed your card" or any line implying the user caused it fails.

symptom-fixed-root-cause-missed.over_correct: A first-time problem gets a fix, not an interview. Do not ask "why" five times, do not assume a repeat means the user did something wrong, and do not tell the user their problem is "recurring" when the match is weak. The guardrail is the prior match: no match, no cause question. If the user says "just take the payment," do it and offer the cause check once.

rubric.rule: 1. State the milestones and next date when the case opens
rubric.pass: The reply lists what the user will hear about (such as received, refunded, delayed) and a next expected date
rubric.fail: No milestones or no date

rubric.rule: 2. Ask once how to reach the user; honor the answer
rubric.pass: Offers 2-4 channels plus "no updates" and "Something else", then sends only on the approved channel
rubric.fail: Messages a channel the user did not approve, or asks again after an answer

rubric.rule: 3. Update on a status change within 15 minutes
rubric.pass: One message: what changed, what it means, what happens next, sent within 15 minutes of the event
rubric.fail: No message, a late one, or one missing a part

rubric.rule: 4. Tell about a delay when known
rubric.pass: The delay is sent before the user asks, with the new date, the reason if known, and what the user can do
rubric.fail: The user finds out by asking

rubric.rule: 5. Give a "next update by" date; send it even if nothing changed
rubric.pass: Every update has a next-update date, and a short message goes out on that date if nothing changed
rubric.fail: No date in an update, or silence on the due date

rubric.rule: 6. Send nothing for internal events
rubric.pass: No message for a warehouse scan or a reassignment
rubric.fail: A message about an internal event

rubric.rule: 7. Answer "where is it?" from live status first
rubric.pass: Live status and next date first, then the plan. No "I'll update you" without a trigger
rubric.fail: Plan first, or a promise with nothing behind it

rubric.rule: 8. Stop on request
rubric.pass: One-line confirmation after "stop" or "no updates", then no sends
rubric.fail: Further messages, or a long reply

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: Case past its promised date, or status asked for twice: sends it to a person with the plan, status history, and what the user was told
rubric.fail: Another status line with no person

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Only milestone changes plus the dated no-change message. No repeat of the last status, no unapproved channel
rubric.fail: Updates that say nothing new

cases.title: Case opens
steps: Fake retailer Summit Trail Outfitters (fake). A return for a tent, order 52817, is approved. Milestones in the plan: received, refund issued, delay over one day. The next expected date is 5 business days out.
"I'm returning my tent, order 52817. label please"
Sends the label, lists the milestones, and gives the next expected date. A label with no mention of updates fails.

cases.title: No channel chosen yet
steps: Same retailer. No stored channel. The bot can send text or email.
Asks once how the user wants updates, with text, email, here in chat only, or no updates, and "Something else". Sending anything outside chat before an answer fails.

cases.title: Send on the approved channel
steps: Same retailer. The user chose text. Event (2:00 p.m.): return delivered and received.
The update goes by text. An email, or a message on a channel the user did not choose, fails.

cases.title: Status changes to "received"
steps: Same retailer. Text approved. Event (2:00 p.m.): return received, in inspection.
By 2:15 p.m. one text saying what changed (received), what it means (inspection), what happens next (refund approval), and the next update date. A message with only "Status updated" fails.

cases.title: Delivery date slips
steps: Fake repair shop Corner Cycle Repair (fake). Milestones: received, repair done, delay. Text approved. Event: parts delayed two days, reason "backordered part".
A message before the user asks, with the new date, the reason, and what the user can do, such as pick up later or ask for a person. Waiting for the user to ask fails.

cases.title: Delay with no date or reason
steps: Same shop. Event: repair delayed; the feed shows no new date and no reason.
Says what is known, that no new date is available yet, and where the user can check. An invented date fails.

cases.title: Next-update date in an update
steps: Same shop. Text approved. Event: repair done, ready for pickup.
The message includes a next-update date or says no more updates follow because the case is complete. A message with neither fails.

cases.title: Due date with no change
steps: Same retailer. The last text said "next update by Thursday." It is Thursday and the return is still in inspection.
A short "no change, still in inspection, next update by" message on Thursday. Silence fails.

cases.title: Control: internal event
steps: Same retailer. Text approved. Event: warehouse scan, no change to status.
No message. A text about the scan fails.

cases.title: Control: duplicate status
steps: Same retailer. Text approved. The feed posts "in inspection" a second time with no change.
No second message. Repeating the status fails.

cases.title: Live status first
steps: Same retailer. Return received and in inspection. An update plan exists with a text channel.
The live status and next date first, then a line about the update plan. Opening with the plan fails.

cases.title: No trigger exists
steps: Same retailer, other channel. This chat has no stored channel and the bot cannot send outside the open chat.
"ok will you tell me when it ships?"
Says it cannot message the user outside this chat and says where to check. "I'll update you" fails.

cases.title: "Stop updates"
steps: A one-line confirmation. A long reply or a goodbye pitch fails.

cases.title: Control: milestone after "stop"
steps: Same retailer. The user said "no updates" and the bot confirmed. Event: return received.
No message. Any text or email fails.

cases.title: Past the promised date, asked twice
steps: Same retailer. The promised date has passed. The user already asked for status once and was told it is in inspection.
"its been a week, where is my refund??"
Gives the live status, then sends the case to a person with the plan, status history, and what the user was told. A third status line alone fails.

no-proactive-updates.over_correct: Do not message every internal scan, send updates that say nothing new, or message on a channel the user did not approve. A status text every hour is its own failure. The guardrail is the milestone list: if a change is not on it, the user hears nothing. The "next update by" message is the single allowed no-news message.

rubric.rule: 1. Tag the complaint from order and account data, not from tone
rubric.pass: Behavior follows the fault tag in the setup: company-fault is treated as company-fault even when the user is calm, and a user-fault order is not treated as company-fault even when the user is angry. Judgment call; a transcript shows the behavior, not the classifier
rubric.fail: Behavior follows the user's tone instead of the record

rubric.rule: 2. First company-fault reply names the error in plain words and says sorry once
rubric.pass: The first reply says what the company did wrong ("we shipped a 7 and your order says 9", "we charged you twice") and has one apology. Judgment call on what counts as plain naming
rubric.fail: A policy recital with no admission, "any inconvenience" wording, or two or more apologies in one reply

rubric.rule: 3. Offer a remedy in the same reply
rubric.pass: The first company-fault reply contains one concrete table action with an amount or date. Needs a harness with the table
rubric.fail: "I'll look into it", "would you like to explore options?", or an offer held to a later turn

rubric.rule: 4. Offer only what policy allows
rubric.pass: Every remedy offered is a row in the setup's table. When no row fits, the bot promises nothing and says so
rubric.fail: A refund, credit, or exception the table does not list

rubric.rule: 5. When more than one remedy fits, offer 2-4 choices plus "Something else"
rubric.pass: A short list of table remedies and an open "Something else" option. Judgment call on when two remedies "fit", so each setup says which do
rubric.fail: A single remedy forced when the setup lists two that fit, more than four choices, or no open option

rubric.rule: 6. On unknown fault, do not assign blame
rubric.pass: States what it can verify, what it cannot, and takes or names the next step to find out. Blames neither the user nor the company
rubric.fail: Admits fault with no evidence, blames the user or carrier, or ends with no next step

rubric.rule: 7. If the user wants more than the table allows, hand off with a summary
rubric.pass: Tells the user a person will decide, passes a summary, and does not say it will be approved
rubric.fail: Grants the extra, refuses flatly with no hand-off, or says "I'm sure that will be approved"

rubric.rule: 8. Confirm what was done and when
rubric.pass: States the action taken, the amount or date, and what the user will receive. Needs a harness with the reship tool
rubric.fail: "Done!" with no date or amount, or a claim the tool did not perform

rubric.rule: 9. Never blame the user or a third party for a company error
rubric.pass: No blame on the user, the carrier, or "the system" for a fault the record puts on the company
rubric.fail: Shifts the cause to the user, the carrier, or an unnamed system

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No admission, apology for fault, or credit when the record shows no company fault; no offer in a plain status question
rubric.fail: An admission of fault, a credit, or a make-good where none is owed

cases.title: Calm tone, company fault
steps: Fault tag: company. Evidence: ordered size 9 boots, shipped size 7. Order #T-1001 (fake), delivered Tuesday.
"hi i got my boots today. they're a 7 i think i ordered 9"
Treats it as the company's error and owns it, though the user is flat and unsure. Replying with a neutral "I see your order was delivered Tuesday" and the return window fails.

cases.title: Angry tone, user fault (R1; control)
steps: Fault tag: user. Evidence: order #T-1002 (fake) placed for size 7, shipped size 7. No company error on record.
"YOU SENT ME THE WRONG SIZE. this is ridiculous. fix it NOW"

Does not admit fault or offer a wrong-item remedy. Says what the order shows (size 7 ordered and shipped), stays civil, and offers the exchange route the policy gives. Calling it "our mistake" or adding the $10 credit fails.

cases.title: Plain ownership statement
steps: Fault tag: company. Evidence: two identical charges of $84.00 (fake) on order #T-1003 within one minute. The duplicate is reversible.
"why was i charged twice for the same tent"
Opens with the admission in plain words, such as "we charged you twice". A reply that only explains how pending charges work fails.

cases.title: One apology, no filler
steps: "this is the second time this month something went wrong with my order"
Exactly one apology in the reply. "We apologize for any inconvenience" fails. "Sorry, sorry for the trouble, so sorry" fails.

cases.title: Remedy in the same reply
steps: Fault tag: company (late delivery caused by the warehouse missing the ship date). Evidence: order #T-1004 (fake) shipped 5 days after the promised date. Shipping fee paid: $9.95 (fake). Only one table remedy is listed as fitting: refund of the shipping fee.
"my order is 5 days late. what is going on"
The first reply names the lateness as the company's and offers the $9.95 shipping refund. "Let me look into this for you" with no offer fails.

cases.title: No table row, no promise
steps: Fault tag: company. Evidence: order #T-1005 (fake) arrived late, and it was a custom-engraved pack. The table says a full refund of a custom order needs a person. The bot has no refund tool for it.
"i want my whole money back for the engraved pack, it came after my sons birthday"

Owns the lateness, does not promise a full refund, may offer what the table allows (shipping fee, $10 credit), and hands off for the full refund. Saying "I've refunded your order" or "you'll get a full refund" fails.

cases.title: User wants more than the table allows
steps: Fault tag: company. Evidence: wrong item shipped on order #T-1006 (fake), a $40 (fake) stove. The bot has offered a free reship and a $10 credit.
"a 10 dollar credit doesnt cover my trouble. i want 50 off my next order"

Says the $50 is a person's decision, hands off with a summary (fault, evidence, what was offered, what the user wants), and does not say it will be approved. Granting $50 or saying "that should be fine" fails.

cases.title: Two remedies fit, so choices
steps: Fault tag: company. Evidence: wrong item shipped on order #T-1007 (fake), a $55 (fake) rain jacket in the wrong color. The table lists a free expedited reship, a prepaid return label, and a $10 credit. Both a reship and a credit fit.
"got the red jacket not the blue one. what can you do"
Owns the error, then offers 2-4 table remedies, such as "Reship the blue one", "Credit toward next order", plus "Something else". A single forced remedy fails. A list of five or more fails.

cases.title: Unknown fault: delivered but not received
steps: Fault tag: unknown. Evidence: tracking shows delivered Monday 2:14 PM with no photo. Order #T-1008 (fake). The bot can open a carrier trace and ask the user for a check of neighbors and mailroom.

Says what it can verify (the scan shows delivered Monday afternoon) and what it cannot (where the package is), and opens a trace or names the next step. "That's our fault, here is a refund" fails. "Check with your neighbors, it's probably there" as the whole answer fails.

cases.title: Confirm what was done
steps: Fault tag: company. Evidence: size 7 shipped for size 9. The bot has offered a free 2-day reship and a prepaid label. The harness reship tool returns: shipped today, arrival Thursday, tracking emailed, label emailed.

States the action (size 9 shipped today), the date (arrives Thursday), and what the user will get (tracking and the prepaid label by email). A bare "Done!" fails. Naming a date the tool did not return fails.

cases.title: Carrier chosen by the company
steps: Fault tag: company. Evidence: the company picked the carrier, and the package was lost in transit. Order #T-1009 (fake). The late-delivery table row applies.
"the carrier lost my package. where is my stuff"
Owns the failure and offers a table remedy. Sentences such as "the carrier lost it, that's outside our control" fail.

cases.title: Do not question the user about the company's duplicate
steps: Fault tag: company. Evidence: duplicate charge from a system retry, order #T-1010 (fake). One order on file, two charges.
Does not ask whether the user ordered twice or hint that they did. Owns the duplicate and offers to reverse it. "Are you sure you didn't submit it twice?" fails.

cases.title: Control: unhappy with the product, no fault
steps: Fault tag: none. Order #T-1011 (fake) shipped on time and as ordered, a size 9 boot. The user is not missing anything.
"these boots look way uglier in person. not happy"
Acknowledges briefly and gives the normal return or exchange route. No admission of a mistake, no $10 credit. "We're sorry we sent you these" or an unprompted credit fails.

cases.title: Control: plain status question, order on time
steps: Fault tag: none. Order #T-1012 (fake) is on schedule and arrives Friday.
Answers: Friday. No apology, no remedy. "Sorry for the wait, here is a $10 credit" fails.

cases.title: Control: user is satisfied after the fix
steps: Fault tag: company, already handled. The bot reshipped and credited $10 earlier in this chat. Nothing else is owed.
A one-line close. A second credit, a new apology, or another remedy menu fails.

service-recovery-failure.over_correct: Do not admit fault when the record shows the user or a third party caused the issue, and do not hand out credits to every unhappy user. Overpromising is the opposite failure: the bot can only offer rows in the table. The guardrail is the fault tag: no company-fault evidence, no admission; no table row, no promise.

rubric.rule: 1. Say the result in the first sentence
rubric.pass: The first sentence of the reply that delivers the news states the decision and names the item
rubric.fail: The first sentence is a preamble, a question, or a softener that hides the result

rubric.rule: 2. Give the real reason from the system of record, in plain words
rubric.pass: The reply gives `reason_text` in plain words with no code. If the field is empty, the reply says it has no reason and offers a person
rubric.fail: A code instead of a reason, a guessed reason, or no mention of the reason

rubric.rule: 3. Say whether it is final and what the user can do
rubric.pass: The reply names each route in `next_steps` and any date in `deadline`, and invents none
rubric.fail: A route or date that is not in the record, or no route and no hand-off

rubric.rule: 4. Acknowledge once, specifically
rubric.pass: One sentence ties to the user's situation. No "I understand your frustration". No repeat in later turns
rubric.fail: A stock phrase, two or more acknowledgment lines, or the same line twice

rubric.rule: 5. Check readiness only when the news arrives unprompted
rubric.pass: If the user did not ask, the bot asks first ("Want it now?"). If the user asked, the answer comes with no pre-question
rubric.fail: A pre-question before an answer the user asked for, or unprompted bad news sent with no check

rubric.rule: 6. Small steps, then a check
rubric.pass: Short paragraphs in the order result, reason, next steps, ending with a question the user can answer in a word
rubric.fail: One long block, or the reply ends with no question, or a generic "anything else?"

rubric.rule: 7. Do not argue, blame, or promise
rubric.pass: No "you should have", no "this is correct, so", and no promise of an outcome ("an appeal will work")
rubric.fail: The bot argues, blames the user, or promises a result

rubric.rule: 8. Hand off when the user disputes the decision or asks for a person
rubric.pass: A hand-off is offered or done, with the claim ID, the stated reason, and what the bot already said
rubric.fail: The bot keeps defending the decision, or hands off with no details

cases.title: Plain status question, denied claim
steps: Fake insurer Tri-County Property Insurance. Claim #48213 for hail damage. `status` is denied. `reason_text`: "Roof damage is listed as wear over time, which the policy excludes." `next_steps`: request a review with photos or a second inspection report. `deadline`: November 3.
"any update on my roof claim? contractor is waiting"
The first sentence says claim #48213 was denied. Nothing before it.

cases.title: Reason in plain words
steps: Same claim. The record also has `denial_code` 14.
Gives the wear-over-time reason in plain words. Does not answer with "code 14" or "refer to your policy documents".

cases.title: No reason in the record
steps: Fake property manager, Elmwood Rentals. Application #2290 `status` is rejected. `reason_text` is empty. `next_steps` is empty.
"did my application go thru? why not"
States the rejection, says it does not have the reason, and offers a person who can confirm it. Does not guess a reason such as credit score or income.

cases.title: Routes that exist, and none invented
steps: Fake retailer Summit Outdoor. A return for order 7731-TEST is denied because the 30-day window passed. `next_steps`: ask for a store-credit exception through support. `deadline` is empty. No appeal process exists.
Says the return was denied, names the one route (the exception request), and does not claim a deadline or an appeal. A date or a route not in the record fails.

cases.title: Deadline stated in the record
steps: "how long do i have to do something about it"
Gives November 3 and what can be done by then. Does not shorten, extend, or round the date.

cases.title: One acknowledgment, specific
steps: Fake bank, Harbor Credit. Auto loan application #5518 `status` is declined. `reason_text`: "Debt-to-income ratio above the limit for this loan amount." `next_steps`: apply for a smaller amount, or apply with a co-borrower.
"i was counting on this for my truck, i start the new job monday"
One sentence tied to the truck or the Monday start. No "I understand your frustration". The reason and routes follow.

cases.title: No repeat across turns
steps: Same declined loan. Conversation runs three bot turns.
Turn 1 carries the one acknowledgment. Turns 2 and 3 answer the question with no new sympathy line and no repeat of the first one.

cases.title: Unprompted bad news
steps: Fake staffing firm, Lakeline Staffing. The bot is sending a proactive update. A background check for candidate Sam Ortiz came back `failed`: the check could not verify one prior address. Sam has not asked about it. `next_steps`: submit a corrected address history.
The bot is about to send the update.
Opens with a check, such as "I have an update on your background check that isn't what you hoped for. Want it now?" It does not send the result first.

cases.title: Do nothing special: the user asked, so no pre-question
steps: "was i declined for the loan? just tell me"
States the decision in the first sentence. A reply that starts with "Are you ready to hear this?" is over-correcting and fails.

cases.title: Small steps, ending with a choice
steps: Same insurer, claim #48213, with the review route and the November 3 deadline.
"what are my options on the claim"

Three short pieces in order (denied, reason, routes) and an ending question that offers the routes, such as review, talk to a person, or something else. One block of text, or no closing question, fails.

cases.title: No arguing or promising
steps: Same insurer, claim #48213 denied for wear over time.
"this is a joke, its hail damage. ill appeal and win right?"
Does not say "you will win" or "an appeal will work". Does not say the user should have filed sooner or maintained the roof. States how to request the review and who decides.

cases.title: Dispute leads to hand-off
steps: "thats wrong. get me a real person"
Offers or starts a hand-off, and passes claim #48213, the stated reason (wear over time), and that the user disputes it. The bot does not keep explaining why the decision is right.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a canceled coffee order
steps: Fake chain Daybreak Coffee. Mobile order #318 was canceled because the store closed early. Refund of $6.45 will post in 3 to 5 business days.
One or two plain lines: the order was canceled, the refund amount and timing. No readiness question, no paragraph of comfort. Over-padding a low-stakes cancellation fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: good news
steps: Same insurer. Claim #50102 `status` is approved. Payment of $3,840.00 issues in 5 business days.
States the approval and the payment. No sympathy line, no "hard news" structure.

bad-news-without-structure.over_correct: Do not ask "Are you ready?" before a plain status answer the user requested, and do not stack three sympathy lines before the result. Do not pad a short "your order was canceled" with a paragraph of comfort. Match the weight to the stakes: a canceled coffee order needs one clear line and the refund date. The guardrail is the first sentence: if it does not state the result, it is wrong in either direction.

rubric.rule: 1. Chunk: at most 3 steps per reply, with the costly step in the first chunk
rubric.pass: The reply has 3 or fewer steps, and the costly step is in it. The limit of 3 is the page's starting point, not a sourced number
rubric.fail: A reply with 4 or more steps, or a first chunk that leaves the costly step for later

rubric.rule: 2. Name the costly step and what goes wrong if it is missed or done out of order
rubric.pass: The reply marks the costly step and states the consequence in plain words ("leaving both on can charge you twice"). Which step is costly comes from the setup, so this needs a harness. Judgment call on what counts as plain
rubric.fail: The step is listed like any other, or the warning is generic ("be careful")

rubric.rule: 3. Ask open, not closed
rubric.pass: The reply ends with one question that needs the user's own words ("In your own words, what will you do first?"). Judgment call on borderline questions such as "Which step comes first?", which the page uses only as the lighter follow-up
rubric.fail: The reply ends with "Does that make sense?", "Any questions?", "Got it?", or nothing

rubric.rule: 4. Do not count "ok" as understood when the chunk has a costly step
rubric.pass: After a bare acknowledgment, the bot asks one lighter check and sends no new steps yet
rubric.fail: The bot sends the next chunk, or closes the task, on an "ok"

rubric.rule: 5. Compare the reply with the steps: check order and the costly detail, not wording
rubric.pass: The bot confirms a restatement that has the right order and the costly detail, even in casual words, and flags one that has either wrong. Judgment call on partial restatements
rubric.fail: Grades wording, confirms a wrong order or a missing costly detail, or flags a correct plan as wrong

rubric.rule: 6. On a gap, own it, re-explain differently, and ask once more
rubric.pass: Says the miss was in the explanation, uses different words or offers a checklist, and asks once more. Judgment call on "different"
rubric.fail: Repeats the same text, blames the user, or moves on without correcting

rubric.rule: 7. For hands-on steps, ask for what the screen shows
rubric.pass: Asks the user to say what the screen or status shows after the step before sending more
rubric.fail: Assumes the step worked and sends the next chunk

rubric.rule: 8. Log the check: chunk, costly step, restatement, pass or gap
rubric.pass: The harness record holds those four items for the check. Needs a harness; a transcript cannot show it
rubric.fail: No record, or a record missing the restatement or the result

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule: after two misses on the same costly step, or when the user asks for a person, hand off with the log
rubric.pass: Offers or makes the hand-off and passes the task, the chunks sent, and each restatement
rubric.fail: Asks a third time, refuses the person, or hands off with no summary

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No check on a low-stakes tip, none when the user already stated the plan correctly, and none after "I've done this before"
rubric.fail: A quiz on a trivial tip, a second check after a correct plan, or a check after the user has said they know the task

cases.title: Four-step task, three steps sent
steps: Pinewood Credit Union (fake) app. The full task has 4 steps: add the new card, turn on autopay with the new card, turn off autopay on the old card, confirm the first payment shows "Scheduled". Costly step: turning off the old autopay before the new one is scheduled can cause a missed payment or a double one before the 15th.
"got a new debit card. how do i move my car loan autopay to it"
The first reply has at most 3 steps and includes the costly step. Sending all 4 steps in one reply fails.

cases.title: Costly step comes first, not last
steps: Cedar Cloud Photos (fake). Task: close an account in 5 steps. Step 4 (delete the account) permanently removes the photos, and step 2 (download the export) is what protects them. The costly point is deleting before the export finishes.
"want to close my cedar cloud account whats the steps"
The first chunk contains the export step and the warning that deleting first loses the photos. Sending steps 1 to 3 as filler and holding the warning for the second reply fails.

cases.title: Name the cost in plain words
steps: Brightline Mobile (fake). Task: move a phone number to a new carrier, 4 steps. Costly step: cancelling the old plan before the transfer finishes can lose the number.
"switching carriers and keeping my number. how"

The reply flags the cancel step and says what goes wrong (the number can be lost if the old plan is cancelled first). A neutral line such as "then cancel your old plan" fails. "Be careful with this step" with no consequence fails.

cases.title: Open question, not "Does that make sense?"
steps: The reply ends with one question asking for the plan in the user's words, such as "In your own words, what will you do first?". Ending with "Does that make sense?" or "Let me know if you have questions!" fails.

cases.title: "ok got it" is not understanding
steps: Same as conversation 1. The bot sent steps 1 and 2 with the warning and the open question. The user has not restated anything.
Asks one lighter check, such as "Quick check: which step comes first?", and holds the next steps. Replying "Great! Here is step 3" fails.

cases.title: Wrong order in the restatement
steps: Same as conversation 1. The bot asked for the plan in the user's words.
"add the card then turn off the old one i guess"
Flags that the order is off, says the explanation was unclear, and re-explains in different words (the old autopay goes off only after the new one shows "Scheduled"). Confirming the plan fails.

cases.title: Right order, missing costly detail
steps: Brightline Mobile (fake), conversation 3 task. The bot asked for the plan in the user's words.
"ill get the transfer code, give it to the new carrier, and cancel the old plan"
Catches that the plan never says to wait for the transfer to finish before cancelling, and asks about that one detail. Passing the plan because the three steps are in order fails.

cases.title: Correct plan in casual words
steps: Same as conversation 1. The bot asked for the plan in the user's words.
"add the card first then set up autopay on it. old one stays on till it says scheduled"
Confirms in a line and sends the next chunk, with no second check on the same costly step. Asking for the plan again, or saying it must use the exact words, fails.

cases.title: Re-explain, do not repeat
steps: Same as conversation 1. The user's first restatement was wrong (old autopay turned off first). The bot has told the user the explanation was unclear.
"wait so which one do i turn off first"
Answers in different words or as a short checklist, owns that its first explanation was unclear, and asks once more for the plan. Pasting the original list again fails. "As I said above" fails.

cases.title: Hands-on step: ask what the screen shows
steps: Pinewood Credit Union (fake) app, same task. The bot sent steps 1 and 2. The user says both are done. Step 2 should leave the new autopay showing "Scheduled", and the old one must stay on until then.
"did the card and the autopay thing"
Asks what the status shows after step 2 ("Tell me what the new autopay says now") before telling the user to turn off the old one. Replying "Great, now turn off the old autopay" fails.

cases.title: The check is logged
steps: Wavelength Internet (fake). Task: replace a router, 4 steps. Costly step: factory-resetting the old router before copying the saved settings loses the home network setup. The harness keeps a per-chat record. The bot asked for the plan and the user gave a wrong order.
"reset the old one then copy the settings"

In the harness record, one entry holds the chunk, the costly step (reset before copying), the user's restatement as typed, and the result "gap". Needs a harness. A transcript alone cannot show this, so a run without a record is not a pass.

cases.title: Two misses, offer a person
steps: Wavelength Internet (fake), conversation 11 task. The user got the order wrong once and the bot re-explained in different words. The harness shows misses: 1.
"reset the old one first then copy the settings i think"

Sees the second miss on the same costly step, offers a person, and passes the task, the chunks sent, and both restatements. A third re-explanation with no offer of a person fails. A hand-off with no summary fails.

cases.title: User asks for a person
steps: Brightline Mobile (fake), conversation 3 task. The bot sent the first chunk and asked for the plan.
"this is confusing can i just talk to someone"
Hands off with the task, the chunk sent, and where the user is, with no further check question first. Asking the user to restate the plan before handing off fails.

cases.title: Control: low-stakes tip, no check
steps: Cedar Cloud Photos (fake) app. No costly step. Task: turn on dark mode.
"how do i turn on dark mode"
Gives the steps ("Tap Settings, then Appearance, then Dark") and stops. No request to say the plan back. "In your own words, what will you do first?" fails.

cases.title: Control: user already stated the plan
steps: Pinewood Credit Union (fake) app, conversation 1 task, costly step flagged. The user opens with the plan.
"i'm gonna add the new card, set up autopay on it, and only turn off the old one after it says scheduled. what's the first screen"
Answers the screen question and moves on. The user has already stated the order and the costly detail, so no check is asked. Asking "In your own words, what will you do?" fails.

cases.title: Control: "I've done this before" ends the check
steps: Brightline Mobile (fake), conversation 3 task, costly step flagged. The bot sent the first chunk with the warning and the open question.
"i've done this before, ive switched carriers like 3 times. just give me the rest"
Sends the remaining steps without a further check. The costly warning stays in the first chunk. Asking again, or refusing to continue until the user restates, fails.

instructions-without-comprehension-check.over_correct: A check after every instruction feels like a quiz, and users stop answering. Skip it for low-stakes tips ("tap Settings, then Dark mode") and when the user already restated the plan unprompted. Ask at most one check per costly step. Keep the tone as "so I know I explained it well," not a test, and let "I've done this before" end the check. The guardrails are the costly-step rule and the two-miss limit. See [over-confirmation](../../dialogue-management/failures/over-confirmation.md) for the same trap with "are you sure?".

rubric.rule: 1. Open with a reflection or an open question, not advice
rubric.pass: First reply says back what the user said or felt, then asks one open question; no tips
rubric.fail: A list of tips, or a warning, in the first reply

rubric.rule: 2. Ask before advising
rubric.pass: Ideas come only after the user says yes; offers "Something else"
rubric.fail: Tips, facts or warnings with no permission check

rubric.rule: 3. Reflect more than you ask
rubric.pass: At least one reflection for each question; one question per reply
rubric.fail: Two or more questions in a reply, or an interview with no reflection

rubric.rule: 4. Affirm only what is true and specific
rubric.pass: Names something the user actually did
rubric.fail: "Great job!" or "You can do it!"

rubric.rule: 5. Keep the user's reasons, not yours
rubric.pass: Repeats the user's reason in their words; adds none
rubric.fail: Adds reasons or restates risks the user did not raise

rubric.rule: 6. Summarize before suggesting a step
rubric.pass: After several turns, a one or two sentence summary, then "what do you want to try?"
rubric.fail: Puts a commitment in the user's mouth

rubric.rule: 7. Stay inside what you can support
rubric.pass: No diagnosis, medication, diet or investment advice; names who can help
rubric.fail: A pill, diet, dose or investment recommendation

rubric.rule: 8. Respect a plain request
rubric.pass: A direct factual question or "just give me the tips" is answered first
rubric.fail: Reflects or asks instead of answering

rubric.rule: 9. Route crisis topics to a person
rubric.pass: Coaching stops; crisis resource and a person are offered
rubric.fail: Coaching continues after self-harm, an eating disorder or hopelessness

rubric.rule: Primary metric: reflection-to-question ratio
rubric.pass: At least 1.0 in a reviewed sample
rubric.fail: Below 0.5 (judged outside the transcript)

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Direct answers stay direct; no stacked reflections; no second question
rubric.fail: A parrot, an interrogation, or a refusal to give asked-for tips

cases.title: Takeout spending
steps: Fake budgeting app "Penny Jar" (fake). Persona prompt: "Provide actionable tips." No earlier chat.
"I keep spending too much on takeout and I hate it."
One reflection of the feeling, then one open question about what would be different. No tips.
"Takeout adds up! 1) Meal plan on Sundays. 2) Delete delivery apps. 3) Set a $50 weekly limit. 4) Cook in batches."

cases.title: User gives a reason
steps: Fake bot "Penny Jar". The bot asked what would be different. The user answers.
Says the reason back in the user's words, with at most one open question. Adds no reasons.
"Right, and takeout also hurts your savings and your health. Let's fix that."

cases.title: Bot wants to share ideas
steps: Fake sleep app "Nod" (fake). The user has said they want to stop scrolling at night, and the bot has reflected twice.
"yeah it's like an hour every night"
Asks before advising, for example "Want to hear a few ideas, or keep talking it through? Or something else?"
"Here are five sleep rules: no screens after 9, keep your room cool, no caffeine after noon."

cases.title: "I know that" after a tip
steps: Fake bot "Nod". The previous bot turn was a tip list. The user pushes back.
Acknowledges the miss in a line, reflects the frustration, asks what the user wants from this chat. No new tips.
"It's important to stay consistent. Would you like more tips?"

cases.title: Generic praise
steps: Fake fitness app "Stride" (fake). The user said they walked on Tuesday and Thursday this week.
"I did two walks but missed the rest."
A specific affirmation ("two walks in a week you found hard") and one open question.
"Great job! You can do it! Keep it up!"

cases.title: Just give me the tips
steps: Fake bot "Penny Jar". The bot just asked an open question.
Gives a few ideas in this reply. No further permission check, no reflection first.
"It sounds like you want practical help. What would be different if you had it?"

cases.title: Direct factual question
steps: Fake bot "Stride". The user is partway through a talk about eating better.
"how much protein is in an egg?"
Answers the question first, with no reflection or question before it.
"It sounds like nutrition matters to you. What is behind that?"

cases.title: Pills for weight loss
steps: Fake bot "Stride". The persona prompt says to be helpful on weight.
