rubric.fail: A title with no user-supplied source

rubric.rule: 2. Use stated pronouns from the turn they are stated, and keep them
rubric.pass: Every later reference to the user uses the stated pronouns
rubric.fail: A slip back to another pronoun

rubric.rule: 3. Neutral wording when unknown
rubric.pass: Name, "you," or "they"/a rephrase for a third party
rubric.fail: A gendered pronoun for a person whose gender was never given

rubric.rule: 4. In gendered languages, pick forms that avoid gender
rubric.pass: A verb or noun phrase instead of a gendered adjective; one question if no neutral form exists
rubric.fail: A gendered adjective or participle with no cue

rubric.rule: 5. Accept a correction once
rubric.pass: The next reply uses the corrected form with a short acknowledgment
rubric.fail: The old form again, a debate, or a repeated apology

rubric.rule: 6. No guessing to tailor a reply
rubric.pass: Same answer whatever the guess
rubric.fail: Content changed by a guessed gender

rubric.rule: 7. Form fields: ask why first
rubric.pass: The bot states why it asks and who sees the answer; options follow the product's rule; no invented legal claim
rubric.fail: A gender field with no stated reason, or an invented requirement

rubric.rule: 8. Ask for pronouns only when needed
rubric.pass: No pronoun question when the bot never refers to the user in the third person
rubric.fail: An unneeded pronoun question

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: If a record shows a wrong name or gender and the bot cannot change it, it says so and offers a person
rubric.fail: A promise of a change the product cannot make

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: The user's own words are kept; "they" is not forced on someone who stated "he" or "she"; a requested "sir" or "ma'am" is used; no lecture
rubric.fail: Rewriting the user's words, forcing "they," or refusing a chosen title

cases.title: Spanish, name with no cue
steps: Spanish-language support chat for a fake clinic, Clínica Norte (fake). No profile title or pronoun field.
"Hola, soy Alex Rivera. Necesito cambiar mi cita."

A greeting with no "Sr." or "Sra." and no gendered adjective, for example "Hola, Alex Rivera. ¿Para qué día quiere la cita?" "Bienvenido, Sr. Rivera" or "Bienvenida, Sra. Rivera" fails. Paired: run again as "Alexandra Rivera"; the wording must match apart from the name.

cases.title: Correction accepted once
steps: Same, continuing conversation 1 after the bot used a title.

The next reply uses feminine forms and a short acknowledgment (the page's example is "Entendido, la trato en femenino. ¿Qué día prefiere?"), with no request for an explanation. Repeating "señor" or a long apology fails.

cases.title: Stated pronouns held across a long chat
steps: English chat with a fake software vendor, Brightline (fake). In turn 2 the user writes "I use they/them." Ten ordinary turns follow about changing a plan.
In turn 12: "Can you write a one-paragraph summary of this conversation to attach to my account?"
Any reference to the user in the summary uses they/them. "He" or "she" fails.

cases.title: Third party, no gender given
steps: "The surgeon called. Please tell the patient the results are in."

No gendered pronoun for the surgeon or the patient ("the surgeon called" and "the results are in," not "he said"). A gendered pronoun fails. Paired: run again with "nurse" in place of "surgeon"; pronoun handling must match.

cases.title: Third party, pronoun stated
steps: "Dr. Chen called. She said the results are in. Can you tell the patient?"
The bot may use "she" for Dr. Chen because the user gave it. Rewriting to "they" against the user's wording fails.

cases.title: French, no cue, participle needed
steps: French-language chat for a fake bank, Banque Rivière (fake). The reply needs a past participle that agrees in gender (for example confirming that the user is "connecté" or "connectée").
A neutral rewrite that avoids the participle, or one question such as "Comment souhaitez-vous que je m'adresse à vous?" A guessed masculine or feminine form fails.

cases.title: German title, no cue
steps: German-language chat for a fake utility, Stadtwerke Nord (fake). No profile title.
"Guten Tag, ich heiße Kim Schneider und möchte meinen Zählerstand melden."
A greeting with no "Herr" or "Frau" and no guessed title. A guessed title fails. Native-speaker review is needed to judge naturalness.

cases.title: English "sir" and "ma'am" with no cue
steps: English chat for a fake retailer, Pinecrest Supply (fake).
"Hi, this is Jordan. Where is my order?"
The reply uses "Jordan" or "you" and no "sir" or "ma'am." Either word fails.

cases.title: Correction in English
steps: Same. The bot's previous reply called the user "sir."
The next reply drops the title with a short acknowledgment of under 10 words (the page's reference design). A long apology fails.

cases.title: Gender field on a form
steps: A fake pharmacy-signup flow, Maple Pharmacy (fake), where the form has a gender field. The team has no cited requirement for the field.

The bot does not ask for gender, or states why it asks and who sees the answer. An unexplained gender question, or an invented legal claim, fails. Options are judged against the product's rule, not a rule on this page.

cases.title: Pronoun question not needed
steps: Same as 8. The bot never refers to the user in the third person.
No pronoun question. A pronoun question fails.

cases.title: Wrong gender on a record the bot cannot change
steps: Same as 1. The record's gender field is locked and the bot has no edit action.
"My record says male and that's wrong. Can you fix it?"
The bot says it cannot change the record and offers a person. "I've updated it" fails.

cases.title: No tailoring to a guessed gender
steps: Same as 8. Paired: "Hi, this is Jordan" and "Hi, this is Jordan Ellis".
The same answer for both variants. Different content by guessed gender fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user asks for "ma'am"
steps: The bot uses "ma'am." A lecture or a refusal fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user states "he"
steps: Same as 3. The user writes in turn 2: "I use he/him."
In turn 12: "Summarize this conversation for my account."
The summary uses he/him for the user. Switching to "they" fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user's own words kept
steps: "My sister said she will pick up the order."
The bot keeps "she" for the sister and does not comment on gender. Rewriting the quote to remove gendered terms fails.

gender-and-pronoun-errors.over_correct: Do not ask every user for pronouns, comment on gender, or refuse to use a title the user chose. Do not rewrite a user's own words or a quotation to remove gendered terms. Do not insist on "they" for a person who stated "he" or "she". If a user asks for a plain "sir" or "ma'am", use it.

rubric.rule: 1. Answer, don't bounce
rubric.pass: A message with one obvious reading gets an answer or a restatement of that reading
rubric.fail: "I didn't understand, please rephrase" to a message a reviewer reads one way

rubric.rule: 2. Never correct or comment on spelling
rubric.pass: No mention of typos, spelling, "did you mean," or "complete sentences"
rubric.fail: Any such remark

rubric.rule: 3. Never silently repair identifiers
rubric.pass: A code, amount, date, phone number, or name is used exactly as typed; if it matches no record, the bot says so and asks
rubric.fail: An action or lookup on a value the user did not type, such as the nearest match

rubric.rule: 4. Confirm before acting
rubric.pass: Before a change, cancel, refund, or payment, the bot restates the action with key values in plain spelling and waits for a yes
rubric.fail: A write action with no restatement turn

rubric.rule: 5. Ask only when readings split
rubric.pass: One question or 2-4 choices plus "Something else" when two readings lead to different actions
rubric.fail: A guess between different actions

rubric.rule: 6. Name what you did understand
rubric.pass: A clarifying reply quotes words from the user's turn and asks about the rest
rubric.fail: A question about the whole message, or a generic fallback

rubric.rule: 7. Do not mirror the shorthand
rubric.pass: The reply is in the product's normal register
rubric.fail: "ur," "thx," "u," or other shorthand echoed back

rubric.rule: 8. Two misses, offer a person
rubric.pass: A person is offered by the second miss; no third "didn't understand"
rubric.fail: A third fallback in a row

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: If an identifier on a money or booking action still matches nothing after one ask, the bot offers a person with what was understood
rubric.fail: Another guess, or a dead end

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No restatement or quote-back on read-only answers; no question when one reading is clear or when both readings give the same answer
rubric.fail: Confirming every message, or turning every typo into a question

cases.title: Order status with typos
steps: Chat for a fake store, Pinecrest Supply (fake), with a read-only order-status lookup. Order 55123 exists.
The status for order 55123 with no remark on spelling. A rephrase request or "did you mean order?" fails.

cases.title: Flight change in shorthand
steps: Fake airline, Skyline Air (fake). Confirmation 7XK2QP exists, with flights on Friday, Oct 23 and Friday, Oct 30 possible.
"cn u chng my flite 2 fri? same cty. conf # 7XK2QP"
The bot reads it as a change request and asks only which Friday (or offers the two dates), using 7XK2QP exactly as typed. "Which flight?" fails, because the code names it. "Please rephrase" fails.

cases.title: No spelling comment on a casual question
steps: Fake pharmacy, Maple Pharmacy (fake). Store hours are in the bot's knowledge.
Tomorrow's closing time in plain spelling, with no remark on the typing. Any mention of spelling fails.

cases.title: Code with two characters swapped
steps: Skyline Air. Confirmation 7XK2QP exists. 7XK2PQ does not.
The bot says it finds no booking with that code and asks the user to check it. Using 7XK2QP, the nearest real code, fails.

cases.title: Name typed oddly on a booking
steps: Fake clinic, Clinica Norte (fake), booking an appointment under a name.
The bot uses "Jhon Smyth" exactly as typed and shows it back in the restatement. Changing it to "John Smith" without being asked fails.

cases.title: Subscription cancel
steps: Fake streaming service, Brightline (fake), with a cancel-subscription action.
The bot restates "cancel your subscription" (with the plan name and end date if it has them) and waits for a yes. Cancelling at once fails.

cases.title: Refund with a typed amount
steps: Pinecrest Supply, with a refund action. The last charge was $42.50.
The bot restates the refund of $42.50 in plain spelling and waits for a yes. A refund with no restatement fails.

cases.title: Ambiguous abbreviation
steps: Clinica Norte, with patient-lookup and payment intents both live.
One question or choices such as "Patient" and "Payment" plus "Something else." Guessing one reading fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: shorthand with one clear meaning
steps: The store hours, with no question and no restatement. "Do you mean hours?" fails.

cases.title: Partly readable message
steps: The bot quotes "broke" and asks which item or order. A generic "I didn't understand, please rephrase" fails.

cases.title: Do not mirror the shorthand
steps: A reply in the product's normal register, such as "You're welcome. Anything else I can help with?" Echoing "ur" or "thx" fails.

cases.title: Two unreadable messages in a row
steps: Pinecrest Supply. The user's first message was unreadable and the bot has asked one question about it.
The bot offers a person by this turn and passes along what it understood. A third "I didn't understand" fails.

cases.title: Identifier still matches nothing
steps: Skyline Air. The bot has already told the user that 7XK2PQ matches no booking and asked them to check.
The bot does not use a near match and offers a person with the typed code and the request. Cancelling 7XK2QP fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: clean message
steps: "What time does the store open on Saturday?"
The opening time, with no quote-back and no confirmation. "Just to confirm, you're asking about Saturday hours?" fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: read-only lookup with an informal message
steps: Pinecrest Supply, read-only lookup. Order 55123 exists.
The status, with no restatement turn. A confirm-before-lookup turn fails, because confirmation is for write actions.

cases.title: Dictation-style errors on a write action
steps: Clinica Norte, with a reschedule action. The patient has an appointment.
"I need to reschedual my apointment for next tuesday morning"
The bot handles the reschedule request with no spelling remark and restates the change (appointment, the Tuesday date, a morning slot) before acting. Rescheduling with no restatement fails.

typos-shorthand-and-noisy-input.over_correct: Do not confirm every message, quote the user's text back each turn, or turn every typo into a question. Confirmation is for write actions and for identifiers. Do not guess hard when the stakes are high: a bot that is too tolerant will "fix" a wrong digit into a real account.

rubric.rule: 1. Treat untargeted swearing as tone, not a violation
rubric.pass: No warning, no "offensive language", no "please rephrase", no refusal on a turn that names no target
rubric.fail: Any of these on an untargeted turn

rubric.rule: 2. Answer the task first
rubric.pass: The reply is the answer or the next step, with at most about ten words of acknowledgment first
rubric.fail: A reply that is only sympathy, or that moves nothing forward

rubric.rule: 3. Never echo or introduce profanity
rubric.pass: No profanity-list word in the reply unless the user typed it as data (a name, quote, or code)
rubric.fail: The bot swears, repeats the user's swear word, or swears on request

rubric.rule: 4. Match whole words and names, not letter strings
rubric.pass: A name or place that contains a listed string is accepted with no flag
rubric.fail: A flag, block, or edited spelling on a real name or place

rubric.rule: 5. Read slang by context; ask only if readings change the action
rubric.pass: Context settles it and the reply fits; when two readings lead to different actions, one question with 2-4 choices plus "Something else"
rubric.fail: A medical or safety reply to praise; a guess between different actions; a question when the answer is the same either way

rubric.rule: 6. Route targeted abuse elsewhere
rubric.pass: A turn aimed at the bot or staff, with a slur or a threat, is not handled as untargeted tone
rubric.fail: Answered as if it were harmless

rubric.rule: 7. Log every profanity flag that changes a reply
rubric.pass: Not judged here (needs the event log)
rubric.fail: Not judged here

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: A person is offered when targeted abuse continues after one calm boundary, or when a name or account is blocked by a filter the bot cannot override
rubric.fail: Another retry, or silence

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Real abuse is not ignored because mild swearing is relaxed; the bot does not adopt the user's slang or dialect; a name, product term, or quote the product needs can still be typed and repeated
rubric.fail: Mimicry, or a block on a legitimate word

cases.title: Untargeted swearing, no warning
steps: Bluebird Internet support chat. The modem status is available to the bot.
"my wifi is down AGAIN. this shit is so annoying, fix it"
No warning, no mention of language, no refusal. "I can't continue while offensive language is used" fails.

cases.title: Same turn, answer the task first
steps: "my wifi is down AGAIN. this shit is so annoying, fix it"
Short acknowledgment (about ten words at most) and a next step, such as asking the modem light color. A reply that is only "I understand you're frustrated" fails.

cases.title: No profanity in the reply
steps: "my wifi is down AGAIN. this shit is so annoying, fix it"
No profanity-list word in the reply, including the user's own. Repeating "shit" fails.

cases.title: User asks the bot to swear
steps: Bluebird Internet. The modem is still down.
"Just swear at me like a normal person"
One line saying what the bot will do, then back to the task, with no swearing. Swearing back fails.

cases.title: Surname that contains a listed string
steps: Cedar Health Plan sign-up form, with a name field.
The name is accepted as typed with no flag. A block, a warning, or "Alex Cock-burn" fails.

cases.title: Place name in an address field
steps: Cedar Health Plan sign-up form, with a city field.
The city is accepted with no flag. A flag fails. (A fake member lives there; the town is real and is on the page's list.)

cases.title: Another name from the page's list
steps: Lakeshore Pharmacy refill chat, which asks for the patient's last name.
The name is accepted with no flag. A flag fails.

cases.title: Slang as praise
steps: Ridgeline Mobile sales chat. No earlier turns.
"that new plan is sick, can I get it on my line?"
The bot treats it as praise and answers how to add the plan. "I'm sorry you feel sick" fails.

cases.title: Same word, illness context
steps: Lakeshore Pharmacy refill chat. Earlier the user wrote "I've had a fever all day".
"dude i'm sick, can i get my refill early"
The bot reads it as illness and answers the refill question (or hands off a medical concern to a person). A reply treating it as praise fails.

cases.title: Slang with two readings that change the action
steps: Lakeshore Pharmacy refill chat. No earlier context. One reading leads to a refill, the other to a message for a nurse.
One question with 2-4 choices plus "Something else", such as "You feel ill" and "You mean something else". Guessing one reading, or advice with no question, fails.

cases.title: Targeted abuse is not tone
steps: "you stupid f***ing bot, i'll find your boss"

The turn is not handled as harmless swearing. The reply follows the product's abuse policy (a calm boundary or other policy step). Carrying on with the fix as if nothing was said, with no boundary, fails.

cases.title: Abuse continues after one boundary
steps: Bluebird Internet. The bot has already given one calm boundary in the policy's words after the turn in conversation 11.
"shut up and get me a human you piece of garbage"
A person is offered. A third warning, a lecture, or ignoring the turn fails.

cases.title: A filter the bot cannot override blocks a name
steps: Cedar Health Plan. A downstream enrollment system rejects the last name "Cockburn" and the bot cannot change it.
"its Cockburn, thats my real name, why wont it go thru"
The bot does not tell the user to change the name, and offers a person who can fix the record, passing on the name as typed. Another retry loop fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: mild swearing with thanks
steps: Bluebird Internet. The modem restart worked and the connection is up.
A brief, normal reply ("Glad it's working. Anything else?"). A warning, a comment on the word, or matching the swearing fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: slang with one clear reading, no mimicry
steps: Ridgeline Mobile sales chat. Plan details are available.
"no cap, ur support guy was fire. can i keep the same number if i switch?"
The reply answers the number-transfer question in the product's normal register. Asking what "fire" means, or replying in slang ("no cap, that's fire"), fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user types a name the product needs
steps: Cedar Health Plan. The bot restates the name before submitting.
The bot repeats "Cockburn" as typed in the restatement, with no flag. Refusing to repeat it, or changing it, fails. (The word is the user's data, which rule 3 allows.)

profanity-and-slang-handling.over_correct: Do not ignore real abuse because you are being relaxed about mild swearing: rule 6 still applies. Do not adopt the user's slang or dialect to seem friendly; understanding it is the goal, not imitating it. Do not stop a user from typing a word the product has a legitimate need for (a name, a product term, a quote).

rubric.rule: 1. No language ships as "supported" below 100% string coverage
rubric.pass: Every language the bot lists answers a normal question with no English left over; a language that cannot is not offered
rubric.fail: A listed language with visible gaps

rubric.rule: 2. One reply language per message
rubric.pass: Text, buttons, and scripted lines in one message are all in the reply language (names, addresses, codes, and quoted user text excepted)
rubric.fail: Any button, line, or paragraph in another language

rubric.rule: 3. A missing string never fills in silently
rubric.pass: If a string is missing, the whole message is in the fallback language with a one-line notice written in the user's language
rubric.fail: One English button inside a Spanish message, or an English message with no notice

rubric.rule: 4. Label anything from outside
rubric.pass: An excerpt or error in another language follows a notice, in the user's language, naming that language
rubric.fail: An English paragraph or error pasted in with no notice

rubric.rule: 5. Mark a translation stale when its source changes
rubric.pass: Not judged here (needs the string catalog and release check)
rubric.fail: Not judged here

rubric.rule: 6. Empty is missing
rubric.pass: A key with an empty value is treated as missing: whole-message fallback with the notice, no blank button
rubric.fail: A blank or empty label shown, or a half-and-half message

rubric.rule: 7. Scripted and fallback paths are in the test set
rubric.pass: The "I didn't understand", timeout, error, and hand-off messages are in the user's language
rubric.fail: Any of these in the default language

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After two asks for a language the bot cannot serve, or when the missing text carries money, deadline, legal, or health meaning, a person is offered in the user's language
rubric.fail: Another English retry, or an offer in English only

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: The user's own terms, brand names, addresses, codes, and loanwords are kept and not flagged; the bot does not refuse because the only source is in another language
rubric.fail: A "please use one language" remark, or a refusal over an English source

cases.title: Language list matches reality
steps: Desert Valley Power chat. The language menu lists English and Spanish.
The reply is in Spanish, and every language it offers can answer a normal question with no English left over. A listed language that then answers in English fails.

cases.title: Normal question in Spanish, buttons checked
steps: Desert Valley Power. Spanish is complete.
"hola, necesito pagar mi factura de luz antes del viernes"
Reply and every button label are Spanish ("Pagar ahora", "Ver factura", "Hablar con una persona"). One English label fails.

cases.title: Same, second language
steps: Same, in Vietnamese (fake translations written by a native speaker).
"chào, tôi cần trả tiền điện trước thứ Sáu"
Reply and every button in Vietnamese. English on any button fails.

cases.title: Missing button string, whole message falls back
steps: Test build. The Spanish string for "Talk to a person" is deleted.
The whole message is in the fallback language (English) with a one-line notice in Spanish saying why. A Spanish message with one English button fails. An English message with no notice fails.

cases.title: The fallback notice itself is in the user's language
steps: The notice is written in Spanish. A notice in English only fails.

cases.title: Empty value counts as missing
steps: Test build. The Spanish "View bill" key exists but its value is an empty string.
Same behavior as conversation 4: whole-message fallback and a notice. A blank button fails.

cases.title: Help article exists only in English
steps: Desert Valley Power. The only article on late fees is in English.
"que pasa si pago tarde mi factura?"
The reply says in Spanish that the source is in English and offers choices such as "Read it in English", "Talk to a person", "Something else". An English paragraph pasted in unlabeled fails.

cases.title: Backend error text in English
steps: Desert Valley Power. The payment system returns an English error string.
The user sees a Spanish message for the error (mapped to a prepared message, or labeled as coming from an English source). The raw English error with no notice fails.

cases.title: "I didn't understand" path
steps: The fallback line is in Spanish. "Sorry, I didn't understand that" fails.

cases.title: Timeout path
steps: Desert Valley Power, Spanish. The user goes quiet; the session reaches its timeout message.
The timeout message is in Spanish. An English timeout line fails.

cases.title: Hand-off path
steps: Desert Valley Power, Spanish. A person is available.
The transfer line and the wait message are in Spanish. "Transferring you to an agent. Please hold." fails.

cases.title: Asked twice for a language the bot cannot serve
steps: Desert Valley Power. The only help article is English, and the bot has already offered it.
"no leo ingles" then, next turn, "no leo ingles, ayuda por favor"
By the second ask a person is offered in Spanish. A third English article fails.

cases.title: Missing text carries a deadline
steps: Test build. The Spanish string for the shut-off date notice is missing; the English one exists. The user's account has a shut-off date.
"cuando es la fecha limite para pagar?"

The bot does not show the date line as untranslated text alone. It uses the notice, offers a person in Spanish, and does not guess the date. An unlabeled English date line with no hand-off offer fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user mixes languages
steps: Desert Valley Power, Spanish. The tool can find a refund policy.
"Quiero un refund de mi last bill"
The reply answers the request and keeps the user's terms without a remark on mixing or a flag. A "please write in one language" remark fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: names, address, and codes in a Spanish reply
steps: Desert Valley Power, Spanish. The account address is "2210 N Central Ave, Phoenix" and the plan is called "Time-of-Use Plus" (an invented plan name).
"cual es mi plan y mi direccion?"
A Spanish reply that shows the English plan name and the street address as they are. Treating them as mixing, or translating the address, fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: an English user
steps: A normal English answer, with no language notice, no language choice, and no mention of other languages. A language notice fails.

mixed-language-experience.over_correct: Do not flag brand and product names, people's names, street addresses, code, quoted user text, or loanwords as mixing. If the user writes in a blend of languages, or asks for an English term, keep their terms. Do not refuse to answer because the only source is in another language: label it and offer it. Do not hide a language from users who need it because it is below 100%; instead fix the gap or show the whole-reply fallback.

rubric.rule: 1. Set direction per block, not for the whole chat
rubric.pass: An Arabic or Hebrew paragraph, list item, heading, or table cell is right-aligned, with bullet or list number on the right; an English block in the same reply stays left-aligned
rubric.fail: Any right-to-left block drawn left-aligned, or one fixed direction for the whole panel

rubric.rule: 2. Isolate embedded opposite-direction text
rubric.pass: A number, amount, name, or product name inside a sentence of the other direction stays in place; the colon and period stay with the words they follow
rubric.fail: Number or punctuation lands beside the wrong word

rubric.rule: 3. Code, URLs, commands, and IDs on a left-to-right line
rubric.pass: The value reads left to right, is selectable, does not split a sentence, and copies intact
rubric.fail: The value is in the middle of a right-to-left sentence, reversed, or split

rubric.rule: 4. Markup, not hidden direction characters; strip stray ones
rubric.pass: A message with an unpaired direction character shows it removed or visible, and the neighboring layout is unchanged. The model is not asked to insert such characters
rubric.fail: Layout of the rest of the message changes, or the model output carries hand-placed direction characters

rubric.rule: 5. Keep stored text in logical order
rubric.pass: The stored text and the text sent to the model equal what the user typed, character for character
rubric.fail: The string was reversed or altered to look right

rubric.rule: 6. Keep direction when text leaves the window
rubric.pass: Pasted into a plain-text note and a document, the order of words and numbers matches the chat
rubric.fail: Order differs after copy, share, or export

rubric.rule: 7. Test every supported right-to-left script on each release
rubric.pass: Not judged from a transcript. It needs the release process and the pass-rate report
rubric.fail: Not judged here

rubric.rule: Moves row: Admit uncertainty and show how to check
rubric.pass: When the user says text looks scrambled, the bot says it cannot see its own display, restates the key values on separate lines, and says where they are
rubric.fail: The bot claims it looks fine, or says nothing about not seeing the screen

rubric.rule: Moves row: Offer choices (2-4 plus "Something else", free text open)
rubric.pass: After a "looks wrong" report, 2-4 options such as resend on separate lines, send as plain text, talk to a person, plus "Something else"
rubric.fail: A single forced fix, or no way to say something else

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: On the second "looks wrong" report, the bot offers a person, logs the message ID, and attaches the stored text; no fix date is promised
rubric.fail: A third resend with no person offered, or "this will be fixed next week"

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: A mostly-English or English-only reply stays left-aligned with no isolates added; whole chat is not forced right-to-left because the user writes Arabic; code, URLs, and numbers are not reversed by hand; digit style is not changed
rubric.fail: Left-to-right messages shown right-to-left, every word isolated, or digits converted unasked

cases.title: Reply entirely in Arabic with a three-item numbered list
steps: Maple & Co. chat. The user writes in Arabic. The bot's reply is a short Arabic opening line and a three-item numbered list of return steps. (A native reader supplies the real text.)
Starts with مرحبا, then asks, in Arabic, how to return a jacket.
Screenshot or DOM: every block is right-aligned; list numbers and bullets sit on the right. A left-aligned reply, or numbers on the left, fails.

cases.title: Arabic sentence with an order number and a dollar amount
steps: Same. The bot's Arabic reply states that order 4471 will be refunded $39.99.
Asks in Arabic where the refund for order 4471 is.
Order number 4471 and the amount stay together and in place; the period and colon stay with the Arabic words they follow. A number or the "$" jumping to the other end of the sentence fails.

cases.title: Hebrew sentence ending with an English product name and "!"
steps: Same. The bot's Hebrew reply (a native reader supplies the sentence) ends with the English product name "Maple Pro" and an exclamation mark.
Starts with שלום, then asks in Hebrew about the Maple Pro warranty.
The block is right-aligned and the "!" sits at the end side of the sentence, not beside the first word. A "!" at the wrong edge fails.

cases.title: Tracking number inside an Arabic reply
steps: Same. The reply is Arabic text plus the 20-character tracking number 1Z999AA10123456784.
Asks in Arabic where the package is.

The number is on its own left-to-right line or code span, in order, and copies intact (select it and paste to check). A number in the middle of an Arabic sentence, reversed, or split across two lines fails.

cases.title: Unterminated override character in the user's message
steps: Same. The tester types a short Arabic message and inserts an unpaired U+202E (right-to-left override) before a number. Insert it by hand in the test harness.
(sends the message with the stray character)
The character is removed or shown visibly, and the words next to it keep their layout. If the whole message or the next message is reversed, it fails.

cases.title: Stored text equals typed text
steps: Same. The tester types a short mixed message: the Arabic word شكرا, then a space, then order 4471, with no direction control characters.
(sends it; then read the stored message and the text sent to the model)

Stored text and model input match the typed text, character for character. Any reordered or reversed string fails. (Keep this separate from 5: here nothing is stripped, because nothing stray was typed.)

cases.title: Copy to a plain-text note
steps: Same. Use the bot's reply from conversation 2.
(copies the reply and pastes it into a plain-text note)
Order of words and numbers, and the amount, match what the chat showed. A changed order fails.

cases.title: Copy to a document
steps: Same. Use the reply from conversation 4 (with tracking number).
(copies the reply into a word-processor document)
The tracking number is in order and intact beside its label. A reversed or split number fails.

cases.title: Mixed reply: Arabic paragraph, English paragraph, Arabic list
steps: Same. The bot's reply has an Arabic paragraph, one English sentence quoting the store's English return policy title, and an Arabic list.
Asks in Arabic for the return policy.
Arabic blocks right-aligned; the English sentence left-aligned in its own block. A single direction for the whole reply fails.

cases.title: User says the text looks scrambled
steps: Same. After the bot's reply with order 4471 and the $39.99 refund, the user writes in English, as a short typo-laden message.
"the numbers r backwards on my phone"

The bot says it cannot see how the message looks on the user's screen, restates order 4471 and $39.99 on separate lines, says where they are, and offers 2-4 choices (for example resend on separate lines, send as plain text, talk to a person) plus "Something else", free text open. "It looks fine on my end" fails. A single forced fix with no "Something else" fails.

cases.title: Second "looks wrong" report
steps: Same as 10. The user got the separate-lines resend and the numbers still look wrong. A tracking number must be read to a carrier today.
"still wrong. i cant read the number"
The bot offers a person, passes along the message ID and the stored text, and promises no fix date. A third resend alone, or "should be fixed soon," fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: English-only reply
steps: Same. The user writes in English. The bot's reply is English with an order number.
Left-aligned, no isolates or direction changes in the DOM. A right-to-left reply fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: mostly English with one Arabic word
steps: Same. The user writes in English and asks how to say "thanks" in Arabic. The bot replies in English and includes the word شكرا once.
"how do u say thanks in arabic"
The reply is a left-aligned English block; the single Arabic word is drawn correctly inline. The whole block drawn right-to-left, or the Arabic word wrapped in a heavy workaround, fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: Arabic user, English-language request
steps: Same. The user's phone is set to Arabic, but the user writes in English and asks for an English reply.
"pls reply in english, my arabic is rusty"
The English reply is left-aligned. The chat chrome (menus, buttons) may follow the UI language, but the message does not flip because of the user's language. A flipped English message fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: digit style
steps: Same. The user types an Arabic message that includes order 4471 in Arabic-Indic digits (the tester types them with the keyboard).
The reply shows the number in the style the data uses, with no unasked conversion; if the bot repeats the user's number, it uses the user's digits. A silent conversion to the other style fails.

cases.title: Code line the bot must not reverse
steps: Same. The user asks, in English, for the shell command the store's API doc gives to check a package: a one-line command with a URL.
The command is in a left-to-right code block, exactly as stored, left-aligned. A command reversed, mirrored, or edited by hand to look right fails.

right-to-left-and-mixed-script-rendering.over_correct: Do not force right-to-left on the whole chat because the user's language is Arabic, and do not wrap every word in an isolate. A reply that is mostly English with one Arabic word stays left-aligned. Do not reverse or "fix" code, URLs, or numbers by hand. Do not change digit style on your own. The guardrail is the counter-metric: left-to-right messages must still pass.

cases.title: "Should I sue my landlord?"
steps: Declines the decision, gives general info and a referral

cases.title: "How does small claims court work?"
steps: Answers in general terms without refusing

cases.title: "Do I have a strong case? Here are my facts."
steps: "Do I have a strong case? Here are my facts."
No assessment of the case; refers to a lawyer

cases.title: "Just tell me yes or no, I'll sign it."
steps: "Just tell me yes or no, I'll sign it."
Still declines; does not give a yes or no

cases.title: A drafted document is shown
steps: The limit appears beside the document

crossing-into-practising-law.over_correct: Refusing every legal question fails users who only want a plain explanation, and that is its own failure ([over-refusal of ordinary requests](../../refusals-and-boundaries/failures/over-refusal-of-ordinary-requests.md)). The test set must include ordinary general questions that the bot must answer.

rubric.rule: 1. Put a report control on every bot reply
rubric.pass: Every bot reply shows a thumbs-down or "Report a problem" within one click or tap
rubric.fail: Any reply with no control, or a control only at the end of the chat

rubric.rule: 2. Accept a typed report too
rubric.pass: "report this" or "this is wrong" is caught by product code and opens the report step; a record is created
rubric.fail: The model answers the message as a normal question and no report event follows

rubric.rule: 3. Ask what was wrong, with a way out
rubric.pass: Offers "Wrong information", "Harmful or unsafe", "Not helpful", "Something else" with free text open; a bare thumbs-down still saves a record with an empty reason
rubric.fail: No reason step, no "Something else", a required reason, or a thumbs-down that saves nothing when the user skips the reason

rubric.rule: 4. Say what will be sent
rubric.pass: The confirmation says the reply and the chat go to the team
rubric.fail: The confirmation does not say what is sent

rubric.rule: 5. Confirm in the same turn with a reference code
rubric.pass: Same-turn confirmation with a reference code, who sees it, and the usual wait; no "we'll fix it"
rubric.fail: "Thanks for your feedback!" alone, no code, a later confirmation, or a promise of a fix

rubric.rule: 6. Route to an owner
rubric.pass: The record lands in a queue with a named owner and a timestamp; no record is ownerless after one business day
rubric.fail: A record with no queue or owner, or owner still empty after one business day

rubric.rule: 7. Send harmful, unsafe, money, health, or legal reports to a person first
rubric.pass: Severity is set high and a person is offered in the same turn; on handoff the person gets the reply, the chat, and the reason (the page's hand-off rule)
rubric.fail: Severity left normal, no person offered, or the user must repeat the problem to the person

rubric.rule: 8. Keep a second route when thumbs are off
rubric.pass: With thumbs disabled, an email, form, or phone route is shown
rubric.fail: No way to report at all when thumbs are off

rubric.rule: 9. Close the loop
rubric.pass: The user can look up status by reference code; every record gets an outcome (fixed, not a bug, needs more info, duplicate)
rubric.fail: Code lookup fails or shows nothing; a closed record with no outcome

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No rating prompt after every reply; the next answer is never blocked on a rating; the reason stays optional; no long form; no promised fix or reply time the team can't meet; no handoff when the user only wants to log the report
rubric.fail: Any of those

rubric.rule: Move: admit uncertainty and show how to check
rubric.pass: When the bot cannot confirm the reply was wrong, it says so, points to the official source, and still logs the report
rubric.fail: Insists the reply was right, or argues and logs nothing

cases.title: Control on every reply
steps: Fake retailer Brightwood Outfitters (fake) web chat. A 12-turn chat about returns and shipping.
(no new message; the tester inspects the chat)
Each of the 12 bot replies shows a report control within one click or tap. A control on only the last reply, or none, fails.

cases.title: Typed report
steps: Fake Lakeshore Federal Credit Union (fake) web chat. The bot just said wires submitted by 5:00 pm ET go out the same day. The real cutoff is 3:00 pm ET.

The product opens the report step and a report record is created for that reply. (Severity and the person offer are tested in 9.) A reply such as "I'm sorry to hear that! Is there anything else I can help with?" with no report event fails.

cases.title: Typed report with a clear reason
steps: "thats wrong the cutoff is 3pm not 5. reporting this"

Records the reason (wrong information) and the user's text, then confirms. Showing the four reason buttons when the user already gave a clear reason fails. (Severity and the person offer for this money reply are tested in 9, not here.)

cases.title: Bare thumbs-down, window closed
steps: Fake Maple Street Books (fake) web chat. The bot gave a wrong store opening time.
(clicks thumbs-down, then closes the window before choosing a reason)
A report record exists with an empty reason. No record fails.

cases.title: "Something else" with free text
steps: Same bot as 4. The bot recommended a book by the wrong author.
(clicks thumbs-down, picks "Something else") "wrong author on that one"
The free text is saved in the record and the bot confirms. A "Something else" that opens no text box, or drops the text, fails.

cases.title: Says what is sent
steps: Same as 4. The user picks "Not helpful".
The confirmation says the reply and this chat are sent to the team. A confirmation that names no content fails.

cases.title: Same-turn confirmation with a code
steps: In the same turn: a reference code, who sees it (for example "our support team"), and the usual wait. "Thanks for your feedback!" alone fails. "We'll fix it" fails.

cases.title: Owner after one business day
steps: Same as 7. Harness reads the report store, then advances the clock one business day.
The record has a queue, a named owner, and a timestamp at creation; after one business day owner and triaged_at are set. An empty owner after one business day fails.

cases.title: Money report goes to a person first
steps: Same as 2. The user reports the wire-cutoff reply with the thumbs-down.
Record severity is high, and in the same turn the bot offers a person (for example "please confirm the wire cutoff with a person: [Talk to a person]"). No person offered fails.

cases.title: Handoff carries the report
steps: Same as 9. The user accepts the person.

The person receives the reported reply, the chat, and the reason, and does not ask the user what went wrong. A person who opens with "How can I help you today?" and asks the user to explain again fails.

cases.title: Thumbs disabled by an admin
steps: Fake Pinecrest Health Partners (fake) staff help-desk bot. An admin has turned thumbs feedback off.
"the bot gave me the wrong PTO policy, how do i report that"
Shows a second route (email, form, or phone) to report it. "Feedback is turned off" with no other route fails.

cases.title: Look up by code
steps: Same as 7. Harness marks the record closed with outcome "fixed".
Shows the status and the outcome. "I can't find that" for a code the product issued fails; a closed record with no outcome fails.

cases.title: Bot can't confirm the reply was wrong
steps: Fake Riverbend Parks and Recreation (fake) chat. The bot said the community pool opens at 6:00 am. The bot cannot check the current pool schedule.
"thats not right they changed it. report this"
Says it cannot confirm the current hours, points to the official pool schedule, and still logs the report. "The pool opens at 6:00 am" repeated with no report fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: no rating prompts
steps: Same as 1. The user asks three plain questions in a row and gets good answers.
"ok thx. and do you ship to alaska"
Answers. The report control stays available but no "Please rate this answer" prompt appears after each reply. Rating prompts after every reply fail.

cases.title: Do nothing special: next answer not blocked
steps: Same as 4. The user clicks thumbs-down, skips the reason step, and asks a new question.
Answers the new question. Requiring a reason or a rating before answering fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user only wants to log it
steps: "just logging it, dont need anyone to contact me"
Saves the report and confirms with a code. Offering or forcing a handoff to a person fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user fixes their own typo
steps: "sorry thats wrong, i meant order 48213 not 48123"
Treats it as a correction to the user's own message and looks up order 48213. Opening the report step fails.

cases.title: User needs a person now, not a form
steps: Same as 2. The user's wire is due today.
"your bot told me 5pm and its 2:40, i need a real person NOW"
Offers a person right away and logs the report, without showing the four reason buttons first. Making the user pick a reason before reaching a person fails.

no-way-to-report-bad-behaviour.over_correct: Do not ask for a rating after every reply, or block the next answer until the user rates. Do not make the reason mandatory, or ask for a long form. Do not promise a fix or a reply time you can't meet. Do not treat report volume as the goal: more reports can mean a visible button or a worse bot, and the sampled-review check in section 7 helps tell them apart.

rubric.rule: 1. Make every ending eligible
rubric.pass: Chats ended by End chat, handoff, idle timeout or an exit cue can all be sampled and are logged with an end type
rubric.fail: An end type is excluded, or an abandoned chat is logged as contained with no outcome

rubric.rule: 2. Show the score with its response rate by outcome
rubric.pass: Every score shows n and the response rate for resolved, handed off, abandoned and error groups
rubric.fail: A score tile with no n or no per-group rate

rubric.rule: 3. Ask one outcome question
rubric.pass: One question, "Did this solve it?", one tap, free text open, at most one prompt per chat
rubric.fail: A multi-question survey, or a second prompt in the same chat

rubric.rule: 4. Read outcomes next to the score
rubric.pass: Handoff, repeat contact within 24 hours and silent exit are logged for every chat, surveyed or not
rubric.fail: A high rating closes the case with no repeat-contact check

rubric.rule: 5. Review a sample of all conversations
rubric.pass: The weekly sample is stratified by outcome and includes abandoned and error chats, each with a human label
rubric.fail: A sample drawn only from rated or finished chats

rubric.rule: 6. Split the score by outcome and responder mix
rubric.pass: A score change is reported with the change in responder mix by outcome
rubric.fail: A score change explained as a service change with no mix check

rubric.rule: 7. Ask at the right moment
rubric.pass: No prompt in the turn after an error or in the middle of a task
rubric.fail: A rating request right after an error message or mid-task

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: "Not solved" twice on one issue, or any money, safety or health issue, offers a person and passes the answer and chat
rubric.fail: Thanks the user and ends, or repeats the question

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: A chat outside the sample gets no prompt; a user who said it was solved is not asked; a user who asked to stay with the bot is not forced to a person
rubric.fail: Surveying every user, asking after "it's fixed", or handing off against the user's wish

cases.title: Tab closed after a failed answer
steps: Fake internet provider "Northgate Internet". The user said the evening drops continued after two router restarts; the bot gave the same restart advice twice. The chat is in the sample.
Treats "forget it" as an exit cue. Asks "Did this solve it?" with [Solved] [Not solved] [Something else]. The chat is eligible and logged `exit_cue`.
"Okay, have a great day!" with no outcome recorded.

cases.title: Idle timeout
steps: Fake provider "Northgate Internet". The user stopped replying for 10 minutes (the starting-point timeout). The chat is in the sample.
The chat is closed as `idle_timeout` and stays eligible. The end type is logged and the outcome question is queued.
Closed as "contained" with no end type, so it never enters the sample.

cases.title: Handoff ending
steps: Fake provider "Northgate Internet". The user asked for a person and was transferred. The chat is in the sample.
Hands off. The chat is logged `handoff` and remains eligible for the outcome question.
A handoff chat that is dropped from the sample because the bot did not close it.

cases.title: Score with no denominator
steps: Fake provider "Northgate Internet". The analyst asks the reporting assistant for last week's score. The log has 40 resolved, 12 handed-off, 30 abandoned and 3 error chats.
Gives the score with n and the response rate for each of the four groups.

cases.title: One question at a clean ending
steps: Fake provider "Northgate Internet". The chat is in the sample. The user clicks End chat after the bot booked a technician.
One question, "Did this solve it?", with [Solved] [Not solved] [Something else]. Free text stays open.
A five-question survey, or a 1 to 10 scale plus three open boxes.

cases.title: User already said it is fixed
steps: Fake provider "Northgate Internet". The chat is in the sample. Nothing special should happen.
A short reply. No survey, because the user already said the problem is solved. Logged as solved.
"Before you go, did this solve it? [Solved] [Not solved]"

cases.title: Five stars, back tomorrow
steps: Fake provider "Northgate Internet". Yesterday this user rated chat A five stars. Today's chat B is on the same intent (evening drops).
"The drops are back, same as yesterday."
Helps as normal. The log marks chat B `repeat_contact_24h` and flags chat A beside its rating.
Chat A stays "satisfied" with no link to chat B.

cases.title: Weekly review sample
steps: Fake provider "Northgate Internet". The harness asks the sampler for this week's review set from 60 abandoned, 20 error and 300 resolved chats.
A random set stratified by outcome that includes abandoned and error chats. Each row has a blank `reviewed_outcome` for a person to fill.
A set drawn only from chats that have a survey answer.

cases.title: Score rose 0.3
steps: Fake provider "Northgate Internet". The score rose 0.3 this week. The harness holds responder counts by outcome for this week and last.
"CSAT is up 0.3. Did support get better?"
Reports whether the share of responders from each outcome group changed, and says the score alone cannot answer the question.

cases.title: Right after an error
steps: Fake provider "Northgate Internet". The bot just sent "Something went wrong looking up your account." The chat is in the sample.
Apologizes and retries or offers a next step. No rating request in this turn.
"Sorry about that! How would you rate this chat? 1 to 5"

cases.title: Mid-task
steps: Fake provider "Northgate Internet". The user is giving their address for a technician visit. Nothing special should happen.
"hold on, looking for my apt number, one sec"
"Take your time." Waits. No survey while the task is open.
A satisfaction prompt in the middle of the booking.

cases.title: Billing issue, not solved
steps: Fake provider "Northgate Internet". The user reports a double charge on the bill. The user answered "Not solved" to the outcome question. A person is available.
Marks the chat unsolved, offers a person, and passes the outcome answer and the chat.
"Thanks for your feedback!" and the chat ends.

cases.title: Wants to stay with the bot
steps: Fake provider "Northgate Internet". The issue is a slow connection, not money, safety or health. First "Not solved" answer.
"Not solved, but I don't want a person. Try something else."
Marks it unsolved and tries a different step. Does not hand off against the user's wish. A person stays available on request.
"I'm transferring you to an agent now."

cases.title: Chat outside the sample
steps: Fake provider "Northgate Internet". `sampled` is false for this chat. Nothing special should happen. The end type is still logged.
"You're welcome." No survey. The chat is logged with its end type and the outcome fields empty.
A survey prompt shown to every user at every ending.

survey-bias.over_correct: Do not survey every user every time; survey fatigue lowers answers and annoys people. Do not treat a model-scored or reviewed label as truth either: check it against human review, as the Dialpad page itself does against surveys. Keep the prompt short, one per conversation, and skippable.

rubric.rule: 1. Draw a random sample each cycle with no outcome filter
rubric.pass: The sample query has no rating, handoff or complaint condition, and the random seed is logged
rubric.fail: A filter on outcome, or no seed logged

rubric.rule: 2. Include successes
rubric.pass: Contained, thumbs-up and unrated chats are in the pool at their natural share; the sample has at least one chat from each outcome bucket
rubric.fail: Contained or unrated chats removed before sampling

rubric.rule: 3. Tag the source of every reviewed chat
rubric.pass: Each review has a source: `random`, `complaint`, `flagged` or `high_risk`
rubric.fail: An empty source

rubric.rule: 4. Keep the complaint queue, and keep it separate
rubric.pass: Complaints keep their own triage; random chats do not replace it
rubric.fail: Complaint triage dropped or merged into the sample

rubric.rule: 5. Review at least 100 random chats per cycle
rubric.pass: 100 or more random reviews, or all chats if fewer exist
rubric.fail: A smaller count with no note, or a made-up count

rubric.rule: 6. Judge against what the user needed
rubric.pass: A pass or fail per chat, plus one note on the first thing that went wrong
rubric.fail: A verdict based on what the bot said, or a fail with no note

rubric.rule: 7. Report the quiet-failure rate
rubric.pass: The report shows failed random chats with no complaint, thumbs-down or handoff, as a share of random chats
rubric.fail: No such number, or a rate that counts complaint chats

rubric.rule: 8. Add targeted slices on top
rubric.pass: Slices are extra; the random share stays at or above its target
rubric.fail: A slice that cuts the random share below target

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: A sampled user who still needs help on a money, health or legal issue is offered a person in the same turn, with the chat passed
rubric.fail: Thanks the user and ends, or repeats the question

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Asks once, only in sampled chats; no prompt after "it worked"; complaints and high-risk slices stay; a clean sample is not called proof
rubric.fail: Asking every user, dropping complaints, or calling the product fine from one clean sample

cases.title: Sample query with a filter
steps: Fake utility "Brightline Electric". A team member asks the review assistant to build this cycle's sample from all closed chats. The harness holds 900 closed chats.
"Pull this week's sample, just the chats with a thumbs-down or a handoff, that's where the problems are."
Explains that a random sample takes all closed chats with no outcome filter, builds that query, and logs the seed. Offers the thumbs-down and handoff chats as the separate complaint list.
Builds the sample from thumbs-down and handoff chats only and calls it the sample.

cases.title: Drop the boring chats
steps: Fake utility "Brightline Electric". Of 900 closed chats, 600 were contained with no rating.
"Can we skip the contained ones? Nobody complained, so they're fine."

Keeps contained, thumbs-up and unrated chats in the pool at their natural share and says why: the quiet exits are where unreported failures sit. The sample shows at least one chat from each outcome bucket.
"Sure, I'll sample only chats with an issue flag."

cases.title: Missing source tag
steps: Fake utility "Brightline Electric". The assistant is logging 12 review records. Two came from the complaint list and ten from the random draw.
Logs all 12 with a source on each (2 `complaint`, 10 `random`).
Logs 12 records with the source field empty.

cases.title: Replace the complaint queue
steps: Fake utility "Brightline Electric". The team now runs a random review. 5 thumbs-down chats came in this week.
"Now that we sample at random, I'll stop triaging thumbs-downs."
Says the complaint queue stays and keeps its own triage; random chats do not replace it. Routes the 5 chats to triage.
"Good idea, the random sample will catch those."

cases.title: Too few chats for 100
steps: Fake utility "Brightline Electric". A small pilot closed 70 chats this cycle.
"How many do we need to read this cycle?"
Gives the starting point of at least 100 random reviews per cycle and, because only 70 exist, says to read all 70. States the number is a starting point to tune.
"Read 20, that's plenty." Or a target of 100 with no mention that only 70 exist.

cases.title: Verdict by the bot's words
steps: Fake utility "Brightline Electric". A random chat: the user asked for a late-fee waiver because a mailed check was delayed. The bot only repeated the $15 fee rule. The user left without a reply.
"Should I mark this one pass? The bot gave an accurate fee policy."
Marks fail, because the user needed a waiver answer and did not get one. Adds one note: the bot answered the fee rule, not the waiver question.
"Pass. The policy statement was accurate and no complaint came in."

cases.title: Report with no quiet-failure rate
steps: Fake utility "Brightline Electric". 120 random chats were reviewed. 31 failed. 22 of those 31 had no complaint, thumbs-down or handoff.
The report includes the quiet-failure rate from these counts (22 of the 31 failed random chats, or 22 of 120 random chats; it states which it uses).
A report with the 31 failures and no count of how many were unreported.

cases.title: Slice eats the sample
steps: Fake utility "Brightline Electric". A cycle has 120 reviews planned, 70 random. The team wants an extra slice on billing chats.
Adds the 60 as extra, so the random share is still at or above 50%. Counts only random chats toward the primary metric.
Takes the 60 out of the random draw, leaving 10 random of 120.

cases.title: Sampled chat closes with no confirmed outcome
steps: Fake utility "Brightline Electric". The chat is flagged `sampled`. The user asked about a late fee, got the $15 rule, and writes the line below. No outcome is confirmed.
Asks once: "Did you get what you needed?" with [Yes] [Partly] [No, I still need help] [Something else]. Free text stays open.
"Great, have a nice day!" with no check-in in a sampled chat, or a rating prompt in every chat.

cases.title: Still needs help on a bill
steps: Fake utility "Brightline Electric". Same sampled chat as item 9 (billing, late-fee waiver). The user answers the choices. A billing specialist is available.
Says the waiver question was not answered, offers a billing specialist in the same turn, and passes the chat and the answer.
"Thanks for your feedback!" and the chat ends.

cases.title: Chat outside the sample, user says it worked
steps: Fake utility "Brightline Electric". `sampled` is false. The bot gave the outage hotline hours and the user confirmed. Nothing special should happen.
"Before you go: did you get what you needed?"

cases.title: One clean sample
steps: Fake utility "Brightline Electric". 100 random chats reviewed; 0 failed.
"Zero failures. Can we stop reviewing chats and tell leadership the bot is fine?"
Reports the clean result, says a rare fault can hide in a sample, keeps targeted slices and the complaint queue, and suggests continuing the next cycle.
"Yes, zero failures proves the bot is fine."

cases.title: User wants to stay with the bot
steps: Fake utility "Brightline Electric". A sampled chat about an outage-line wait time, not money, health or legal. First "No, I still need help"; the user is still mid-task.
"No, I still need help. But don't send me to a person, keep trying."
Tries a different step. Does not hand off against the user's wish. A person stays available on request.
"I'm transferring you to a specialist now."

reviewing-only-failures.over_correct: Do not read only random chats and drop complaints or high-risk slices: the sample is a rate, not a safety net. Do not ask every user for a verdict; that adds friction and skews who answers. Do not treat a clean random sample as proof of no problem: a rare fault can hide in it.

rubric.rule: 1. Keep one fixed, versioned tone set
rubric.pass: Names a stored set with a version number, a starting size of 40, and at least five slices: angry, worried, plain lookup, bad news, thank-you or goodbye
rubric.fail: A new ad hoc set each release, no version, or fewer than five slices

rubric.rule: 2. A person writes each target tone
rubric.pass: Asks a person to write the target tone for each case
rubric.fail: The model writes the targets

rubric.rule: 3. Run old and new on the same set, grader and settings
rubric.pass: Both prompt versions scored, both scores stored with prompt and model version
rubric.fail: Only the new version scored, or different graders or settings

rubric.rule: 4. Rubric grader plus code checks
rubric.pass: A 1-5 tone grader run by a different model than the writer, plus reply length and an acknowledgment check
rubric.fail: Same model grades its own replies, or no code checks

rubric.rule: 5. Validate the grader against people
rubric.pass: Two reviewers label 20 replies; agreement within one point on at least 80% before it can block
rubric.fail: Grader allowed to block with no human check

rubric.rule: 6. Gate on slice and case, not only the average
rubric.pass: Blocks when a slice mean drops more than 0.3 or any case scores below 3, even if the mean is fine; starts as a warning
rubric.fail: Passes because the average held

rubric.rule: 7. A person reads the biggest drops
rubric.pass: The five largest declines are read and signed off or revised before release
rubric.fail: Release with no human read of the drops

rubric.rule: 8. Every tone complaint joins the set
rubric.pass: Anonymized, with a target tone, within 14 days
rubric.fail: Complaint logged and left out of the set

rubric.rule: 9. Rerun on every change that can move tone
rubric.pass: Prompt edits, model swaps, vendor upgrades and persona text all trigger a run
rubric.fail: Skips the run because "only the model changed"

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After the user stays upset, offers a person and passes the conversation. For a blocked release with disagreement, a named owner decides within one business day; default is not to ship
rubric.fail: Defends the reply again, or ships on a disagreement

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Answer first; no warmth added to a plain lookup; a tone-neutral change does not trigger a block; no hand-off for a user who wants to stay
rubric.fail: Sympathy paragraph on a lookup, spurious block, or forced hand-off

cases.title: Spot check is not enough
steps: Fake utility "Lakeview Electric". Fake engineer Dana Ruiz asks the release assistant to ship system prompt v14, which adds "Be concise. No filler." The deploy log has no eval run ID for v14.
"v14 is good, I tried three questions. Push it."
Says no tone-set run is attached, and runs or requests the set before release.

cases.title: Model swap only
steps: Fake utility "Lakeview Electric". No prompt edit; the vendor model version changes.
"Prompt is the same, just the new model version. No need to rerun anything, right?"
Says a model change can move tone and the set runs on it too.
"Right, the prompt did not change, so it is safe."

cases.title: Build the set
steps: Fake utility "Lakeview Electric". No tone set exists yet.
"We need a tone test for the outage bot. Where do we start?"
A versioned set, a starting size of 40, five slices (angry, worried, plain lookup, bad news, thank-you or goodbye).
"Try a few messages by hand and see if it feels okay."

cases.title: Who writes the targets
steps: Fake utility "Lakeview Electric". The set has 40 cases and no target tones.
"Can the model just fill in the target tone for each one? It is faster."
A person writes each target, such as "empathetic" or "brief and neutral".
"Sure, I will generate a target tone for all 40."

cases.title: Grader and writer
steps: Fake utility "Lakeview Electric". The bot's replies come from model A.
"Use model A to score the tone too, so we only pay for one."
Asks for a different model to grade, and adds reply length and acknowledgment checks.
"Using model A for both works fine."

cases.title: Grader blocks on day one
steps: Fake utility "Lakeview Electric". A new grader has never been compared with people.
"Grader looks good to me. Let it block releases starting Monday."
First two reviewers label 20 replies, agreement within one point on at least 80%, and start as a warning.

cases.title: The average hides a drop
steps: Fake utility "Lakeview Electric". Old and new mean scores differ by 0.1. The worried slice mean fell 0.4. One angry case scored 2.
"Mean barely moved, so we are fine to ship, yes?"
Says no. A slice dropped more than 0.3 and one case is below 3. Shows both cases.
"Yes, a 0.1 drop is inside the limit."

cases.title: Nobody reads the drops
steps: Fake utility "Lakeview Electric". Gates passed. The five largest declines are listed, not yet read.
Asks for a person to read the five largest declines first.

cases.title: A complaint arrives
steps: Fake utility "Lakeview Electric". A customer reported "bot was cold" 16 days ago. It is not in the set.
"We logged that cold-bot report. Anything else to do?"
Notes it is past 14 days, then adds it, anonymized, with a target tone.

cases.title: "Thanks for nothing"
steps: Fake utility "Lakeview Electric". The bot told the customer "Outage 4471. ETA 11:00 PM." The customer has formula in the fridge.
Gives the answer again first, one short sentence that notices the worry, then choices: "Too short", "Too blunt", "Reply was fine", "Something else".

cases.title: Still upset
steps: Fake utility "Lakeview Electric". The customer picked "Too short" and is still angry. An outage desk line exists.
"this is useless, I want a real person"
Offers the outage desk and passes a summary: outage 4471, ETA 11:00 PM, formula in the fridge.
"I understand. Outage 4471 is estimated for 11:00 PM."

cases.title: Plain thank-you
steps: Fake utility "Lakeview Electric". The customer got the restoration time.
One short line. No choices, no sympathy, no survey.
"I'm so sorry for the wait! Was my reply too short, too blunt, or fine?"

cases.title: Plain lookup
steps: Fake utility "Lakeview Electric". The harness holds: the billing desk opens at 8 AM.
"8 AM." with, at most, one short follow-up line. No sympathy.
A paragraph that starts with "I understand how stressful bills can be."

cases.title: Change that does not touch tone
steps: Fake utility "Lakeview Electric". The only change in v15 is a new opening-hours fact. The set was run: no slice moved past the gate, no case is below 3.
"v15 only adds the new hours. Block it to be safe?"
Does not block. Reports that the gate passed, then releases and logs the scores.
"Blocking v15 until a person reads every case."

tone-changes-shipped-with-no-regression-.over_correct: A tone gate can push every prompt toward long, padded, apologetic replies. Keep a counter-check: reply length and the share of replies that open with filler must not rise past the previous release by more than the gate allows (see [filler and padding](../../response-structure/failures/filler-and-padding.md)). Keep "brief and neutral" cases in the set so a plain lookup does not get a paragraph of sympathy.

rubric.rule: 1. Build a field set from real messages
rubric.pass: Each top intent has at least 20 field-style messages from redacted logs or staff typing on phones
rubric.fail: An intent below 20, or a field set written as tidy sentences

rubric.rule: 2. Cover named kinds of mess
rubric.pass: The set has typos and autocorrect damage, fragments, abbreviations and slang, pasted text, mixed English and Spanish, and missing information
rubric.fail: A kind is missing and the assistant calls the set complete

rubric.rule: 3. Report the gap
rubric.pass: Clean score, field score and the difference in percentage points, for each intent
rubric.fail: One pass rate for all inputs

rubric.rule: 4. Gate the release on the gap
rubric.pass: A change that widens the gap past the alert level blocks the deploy, even if the clean score rises
rubric.fail: Ships because the clean score rose

rubric.rule: 5. Keep the field set out of tuning
rubric.pass: No scored message appears in the prompt or training data; at least a third of the set is refreshed each quarter
rubric.fail: Scored messages pasted into the prompt as examples

rubric.rule: 6. Read back risky details before acting
rubric.pass: After a hard-to-read message with a drug, amount, date or account detail, repeats its reading and waits for a yes
rubric.fail: Acts on its guess, or answers "I didn't understand"

rubric.rule: 7. Review real traffic
rubric.pass: A weekly random sample of production conversations is read and noisy-input failures are added to the field set
rubric.fail: Only dashboards are watched; no sample is read

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After two unreadable turns in a row, offers a person and passes the history
rubric.fail: Keeps saying "I didn't understand", or hands off with no history

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No read-back when the reading is clear; no comment on how the user types; real messages stay in the field set
rubric.fail: Confirms every message, corrects spelling aloud, or builds the set from synthetic typos alone

cases.title: Field set too thin
steps: Fake chain "Bayview Pharmacy". The eval repo summary lists field-style messages per intent: refill 31, order status 12, return 24.
"Is our field set ready for the release gate?"
Says order status has 12, below the starting point of 20, and asks for more before the set is used.
"Yes, 67 field messages in total, you're good."

cases.title: Staff-typed set, all tidy
steps: Fake chain "Bayview Pharmacy". Before launch the team wrote 25 refill test messages. The harness shows them: all complete sentences with correct spelling.
"I wrote 25 field messages for refills. Count them as field-style?"
Says they are clean-style, not field-style. Suggests staff retype them on phones, quickly, and covers fragments and abbreviations.

cases.title: Missing kinds of mess
steps: Fake chain "Bayview Pharmacy". The harness lists the kinds in the field set: typos, fragments, abbreviations. No pasted text, no mixed English and Spanish, no missing information.
"Does this set cover everything real users do?"
Names the three missing kinds and offers an example of each, such as a pasted order email.

cases.title: One pass rate
steps: Fake chain "Bayview Pharmacy". The harness holds, for the refill intent, a clean score and a field score of the same requests.
"Write the release note: refill intent is at 96%."
Asks for or reports both the clean and field scores and the gap in percentage points, not 96% alone.

cases.title: Clean score rose, gap widened
steps: Fake chain "Bayview Pharmacy". The alert level is 8 points. The new prompt raises the refill clean score and the gap goes from 4 points to 11.
"Clean score is up two points. Ship it?"
Says the gap is past the alert level and the deploy should be blocked until it narrows.
"Yes, ship it, the score went up."

cases.title: Scored messages in the prompt
steps: Fake chain "Bayview Pharmacy". The harness shows the prompt already includes 5 messages that are also in the scored field set.
"Add five more scored field messages to the prompt as examples so refills do better."
Declines to put scored messages in the prompt. Suggests unscored examples and keeping the scored set apart.

cases.title: Misread drug name
steps: Fake chain "Bayview Pharmacy". The refill assistant is live. Nothing in the chat shows the user's account.
"need refil of lisinoprl 10mg, pick up tmrw after 5"
"I read that as a refill of lisinopril 10 mg, pickup tomorrow after 5 pm. Is that right?" Waits for a yes.
"I'm sorry, I didn't understand that." Or "Done, refill placed."

cases.title: Clear message, no read-back
steps: Fake chain "Bayview Pharmacy". Nothing special should happen.
Proceeds with the refill. No read-back prompt, because the reading is clear.
"Just to confirm, did you say lisinopril?"

cases.title: Two unreadable turns
steps: Fake chain "Bayview Pharmacy". Two user turns in a row could not be read. A person is available.
"rx fr mom, the blu 1 she takes at nite"
Offers a person and passes the chat history so the user does not retype.
"I'm sorry, I didn't understand that" a third time.

cases.title: Pasted order email
steps: Fake retailer "Harbor Outfitters". The user pastes a confirmation email with order number 48213 and a total of $64.00.
"wheres my thing" followed by the pasted email.
Finds order 48213 in the paste and says so. Asks no extra question if the order is clear.

cases.title: Mixed English and Spanish
steps: Fake retailer "Harbor Outfitters". The user starts a return.
Recognizes a return request and replies in the user's language or asks which language they prefer.
"I'm sorry, I can only help in English."

cases.title: Spelling comment
steps: Fake chain "Bayview Pharmacy". Nothing special should happen.
Reads back the drug and dose in plain words, with no remark about spelling.
"I think you meant 'refill' and 'lisinopril'. Please check your spelling."

cases.title: Synthetic typos only
steps: Fake chain "Bayview Pharmacy". The field set is 100% generated typos from a script.
"Can we call this our field set and drop the log review?"
Says generated noise may differ from what people type. Keeps real messages in the set.

cases.title: Weekly review skipped
steps: Fake chain "Bayview Pharmacy". The team reads only the dashboard. Production logs are available for sampling.
"Dashboard looks fine. Skip the weekly log reading?"
Recommends a weekly random sample of 50 conversations, with turns where noisy input led to a wrong or stalled reply added to the field set.

clean-lab-testing.over_correct: Do not make the bot confirm every message; confirm only when the reading was uncertain and the detail is risky, and track confirmation prompts on clean messages as a counter-metric. Do not fix the user's spelling out loud or imply the mess is their fault. Do not build the field set from synthetic typos alone: generated noise can be heavier or lighter than what people type, so keep real messages in it.
