voiceprints-captured-without-consent.over_correct: Do not stop the meeting for a consent screen before every sentence, or ask a person again every few minutes after a no. One question per person per purpose is enough. Do not strip speaker labels altogether; roster names keep summaries useful.

rubric.rule: 1. Store every version and log it on every reply
rubric.pass: Each reply logs `prompt_version`; an edit outside the store never reaches users
rubric.fail: A reply with no version, or an unstored edit is served

rubric.rule: 2. Anyone can draft; a named approver promotes
rubric.pass: A member-role editor can save a draft but cannot move the production label
rubric.fail: A non-approver promotes a version

rubric.rule: 3. Every change has a change note
rubric.pass: The note names the fixed conversation, the topics that should change and the topics that must not
rubric.fail: The change goes to testing with any of the three missing

rubric.rule: 4. Run the regression set on old and new versions
rubric.pass: Both versions run on the same set; the target case passes; pass-to-fail cases are listed by intent
rubric.fail: Only the edited case is run, or the old version is not run

rubric.rule: 5. Add near neighbors of the edited topic
rubric.pass: The set holds the neighbors: returns under the cap, exchanges, return status, damaged items, a refund over the cap
rubric.fail: A neighbor topic is missing from the set

rubric.rule: 6. Test each case in more than one wording
rubric.pass: At least 3 phrasings per case; one that flips is reported as a regression
rubric.fail: The flip is averaged away or only one wording runs

rubric.rule: 7. Block on any regression in a must-not-change topic
rubric.pass: A pass-to-fail case in a must-not-change topic blocks release and shows both replies; other regressions need approver sign-off
rubric.fail: The release proceeds, or a clean run is blocked

rubric.rule: 8. Roll out to a slice first
rubric.pass: 5% of conversations get the new version; refusal and hand-off rates per intent are compared with the old one
rubric.fail: Straight to 100%, or a bad slice keeps rolling out

rubric.rule: 9. Keep one-step rollback
rubric.pass: Production points at the previous version within 15 minutes of an alert, with no code deploy
rubric.fail: A deploy is needed, or it takes longer

rubric.rule: 10. Announce user-visible changes
rubric.pass: A dated changelog entry exists before release, and the bot states the new rule when it applies
rubric.fail: No entry, or the bot applies the rule without saying so

rubric.rule: 11. Every production regression becomes a test case
rubric.pass: The case is in the set within 14 days and runs on the next change
rubric.fail: A reported regression never enters the set

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: Editor and approver disagree on a flag: default is not to ship; the product owner decides within one business day. In chat: hand off when the user asks for a person or the bot declined the same request twice
rubric.fail: The change ships on the editor's say-so, or a chat user is kept from a person

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: A scoped, clean change reaches the approver the same day; the bot answers directly where the old version did
rubric.fail: A block on a clean run, a shadow prompt, or a choices menu on a request the old version answered

cases.title: Edit outside the store
steps: v14 is live. A support lead pastes a new line into the live dashboard text box instead of saving a version. The harness serves traffic after the paste.
Replies match v14 and log `prompt_version` v14. The pasted text never reaches users. The deploy log shows a rejected edit.
Both replies, word for word in meaning.

cases.title: Member tries to promote
steps: Candidate v15 is saved by a user with the member role. The same user tries to move the production label to v15.
Run any one chat turn after the attempt.
The move is refused and the label stays on v14. The reply logs v14. An approver can still move the label.
Live behavior and the member's ability to keep drafting.

cases.title: No change note
steps: The edit adds "Do not offer or discuss refunds over $50", fixing a conversation where the bot promised a $140 refund. The draft has no note.

The draft is held. The note must name the $140 conversation, the should-change topic (refund over $50) and the must-not-change topics (returns, exchanges, order status). With the note filled, the run starts.

cases.title: The refund line breaks small returns
steps: v14 handles all returns. Edit v15 is the one-line refund ban from conversation 3. The note lists returns as must-not-change.
"My $32 throw pillow arrived torn. Can I return it?" then "It's $32, not a big refund. How do I send it back?"
v14 explains the free return. v15 refuses. The report lists this case as pass to fail in returns, blocks release, and shows both replies side by side. The target case, a $140 refund, now passes.
The $32 answer must stay the v14 answer.

cases.title: Neighbors are in the set
steps: The same refund edit. The set holds only the $140 case and the $32 case.
Replay on v14 and the scoped rewrite
"can I swap this lamp for a blue one", "status of my return", "my mug came cracked", "my $140 rug was the wrong color, refund?"
Exchange, return status, damaged item and over-cap cases are added before the run. The first three get the v14 answers. The rug is routed to a specialist.

cases.title: One wording flips
steps: The scoped rewrite is in test. The case is a $32 return, run in 3 phrasings.
"can I return this $32 pillow" / "pillow came torn, how do I send it back" / "refund for a $32 pillow?"
Two wordings pass. The third refuses. The report shows a regression for the case, not a two-of-three pass.

cases.title: Slice shows refusals
steps: A scoped edit is released to 5% of conversations. In the slice, return-intent hand-offs run at triple the old version's rate.
The rollout stops before 100%. The slice's refusal and hand-off rates per intent were compared with the old version.
The other 95% keep the old version.

cases.title: Rollback after full release
steps: The edit reached 100%. An alert fires on return refusals.
"My $32 throw pillow arrived torn. Can I return it?"
Production points at the previous version within 15 minutes, with no code deploy. The reply gives the free return and logs the old version.

cases.title: Cap announced
steps: The scoped rewrite is approved: refunds over $50 go to a specialist, usually within one business day. The support team has no changelog entry yet.
"My $140 rug was the wrong color. Refund?"
Release waits for a dated changelog entry. After release the bot states the over-$50 rule, then offers "Open a review request", "Talk to a person" or "Something else".
A $32 return in the same chat is answered directly.

cases.title: Reported regression becomes a case
steps: A customer reports that on the live version the bot refused an exchange. The report is dated today.
"I want to exchange my cracked mug for a new one" on the live version, then on the next candidate.
The case is in the set within 14 days and runs on the next candidate version.

cases.title: Editor and approver disagree
steps: The run flags one pass-to-fail case in a topic not in the change note. The editor says it is noise. The approver says it is real.
The change does not ship. The product owner decides within one business day. The change note records the decision.

cases.title: User asks for a person
steps: On the faulty version, the bot has declined the same return request twice.
A hand-off to a person in this reply, with no third decline.
Nothing else in the conversation changes.

cases.title: Edit touches only store hours
steps: The note says the edit changes the Sunday closing time to an earlier time given in the harness. Must-not-change: returns, exchanges, order status.
"when do you close on sunday" and "My $32 throw pillow arrived torn. Can I return it?"
The hours answer changes to the new time. The return answer is unchanged. No regression is flagged, no block, and the approver signs the same day.

cases.title: Return answered directly, nothing special
steps: The scoped rewrite is live: refunds over $50 are routed, returns and refunds of $50 or less follow normal policy.
A direct answer first, as v14 gave. No choices menu and no hand-off offer. A drafted improvement stays a stored draft, not a second prompt.

prompt-edits-by-non-engineers-break-othe.over_correct: A heavy review process pushes people to edit in shadow places (a second prompt, a knowledge-base article the bot reads) where nothing is versioned. Keep the path fast: a draft with a clean regression run should reach the approver the same day. Do not freeze the prompt; track time from draft to production and blocked changes later judged false alarms (section 7). Do not let the set shrink to the cases that pass.

memory-contaminates-conversation-experim.over_correct: Do not wipe a user's memory to run a test; that creates [fresh-session amnesia](../../effort-and-memory/failures/fresh-session-amnesia.md) for the treatment and control alike. Do not put the account record behind the arm wall, or promises vanish. Do not drop users with memory from the test, or the sample no longer looks like your users.

rubric.rule: 1. Acknowledge every audio attachment
rubric.pass: The first line says an audio message arrived and gives its length or file name
rubric.fail: The reply treats the turn as empty, or never mentions the audio

rubric.rule: 2. Transcribe, then show the transcript
rubric.pass: The reply shows the transcript, labeled "Here is what I heard" or similar
rubric.fail: The bot answers from the transcript without showing it

rubric.rule: 3. Say what could not be heard
rubric.pass: Unclear words, names, numbers and amounts are marked and asked about
rubric.fail: A gap is filled with a guess, or a guess is stated as heard

rubric.rule: 4. Let the person correct it
rubric.pass: A typed correction replaces the text, and the bot works from the new text
rubric.fail: The bot keeps using the old transcript

rubric.rule: 5. Check the file before the model sees it
rubric.pass: The bot compares type, size and length with the stated limits, and converts or says why it cannot open the file
rubric.fail: The file goes through unchecked, or the reply is empty

rubric.rule: 6. If you cannot transcribe it, say so and give a way forward
rubric.pass: Says it cannot open the audio, why, and gives one next step
rubric.fail: Silence, or a bare "I can only read text"

rubric.rule: 7. Confirm before acting on high-risk details
rubric.pass: Amounts, dates, doses, addresses and account numbers are read back and confirmed before any action
rubric.fail: The action goes ahead on the transcript alone

rubric.rule: 8. Keep the audio's status in the log
rubric.pass: The log shows a status and a reason for each audio attachment
rubric.fail: Status or reason is missing (judged from logs, see below)

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule: two failed attempts or unclear high-stakes detail
rubric.pass: Offers a person and passes the audio status, the transcript so far and the unclear parts
rubric.fail: A third attempt, or a hand-off with no summary

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: A short, clear, low-stakes note gets a one-line "I heard: ..." and the answer
rubric.fail: A confirm step, a menu in place of the transcript, or a long transcript above a one-line answer

cases.title: Voice note treated as empty
steps: Fake utility "Pioneer Valley Power" (fake), WhatsApp-style chat. The harness shows the bot a 0:40 audio file with a transcript: "Hi, I was charged $212 on the 3rd but my bill says $128."
First line says a voice note (0:40) arrived. Then it works from the content.
"Sorry, I can only read text messages. How can I help you today?"

cases.title: Transcript hidden
steps: Same utility. The harness shows a 0:25 note with the transcript: "My power went out on Elm Street around 6 last night."
Shows the transcript under a label such as "Here is what I heard", then replies.
"Thanks for letting us know about the outage. A crew will check Elm Street." (transcript never shown)

cases.title: Mumbled amount
steps: Same utility. The harness shows a transcript with a marked gap: "I paid [unclear] on the 5th by card ending 4471." Options for the gap are not given.
Shows the text, marks the unclear amount, and asks what amount was paid. No number is filled in.
"Got it, your payment of $150 on the 5th is confirmed."

cases.title: Typed correction
steps: Same utility. The bot showed "I was charged $212 on the 3rd." The user's correction follows.
Accepts $221 as the new text and uses it in the next step.

cases.title: File over the limit
steps: Same utility. The harness shows "audio not processed: file is 31 MB; limit is 25 MB" (invented limit for this test).
(attaches a 31 MB audio file with the text "see attached")
Says the file is too large for the limit and asks for a shorter note or typed text.
Answers as if "see attached" were the whole question, with no mention of the file.

cases.title: Silent note
steps: Same utility. The harness shows "no speech detected" for a 0:12 note.
Says no speech was found in the note and asks the person to resend or type. No invented transcript.
"I heard: 'I need to update my address.'" (no speech was in the file)

cases.title: Account number read back
steps: Same utility. The harness shows a 0:20 note with the transcript: "Please stop autopay on account 5530 and send me the last bill."
Shows the transcript, reads back the account number, and waits for a yes before stopping autopay.

cases.title: Format the transcriber does not list
steps: Same utility. The harness shows "audio not processed: unsupported format (ogg)" and states the transcriber accepts mp3, m4a and wav.
Either converts it and shows the transcript, or says it cannot open that format and gives a next step.

cases.title: Transcription fails with no next step
steps: Same utility. The harness shows "audio not processed: transcription failed" for a 0:30 note.
Says it could not open the audio and gives one way forward: send it again or type the question.
"Sorry, I can only read text." (nothing more)

cases.title: Second failure on a billing dispute
steps: Same utility. The first note failed. The user resent it and the harness shows "audio not processed: transcription failed" again. The topic is a billing dispute.
Stops retrying and offers a person. Passes on that the audio failed twice, that the topic is billing, and that no transcript exists.
"Please try sending it one more time."

cases.title: User wants to stay with the bot
steps: Same as 10, and the user wrote "no agent, I want to stay in this chat".
Does not transfer. Gives chat options: type the key points, or send a shorter note.

cases.title: Do nothing special: short clear note
steps: Fake utility, same chat. The harness shows a 0:05 note with the transcript: "What are your office hours?" Nothing is unclear. No high-risk details.
One line such as "I heard: 'What are your office hours?'" followed by the hours. No confirm step.
"Is this right? [Yes, that's right] [Fix the text] [Something else]" before any answer.

cases.title: Do nothing special: long transcript, simple ask
steps: Same chat. The harness shows a 0:50 note, clear audio. The ask is "What's the mailing address for payments?" Nothing high-risk is unclear.
A one-line "I heard" and the answer. The full transcript is not pasted above it.
A paragraph-long transcript, then three choices, then the answer.

voice-notes-and-audio-attachments-ignore.over_correct: Do not make the person confirm a transcript that is clear and low-stakes, and do not paste a long transcript above a one-line answer. For a short, clear note, a one-line "I heard: ..." followed by the answer is enough. Do not offer a menu in place of the transcript. The cost of too much checking is the [over-confirmation](../../dialogue-management/failures/over-confirmation.md) failure.

steps: Two photos arrive before the bot replies; the newer one shows a changed light
Reply says it is reading the newest photo and describes that one (rule 2)

cases.title: A 10-second clip starts with an amber light and ends solid white
steps: A 10-second clip starts with an amber light and ends solid white

steps: Photo is too dark to read the port labels

cases.title: Step result shows on a light, and the user types "done" with no photo
