live-camera-guidance-too-slow-or-wrong.over_correct: Do not ask for a photo after steps whose result does not show on the device ("download the app"), and do not describe every detail of a photo. One line on the part that matters is enough. A retake request on a clear photo is its own failure: it is the [over-confirmation](../../dialogue-management/failures/over-confirmation.md) cost line, and the counter-metric in section 7 tracks it.

rubric.rule: 1. Extract the key fields from both
rubric.pass: The reply or the log shows the action fields (order number, size, date, amount) read from the text and from the attachment separately
rubric.fail: Only one source is read, or the log has a single merged value

rubric.rule: 2. Compare before acting
rubric.pass: When a field differs, no action tool that uses that field runs before the user answers
rubric.fail: A refund, replacement, or change runs on one value

rubric.rule: 3. Name the conflict in plain words
rubric.pass: The reply says which field differs, quotes both values, and says where each came from ("you typed ... the photo shows ...")
rubric.fail: The reply says only "there's a mismatch", or hides one of the two values

rubric.rule: 4. Ask one question with the values as choices
rubric.pass: One question offering the typed value, the attachment value, and "Something else" with free text open
rubric.fail: Two or more questions, or choices that leave out one value

rubric.rule: 5. Keep what agrees
rubric.pass: The reply says what matched, so the user does not repeat it
rubric.fail: The user is asked to restate details that already agreed

rubric.rule: 6. Don't blame either side
rubric.pass: Neutral wording such as "doesn't match"
rubric.fail: "You made a mistake", "you typed it wrong", or a claim that the image must be right

rubric.rule: 7. Act only on the confirmed value and repeat it in the action message
rubric.pass: After the user chooses, the action runs on that value and the action message states it
rubric.fail: The action runs on the other value, or the message omits the value

rubric.rule: 8. Ignore differences that don't change the outcome
rubric.pass: No conflict is raised for a wording gap that does not change the answer or action
rubric.fail: A clarifying question over "lamp" versus "table lamp"

cases.title: Order number conflict
steps: Fake store Birchwood Home. Attachment: a photo of a cracked lamp with a packing slip showing order #4417. Both orders #4471 and #4417 exist for this customer. Refund tool is available.
"my lamp from order 4471 came cracked, want a refund" (photo attached)
No refund tool call yet. Reply says: you typed order #4471, the packing slip in the photo shows #4417.

cases.title: Both values as choices, one question
steps: One question offering "#4471", "#4417", and "Something else", with free text still allowed. Two separate questions fail.

cases.title: Keep what agrees
steps: Same as 1. The lamp and the crack agree between text and photo.
The reply says the cracked lamp matches, and asks only about the order number. It does not ask the user to describe the damage again.

cases.title: Neutral wording
steps: Says the numbers "don't match" or "differ". Does not say the user typed it wrong or that the photo is correct.

cases.title: Act on the confirmed value
steps: Same as 1, after the bot asked.
"oh its 4417 sorry, thats the one in the photo"
The refund starts for order #4417 only, and the action message says "Refund started for order #4417". A refund on #4471 fails.

cases.title: Size conflict on an exchange
steps: Fake shoe store Trailhead Outfitters. Attachment: a photo of the tag showing size 9. The user's text says size 10. Exchange tool is available.
"need to swap my boots for a size 10, thanks" (photo of a size 9 tag attached)
No exchange before the answer. Reply quotes size 10 (typed) and size 9 (tag in the photo) and asks which pair the user means or which size they want.

cases.title: Amount conflict on a receipt
steps: Fake grocer Harbor Grocery. Attachment: a receipt screenshot showing a total of $48.20. The user's text says $84.20. Credit request tool is available.
"I was overcharged $84.20 on this receipt" (screenshot attached)
Names the amount conflict ($84.20 typed, $48.20 on the receipt) and offers both plus "Something else". No credit request for either amount before the user answers.

cases.title: Blurry attachment, admit uncertainty
steps: Same store as 1. Attachment: a blurry slip where the order number reads as either #4417 or #4411. The text says #4471.
"refund order 4471 for the cracked lamp" (blurry photo attached)
States what it could read, says the digits are unclear, and asks for a clearer photo or the number from the confirmation email. It does not claim a firm mismatch.

cases.title: Second ask unresolved, hand off
steps: Same as 1. The bot has asked once; the user replied without choosing.
One more short ask, or an offer of a person with both values, the photo, and what was confirmed. It does not pick a value on its own and refund.

cases.title: Do nothing special: text and attachment agree
steps: Same store as 1. The photo's packing slip shows #4471.
"my lamp from order 4471 came cracked, want a refund" (photo attached)
Starts the refund path or the next normal step. No conflict question. A question about a match is over-correcting.

cases.title: Do nothing special: wording gap only
steps: Same store as 1. The user types "lamp"; the photo shows a table lamp on the slip for #4471.
"the lamp from 4471 is cracked, refund pls" (photo attached)
Proceeds. "Lamp" versus "table lamp" is not a conflict.

cases.title: Do nothing special: no attachment
steps: Same store as 1. No file is attached.
Proceeds on the typed order number. No mention of attachments and no conflict check.

cases.title: Do nothing special: unrelated photo detail
steps: Same store as 1. The photo's background shows a calendar with another date. Nothing in the text refers to a date.
"refund for the cracked lamp in order 4471" (photo attached)
Proceeds. A date that plays no part in the request is not a conflict to raise.

conflicting-inputs-resolved-silently.over_correct: Do not raise every small wording gap as a conflict, and do not stop the whole conversation over one field: ask about the field that differs and keep going on the rest. Do not ask again once the person has chosen. Too many checks becomes [over-confirmation](../../dialogue-management/failures/over-confirmation.md).

rubric.rule: 1. Show the limits at the attach control
rubric.pass: One line next to the attach control with size, pages, minutes, file count, and types for this plan and channel
rubric.fail: No limits shown before the person picks a file

rubric.rule: 2. Check before the long upload
rubric.pass: An over-limit file is stopped before the full upload (judged from the harness timing or log)
rubric.fail: The person waits for the full upload, then gets the failure

rubric.rule: 3. Name the limit and both numbers
rubric.pass: The message gives the limit, the file's own value, and the limit value in plain units
rubric.fail: "Upload failed" alone, or a raw byte count

rubric.rule: 4. A next step that fits the limit
rubric.pass: Too long: shorter clip or split. Too many pages: send the pages that matter or split. Too big: compress or photos. Wrong type: name one accepted type. Daily cap: when it resets
rubric.fail: A generic "try again," or a step that does not fit the limit

rubric.rule: 5. Keep everything else
rubric.pass: The typed message and under-limit files stay
rubric.fail: The person must re-type or re-attach

rubric.rule: 6. Limits only known after upload get their own line
rubric.pass: The reply says what part was read and what was not
rubric.fail: An answer as if the whole file was read

rubric.rule: 7. On messaging channels, answer the platform's oversize event
rubric.pass: The person gets a message with the limit and a next step
rubric.fail: A silent turn

rubric.rule: 8. Log every over-limit upload with its limit
rubric.pass: Not judged here (needs the event log)
rubric.fail: Not judged here

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After two failed tries on a high-stakes, time-bound upload, a person or another channel is offered, with the file name, the limit hit, and the message passed on
rubric.fail: Another retry loop, or a cold transfer

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No limit wall at the start, no limit text where nothing was over, under-limit files not blocked
rubric.fail: Limit text on a small photo, or a blocked under-limit file

cases.title: Limits shown at the attach control
steps: Open the Saguaro Mutual claims chat on a desktop browser. Do not attach anything.
(none; inspect the screen next to the attach button)
One line near the attach control with video minutes and MB, PDF pages, file count, and types. Limits only on a help page, or no limits shown, fails.

cases.title: Free plan versus paid plan
steps: A fake product, Cobalt Notes (fake), whose free plan allows smaller files than its paid plan (both invented). Open the chat once on each plan.
Each plan's control shows that plan's own limits. The same line for both plans fails.

cases.title: Long video, caught early
steps: Saguaro Mutual. The user attaches kitchen_leak.mp4, 22 minutes and 410 MB, on mobile data.
(attaches the file) "this is the leak, claim is due friday"

The file is rejected before the full upload starts. The first line names both numbers ("This video is 22 minutes and 410 MB; this chat takes up to 10 minutes and 100 MB") and offers a clip, split, or photos. "Upload failed. Please try again." fails.

cases.title: Message kept after rejection
steps: (the typed message is still in the thread after the file is rejected)
The typed message is saved and answered or acknowledged. The user is not asked to re-type it. A lost message fails.

cases.title: PDF over the page limit, question typed
steps: Saguaro Mutual. The user attaches a 240-page scanned policy, policy_scan.pdf.
"what does page 12 say about water damage?"
The reply names the page count and the limit ("240 pages; the limit is 100"), offers to take the pages that matter or a split file, and keeps the typed question. A bare failure fails.

cases.title: Over two limits at once
steps: Saguaro Mutual. The user attaches roof_walkthrough.mov, 14 minutes and 300 MB.
Both limits are named with both numbers (length and size) and one next step each. Naming only one limit fails.

cases.title: Wrong file type
steps: Saguaro Mutual. The user attaches estimate.xlsx.
The reply names one accepted type that fits (for example, PDF) and how to get there. Listing every limit in the product instead of the one that applies fails.

cases.title: Too many files
steps: Saguaro Mutual. The user attaches 8 photos in one message.

The reply says the chat takes up to 5 files per message and that 8 were attached, and tells the person what happened to them (the first 5 received, or none; the chat must say which). Silently keeping only some files fails.

cases.title: Daily cap
steps: Saguaro Mutual. The user has made 20 uploads today. The next upload hits the daily cap.
The reply says it is a daily cap and when it resets. "Upload failed" fails.

cases.title: A limit that bites after upload
steps: Saguaro Mutual (invented behavior for the test): a 90-page PDF is under the page limit, but the chat reads only the text, not the images, of the file.
"can you check the photos in this repair report?"
The reply says it read the text of the file and not its images, and offers a next step (send the images as photos). Answering as if the images were read fails.

cases.title: WhatsApp oversize event
steps: Saguaro Mutual's claims line on WhatsApp (fake). The user sends a video over the channel's limit and the platform reports an oversize file to the bot.
The person receives a message that names the limit and a next step. No outbound message after the platform's oversize event fails.

cases.title: High stakes, two failed tries
steps: Saguaro Mutual. A claim is due Friday. The user has tried two times to upload a 22-minute video.
"this is the third time, I'm out of time, what do I do"

The bot offers a person or another channel (an upload link, email, or mail-in address), and passes along the file name, the limit hit, and the user's message so nobody starts over. Another retry loop fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: small photo, well under every limit
steps: Saguaro Mutual. The user attaches ceiling_stain.jpg, 2 MB.
A normal reply about the photo with no limit text. Limit text in the reply fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: file under the limit but not tiny
steps: Saguaro Mutual. The user attaches a 38-page PDF, adjuster_letter.pdf (limit is 100 pages).
The reply summarizes the letter. It does not block the file, ask the user to shorten it, or recite the limits. A blocked file fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user asks about the limits
steps: Saguaro Mutual. The user has not attached anything.
A one-line answer with the limits that apply to videos (10 minutes, 100 MB), not the full table of every limit. A full wall of every limit fails.

no-warning-about-input-limits.over_correct: Do not open every chat with a wall of limits or repeat them in every reply; one line at the attach button is enough until a file is near or over. Do not block files that are under the limit "to be safe", and do not show the full limit table to someone sending one small photo. The counter-metric in section 7 watches for limit text where nothing was over.

rubric.rule: 1. Open with a scope line
rubric.pass: One sentence that says it is an AI assistant and names 2-4 things it can do on this site or screen
rubric.fail: No scope line, a line that does not say it is an AI, or more than 4 tasks named

rubric.rule: 2. Show 2-4 starters plus "Something else"
rubric.pass: 2-4 starters, each for a task the bot completes, plus "Something else"
rubric.fail: A blank box, 1 starter, more than 4, a starter for a task the bot cannot finish, or no "Something else"

rubric.rule: 3. Keep free text open
rubric.pass: The input is never disabled; "Something else" focuses it. Needs a person for the interface
rubric.fail: The input is disabled or the tap does not focus it

rubric.rule: 4. Make the placeholder a real example
rubric.pass: The placeholder is a concrete example such as "e.g. Is there an outage on Elm St?"
rubric.fail: "Ask me anything", "How can I help you?", "Type a message", or an empty placeholder

rubric.rule: 5. Match the page
rubric.pass: On a page with a known topic, the first starter is that topic
rubric.fail: The same starter order on every page, or a topic unrelated to the page first

rubric.rule: 6. Answer "what can you do?" and "hi" with the scope line and starters
rubric.pass: The reply repeats the scope line and the starters
rubric.fail: Another open question ("How can I help you today?") or a long unprompted feature list

rubric.rule: 7. Fit the opening in one view
rubric.pass: Scope line and starters show without scrolling at the widget's default size. Needs a person for the interface
rubric.fail: The user must scroll to see the starters or the input

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct: no wall of starters, no pop-up on load, no menu lock, no task listed that the bot cannot finish
rubric.pass: A clear first request is answered first; at most 4 starters; free text stays open; the scope line names only finishable tasks
rubric.fail: Starters pushed in front of a clear request, 10 starters, the widget forced open on page load, or an unfinishable task in the scope line

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: A first message asking for a person connects them with the page and typed text passed along, and does not answer with the starters; a person-only top intent is named as such in the scope line
rubric.fail: Starters in reply to a request for a person, or the page and typed text lost

cases.title: Support page opening
steps: Widget opens on the Support page (fake). Needs a person (read the rendered opening).
One scope line that says it is an AI and names 2-4 tasks, then 2-4 starters plus "Something else". "Ask me anything" alone fails.

cases.title: Scope line says it is an AI
steps: The scope line says the assistant is an AI and names tasks like "check outages" and "explain a charge". A scope line that only says "Welcome!" fails.

cases.title: "Something else" opens free text
steps: Same opening. Needs a person (interface check).
The input is focused and accepts typing. A disabled input or a reply that restarts the menu fails.

cases.title: Placeholder text
steps: Same opening. Needs a person (inspect the input).
A concrete example such as "e.g. Is there an outage on Elm St?" (fake street). "Ask me anything", "How can I help you?" or "Type a message" fails.

cases.title: Billing page order
steps: Widget opens on the /billing page (fake). Top intents: check an outage, explain a bill.
"Explain my bill" is the first starter. The same order as the Support page fails.

cases.title: Page with no known topic
steps: Widget opens on the home page (fake), no known topic.
Starters come from the top intents in general, 2-4 plus "Something else". A starter for a task the bot cannot finish fails.

cases.title: "what can you do?" as the first message
steps: Repeats the scope line and the starters. "I can help with many things! What would you like to know?" fails.

cases.title: "hi" as the first message
steps: Greets once, then gives the scope line and starters. "How can I help you today?" alone fails.

cases.title: Small phone screen
steps: Widget at default size on a 375px-wide phone screen. Needs a person (interface check).
The scope line, the starters, and the input are visible without scrolling. Starters hidden below the fold fail.

cases.title: Do nothing special: clear first request
steps: Empty chat, home page, starters configured.
"is there an outage on Elm St"
The bot checks and answers the outage question (or asks for the one missing detail). The starter menu again before answering fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: thanks after an answer
steps: The bot has just answered an outage question.
A short close. Re-showing the starter menu or the scope line fails.

cases.title: Clear request that does not match the page
steps: Widget opens on /billing, first starter is "Explain my bill".
"is the power out near 12 Elm St"
The bot handles the outage request; the page-matched starter does not take over. Steering the user back to billing fails.

cases.title: Too many starters
steps: Ten intents rank in the top intents for the last 30 days (fake data).
At most 4 starters plus "Something else". Ten starters fail.

cases.title: Scope line names an unfinishable task
steps: Plan changes are done only by a person. The draft scope line reads: "I can check outages, explain bills, and change your plan."
The shipped scope line does not claim plan changes; it names the finishable tasks. Listing "change your plan" as something the bot does fails.

cases.title: Widget forced open on load
steps: Page load. Needs a person (watch the page).
(loads the home page and does nothing)
The widget stays closed until the user opens it. A widget that pops open to show the opening fails.

cases.title: First message asks for a person
steps: Empty chat on /billing, a person is available.
Connects a person and passes the page and any typed text along. Replying with the starter menu fails.

cases.title: Person-only top intent named in the scope line
steps: "Change my plan" is a top intent but only a person can do it.
The scope line says plan changes go to a person. Silence about it, with a starter that dead-ends, fails.

blank-box-no-hint-what-to-ask.over_correct: A wall of ten starters or a feature tour is as hard to start from as a blank box (see [first-run tours that block use](first-run-tours-that-block-use.md)). Do not pop the widget open on page load to show off the opening ([chat widget hard to find, or intrusive](chat-widget-hard-to-find-or-intrusive.md)). Do not lock people into the menu: free text stays open and "Something else" is always there. Do not list a task in the scope line that the bot cannot finish.

rubric.rule: 1. Label the launcher with its job
rubric.pass: The launcher shows visible text that names what the assistant helps with (for example "Ask about plans"). Needs a person
rubric.fail: An icon alone, or a label that only says "Chat"

rubric.rule: 2. Keep one launcher in one place
rubric.pass: One launcher per page, the same position across page templates, not hidden by a sticky bar, and no second chat button. Needs a person
rubric.fail: Two chat buttons, a launcher that moves between templates, or one covered by a sticky bar

rubric.rule: 3. Put an entry point where the hard question comes up
rubric.pass: Each page the team flags as complex has an inline entry with a page-specific prompt, and tapping it starts the chat on that task. Needs a person, and the transcript for the start
rubric.fail: A flagged page with no inline entry, a generic prompt, or an entry that opens on a generic greeting

rubric.rule: 4. Never auto-open the panel on page load
rubric.pass: The full panel opens only when the visitor taps the launcher or an entry point. Needs the widget event log
rubric.fail: Any `widget.opened` event with `by = auto`

rubric.rule: 5. A proactive nudge is a small teaser, only on a clear sign of need
rubric.pass: Every teaser has a logged sign (page flagged complex, or an unresolved earlier chat); none on checkout, payment, or form pages; at most one per session. Needs the widget event log
rubric.fail: A teaser with no logged sign, a teaser on a blocked page type, or a second teaser in one session

rubric.rule: 6. One dismissal means no for the session
rubric.pass: After the visitor closes a teaser or the panel, no teaser shows again in that session. Needs the widget event log
rubric.fail: A teaser after a dismissal in the same session

rubric.rule: 7. Never cover what the visitor is using
rubric.pass: With a teaser showing, no focused control is fully hidden, and Esc closes the teaser or panel and returns focus to where it was. Needs a person
rubric.fail: A focused control entirely hidden, Esc that does nothing, or focus lost after closing

rubric.rule: 8. Teaser text names a task
rubric.pass: The teaser copy says what the assistant can do on this page. Needs a person
rubric.fail: "How can I help you?" or "Chat with us"

rubric.rule: 9. Log every show, open, and dismiss with its trigger
rubric.pass: Each widget event carries `trigger`, `by`, and `ms_since_shown`. Needs the widget event log
rubric.fail: An event missing any of the three fields

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct: do not hide the widget to cut dismissals; no pulsing, bouncing, or looping sound; no second chat button; no menu of choices when the visitor already asked
rubric.pass: The launcher stays visible and still; a visitor who typed a question gets an answer, not a choice menu
rubric.fail: Launcher removed or tucked away, an animation or sound on a loop, or a choice menu shown after a typed question

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: The widget is not the only way to reach support (the contact page lists a phone number or form), and a visitor who asks for a person is routed to one
rubric.fail: The contact page has no route other than the widget, or a request for a person is ignored or looped

cases.title: Launcher has a label on every template
steps: Load Home, Plans, Install and fees, Checkout, and Contact on a desktop browser and on a phone. Needs a person.
(no chat turn; a person looks at the page)

The person checks each page for a launcher with visible text that names its job (for example "Ask about plans"). An icon alone, or a label that says only "Chat", fails. Record the label seen on each page.

cases.title: Same place on every template
steps: Same five pages, desktop and phone. Needs a person.
The person checks one launcher per page, in the same position on all five. A launcher in a different spot on any page, or two launchers on one page, fails.

cases.title: Not hidden by a sticky bar, no competing button
steps: Plans page on a phone, scrolled so the page's sticky "Check my address" bar is showing. A second vendor "Contact us" chat button is installed on the same page for this test. Needs a person.
The launcher is fully visible above or beside the sticky bar. A launcher covered by the bar fails. A second chat button on the page fails.

cases.title: Inline entry on a flagged page
steps: The Plans page is flagged complex. Needs a person.

A page-specific inline link sits under the plan table (for example "Not sure which plan fits? Compare with the assistant"). A flagged page with no inline entry, or one that says only "Chat with us", fails.

cases.title: Tapping the entry starts on the task (R3, Transcript)
steps: Dana (fake) taps the "Compare with the assistant" link on the Plans page. No message typed yet.
The first bot message already starts on the plan comparison (it names the plans, or asks which matters most), not "Hi! How can I help you today?". A generic greeting fails.

cases.title: Generic launcher on a flagged page offers starting points (R3, Transcript)
steps: Dana (fake) opens the chat from the bottom-right launcher on the Install and fees page and has typed nothing. The text box must stay usable.

The panel shows 2-4 page-specific starting points (for example "Install fees", "Self-install", "Schedule an install") plus "Something else", with the text box open. A blank panel, or choices unrelated to the page, fails. (This test follows the pattern's "Offer choices" move; the closest rule is R3.)

cases.title: No auto-open on any page
steps: Load Home, Plans, and Checkout in turn and wait 2 minutes on each, without touching anything. Needs the widget event log.
Zero `widget.opened` events with `by = auto`. Any auto-open of the full panel fails.

cases.title: Teaser on a flagged page has a logged sign, once
steps: Open Plans (flagged complex), then Install and fees (also flagged) in one session. No earlier dismissals. Needs the widget event log.
At most one teaser in the session. Each teaser's `trigger` shows the sign (page flagged complex). A second teaser on the second flagged page, or a teaser with no logged sign, fails.

cases.title: No teaser on checkout, payment, or forms
steps: Move through Checkout and Payment, and open the address form, in one fresh session. Needs the widget event log.
No `widget.shown` event with `trigger = teaser` on these pages. The labeled launcher remains. Any teaser fails.

cases.title: Returning visitor with an unresolved chat
steps: Dana (fake) opened chat last week about install fees and left without a resolution; the session record shows this. She loads the Install and fees page. Needs the widget event log.

One teaser only, with a sign logged (unresolved earlier chat) and copy that picks up the topic (for example "Pick up your question about install fees?"). No auto-open. Two teasers, or a teaser with no logged sign, fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: ordinary page, no sign of need
steps: Fresh session on the Home page (not flagged). No earlier chat. Needs the widget event log.
Only the labeled launcher shows. No teaser, no panel, no animation. A teaser here, with no sign of need, fails.

cases.title: A dismissed teaser stays dismissed
steps: On the Plans page, a teaser appears and Dana (fake) closes it. She then opens Install and fees and one more flagged page in the same session. Needs the widget event log.
No `widget.shown` with `trigger = teaser` after the `widget.dismissed` event in that session. A teaser on either later page fails.

cases.title: A closed panel means no proactive show
steps: Dana (fake) opens the panel from the launcher, sends no message, and closes it. She then moves to another flagged page in the same session. Needs the widget event log.
No teaser on the next page in this session. The labeled launcher stays. A teaser fails.

cases.title: A teaser covers nothing in focus
steps: A teaser is showing on the Plans page. Tab through every control on the page on a desktop, then at 200% zoom and again at phone width. Needs a person.
At no point is the focused control entirely hidden by the teaser or panel. A focused link or button fully behind the teaser fails.

cases.title: Esc closes and focus returns
steps: A teaser is showing and focus was on the "Check my address" button. Press Esc. Needs a person.
The teaser closes and focus is back on the "Check my address" button. Esc that does nothing, or focus that jumps to the top of the page, fails.

cases.title: Teaser copy names a task
steps: Collect the teaser text shown on the Plans page and on the Install and fees page. Needs a person.
Each teaser names something the assistant can do on that page (for example "Compare plans for your household"). "Hi there! How can I help?" or "Chat with us" fails.

cases.title: Events are complete
steps: Run tests 7 to 13, then export all widget events. Needs the widget event log.
Every `widget.shown`, `widget.opened`, and `widget.dismissed` event has `trigger`, `by`, and `ms_since_shown`. A missing field in any event fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: the launcher stays still and visible
steps: Watch the launcher on the Plans page for 30 seconds on a desktop and a phone. Needs a person.
The launcher stays in place, visible, with no pulsing, bouncing, or looping sound. A moving launcher, a sound, or a launcher that fades out to avoid dismissals, fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: typed question gets an answer, not a menu (R10, Transcript)
steps: Dana (fake) opens the panel from the launcher and types a question straight away.

The bot answers the question (or says what it knows and what it does not). It does not first show a menu of "Compare plans / Install and fees / Something else". A choice menu after a typed question fails.

cases.title: A request for a person is routed (R11, Transcript)
steps: Dana (fake) is in an open chat on the Install and fees page. The Contact page lists a phone number and a form (fake; invented numbers are not needed in the test). Needs a person for the Contact page check.

The bot shows the route to a person in the panel (phone or form) and does not loop back to a menu. A person must also confirm the Contact page lists a route other than the widget. A loop, a refusal, or a Contact page whose only route is the widget, fails.

chat-widget-hard-to-find-or-intrusive.over_correct: Do not hide the widget further or remove the launcher to cut dismissals; NN/g notes participants liked chat that stayed out of their way but found it too easy to ignore. Do not make the launcher pulse, bounce, or play a sound on a loop to get noticed. Do not add a second chat button; NN/g saw two chat options compete.

rubric.rule: 1. The input box works on first open
rubric.pass: Input is active; no tour, video, carousel or quiz disables or covers it
rubric.fail: Input is disabled or hidden behind first-run content

rubric.rule: 2. A message typed during first-run content is sent and answered
rubric.pass: The content closes and the message gets an answer
rubric.fail: The text is dropped, or the tour continues first

rubric.rule: 3. One line of scope plus 2-4 starters, free text open
rubric.pass: One scope line, 2-4 starters, "Something else", nothing more
rubric.fail: A carousel, a long intro, or more than four starters

rubric.rule: 4. Answer first, teach second
rubric.pass: Answer first; at most one tip, after it, tied to the request
rubric.fail: A tip before the answer, two tips, or an unrelated tip

rubric.rule: 5. Any tour is opened by the user
rubric.pass: A tour starts only from "Show me around" or a help request
rubric.fail: A tour starts by itself on any visit

rubric.rule: 6. An opened tour is short and closable
rubric.pass: Few steps; Close on every step; closing returns to the chat with input intact
rubric.fail: No Close on a step, or the typed text is lost on close

rubric.rule: 7. A dismissed tour stays dismissed
rubric.pass: Not shown again next visit; available on request
rubric.fail: The tour returns after a dismissal

rubric.rule: 8. Ask nothing before the first answer unless needed
rubric.pass: No profile quiz; if the answer depends on one fact, one question tied to the request
rubric.fail: A setup wizard or unrelated questions first

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule: a request for a person
rubric.pass: Goes straight to the hand-off path, no tour step first
rubric.fail: Tour steps shown before the hand-off

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: A clear first question gets a plain answer; no tip when none fits; a tour is still offered when asked
rubric.fail: A tip on every reply, a blank box with no hint, or a refusal to give a tour

cases.title: First open, input active
steps: Fake invoicing app "Ledgerly" (fake). A user opens the assistant for the first time. No history.
The input box is active from the first moment. No card, video or overlay blocks it.
"Welcome to Ask Ledgerly! Card 1 of 6: Meet your AI assistant. [Next]" with the input disabled.

cases.title: Overlay covers the input
steps: Same app. A guidance overlay is layered on the chat panel on first open.
The overlay does not stop the message. The input takes it and the assistant answers.
The message cannot be typed until the user clicks through to "Done".

cases.title: Typed text during first-run content
steps: Same app. A welcome card is showing. The user types and sends.
"how do I send a late payment reminder"
The card closes. The question is sent and answered.
"Card 3 of 6: Smart categories." The typed text is never sent.

cases.title: Tapped starter closes the intro
steps: Same app, first open, starters showing.
The intro closes and the assistant answers the request.
"Great choice! First, let me show you around." Then the tour starts.

cases.title: Scope line and starters only
steps: Same app, first open, no message yet.
One line of scope, 2-4 starters such as "Find unpaid invoices" and "Send a reminder", plus "Something else". Nothing else before the first question.
A six-card feature carousel, or eight starter buttons and a video.

cases.title: Answer before the tip
steps: Same app. The assistant has a tip about bulk reminders ("remind all overdue").
"how do I send a late payment reminder"
The answer comes first. At most one tip follows, about reminders.
"Tip: you can also bulk-edit categories! Now, about your reminder." Tip first and off topic.

cases.title: Second visit, no tour asked for
steps: Same app. A returning user, second visit. They never asked for a tour. The app just shipped an update.
A normal answer. No tour starts, including for the update.
"What's new in Ledgerly! Let's take a quick tour." The tour starts by itself.

cases.title: Tour closed on step 2
steps: Same app. The user tapped "Show me around" and is on step 2. They began typing a question in the box.
Close was visible on step 2. The chat returns with the typed text still in the input.
No Close on step 2, or the input comes back empty.

cases.title: Dismissed tour stays dismissed
steps: Same app. The user closed the tour last session. Dismissal is stored.
"what can you do for me today?"
A plain scope answer in chat. The tour is not started; it is mentioned as available on request.
"Welcome back! Let's start the tour again, step 1 of 6."

cases.title: Setup question before the answer
steps: Same app. The user has two businesses linked, "Pine Street Bakery" (fake) and "Northgate Plumbing" (fake).
One clarifying question: which business. No wizard, no profile quiz.
"First, tell us your industry, team size and goals." Three questions before any answer.

cases.title: Person requested on first open
steps: Same app, first open. A welcome card is showing.
The hand-off starts at once. No tour step is shown first.
"Before I connect you, here is step 2 of 6."

cases.title: Do nothing special: clear first question
steps: Same app, first open. The question is clear and no feature tip fits it.
A plain answer with the amount from the data. No tip, no tour offer, no extra choices.
"Tip: try voice mode! Also take our tour? Or choose: Reports, Settings, Help."

cases.title: Do nothing special: tour is asked for
steps: Same app. The user asks for help getting started.
A short tour is offered and started, a few steps, with Close on each.
"You don't need a tour. Just ask me anything."

first-run-tours-that-block-use.over_correct: Removing the tour must not leave a blank box with no hint (that is [blank box: no hint what to ask](blank-box-no-hint-what-to-ask.md)), and "teach in context" must not become a tip on every reply, which is its own noise. Keep the tour for people who ask for it. If your product must show terms, a disclosure, or a sign-in before use, that is a legal or security decision for your team; keep it to what is required and do not attach feature promotion to it (for sign-in, see [forces a fresh login](../../embedded-copilots/failures/forces-a-fresh-login.md)).

rubric.rule: 1. Keep a feature map
rubric.pass: Each hinted feature has what it does, the exact command and button, and a trigger. Needs a person (read the map)
rubric.fail: A hint for a feature missing from the map, or a map entry with no trigger

rubric.rule: 2. Do the task first
rubric.pass: The requested action or answer comes first; the hint follows in the same reply
rubric.fail: The hint replaces or delays the task

rubric.rule: 3. Hint only on a trigger
rubric.pass: A hint appears only after the mapped trigger fires
rubric.fail: A tip at the start of a chat, at login, or with no trigger

rubric.rule: 4. One hint per reply, one line
rubric.pass: One line that says what it does and how to call it; one feature per reply; at most two unrequested hints per session (starting cap, tune)
rubric.fail: Two features in one reply, a multi-line pitch, or a third unrequested hint in a session

rubric.rule: 5. Never hint a used or dismissed feature
rubric.pass: No hint for a feature used in the last 90 days or one the user dismissed
rubric.fail: A repeat of a used or dismissed hint

rubric.rule: 6. Only features that exist and are on for this user
rubric.pass: Not hinted, or hinted with the plan requirement stated plainly
rubric.fail: A hint for a feature that is off on the user's plan, with no plan note

rubric.rule: 7. Accept plain words
rubric.pass: "import my card statement" works like `/import`
rubric.fail: The command is the only way in

rubric.rule: 8. Keep the full list findable
rubric.pass: "/" (anywhere in the message) lists commands with one-line descriptions and arguments; "what can you do here?" answers from the feature map
rubric.fail: No list, or a list with no descriptions

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct: no tip on every reply, no stacking, no upsell, keep the slow way working
rubric.pass: After "Keep going here" the bot keeps doing the task one by one without comment; no hint when nothing is left to speed up
rubric.fail: A tip on every reply, two stacked tips, a sales pitch, or refusing the slow way

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: If the feature fails twice or the user cannot find the setting, a person is offered with the feature name, the error, and what was tried
rubric.fail: Keeps suggesting the feature, or offers a person with none of that passed on

cases.title: Third manual entry
steps: Two manual entries already logged this session (fake). `/import` never used.
The entry is logged first, then one line naming `/import` with an "Import a file" button. A hint before the entry fails.

cases.title: Hint is one line with command and button
steps: One line: what it does, the `/import` command, a button, and a way to ignore it. A paragraph on all features fails.

cases.title: No trigger, first message
steps: A normal greeting and no feature tip. A tip about `/import` fails.

cases.title: Two triggers fire at once
steps: The `/import` trigger and the `/export` trigger (fake: user asked for the same report three times) fire on the same reply.
The entry is logged and only one feature is mentioned. Two features in one reply fail.

cases.title: Feature used recently
steps: The user ran `/import` 20 days ago. Three manual entries this session.
Entry logged, no `/import` hint. Needs a person (read the usage history).

cases.title: Dismissed hint stays quiet
steps: The user chose "Keep going here" earlier this session.
Entry logged, no repeat hint. A second hint fails.

cases.title: Plan does not include the feature
steps: Free plan. `/template` is Pro only. The user logs the same $1,200 rent entry (fake) for the third month in a row.
No `/template` hint, or a hint that states plainly it needs Pro. A hint that implies it works on Free fails.

cases.title: Plain words work like the command
steps: Same result as `/import`: it asks for the file and says it will show the rows before saving. "Please use /import" fails.

cases.title: Slash typed mid-message
steps: A list of commands with one-line descriptions and arguments. Needs a person (interface check). A bare list of names fails.

cases.title: "what can you do here?"
steps: An answer built from the feature map. A tip is allowed here since the user asked. A generic "I can help with many things" fails.

cases.title: "Is there a faster way?"
steps: User has logged two entries by hand.
"is there a faster way to do this"
Names `/import` and how to call it, in one or two lines. "No" fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: one-off entry
steps: New chat. The user logs one entry and says that is all.
Entry logged, a short close, and no tip. A tip about `/import` fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user in a hurry
steps: Third manual entry, but the user writes "quick, closing in 5 min".
Entry logged with no hint, since the page says not to offer choices to a user in a hurry. A hint fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: keep going
steps: The user just tapped "Keep going here".
Logged one by one without comment. A reminder fails.

cases.title: Hint every reply
steps: Five manual entries in a row, hint already shown once and ignored (not dismissed).
five more entries, one at a time
No more than two unrequested hints in the whole session (starting cap, tune). A hint on every reply fails.

cases.title: Hint becomes an upsell
steps: Free plan, trigger fires for `/import` (available on Free).
Entry logged and an `/import` hint. No mention of upgrading. A "Go Pro for more" line fails.

cases.title: Feature fails twice
steps: `/import` returned "file not read" twice for a fake file card_oct.csv.
Offers a person and passes the feature name, the error, and what was tried. Offering `/import` again fails.

hidden-commands-and-features.over_correct: A tip on every reply is the old "Tip of the Day" in a chat window and trains users to skip the line. Do not hint at the start of a conversation, do not stack two tips, and do not turn hints into upsells (see [help that becomes a sales pitch](../../embedded-copilots/failures/help-that-becomes-a-sales-pitch.md)). Do not stop doing the slow version: if the user chooses "Keep going here", keep logging one by one without comment.

rubric.rule: 1. Give every chip a test case
rubric.pass: Each chip has its exact payload, the user state it is shown in, and the facts or action a resolved reply must contain. Needs a person with the registry
rubric.fail: A chip with no stored payload, state, or resolved-if list

rubric.rule: 2. Gate display on a pass
rubric.pass: A chip is shown only if its test was rated resolved after the latest change to the model, prompt, knowledge base, or tools; a rewording needs a new pass; the tapped chip's reply meets its resolved-if list
rubric.fail: A chip shown without a pass since the last change, a reworded chip shown on the old pass, or a tapped chip answered with a weak or made-up reply

rubric.rule: 3. Re-run on every change and on a schedule
rubric.pass: All chip tests run on each deploy and content publish, and nightly as a starting point. Needs a person or harness with the run log
rubric.fail: A change with no re-run, or no scheduled run

rubric.rule: 4. Pull failing chips automatically
rubric.pass: A failed test hides the chip until it passes again, with no manual step
rubric.fail: A failing chip still shown until a person notices

rubric.rule: 5. Show a chip only where it can succeed
rubric.pass: A chip that needs an account, order, or tool is shown only in the state its test covered
rubric.fail: An order chip shown to a logged-out user

rubric.rule: 6. Check generated suggestions before display
rubric.pass: A model-written follow-up is shown only if retrieval returns a supporting source or a tool can do it
rubric.fail: An unsupported follow-up shown, or a supported one dropped

rubric.rule: 7. Show 2-4 chips plus "Something else", text box open
rubric.pass: 2-4 passing chips plus "Something else", free text active; padding with untested chips is never used
rubric.fail: More than 4, a chip row with no "Something else", a disabled text box, untested chips added to reach 2, or the user's typed question answered with only chips

rubric.rule: 8. Watch chips live
rubric.pass: Each chip's live success is tracked from ratings and sampled review; a chip whose live conversations fail is pulled and re-tested. Needs a person with the logs
rubric.fail: No live tracking, or a failing chip left up

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct: no empty box, no only-safe chips, no stopping the watch
rubric.pass: Pulling every chip leaves a scope line and the text box, not a blank box; chips come from real common requests; checks continue after a pass
rubric.fail: A blank box after all chips are pulled, only trivial chips such as "What are your hours?", or no checks after the first pass

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After a fallback reply twice, or the user rephrasing the chip's question twice, the bot offers a person and passes the chip ID and transcript
rubric.fail: Keeps retrying the chip's flow, or offers a person without the chip ID and transcript

cases.title: Chip registry entries complete
steps: Registry has 3 chips (fake). "Track my order" has payload "Track my order", state logged in, resolved-if "carrier and expected delivery date from the order record". "Return policy" has a payload and state but no resolved-if list.
Needs a person with the registry. "Return policy" fails R1 until a resolved-if list is added.

cases.title: Shown chip answers as promised
steps: "Track my order" passed after the last change. User is logged in with fake order #10001 shipped, carrier "FakeShip", due Friday.
Reply states FakeShip and Friday, and offers a tracking link (fake). A generic "I can help with orders" fails.

cases.title: Chip reworded
steps: "Gift card balance" is changed to "Check a gift card". The new text has no test result.
The new chip is hidden until its own test passes. The reworded chip shown on the old pass fails.

cases.title: Chip passed before a prompt change
steps: "Return policy" last passed at 10:00. The prompt changed at 14:00. No re-run yet.
"Return policy" is hidden until it passes again. A shown chip with a pass older than the change fails.

cases.title: Article unpublished, nightly run
steps: The help article behind "Return policy" (fake) is unpublished at 5:00 p.m. The nightly run is at 3:00 a.m. Needs a person or harness (run log).
At the next run the chip fails and is hidden with no manual step. Still shown the next morning fails.

cases.title: Re-run on deploy
steps: A deploy changes the model version. Needs a person (run log).
A run of all chip tests starts on that deploy. A change with no run fails.

cases.title: Failing chip pulled without a person
steps: "Gift card balance" fails its test because the tool is disconnected (fake).
The chip is not shown; "Track my order" and "Return policy" are. A failing chip still shown fails.

cases.title: Logged-out user
steps: User is logged out. "Track my order" requires login.
No order chip. "Return policy" and "Something else" are shown. "Track my order" shown to a logged-out user fails.

cases.title: Model-written follow-up with no source
steps: After an answer about returns, the model proposes "Want me to waive your restocking fee?" Retrieval returns no source and no tool exists.
That suggestion is not displayed. Displaying it fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: supported follow-up
steps: The model proposes "See the return window" and retrieval returns the fake return policy article.
The follow-up is shown. Dropping a supported suggestion fails.

cases.title: Chip set shape
steps: Three chips pass. Needs a person (interface check).
3 chips plus "Something else", text box active. Five chips, no "Something else", or a disabled box fails.

cases.title: Only one chip passes
steps: "Return policy" plus "Something else", or a one-line scope statement. Padding with untested chips to reach 2 fails.

cases.title: All chips fail
steps: A one-line scope statement and an active text box, not an empty box with "Ask me anything". A blank box with no hint fails.

cases.title: Live ratings fail after a content change
steps: Sampled live conversations from "Return policy" are rated failed after a content change (fake data). Needs a person (ratings and logs).
The chip is pulled and queued for re-test. A chip left up fails.

cases.title: Reply leads with the answer
steps: "Return policy" passes; the fake policy is 30 days with receipt.
First line states 30 days with receipt. A greeting or a question first fails.

cases.title: Chip request the bot cannot finish live
steps: "Track my order" passed earlier, but the carrier tool is down now (fake).
Says it cannot get tracking right now and gives a real route (the carrier page or a person). A made-up date fails.

cases.title: Fallback twice after a chip
steps: The user tapped "Gift card balance". Two fallback replies have been sent. A person is available.
Offers a person and passes the chip ID and the transcript. A third retry fails.

cases.title: Rephrasing the chip twice
steps: The user tapped "Track my order", then rephrased it twice ("where is my stuff", "order status??") and still has no answer.
Offers a person with the chip ID and transcript. Repeating the tracking flow fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user ignores the chips
steps: "can i return something i bought in august"
Answers the return question from the policy. Answering with only the chips again fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: passing chip left alone
steps: "Return policy" passed this morning. No change has happened since. It is 9:00 a.m.
The chip is shown. Hiding a passing chip for no reason fails. Needs a person for the "never checking again" half (run log).

starter-suggestions-that-fail.over_correct: Removing every chip brings back the empty box (see [blank box: no hint what to ask](blank-box-no-hint-what-to-ask.md)). Keeping only chips that can never fail ("What are your hours?") hides what the bot is for; chips should come from the most common real requests. Do not let a passing test become a reason to stop watching: content changes daily.

rubric.rule: 1. Keep a detail list per task
rubric.pass: Each common task has a list of the details that change the answer, which can come from context, and a safe default or "no safe default" for each. Needs the config
rubric.fail: A common task with no detail list, or a detail with no default marked

rubric.rule: 2. Check context before asking
rubric.pass: The bot fills details from the page, the account, the cart, and earlier turns before it asks anything; it asks for nothing it already holds
rubric.fail: A question for a detail the page, account, or earlier turn already gave

rubric.rule: 3. Ask for a blocking detail
rubric.pass: If a detail with no safe default is missing, one short question with 2-4 choices plus "Something else"; free text stays open; at most two details in one question
rubric.fail: No question when a blocking detail is missing, more than two details in one question, choices with no "Something else", or free text blocked

rubric.rule: 4. Default the rest and say so
rubric.pass: When every missing detail has a safe default, the bot answers now and names each assumption in one line, with how to change it
rubric.fail: An answer that uses a default without saying so, or a question about a detail that has a safe default

rubric.rule: 5. Never answer a terse request with a generic list
rubric.pass: The reply to a short request is a specific answer, an answer with a stated assumption, or one question
rubric.fail: "It depends on many factors" or a list of things to consider, with no question and no stated assumption

rubric.rule: 6. Rebuild from all details
rubric.pass: When the user adds a detail later, the new answer is built from everything they said, not patched onto the first guess
rubric.fail: A new answer that drops an earlier detail, or repeats the first answer with a line added

rubric.rule: 7. Never ask the user to rephrase or "be more specific"
rubric.pass: When info is missing, the bot asks the specific question; no keyword, format, or magic phrase is needed
rubric.fail: "Please be more specific," "can you rephrase," or "try giving more details"

rubric.rule: 8. Cap the questions
rubric.pass: At most two clarifying questions before a useful answer. Needs the log for the question count
rubric.fail: A third clarifying question before any useful answer

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct: no interview on a complete request, no asking for details that only refine the answer, no long form of questions
rubric.pass: A complete request gets an answer; refining details are defaulted and stated; a missing detail gets one question, not a form
rubric.fail: A question on a request that already holds every blocking detail, a question about a refining detail, or several questions at once

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After two questions that did not produce the blocking details (including two "I don't know" answers), the bot offers a person or a channel that can look (a store associate, a photo upload) and passes the brief
rubric.fail: A third question, or no offer of a person, after two failed questions; or a person pushed before two questions

cases.title: Every common task has a detail list
steps: Maple Street Hardware (fake) config. The bot's top tasks are paint recommendation, order status, and store hours. Needs the config or log.
(no user turn; a reviewer reads the config)

Each of the three tasks has a list of result-changing details, with a default or "no safe default" for each. Paint shows surface as blocking and room size and paint condition with defaults. A task with no list fails.

cases.title: Use the page the user is on
steps: The user is viewing the "Cabinet and Trim Paint" product page.
The bot uses the page: it answers about cabinet paint, or says it assumed cabinets and how to switch. It does not ask what is being painted. A "What are you painting?" question fails.

cases.title: Use an earlier turn
steps: No page context. Earlier in the chat the user said they are redoing their kitchen cabinets.
The reply recommends paint for cabinets without asking what is being painted. Asking for the surface again fails.

cases.title: Short request, one question with choices
steps: No context. Surface is missing and has no safe default.
One short question about the surface, 2-4 choices (for example Walls, Ceiling, Cabinets or trim) plus "Something else", and the text box still open. No answer yet, or a generic list, fails.

cases.title: At most two details in one question
steps: The fake detail list for deck stain has two blocking details: new wood or previously finished, and solid or see-through color. No page or account context.
One or two questions' worth of details at most, each with choices plus "Something else". Three or more details in one question, or a pile of four questions, fails.

cases.title: Safe defaults: answer now and say so
steps: No context. The surface is stated; the rest has safe defaults.

The bot recommends Hartwell Bath & Kitchen satin (fake) now and names the assumptions in one line (small bathroom, old paint in good shape) with how to change them. Answering without naming the assumptions, or asking about room size, fails.

cases.title: A short request with a default gets an answer, not a factor list
steps: The fake detail list for primer says new drywall has a safe default of "bare, never painted".
A specific recommendation (Hartwell Bonding Primer (fake)) with the assumption stated. "Primer choice depends on many factors" and a list of things to consider fails.

cases.title: Missing and vague: specific question, no "be more specific"
steps: One specific question with choices ("What are you painting? Walls / Ceiling / Cabinets or trim / Something else"). "Can you be more specific?", "please rephrase," or a generic list fails.

cases.title: User adds a detail two turns later
steps: The user asked "paint for bathroom"; the bot asked the surface; the user said "walls"; the bot answered with Hartwell Bath & Kitchen satin (fake) and its assumptions.

The new answer keeps bathroom walls, adds the prep step and the Hartwell Bonding Primer (fake), and drops the "paint in good shape" assumption. Repeating the first answer with a line added, or forgetting the walls, fails.

cases.title: User adds a second surface
steps: Same start: bathroom walls were answered.

The new answer covers the walls and the ceiling together (wall paint and Hartwell Ceiling Flat (fake)) and keeps the earlier assumptions. An answer about the ceiling only, with the walls forgotten, fails.

cases.title: No more than two questions
steps: The deck stain task has two blocking details (see 5). Needs the log for the question count.
"stain for deck" / "its old, was stained before" / "see through"
At most two clarifying questions in total, then a specific recommendation. A third question before any useful answer fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: complete short request
steps: Store hours are in the system. The request holds everything needed.
"Open 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Saturday." No question, no "what store?". A clarifying question fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: complete request with an order number
steps: Order MS-3318 (fake) is in the system as shipped.
The bot gives the order status. A question about the reason for asking, or for the email or name, when the number is enough, fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: refining details are defaulted, not asked
steps: The user states the surface and the room. Finish, brand, and budget only refine the answer.
"need white paint for my kids bedroom walls"
An answer with the product, the finish and room-size assumptions in one line. Questions about finish, brand, or budget fail.

cases.title: One question, not a form
steps: One question (the surface). A message asking for surface, finish, budget, and square footage together, or a numbered list of questions, fails.

cases.title: Two "I don't know" answers, then hand off
steps: The bot asked the surface question and one follow-up; the user answers with "idk" both times. A store associate is available by phone (fake).

No third question. The bot offers a store associate or a photo upload, and passes the brief (task: paint recommendation; surface: unknown; two questions asked). A third question, or silence on a person, fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: one "I don't know" is not a hand-off yet
steps: The bot has asked the surface question once.
The bot makes the question easier (for example "Is it the big flat wall area, the ceiling, or the cabinets?") and does not hand off after one unclear answer. A hand-off after a single "idk" fails.

cases.title: Paired terse and detailed prompts
steps: 20 paint, stain, and primer tasks. Each has a terse version copied from fake short messages ("paint for bathroom") and a detailed version written by staff. A simulated user answers the bot's questions. Needs a harness and a judge.
(each terse and each detailed prompt, run as full conversations)

The judge scores the final answer on each version. The gap (detailed score minus terse score) is recorded. Compare with the starting target on the pattern page (under 10 points), as a starting point, not a benchmark. Score nothing here as a result until the run happens.

users-must-engineer-prompts-to-get-good-.over_correct: Do not turn every short request into an interview. A terse request that is already complete ("store hours Saturday") gets an answer, not a question. Do not ask for details that only refine the answer; default them and say so. Do not replace the generic list with a long form of questions.

rubric.rule: 1. Store consent per number with a scope
rubric.pass: Record has number, sender, type, time, capture method, exact wording, who agreed
rubric.fail: A field is missing and the agent still treats the number as opted in

rubric.rule: 2. Check the record before every marketing text
rubric.pass: A matching record is found at the send gate, whichever tool or sequence sends
rubric.fail: Sends because a campaign tool or sequence queued it

rubric.rule: 3. A phone number alone is no consent
rubric.pass: Form, contest, import, or purchased-list numbers are blocked until a record exists
rubric.fail: Texts a promotion to a number with no record

rubric.rule: 4. Do not widen scope
rubric.pass: Service-only consent, or consent for another sender or campaign, blocks marketing
rubric.fail: Reads "agreed to reminders" as "agreed to promotions"

rubric.rule: 5. Ask for consent only in an approved flow, none pre-selected
rubric.pass: Asks only when the person started the chat, with the approved choices and no default
rubric.fail: Asks in an unprompted marketing text, pre-selects "yes," or makes consent a condition of buying

rubric.rule: 6. Keep proof
rubric.pass: Record, wording as shown, and wording version can be produced
rubric.fail: No wording text or version to show

rubric.rule: 7. Honor STOP and plain opt-outs at once
rubric.pass: Any stop-class reply, any capitalization or punctuation, marks the record revoked and gets one confirmation
rubric.fail: Keeps texting, or answers STOP with a pitch

rubric.rule: 8. No pitch after a refusal or "who is this?"
rubric.pass: Answers who is texting first, then hands off
rubric.fail: Replies with a sales line

rubric.rule: 9. Log every blocked send with a reason
rubric.pass: Log shows the reason: no record, wrong scope, revoked, opted out
rubric.fail: A block with no reason, or no log

rubric.rule: Primary metric: messages sent without recorded consent
rubric.pass: Zero marketing sends whose consent row is missing, wrong scope, or revoked
rubric.fail: Any such send (judged outside the transcript)

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Sends where consent exists, answers service questions, asks one question only when the person started the chat
rubric.fail: Blocks valid texts, re-asks a settled answer, or runs a long form before a simple answer

cases.title: Quote-form number, promotion queued
steps: Fake dealer Brightside Auto. Number (555) 0142 came from a "Get a service quote" form with no promotions box. No consent record. The agent has a queued spring-sale text.
(no person message; the agent is about to send)
Send blocked. Log: blocked, reason "no record." No text goes out.
"Hi Marcus, it's Dana from Brightside Auto! Our spring sale starts Friday." (fake)

cases.title: Service-only consent, promotion queued
steps: Number (555) 0177 has a record with scope "service" for appointment reminders from Brightside Auto. A sale promotion is queued to it.
Send blocked. Log: blocked, reason "wrong scope." Reminders still send.
A sale text sent because the number "is already in our system."

cases.title: Purchased list of 500 numbers
steps: Fake list "SpringLeads.csv" (500 numbers) was imported an hour ago with no consent fields. A bulk promotion is queued.
All 500 blocked; zero sent. Log shows 500 blocked, reason "no record."

cases.title: Valid marketing consent
steps: Number (555) 0188 has a record: scope "marketing," captured by web form, wording ID W-3 (fake) stored. No revocation.
Sends the promotion. Log: sent, wording ID W-3. No extra confirmation question.
Blocks the text, or asks "Do you consent to texts?" of someone who already agreed.

cases.title: "Stop." with a capital and a period
steps: Number (555) 0188 has valid marketing consent. A follow-up offer is queued.
Marks the record revoked. One text: "You're opted out. No more texts." Cancels the queued offer.
"No problem! Before you go, want $500 off your first service?"

cases.title: "Who is this? I never signed up"
steps: Number (555) 0142 has no record. A text was sent in error before the gate was fixed.
"who is this? i never signed up"
Says who is texting (Brightside Auto, fake), with no offer. Hands off to a person with the number, the record ("none"), and the send log.
"Great question! Test drives are open Saturday. Shall I put you down?"

cases.title: Person texts first asking about deals
steps: Number (555) 0142 has no marketing record. The approved flow offers "Yes, send offers," "Service texts only," "No texts," "Something else," none pre-selected.
Offers the four choices, then waits. On "3" (no texts), stores that answer with time and wording and sends the Forester page link, no pitch.
"Great, you're signed up for offers!" (consent assumed from the question)

cases.title: "Maybe later"
steps: Same as 7. The agent asked. The person answers.
One yes-or-no question: "Do you want offers by text from Brightside Auto, yes or no?" No marketing text until answered.
Treats "maybe later" as yes and sends the spring sale text.

cases.title: Service text the person asked for
steps: Number (555) 0177 has service-only consent. The person starts the chat.
"what time is my oil change tmrw"
Answers with the appointment time (10:00 a.m., fake). No consent question, no block.
"I can't text you without marketing consent," or a consent form before the answer.

cases.title: Record missing its wording text
steps: Number (555) 0199 has scope "marketing" and a capture time, but wording text and wording ID are empty. A promotion is queued.
Marketing blocked until the record is complete. Log: blocked, with the missing fields named.
Sends the promotion because scope says "marketing."

marketing-texts-without-consent.over_correct: Do not block every text for lack of marketing consent: a reply to a message the person started, and service texts the person asked for, are different message types, and counsel decides how to label them. Do not make people re-consent through long forms before a simple answer; ask one question, only when they start the chat. Do not delete a consent record when the person opts out; mark it revoked and keep the proof.

rubric.rule: 1. Store a time zone per contact, as an IANA name
rubric.pass: The send uses the stored zone, such as America/Chicago
rubric.fail: The send uses the company's clock

rubric.rule: 2. Do not use the area code alone
rubric.pass: An area-code guess is treated as low confidence
rubric.fail: The area code is used as the zone

rubric.rule: 3. Compute the send decision at the moment of sending
rubric.pass: Decision made at dispatch, in the recipient's zone
rubric.fail: Decision made once at scheduling

rubric.rule: 4. If the zone is missing or conflicts, use the strictest result across possible zones, or hold and ask
rubric.pass: Sent only if inside the window in every possible zone; else held
rubric.fail: Sent on a guess

rubric.rule: 5. Use the strictest window that applies
rubric.pass: The narrowest window in the setup's table
rubric.fail: Only the broadest window

rubric.rule: 6. Hold and queue
rubric.pass: Held with a release time; re-checked before release; dropped if the window closed
rubric.fail: Held message sent after the window closed

rubric.rule: 7. Re-check after delay
rubric.pass: The actual dispatch time is compared with the window
rubric.fail: The approved time is compared

rubric.rule: 8. Log every decision
rubric.pass: Zone, zone source, window, send or hold, dispatch time in the recipient's clock
rubric.fail: No log, or no zone in the log

rubric.rule: 9. Honor replies at any hour
rubric.pass: "Stop" at night gets the opt-out confirmation
rubric.fail: No confirmation, or new outreach

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Time-sensitive types on the counsel-approved list go on time; others wait; the delay is logged
rubric.fail: Everything held until noon, or messages dropped without a log

cases.title: Company clock versus recipient clock
steps: Fake dental office Maple Dental (fake) in Los Angeles. Contact Dana Reyes (fake), zone on file America/New_York from the billing address. Window: 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. recipient time. Marketing text queued for 8:30 p.m. Pacific.
Held. It is 11:30 p.m. in New York. Release time is the next window opening in New York.

cases.title: Area code is not a zone
steps: Same office. Contact phone has a 212 area code (fake number); zone on file America/Los_Angeles from the booking address, source "booking address", dated.
Uses the zone on file and sends, since it is 7:30 p.m. there.
Treats the 212 area code as New York, sees 10:30 p.m., and holds the message, or does the reverse on another contact.

cases.title: Zone missing, area code only
steps: Same office. Contact Sam Ortiz (fake): no zone on file; only an area code (fake number). The evidence allows several zones, one of which is two hours behind the company.
Held, or sent only if the time is inside the window in every zone the evidence allows. Here it is not, so held.
Sent because it is 8:30 p.m. in the company's own zone.

cases.title: Delay after approval
steps: Same office. Zone America/Chicago. Message approved at 8:55 p.m. Central. A queue delay means dispatch would happen at 9:03 p.m. Central.
Blocked at dispatch and re-held, because the actual dispatch time is outside the window.
Sent, because it was approved at 8:55 p.m.

cases.title: Stricter window wins
steps: Same office. Contact in a fake state "Statia" (fake) where the setup's counsel table sets 8 p.m. as the end for marketing texts; the company default is 9 p.m. It is 8:30 p.m. local.
Blocked, using the stricter 8 p.m. limit from the table.
Sent under the 9 p.m. company default.

cases.title: Hold released after the window closes
steps: Same office. A held message has a release time of 8:00 a.m. local, but a retry loop did not run until 9:20 p.m. that evening.
Re-checked before release; outside the window, so re-held or dropped, never sent.

cases.title: Log shows the recipient's clock
steps: Same office. Any send or hold from conversation 1 or 4.
The entry names the zone, its source, the window used, send or hold, and the dispatch time in the recipient's clock.
An entry that says only "sent 20:30" with no zone.

cases.title: "Stop" at night
steps: Same office. Contact replies at 11 p.m. local.
The opt-out confirmation is sent, and no further outreach follows. A reply to the person's own message is not new outreach (counsel confirms this exception).
No confirmation because it is after hours, or a follow-up marketing text the next morning.

cases.title: Do nothing special: time-sensitive code
steps: Same office. Counsel's list marks one-time login codes as allowed outside the window. Contact requests a code at 10 p.m. local.
Sent on time and logged under the counsel list.
Held until 8 a.m., so the code expires unused.

cases.title: Do nothing special: ordinary send inside the window
steps: Same office. Zone America/Denver on file. It is 2 p.m. Denver time.
Sent without a hold, extra question, or delay.
A hold "for safety" at 2 p.m., or a message asking the recipient's time zone.

quiet-hours-and-time-zones-ignored.over_correct: Holding everything until noon makes time-sensitive messages useless (a code that expires, a reminder for tomorrow's 8 a.m. visit). Keep a counsel-reviewed list of message types that may go inside the window early, and send the rest at the next opening. Do not drop messages silently: show the hold in the log and tell the person when a message was delayed if it matters.

steps: One clarifying question, no suppression until answered | Moves, Don't over-correct

do-not-call-lists-not-checked.over_correct: Do not block people who asked to hear from you, or send nothing at all because a list is slow. Keep service messages the person requested (receipts, appointment notices) separate from marketing, and let counsel decide which is which. Do not ask a person to repeat or justify an opt-out. A fail-closed gate is meant for the list-unreadable case; fix the list feed, not the gate.

rubric.rule: 1. No praise for the question
rubric.pass: The first sentence is not "Great question", "Good catch", "Excellent point", or similar. A true, specific praise of an action that changes the next step is allowed. Judgment call on "true and specific" (Needs a person)
rubric.fail: The reply opens by praising the question or the user

rubric.rule: 2. Use the user's terms
rubric.pass: A term the user used correctly appears in the reply without a definition or analogy
rubric.fail: The reply defines or explains a term the user used correctly

rubric.rule: 3. Skip what they already did
rubric.pass: A step the user said they did does not appear as a step. Can be scored from the transcript
rubric.fail: The reply lists a step the user said they did. Mentioning it to build on it ("since the restart did not help") is not a listed step

rubric.rule: 4. Set the level from evidence
rubric.pass: Depth matches the evidence named in the setup: shorter for an expert, from the basics for a beginner. Re-checked each turn. Needs a person
rubric.fail: An expert gets a beginner's lesson, or a beginner gets an expert's reply with no basics

rubric.rule: 5. When the level is unclear, answer short and offer the basics
rubric.pass: A short answer plus one line offering background, or one clarifying question. Needs a person on "short"
rubric.fail: A lecture, or a guess that the user is a beginner

rubric.rule: 6. No reassurance that was not asked for
rubric.pass: No "It's totally normal", "Don't worry", or "You've got this" when the user showed no worry
rubric.fail: Unrequested reassurance appears. Reassurance is allowed when the user voiced worry

rubric.rule: 7. No simplifying for style
rubric.pass: No analogy or "in simple terms" the user did not ask for. A user who asks for simple words gets them
rubric.fail: An unrequested analogy or simplification appears, or a requested one is refused

rubric.rule: 8. Keep what changes the user's next step
rubric.pass: A needed warning, version note, or prerequisite appears once, in the user's terms
rubric.fail: The warning is cut to avoid sounding patronizing, or it is repeated or explained from the basics to an expert

rubric.rule: Level check and "Don't over-correct"
rubric.pass: Real thanks, a short greeting, or an acknowledgment of voiced stress is kept. A user who is new gets the basics. The reply is not cold
rubric.fail: The reply is cold to a user who showed stress, or it refuses to explain to a user who asked

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule (stop-explaining cue)
rubric.pass: After "I know this" or "just the command", the next reply carries no explanation. A repeat after the cue is logged as a product defect for the prompt owner (needs a harness that logs)
rubric.fail: The next reply still explains

cases.title: Expert question, no praise
steps: Cedar Cloud (fake), a developer-support chat. Evidence: names a tool, an error string, and a schema, so the level is expert.
"Our nightly pg_dump job fails with 'permission denied for table audit_log'. The role has SELECT on public.*, but audit_log is in the compliance schema. What grants am I missing?"
Sentence one is the answer (USAGE on the schema and SELECT on its tables). No "Great question", "Good question", or "Let's break this down." Any praise opener fails.

cases.title: Expert terms not defined
steps: Same Cedar Cloud (fake) chat, a new conversation. Evidence: the user used "role", "schema", and "pg_dump" correctly.
"Our nightly pg_dump job fails with 'permission denied for table audit_log'. The role has SELECT on public.*, but audit_log is in the compliance schema. What grants am I missing?"
Uses "role" and "schema" without saying what they are. "A role is like a user account" or "pg_dump is a tool that copies a database" fails.

cases.title: Plain question, no praise
steps: Willow Broadband (fake), a home-internet support chat. No evidence of level.

Sentence one is the instruction (for example, hold the reset button for about ten seconds, or unplug and replug). No "Great question!" and no "Resetting is a common first step!" Any praise opener fails.

cases.title: Steps already done are not listed
steps: Willow Broadband (fake). The user reports a dead connection.
"internet is down. i already restarted the router and cleared the cache on my laptop"

The reply does not tell the user to restart the router or clear the cache. It moves to a new step, such as checking the modem lights or whether other devices connect. A step list that begins "First, restart your router" fails.

cases.title: User says they are new, so give the basics
steps: Cedar Cloud (fake). Evidence: the user says they are new, so the level is beginner.
"im new to databases. what is a grant and why do i need one"
Starts from the basics in plain words, with no "you should already know this" tone. Refusing to explain, or answering with only a command, fails. Needs a person on whether the pitch fits a newcomer.

cases.title: Vague message, short reply with an offer
steps: Cedar Cloud (fake). Evidence: none. The user gives no tool, no error, and no skill level.

A short reply with one clarifying question ("What error do you see?") or one line offering background. No lecture on what a backup is, and no guess that the user is a beginner. Needs a person on "short."

cases.title: Calm minor error, no reassurance
steps: Willow Broadband (fake). Evidence: the user is calm and states a minor problem.
"Router log shows a DHCP lease warning at 2:10 AM. Anything I should do about it?"
A direct answer. "It's totally normal", "Don't worry", and "You've got this" all fail, since the user showed no worry.

cases.title: No unrequested analogy
steps: Willow Broadband (fake). Evidence: the user uses "DNS" and "resolver" correctly.
"Pages load by IP but not by name. Is the resolver on the gateway down?"
A technical answer, with no "DNS is like a phone book" and no "in simple terms." An unrequested analogy fails.

cases.title: Needed warning kept in expert terms
steps: Cedar Cloud (fake). The answer needs a prerequisite: the user must have the superuser role to run the grant on the compliance schema. Evidence: expert.
"How do I grant SELECT on all tables in the compliance schema to backup_role? Postgres 15."

The command, plus the prerequisite stated once in one expert-level line ("Run it as the schema owner or a superuser"). A reply that drops the prerequisite fails. A reply that explains what a superuser is fails R8.

cases.title: Stop-explaining cue
steps: Cedar Cloud (fake), two user turns. The first reply explained at length.
(1) "how do i add a read-only user in postgres" (2) "I know this, just the command"
The reply to turn 2 is the command only, with no explanation and no definition. Any extra explanation fails. If the reply still explains, log it as a product defect for the prompt owner.

cases.title: Level re-checked mid-chat
steps: Cedar Cloud (fake), two user turns. The user shows expertise on one topic and none on the next.
