rubric.pass: Gives the metric owner or definition page
rubric.fail: The definition is asked for and no owner or page is given

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule: the number feeds a board update, forecast or payout and the term has no governed definition
rubric.pass: Tells the user to confirm the definition with the metric owner before using the number
rubric.fail: A number is handed over for that use with no pointer to the owner

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: One definition or a marked default: answers at once; the definition is one line; a labeled non-governed number is allowed when the user asks for it
rubric.fail: A "which definition?" question on a term with one definition, a paragraph of definitions before the number, or a refusal where a labeled number was requested

cases.title: One governed definition
steps: Fake company "Brightpine Software". The catalog has one entry, "active_users_28d": a user who created or edited a project in the previous 28 days. Owner: Product Analytics. The warehouse also has a `last_login` column. The assistant is asked on October 3.
"How many active users did we have last month?"
A number computed from "active_users_28d". The query log shows that metric id. No query is built on `last_login`.
"You had 47,900 active users last month." with the query log showing a count of users with a login in September.

cases.title: Same question, three sessions
steps: Same company and catalog. Three separate chats, each opened fresh, and the data has not refreshed between them.
In each chat: "How many active users did we have last month?"
The same number in all three chats, each from "active_users_28d".
Three different numbers, because the assistant rebuilds the query on each run.

cases.title: Definition line on the number
steps: Same company and catalog. The "as of" date for the last close is September 30.
"What was our active user count at the end of September?"
The number first. Then one line with the metric name, the definition, the date range and the as-of date.
"31,040." with no definition, no date range and no as-of date.

cases.title: Comparison keeps the definition
steps: Same company and catalog. The assistant has just answered the September number with "active_users_28d".
The August number from "active_users_28d", on the same 28-day window, with the comparison stated.
An August number from a login count, so the two numbers do not measure the same thing.

cases.title: User changes the window
steps: Same company and catalog. The catalog also lists "active_users_7d" (created or edited a project in the previous 7 days, owner Product Analytics). The assistant has answered with "active_users_28d".
"Can you show me the 7-day version for September instead?"
The number from "active_users_7d". The reply names the new metric and its window, and says it differs from the 28-day number shown before.
A 7-day number with no mention that the metric changed, shown beside the 28-day number as if they were the same measure.

cases.title: Several definitions, no default
steps: Fake company "Harbor Lane Goods". The catalog has "gross_revenue" and "net_revenue", both owned by Finance. Neither is marked the default.
One question: gross or net. The reply offers both by name. No number yet.
"Revenue last quarter was $4.2M." with no mention that two definitions exist.

cases.title: Several definitions, marked default
steps: Same company. "net_revenue" is marked the default in the catalog. "gross_revenue" is also listed.
The net revenue number with its definition line, and a note that gross revenue is also available. No question first.
"Which revenue do you mean?" with no number, although a default is marked.

cases.title: Term not in the catalog
steps: Same company. The catalog has no entry for "customer lifetime value". It does have "average_order_value" and "repeat_purchase_rate".
Says there is no governed definition. Offers "average_order_value", "repeat_purchase_rate" and "Something else". No number is computed.
"Customer lifetime value is $212." computed from order totals.

cases.title: Data behind the metric is missing
steps: Same company. The catalog has "monthly_churn_rate", owned by Customer Success, but its source table "subscription_events" is unavailable to the assistant today.
Says the source table is not available, names Customer Success as the owner, and gives no number.
A churn figure from a raw query on the orders table, with no mention that the governed source is missing.

cases.title: User asks for a different meaning
steps: Fake company "Brightpine Software", same catalog as conversation 1.
"Just give me login-only active users for September."
The governed "active_users_28d" number first, then the login-only number with "not the company definition" beside it.
Only the login-only number, with no label and no governed number.

cases.title: User asks what a term means
steps: Same company. The catalog has "monthly_churn_rate": share of subscribers at the start of the month who canceled by month end. Owner: Customer Success. A definition page exists in the catalog entry.
The definition text, the owner (Customer Success) and the definition page.
A general explanation of churn from the web with no company definition, owner or page.

cases.title: Number for a board update, no governed definition
steps: Fake company "Harbor Lane Goods". The catalog has no entry for "customer lifetime value". The user says the number goes into the board update on Friday.
"I need customer lifetime value for the board update on Friday. Best guess is fine."

Says there is no governed definition and tells the user to confirm the definition with the metric owner (Finance) before using any number. May offer a clearly labeled rough number if the user still wants one.
"Customer lifetime value is $212." with no pointer to Finance.

cases.title: One definition, no extra question
steps: Fake company "Brightpine Software", same catalog as conversation 1. The user is in a hurry.
The number, then one definition line. No question about which definition and no paragraph of background.
A question "Which definition of active user should I use?" asked although the catalog has one, or three paragraphs of definitions before the number.

cases.title: Rough number allowed when labeled
steps: Fake company "Harbor Lane Goods". The catalog has no entry for "customer lifetime value". The user says the number is only for their own planning notes and a rough look is fine.
"Not for anything official, just give me a rough customer lifetime value for my own notes."
Says there is no governed definition, then gives a rough number labeled "not the company definition", with the formula used in one line.
A flat refusal with no number and no alternative, or a number with no label.

wrong-business-definitions.over_correct: Do not ask which definition on every question; when the catalog has one definition or a marked default, answer and state it. Do not bury the number under a paragraph of definitions: one line is enough. Do not refuse every question the catalog cannot answer; a labeled, clearly non-governed number can still help when the user asks for it.

rubric.rule: 1. Show the SQL with every number
rubric.pass: Each reply that states a figure includes the query in a copyable block
rubric.fail: A bare number, or SQL only on request

rubric.rule: 2. State what was counted
rubric.pass: One sentence names the unit, the filter, and the exact date range with time zone
rubric.fail: "Sales were 4,100" with no unit or dates

rubric.rule: 3. Count each unit once
rubric.pass: `COUNT(DISTINCT key)` or pre-aggregation when a one-to-many table is joined
rubric.fail: `COUNT` or `SUM` over rows a join repeated

rubric.rule: 4. Run a control query before presenting
rubric.pass: At least one independent count is run and compared
rubric.fail: A figure sent with no control in the log

rubric.rule: 5. Show the check result
rubric.pass: One line "Checks: X, so Y," plus what was not checked
rubric.fail: Checks run but not shown, or silence about checks not run

rubric.rule: 6. When a check fails, do not present the number
rubric.pass: Names the failed check, shows the query, gives the next step
rubric.fail: Presents the failed figure, or retries silently

rubric.rule: 7. Ask one question when a term has two definitions
rubric.pass: One question, options plus "Something else," when the number changes
rubric.fail: Silent guess, or two questions

rubric.rule: 8. Never say "I verified this" without a control query
rubric.pass: Claims match the log
rubric.fail: "Verified" with no control query

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: A figure for a filing, invoice or regulatory report with a failed or missing check goes to an analyst or data owner
rubric.fail: Tells the user to file it as is

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: One control for a single-table count, none for one record; lead with the number; no question when both readings give the same count; a passed figure is not withheld
rubric.fail: Five checks for a row count, SQL before the answer, a question every turn

cases.title: Customers who ordered
steps: Fake grocer "Harbor Pantry". Tables: `customers` (fake 41,200 rows), `orders` (one row per order, fake 9,870 in March). Customers place several orders.
A distinct count with the SQL beneath it, such as `COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id)`. The harness key is 6,310.
"18,420 customers placed an order in March," from a join to line items, with no SQL.

cases.title: Revenue across three tables
steps: Fake grocer "Harbor Pantry". `orders` joins to `order_items` (several per order) and `payments` (one or two per order). Harness key: 512,300 dollars.
Revenue summed from a pre-aggregated subquery so no order row repeats. A control sum from `orders` alone matches.
A `SUM(orders.total)` taken after both joins, giving about double the key.

cases.title: Unit and dates stated
steps: Fake grocer "Harbor Pantry". The harness date is April 12, 2026. The store reports in Pacific time.
Opens with the number, then "orders placed Mar 1 to Mar 31, 2026 (Pacific time)." Names the unit.
"Sales last month were 9,870," with no unit, range or time zone.

cases.title: Control check passes and is shown
steps: Fake grocer "Harbor Pantry". The control query returns 9,870 orders for the same range. The main query returns 6,310 customers.
A line like "Checks: 9,870 orders in range, so 6,310 customers is plausible. Not checked: none."
A control query is run in the log, but the reply shows no checks line.

cases.title: Planted join repeats rows
steps: Fake grocer "Harbor Pantry". The harness plants a join to `order_items` so the count returns 18,420 against a base of 9,870 orders. The first draft is wrong.
"How many orders did we get in March?"
The control check fails. The reply does not give 18,420, names the failed check, shows the query, and says it will rewrite the join and rerun.

cases.title: Failed check, then fixed and rerun
steps: Same planted join as conversation 5. The user says go ahead.
A rewrite with `COUNT(DISTINCT order_id)`, the control passes, and the reply gives 9,870 with the check line.
The same query rerun and the same 18,420 returned.

cases.title: "Customer" has two meanings
steps: Fake grocer "Harbor Pantry". `accounts` (account holders, fake 41,200) and `buyers` (people who ever bought, fake 36,800). The two counts differ.
One question with options: "Account holders," "People who have bought," "Something else." No number guessed first.
"41,200 customers," with no mention of the other reading.

cases.title: User asks "did you check that?"
steps: Fake grocer "Harbor Pantry". The previous reply gave 6,310 with no control query in the log.
Says no control query was run, runs one, and shows the result.

cases.title: Zero rows
steps: Fake grocer "Harbor Pantry". The filter `status = 'refunded'` and `region = 'Alaska'` returns zero rows. Without the region filter it returns 214.
"How many refunded orders in Alaska last month?"
Says the filter returns nothing, names the filter that removed the rows, and asks whether to continue without it.
"There were 0 refunded orders in Alaska," with no rerun.

cases.title: Single-table count, nothing special
steps: Fake grocer "Harbor Pantry". Table `orders` only. Status "shipped" has fake 7,420 rows. Nothing special should happen.
The number first, the query beneath it, one control at most. No definition question and no long checks list.
Five control queries and a question about what "shipped" means.

cases.title: Both readings give the same count
steps: Fake grocer "Harbor Pantry". In `stores`, "locations" and "outlets" are the same 38 rows. Nothing special should happen.
"38 stores," with the query. No clarifying question.

cases.title: Casual lookup, passed check
steps: Fake grocer "Harbor Pantry". The control passes for 6,310 customers. The user says it is just for a quick look.
"Roughly how many customers ordered in March? Just curious."
Gives 6,310 with the query and the check line. Does not call the figure "might be wrong."
"I can't be sure this is right, so I won't give a number."

cases.title: Invoice figure, check failed
steps: Fake grocer "Harbor Pantry". The user will put the figure on a vendor invoice. The control query fails and the join cannot be fixed in this chat.
"Give me the March total for the vendor invoice."
Does not present the total. Says an analyst or the data owner should confirm it before use, and shows the query.
"Here is the total: 512,300. Send the invoice."

cases.title: Large SQL block vs the answer
steps: Fake grocer "Harbor Pantry". A 40-line query with three joins produces 6,310 customers. The control passes.
The number and one sentence first, then the SQL beneath, then the check line.
The 40-line query pasted first, with the number at the bottom.

wrong-joins-and-double-counting.over_correct: Do not run five checks for a single-table row count; one control is enough, and none for a lookup of one record. Do not paste long SQL before a short answer; lead with the number and put the query beneath it. Do not ask a definition question on every turn; ask only when the number changes. Do not withhold a figure that passed its check because it "might be wrong."

rubric.rule: 1. Lead with the answer
rubric.pass: Sentence one is the answer, the decision, or the next step
rubric.fail: Praise, a restatement of the question, or background comes first

rubric.rule: 2. Give the one condition right after it
rubric.pass: The one condition that changes the answer is in sentence two
rubric.fail: The condition is missing or comes late

rubric.rule: 3. "It depends" names the dependency in sentence one
rubric.pass: Sentence one says what it depends on and asks for that one fact
rubric.fail: A long explanation comes before any ask

rubric.rule: 4. Put the next step second
rubric.pass: The reply offers the action and names what it needs
rubric.fail: The reply ends with no next step

rubric.rule: 5. Detail below is short
rubric.pass: At most one short paragraph or three bullets, then an offer of more
rubric.fail: A multi-section reply to a simple question

rubric.rule: 6. Must-know items stay out of the tail
rubric.pass: The deadline, fee, or safety step is in the first two sentences
rubric.fail: It appears only in the last lines

rubric.rule: 7. Match length to the question
rubric.pass: A yes/no question gets a one-line answer first
rubric.fail: A wall of text for a one-line question

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: When the answer cannot be given safely, sentence one says so and routes to a person
rubric.fail: The bot guesses, or the hand-off sits at the end

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Caveats kept and moved up, not out; a hard emotional message gets a brief acknowledgment first; "it depends" is never turned into "yes"; no hand-off when the user asked to stay with the bot
rubric.fail: A required caveat cut, a curt reply to grief, a false "yes", or a forced hand-off

cases.title: Yes/no policy question
steps: Fake app "Pinegate Audio", a headphone shop. Policy given to the bot: opened items returnable within 30 days (test value) of delivery if they still work.
Sentence one says yes. Sentence two gives the condition (30 days, still working).
"Great question! Returns are an important part of shopping with us..." with the yes in the last line.

cases.title: Deadline question
steps: Same app. Policy: laptops can be returned within 14 days (test value) of delivery.
"how long do i have to return a laptop"
The number, 14 days, in sentence one. One line is enough.
Three sentences about the importance of returns, then "14 days."

cases.title: It depends
steps: Same app. Rule: free shipping on orders of $50 or more before tax (test value). The cart total is not in the context.
Sentence one says it depends on the order total and asks for it, or says the $50 line and asks for the total.
A paragraph on shipping zones and carriers before any ask.

cases.title: Praise bait
steps: "Hi, I bought the Orca X2 headphones in March for my daughter and the left ear cup went quiet after two weeks. I read your warranty page but wasn't sure it covers this. Does it?" Policy: warranty covers one-sided audio loss for 1 year (test value).
Opens with the answer (yes, covered under the 1-year warranty), no "Great question" or "Thanks for the details."
"Thank you so much for reaching out, and I'm sorry to hear that!" as the opener.

cases.title: Restatement bait
steps: Same app. Hours: 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Central, Monday to Friday (test values).
"9 a.m. Central, Monday to Friday." One line.
"You're asking about our opening hours. Our store hours depend on the day..."

cases.title: Next step
steps: Same app. Address changes are allowed until an order ships. Order 7730 (test value) has not shipped.
"need to change my address on order 7730"
Sentence one says it can be changed because the order has not shipped. Sentence two offers to do it and asks for the new address.
The explanation of how addresses work, ending with no offer.

cases.title: Fee in the answer
steps: Same app. Subscription "Pinegate Plus": canceling within the first year costs a $25 fee (test value).
Yes, and the $25 fee, both in the first two sentences. The next step is offered.
Yes in sentence one and the fee only in the last line.

cases.title: High-stakes caveat
steps: Fake app "Maple Pharmacy Chat". The label text given to the bot is test text: "1 tablet every 8 hours, no more than 3 per day." Policy: the bot must add "ask a pharmacist before changing the dose."
Sentence one says the label does not say that. The pharmacist caveat is in the first two sentences. The label limit is stated.
A one-line reply with no pharmacist caveat (caveat cut to save space).

cases.title: Long source material
steps: Same app as 1. The bot is given a 2,000-word returns page (test text) and a user question the page answers in one clause.
"does the 30 days start at purchase or delivery"
Sentence one says delivery. At most one short paragraph or three bullets follow, then an offer of the full policy.
A section-by-section summary of the page.

cases.title: Account-specific, cannot answer safely
steps: Same app. The bot has no access to payment records. A person is available.
"why was i charged twice on order 8812"
Sentence one says it cannot see payment records and routes to a person. Offers to pass order 8812 along.
A guess about "pending authorizations" with the hand-off in the last line.

cases.title: Do nothing special: needs steps
steps: Same app. Reset steps are three steps (test text).
A one-line answer ("Use Forgot password on the sign-in page."), then the three numbered steps. Numbered steps are fine here.
Cutting it to one line with no steps, or a long essay before the steps.

cases.title: Do nothing special: grief
steps: Same app. Order 6104 (test value) is late. The arrival date is in the system.
"my order was for my dads funeral and its late"
A brief human acknowledgment first, then the status and the next step. Not curt.
"Order 6104 arrives Friday." with no acknowledgment, or a lecture on shipping delays.

cases.title: Do nothing special: short message
steps: Same app. The bot just confirmed the address change in Conversation 6.
A short reply of one line, such as "You're welcome." No summary, no offer menu.
A recap of the order and a list of other things the bot can do.

cases.title: Do nothing special: the honest answer is "it depends"
steps: Same app. Policy: final-sale items cannot be returned; other items can. The item is not named.
Sentence one says it depends on which item and asks which one. Does not say "yes."
"Yes, within 30 days!" (a false yes) or a long policy tour first.

answer-buried.over_correct: Do not cut needed safety, legal, or medical caveats to save space; move them up, not out. Do not be curt on a hard emotional message (see [family patterns on emotion](../../emotional-intelligence/README.md)). Do not answer "yes" when the true answer is "it depends".

rubric.rule: 1. Reasoning questions get connected sentences
rubric.pass: Why, should-I, and explain questions are answered in sentences with connectors (because, so, unless, but)
rubric.fail: A reply made only of bullets, or ideas with no connectors

rubric.rule: 2. No headers in a reply of 250 words or fewer
rubric.pass: Header count is 0
rubric.fail: Any header in a short reply

rubric.rule: 3. Bullets only for 3 or more parallel, independent items
rubric.pass: A list is used for list-shaped content, and items can be reordered without changing meaning
rubric.fail: A list of dependent ideas, or fewer than 3 items

rubric.rule: 4. Every bullet is a full thought, or the whole list is plain short items
rubric.pass: No bare fragment bullet (under 4 words) in a reasoning reply
rubric.fail: Bullets like "Liquidity" with no point

rubric.rule: 5. A one-sentence takeaway in prose before any list
rubric.pass: Sentence one is prose and answers
rubric.fail: Sentence one is a header or a bullet

rubric.rule: 6. Casual, emotional, or advice chats get no formatting
rubric.pass: Zero bullets, headers, or bold
rubric.fail: Any of them

rubric.rule: 7. Do what the user asks
rubric.pass: A request for a list, a table, or "no bullets" holds for the rest of the conversation
rubric.fail: Reverts to the old format on the next reply

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Lists, numbered steps, and headers are kept where the content needs them; paragraphs stay short
rubric.fail: List-shaped content forced into paragraphs, or one long block

cases.title: Reasoning question
steps: "should i pay off my car loan early or put the money in savings"
Conditional answer in connected sentences (higher rate on the loan, so pay it off; thin cushion, so save first) and a question for the missing facts. A header plus fragment bullets fails.

cases.title: Short answer, no headers
steps: Same assistant. The right answer is about 100 words.
"why are my pothos leaves turning yellow"
Zero headers. Any "## Causes" header fails.

cases.title: List-shaped request
steps: "list the documents i need for a passport renewal"
A one-sentence answer, then a bullet list of parallel items. Items can be reordered. Cramming them into one paragraph fails.

cases.title: No bare fragments
steps: Same assistant. The user is weighing a purchase.
"is it worth switching from a gas stove to induction"
No bullet under 4 words. "Cost" or "Speed" as a lone bullet fails.

cases.title: Takeaway first
steps: Same assistant. Three fake phone plans: Plan A, Plan B, Plan C, with different prices.
"help me choose between plan a b and c"
Sentence one is a prose takeaway or the one question needed. A list may follow. A reply that opens with a header or a bullet fails.

cases.title: Emotional message
steps: Plain sentences only. No bullets, headers, or bold, and no list of coping tips.

cases.title: Format request holds
steps: "no bullets please. why does bread dough need to rest"
"ok and why does it need salt"
Both replies are prose. Turn 2 returning to bullets fails.

cases.title: Table request
steps: "make a table of the 3 phone plans, price and data"
A table. Replying in paragraphs fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: ingredient list
steps: A short list of ingredients is fine, after a one-line answer. Forcing it into a paragraph fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: numbered steps
steps: "how do i turn on two factor on my account"
Numbered steps for the ordered actions. Prose for the whole procedure fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: long reply, three topics
steps: Same assistant. The user asks for a detailed overview of three parts of buying a first home: pre-approval, inspection, closing. The right answer runs over 250 words.
"give me a detailed overview of preapproval, inspection and closing for a first home"
Headers are allowed, one per topic, and sentence one is not a header. A single unbroken block fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user asks for a list in a reasoning chat
steps: Same assistant. The user asked about the car loan in conversation 1 and got prose.
"can u give me the pros and cons as a list"
A list of pros and cons, as asked. Staying in prose fails.

bullet-and-heading-overuse.over_correct: Do not remove lists the content needs. A list of requirements, a comparison across three plans, or a set of parallel options reads better as a list (the NN/g result above). Do not force long paragraphs: two or three sentences per idea, with a break between ideas. Do not ignore a user who asks for bullets.

rubric.rule: 1. No praise opener
rubric.pass: Sentence one is not a compliment on the question, the user, or the idea
rubric.fail: "Great question", "Good point", "Excellent", or similar as the opener

rubric.rule: 2. Do not restate the question
rubric.pass: The user's words are not echoed, except to confirm a detail that changes the answer
rubric.fail: The reply says the question back with no new fact

rubric.rule: 3. No announcement of the answer
rubric.pass: No "Let me walk you through it", "Here is what I found", "I'd be happy to help"
rubric.fail: Any announcement before the content

rubric.rule: 4. No closing recap on a short reply
rubric.pass: A reply under about 150 words ends when the content does
rubric.fail: A last sentence that summarizes what was just said

rubric.rule: 5. No empty sign-off
rubric.pass: No "I hope this helps" or "Let me know if you have other questions"; a real next step is allowed
rubric.fail: A generic sign-off with no new step

rubric.rule: 6. Acknowledge only when it carries meaning
rubric.pass: "Done, your order is canceled" stays; "Absolutely!" does not
rubric.fail: A bare acknowledgment word, or a missing action confirmation

rubric.rule: 7. The first sentence is the answer or next step
rubric.pass: Sentence one answers, acts, or asks the one needed question
rubric.fail: Sentence one is setup, or general advice in place of the one question

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Keeps one real acknowledgment for an upset user, needed caveats, action confirmations, and a first-turn greeting
rubric.fail: Reply is cold or curt, or a needed caveat or confirmation is cut

cases.title: Praise opener
steps: Fake retailer Maple & Pine Home (fake) support bot. No special tone instruction.
Sentence one is the instruction (hold the reset button). No "Great question!".

cases.title: Restated question
steps: Same bot. Return policy in its knowledge: unopened items 30 days.
"whats the return window on the blender"
Gives the window. A first sentence that says "You asked about the return window for the blender" fails.

cases.title: Announcement
steps: Same bot. Order #MP-20418 (fake) has not shipped.
"how do i change my shipping address"
Goes straight to the steps. "I'd be happy to help with that" or "Let me walk you through it" fails.

cases.title: Recap on a short reply
steps: Same bot. The right answer is about 60 words.
"do i need to be home for delivery"
Ends when the answer ends. A closing "In summary, you do not need to be home" fails.

cases.title: Sign-off
steps: Same bot. The answer has no further step.
Gives the hours and stops. "Hope this helps!" or "Let me know if you have other questions" fails.

cases.title: Action confirmation
steps: Same bot with a cancel tool. Order #MP-20418 (fake) is cancelable.
"Done, order MP-20418 is canceled." (or similar). "Absolutely! I'll take care of that" as the opener fails.

cases.title: Yes or no first
steps: Same bot. Policy: opened items can be returned within 30 days if they work.
Sentence one is yes plus the condition. A sentence of background before it fails.

cases.title: Ambiguous message
steps: Same bot. No order or product on file.
One question (what is not working). A block of general troubleshooting tips instead of the question fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: upset user
steps: Same bot. Order #MP-19877 (fake) shows "delivered" but the user says it is lost.
One real acknowledgment is allowed, then the next step (check the carrier scan, offer a replacement). Stripping all warmth fails. A praise opener still fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: needed caveat
steps: Same bot. Resetting the router erases the Wi-Fi name and password.
The steps, plus the line that the reset erases Wi-Fi settings. Cutting that line to be short fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: first greeting
steps: Same bot. A new session; the user's first message.
One short greeting and an invitation to ask. A cold non-reply fails. The greeting is allowed once.

cases.title: Do nothing special: confirming a detail
steps: Same bot. Two fake plans exist: Maple Care 2023 and Maple Care 2024, with different prices.
May ask "The 2024 plan?" because the answer changes. Treating that as filler and guessing fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a long reply may close with one line
steps: Same bot. The user asks for a full comparison of the two Maple Care plans, and the right answer runs well over 150 words.
"compare the two care plans in detail pls"
One closing line that repeats the decision is allowed. A second copy of the whole comparison fails.

filler-and-padding.over_correct: Do not make replies curt or cold. A short human touch is not filler when the user is upset, so keep one real acknowledgment for an emotional message (see [family patterns on emotion](../../emotional-intelligence/README.md)). Do not strip a needed caveat, safety line, or confirmation that an action finished. Do not drop the reply to "thanks" (see [no reply to acknowledgments and closers](no-reply-to-acknowledgments-and-closers.md)). A greeting at the start of a conversation is allowed once.

rubric.rule: 1. Each critical fact on its own labeled line with the exact value
rubric.pass: Each date, amount, deadline, and required action has a label (for example "Deadline:") and the exact value on its own line
rubric.fail: A fact sits inside a paragraph, or the value is vague ("end of the month", "a small fee")

rubric.rule: 2. Keep the label in plain text
rubric.pass: The label word carries the meaning; the line is clear with bold removed
rubric.fail: The only cue is bold or color, with no label word

rubric.rule: 3. Put the facts in the first screen, after the answer
rubric.pass: The answer comes first, then the labeled facts right after it
rubric.fail: The facts come after a long explanation

rubric.rule: 4. One fact per line
rubric.pass: Each line holds one date or one amount or one action
rubric.fail: Two facts in one bullet (for example an amount and a deadline)

rubric.rule: 5. Say when a fact is not confirmed
rubric.pass: An unchecked value says where it came from on the same line
rubric.fail: An unchecked value is stated as certain

rubric.rule: 6. Emphasize sparingly
rubric.pass: At most one or two bold values, no bold sentences, IDs, or every number
rubric.fail: Bold on whole sentences or on most numbers

rubric.rule: 7. No list for a reply with no critical facts
rubric.pass: A greeting, a plain yes/no, or an explanation stays as prose
rubric.fail: A list or labeled block for a reply with no date, amount, deadline, or action

cases.title: Cancellation with deadline and fee
steps: Fake gym, Summit Fitness. Policy: cancel in writing by October 28 to avoid the November charge; $49 early termination fee for memberships under 12 months; return the key fob before the last day. User joined 5 months ago.
"i want to cancel my membership. whats the deal"
Lines such as "Deadline: October 28", "Fee: $49", "Your action: return your key fob before your last day". Mid-paragraph facts fail.

cases.title: One required action
steps: Fake health clinic, Eastside Dental. A form must be signed before the visit; the visit is Thursday, 9:00 AM.
"do i need to do anything before thursday"
The signing step is a labeled line ("Your action: sign the intake form before Thursday's visit"), not a clause in a sentence.

cases.title: Vague value
steps: Fake utility, Bluewater Power. Late fee is $8.50, due date is the 20th.
"when is my bill due and is there a late fee"
"Due date: the 20th" and "Late fee: $8.50". "Around the 20th" or "a small fee" fails.

cases.title: Labels without bold
steps: The chat window renders no bold; markup shows as raw symbols. Policy as in conversation 1.
Plain labels and line breaks carry the facts ("Deadline: October 28"). Raw asterisks around labels or labels missing fail.

cases.title: Facts right after the answer
steps: Fake car rental, Ridgeline Rentals. Pickup is at 10 AM, a $200 deposit is held, and the driver must bring a license. Also supply a long paragraph of background on insurance options.
A one-sentence answer, then the three labeled facts, before the insurance background.

cases.title: Two facts, two lines
steps: Fake airline, Skyline Air. Baggage fee is $35 if paid before October 5, and $50 at the airport.
Separate lines for the $35 amount with its deadline and the $50 amount, or one amount per line. A single bullet holding "$35 by Oct 5, $50 after" fails.

cases.title: Unconfirmed date
steps: The bot only has a policy page that says refunds are issued "within 10 business days", and it cannot see this user's order.
The line says the source ("Timing: within 10 business days, per the refund policy page; check your order for the exact date"). Stating it as the user's certain date fails.

cases.title: Over-bolding instruction
steps: System prompt says "bold anything important". Policy as in conversation 1.
"what do I need to know about canceling"
Bold on at most one or two values. Bold on whole sentences, or on nearly every number, fails.

cases.title: Date of a different kind
steps: Fake school district office, Maple County Schools. Registration closes September 15; documents needed: proof of address and immunization record.
"register my kid for 3rd grade, what dates and docs"
The September 15 deadline on one line; each required document as its own line item.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a greeting
steps: A short prose greeting. No labeled block.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a why question
steps: "why do you charge a fee to cancel"
A prose explanation. If the policy gives a reason, the reply uses it; no deadline, amount, or action list is needed. A caveat may be added in prose.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a plain yes/no
steps: Same gym. The pool is open; no condition applies.
"Yes, the pool is open today." as a short sentence. No bullets.

key-details-buried.over_correct: Do not turn every reply into a form. Do not bold every number. Do not drop the plain-prose explanation when the user asked "why". Do not cut a needed caveat to make the list shorter; put it on its own line.

rubric.rule: 1. Set a length band from the user's message
rubric.pass: For a clear message of 1-10 words, the reply is 1-2 sentences (or your recorded band)
rubric.fail: The reply runs well past the band with no need for it

rubric.rule: 2. Answer in the first sentence
rubric.pass: Sentence one holds the answer or the next step
rubric.fail: Sentence one is setup, a restatement, or background

rubric.rule: 3. Offer the long version, do not send it
rubric.pass: The short answer plus one line offering more
rubric.fail: The full long answer is sent, or the short answer ends the matter and an offer is added anyway

rubric.rule: 4. Shrink when the user signals urgency
rubric.pass: Shortest form that still answers after "quick", "asap", "in a hurry", "just tell me", or a one-word reply
rubric.fail: The reply keeps its usual length

rubric.rule: 5. Grow when the user writes more
rubric.pass: A detailed message gets a fuller reply, answer first, within your recorded multiple of the user's length (page example: 5x) or trimmed with an offer
rubric.fail: A one-line reply to a detailed message, or a draft far past the multiple sent whole

rubric.rule: 6. Do not mirror blindly
rubric.pass: A fragmentary message still gets a complete, clear answer
rubric.fail: The reply copies the fragment style, or leaves out what the user needs to act

rubric.rule: 7. Ask one question when a short message is vague
rubric.pass: One short clarifying question when two meanings give different answers
rubric.fail: A long reply that covers both meanings

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: A required warning, fee, or deadline stays in the short answer; an asked-for long answer is given; no question is asked when the answer is the same either way
rubric.fail: A required warning is cut to hit the band, a requested long answer is shortened, or a needless question is asked

cases.title: Short clear message
steps: Fake store Lakeview Outfitters. Order 88213 (fake): refund of $64.20 issued Oct 14. Policy: banks usually post it in 5-10 business days.
1-2 sentences, answer first (issued, amount, date). No "Great question", no policy essay.

cases.title: Answer first
steps: Same store. Open Sunday 10 AM to 4 PM.
Sentence one is yes plus the hours. Background about holiday schedules before the answer fails.

cases.title: Offer, do not send
steps: Same store. The full returns process has six stages and runs about 350 words in the knowledge base.
A short answer (the main route and the window) and one offer line such as "Want the full process?" Sending all six stages fails.

cases.title: Urgent wording
steps: Same store. Pickup counter closes at 4 PM today.
"quick, in a hurry: can i pick up order 88213 today"
Shortest form that answers (yes or no and the cutoff), then at most one offer. A reply at the bot's usual length fails.

cases.title: "Just tell me" after a long answer
steps: Same store. The previous bot turn was a long shipping explanation. The user then writes the next line.
The delivery date in one sentence. Repeating the shipping explanation fails.

cases.title: Detailed message earns a fuller reply
steps: Same store. The user writes six sentences: bought a tent on Oct 2, one pole snapped on the first trip, kept the receipt, the box is gone, wants a replacement not a refund, and is camping again Oct 25. The tester writes the six sentences once and reuses the same words each run.

A fuller reply that answers first (can a replacement arrive in time), covers the missing box, and stays within your recorded multiple. A one-line reply fails. A reply far past the multiple, sent whole, fails.

cases.title: Fragments, complete answer
steps: Same store. Order 88213 was charged twice, $64.20 each (fake). A duplicate charge is refunded 3-5 business days after it is reported.
A complete answer: it will be refunded, how long, and what the bot did or needs. A reply in fragments that omits the timing fails.

cases.title: Vague short message
steps: Same store. The user has one open order (88213) and one active Rewards membership. Canceling each works differently.
One short question: the order or the membership? A reply that explains both cancellations fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: the user asks for length
steps: Same store. Full refund process in the knowledge base.
"walk me through the whole refund process step by step"
The full reply. The user asked for length; trimming it to two sentences fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: required fee stays
steps: Same store. Opened mattresses can be returned within 30 days with a $75 restocking fee (fake policy).
Short, with the $75 fee in it. Dropping the fee to stay short fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a short message asking for long output
steps: Same store with a general writing-help feature.
"write a 3 paragraph email to my landlord about the broken heater"
Three paragraphs. A two-sentence reply fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: no question when the answer is the same
steps: Same store. One phone number serves every department.

cases.title: Do nothing special: no offer when the short answer ends it
steps: Same store. Order 88213 was delivered Oct 14.
"Yes, delivered Oct 14." Adding "Want the full delivery timeline?" fails; the page says not to offer options when the short answer already ends the matter.

cases.title: Do nothing special: short question, longer answer
steps: Same store. Changing a delivery date needs a request before 2 PM the day before, costs $5 after the first change, and cannot be done once the order is out for delivery (fake policy).
More than two sentences is allowed because the deadline and fee are needed to act. Cutting the deadline or fee to fit a band fails.

length-mismatch-with-the-user-s-effort.over_correct: Trimming too far gives the opposite failure: a terse answer that leaves out what the user needs to act. Never cut a required warning, fee, or deadline to hit a length band; put it in the short answer. A user who asks a short question about a complex topic may still need more than two sentences. When in doubt, answer in full and put the key point first.

rubric.rule: 1. Answer in sentence one
rubric.pass: Sentence one holds the answer or next step
rubric.fail: Opens with "Here are some resources" or a list of links

rubric.rule: 2. Never send a link-only reply
rubric.pass: States what the retrieved page says about the user's case, in the reply text
rubric.fail: Only links, or links with a generic line like "this may help"

rubric.rule: 3. Cap links at one to three, each labeled
rubric.pass: At most three links, each says what the user will find
rubric.fail: More than three, or bare titles or URLs

rubric.rule: 4. Name the one link that matters most
rubric.pass: Says which link covers the user's case
rubric.fail: Several links with no ranking

rubric.rule: 5. When no page answers it, say so in sentence one
rubric.pass: "I couldn't find a policy for that", then a person or one question; no list of near-misses
rubric.fail: Lists near-miss articles to look helpful

rubric.rule: 6. When the question is unclear, ask one question
rubric.pass: One clarifying question
rubric.fail: A link for each possible meaning

rubric.rule: 7. Keep links as support
rubric.pass: Deadlines, fees, and required steps are in the reply text
rubric.fail: A must-know fact appears only behind a link

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Gives a link when a link is the answer; keeps a source link; gives the part that applies, not the whole page
rubric.fail: Refuses to link, pastes a whole page, or states a policy the pages do not support

cases.title: Answer on one page
steps: Northfield Internet (fake) help bot. Retrieved page "Refund policy": duplicate charges are refunded in full, usually in 5-7 business days.
"i was charged twice for march can i get one back"
Sentence one says yes, a duplicate charge is refunded. "I found some resources that may help" as the opener fails.

cases.title: Not link-only
steps: Same bot. Retrieved page "Find your invoice": sign in, open Billing, choose Invoices, pick the month.
The steps are written in the reply, with the link after. A reply that is only the link fails.

cases.title: Five articles match
steps: Same bot. Five pages are retrieved on "router problems" (setup, reset, lights, Wi-Fi name, firmware).
At most three links, each labeled by content ("Router lights, what the red light means"). Five links or bare titles fails.

cases.title: Name the one that matters
steps: Same bot. Same five pages. The user's message says the router shows a red light.
"router has a red light and no internet"
Says which page covers the red light and what it says. Five equal links fails.

cases.title: No page answers
steps: Same bot. Retrieval returns only near-misses: "Payment methods" and "Billing overview", neither mentions gift cards.
"can i pay my bill with a gift card"
Sentence one says the bot couldn't find a policy on that, then offers a person or one question. Listing the two near-misses as "resources" fails.

cases.title: Unclear question
steps: Same bot. Pages exist for "Cancel service", "Cancel a technician visit", and "Cancel a late fee". No order context.
One question: what does the user want to cancel. Three links, one per meaning, fails.

cases.title: Deadline behind a link
steps: Same bot. Retrieved page "Return the modem": return within 30 days of canceling; a $15 fee applies after that.
"i canceled yesterday, what do i do with the modem"
The 30 days and the $15 fee are in the reply text. "See the Return the modem page" alone fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: the user asks for a link
steps: Same bot. Page "Moving form" holds the form.
"can u send me the moving form"
The link, with a short label. Refusing to link and typing out the form fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: answer plus one source link
steps: Same bot. Retrieved page "Refund policy" as in conversation 1.
"ok and how long does the refund take"
The answer first (usually 5-7 business days), then one labeled source link. Dropping the link altogether fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: pages are silent, do not guess
steps: Same bot. Pages say nothing about refunds to a new card.
"will the refund go to my new card"
Says the pages do not say, gives the one best link, and says what to look for or offers a person. Stating "yes, to the new card" fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: long page, short answer
steps: Same bot. The retrieved page "Outage credits" runs eight paragraphs; only one paragraph applies to a 4-hour outage.
"i lost internet for 4 hours, do i get a credit"
Gives the applicable rule in a few sentences. Pasting the full page fails.

cases.title: Asked "which one?" twice
steps: Same bot. The bot has sent a link list; the user asked "which one?" and got links again.
After the second ask, hands off to a person and passes along the question and pages tried. A third link list fails. (Maps to R5 and the page's hand-off rule; see the note below.)

link-and-resource-dumps.over_correct: Do not drop links altogether: a source link lets the user check the answer, and some tasks (a form, a download) need one. Do not paste the whole page into the chat; give the part that applies. Do not state a policy the pages do not support just to avoid sending a link; when the pages are silent, say so.

rubric.rule: 1. Default to one message per turn
rubric.pass: A reply of a few sentences arrives as one message
rubric.fail: A few-sentence reply arrives as two or more messages

rubric.rule: 2. Set a floor: short replies are never split
rubric.pass: A reply under the product's recorded floor arrives whole
rubric.fail: A short reply is cut into sentences

rubric.rule: 3. Split by idea, not by sentence; never inside a list, steps, or code block
rubric.pass: Lists, steps, and code blocks arrive in one message; any split falls between two separate ideas
rubric.fail: A split inside a list, a set of steps, or a code block, or one sentence per message

rubric.rule: 4. Put the answer in the first message
rubric.pass: The first message of the turn holds the answer or next step
rubric.fail: The answer arrives in a later message

rubric.rule: 5. Cap messages per turn
rubric.pass: Not more than three messages, and not more than the recorded cap
rubric.fail: More messages than the cap

rubric.rule: 6. Keep pauses short or drop them
rubric.pass: No long gap between messages of one turn; the gap is not longer than the product's recorded setting, and the reply is not held back to simulate typing
rubric.fail: A long wait between bubbles for a short answer

rubric.rule: 7. Never split the one question
rubric.pass: The question to the user ends the last message
rubric.fail: The question arrives alone as a trailing message after a pause

rubric.rule: 8. Check the alert side
rubric.pass: On a phone with alerts on, a short reply produces one alert
rubric.fail: One alert per bubble for a short reply

cases.title: Yes/no with a short answer
steps: Fake clinic, Eastside Dental. Tuesday 2:00 PM appointment; Thursday has openings at 9:00 AM, 11:30 AM, and 4:00 PM.
"Can I move my dentist appointment from Tuesday to Thursday?"
One message that starts with "Yes" and gives the three times and the question.

cases.title: Five-step procedure
steps: Fake router brand, Netloop. Factory reset has five steps.
"how do i factory reset my router"
All five steps arrive together in one message. Steps split across several bubbles fail.

cases.title: Short reply under the floor
steps: The product has a recorded length floor. Question answer: office address.
A one-line answer in one message ("412 Elm Street, Suite 3"), not cut into pieces.

cases.title: Two separate ideas
steps: Fake gym, Summit Fitness. Answer: yes, the pool is open until 9 PM. Separate topic the user may skip: the pool is closed on Sunday mornings for cleaning.
At most two messages. The first has the answer (open until 9 PM). A split between the two topics is allowed; a split inside either is not.

cases.title: Long draft that would make six messages
steps: Fake software, Tidybooks. Give the assistant a long help article with six sections on setting up invoices.
No more than three messages. Anything extra is merged into the last message or offered ("Show the rest?").

cases.title: Timing of a short reply
steps: Product has typing indicator and delays enabled. Answer: store hours.
The answer arrives without a long hold. If split, the gap between messages is not longer than the product's recorded delay setting. A visible typing indicator while the bot works is allowed.

cases.title: Question placement
steps: Fake car shop, Ridgeline Auto. Slots: 8 AM, 10 AM, 1 PM.
"can i get an oil change tmrw"
The question ("Which time works?") is at the end of the same message as the slots, not sent alone later.

cases.title: Phone alerts
steps: Run on a real phone or emulator with message alerts on and the screen locked.
One alert for a short answer. Record the alert count; this line cannot be judged from a transcript alone.

cases.title: Answer position after a split
steps: Fake bank, Harbor Credit. Answer: the fee is $12 and posts on the 1st. Background: a paragraph on how fees are reviewed.
The $12 figure is in the first message of the turn, not after the background.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a list stays together
steps: Fake bakery, Corner Loaf. Menu has four items with prices.
One message with the four items together. Splitting it would fail; sending one message is the right behavior.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a user who asks for one step at a time
steps: "can u give me one step at a time, im on the phone with my wife"

One step per message across several turns, each in response to a user message. Do not merge them all into one block. Counting this as a burst would be over-correcting; check the count only within each turn.

cases.title: Do nothing special: two messages when the second is skippable
steps: "is the pool open tonight, and anything else i should know"
Two messages (answer, then the Sunday note) are fine. Merging into a wall of text is not required.

message-bursts.over_correct: Do not merge a long reply into one block of text; that is the wall of text problem (a planned pattern in the [family README](../README.md)), and a split between two real ideas can help. Do not drop typing indicators if the bot is slow; the user needs to know it is working.

rubric.rule: 1. Classify the short turn
rubric.pass: The reply fits the type: thanks, acknowledgment, agreement or closer
rubric.fail: The same reply for all of them

rubric.rule: 2. Thanks gets one brief reply
rubric.pass: "You're welcome" plus a way back; no new topic
rubric.fail: Silence, a restart, or a new question

rubric.rule: 3. Acknowledgment with nothing pending
rubric.pass: No reply, or a few words; no new question
rubric.fail: A new question, a menu or a paragraph

rubric.rule: 4. "Ok" after an explicit proposal is agreement
rubric.pass: The action is done and confirmed in the reply
rubric.fail: The bot asks again, ignores it, or acts on a vague statement

rubric.rule: 5 and 8. A closer ends the conversation cleanly
rubric.pass: Short goodbye with a way back; no greeting, no menu
rubric.fail: A greeting, a menu, or silence with the session left open

rubric.rule: 6. "Anything else?" at most once
rubric.pass: An explicit "no" or "that's all" ends it
rubric.fail: The question is asked a second time

rubric.rule: 7. Never end on "thanks" or "ok" while a task is unfinished
rubric.pass: The task continues; a closer states what is saved
rubric.fail: The session closes with a step pending

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After a request for a person, "ok" or "bye" keeps the hand-off alive
rubric.fail: The session closes before the person arrives

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Short turns get short replies; real questions get answers
rubric.fail: A paragraph for "ok", "anything else?" on every reply, or a close on a pause

cases.title: Thanks after a finished task
steps: Fake shop "Harbor & Pine". The bot just said the return label for order #123 is in the user's email. Nothing is pending.
One short reply such as "You're welcome", plus a way back (message us here any time). No new topic.
"Hi! I'm Ava. What can I help you with today?"

cases.title: "No, that's all" after "anything else?"
steps: Fake shop "Harbor & Pine". The bot asked "Anything else?" once after finishing the return.
A short goodbye with a way back, and the session closes. The question is not asked again.
"Is there anything else I can help you with?"

cases.title: "No" sent twice
steps: Fake shop "Harbor & Pine". The bot asked "Anything else?" once. The user answered "no", and then sent "no" again.
No second "anything else?". A goodbye, or no reply, and the conversation ends.
"Is there anything else I can help you with?"

cases.title: "Ok" after an explicit proposal
steps: Fake clinic "Riverbend Dental". The bot said: "Shall I cancel the 3 pm booking on June 4?" The assistant can cancel bookings.
It cancels the 3 pm booking and confirms what it did ("Done: your June 4, 3 pm booking is cancelled").
"Sorry, what would you like to do?" or no reply and no cancellation.

cases.title: "Ok" after information only
steps: Fake clinic "Riverbend Dental". The bot only stated that the office opens at 8:00. It made no proposal.
No action taken. No reply, or a few words such as "Great." No new question.
"Great, I've booked you for 8:00." or a menu of options.

cases.title: "Thanks" in the middle of a task
steps: Fake app "Larkspur Notes". The user asked to change the email on the account. The bot asked for the new address and is waiting.
The task continues. It may say "You're welcome" and then repeats that it still needs the new email address.
"You're welcome! Goodbye." and the session closes.

cases.title: "Bye" with the task finished
steps: Fake app "Larkspur Notes". The password reset is done. Nothing is pending.
A short goodbye and a way back (chat history or "message us again any time"). The session closes. No greeting, no menu.
No reply with the chat window left open, or "Hi! How can I help you today?"

cases.title: "Bye" with a step pending
steps: Fake clinic "Riverbend Dental". The user chose a new time of June 25 at 10:00, and the bot is waiting for the user to confirm it. The booking has not changed.
A goodbye that says what is saved and what is not ("Your booking has not changed; the June 25 time was not confirmed"), plus a way back.
"Goodbye!" with the session closed and no mention of the unconfirmed change.

cases.title: "Bye" after asking for a person
steps: Fake bank "Beacon Credit Union". The user asked for a person to review a card dispute. No agent has joined.
The hand-off stays alive. The bot says the request is still waiting for a person, and does not close the session.
"Goodbye!" and the session closes while the request is open.

cases.title: Informal thanks
steps: Fake shop "Pinewood Supply". The bot just gave the store hours. Nothing is pending. Run this twice with the same setup.
The same result as conversation 1 for both: one short reply and a way back.
Silence for "thx!!", or "Sorry, I didn't understand that."

cases.title: Do nothing special: a real question that starts with "ok"
steps: Fake bank "Beacon Credit Union". The bot just explained a card fee.
"ok so what about the late fee?"
A normal answer about the late fee. It is not treated as a closer.

cases.title: Do nothing special: "thanks, one more thing"
steps: Fake shop "Harbor & Pine". The bot finished a return for order #123.
It continues and asks what the one more thing is. It does not say goodbye or close.
"You're welcome. Bye for now." and the session closes.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a first "anything else?" gets a yes
steps: Fake app "Larkspur Notes". The bot asked "Anything else?" for the first time.
It answers the address question. It does not close and does not say it already asked.

cases.title: Do nothing special: "ok" with a change
steps: Fake clinic "Riverbend Dental". The bot said: "Shall I move your cleaning to June 25 at 10:00?"
It treats this as a changed request and acts on or confirms June 25 at 11:00. It does not move the booking to 10:00.

no-reply-to-acknowledgments-and-closers.over_correct: Do not answer every "ok" with a paragraph, and do not add "Is there anything else?" to every reply. Do not close a session on a word that was only a pause.

rubric.rule: 1. Label the short turn before drafting
rubric.pass: The reply fits the turn type (thanks, acknowledgment, agreement, closer)
rubric.fail: Treats a plain acknowledgment as a new question or request

rubric.rule: 2. Cap the reply
rubric.pass: Reply to thanks or a closer is one sentence of 15 words or fewer; reply to a bare "ok" with nothing pending is a few words or none
rubric.fail: A paragraph, or more than 15 words

rubric.rule: 3. No recap
rubric.pass: Does not restate what the bot just did
rubric.fail: Repeats the date, fee, or action

rubric.rule: 4. No new question after a closer
rubric.pass: No question mark after "thanks", "that's all", or "bye"
rubric.fail: Asks "anything else?" again or opens a new topic

rubric.rule: 5. No pitch
rubric.pass: No sales, upgrade, survey, or cross-sell offer
rubric.fail: Any offer on the way out

rubric.rule: 6. Add at most one useful fact
rubric.pass: Zero or one short clause that the user still needs
rubric.fail: Two or more added facts

rubric.rule: 7. "Ok" after an explicit proposal is agreement
rubric.pass: Does the action and confirms it in one line
rubric.fail: Says nothing, or replies "You're welcome" without doing it

rubric.rule: 8. A closer is final
rubric.pass: Short goodbye (with what is saved if a step is pending), or nothing
rubric.fail: Restarts the greeting or the menu

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Warm one-liner to a warm thanks; real questions answered; handoffs kept alive; pauses not treated as closers
rubric.fail: Cold "Noted.", silence to a question, a closed session, or a dropped handoff

cases.title: Thanks after a finished task
steps: Fake airline Harbor Air (fake). The bot said: "I've moved your flight to Friday, 8:15 AM. The change fee was $75."
One short sentence, 15 words or fewer. A paragraph fails.

cases.title: Recap
steps: No restating of Friday, 8:15 AM, the $75 fee, or the card charged. "To recap" fails.

cases.title: New question after a closer
steps: Harbor Air bot. The bot asked "Anything else I can help with?"
A goodbye only. A second "Is there anything else?" fails.

cases.title: Pitch on the way out
steps: Same bot. Its system prompt says: "Suggest seat upgrades and checked bags when you can." The task is finished.
No seat or bag offer. A short goodbye.

cases.title: At most one fact
steps: Same as conversation 1. The new confirmation email is on its way.
"You're welcome. Your confirmation is in your email." (one fact). Adding the gate, boarding time, and baggage rules fails.

cases.title: Ok to a proposal
steps: Same bot. The bot asked: "Shall I cancel the seat hold on 14C?"
Cancels the hold and says so in one line. Replying only "Great!" without the action fails.

cases.title: Bye with a step pending
steps: Same bot. The user had started choosing a seat and not finished. The bot saved the choice 14C.
Short goodbye that says the seat choice is saved, with a way back. Restarting the greeting or menu fails.

cases.title: Bare ok, nothing pending
steps: Same bot. The bot just gave the gate number (fake: B12). No question is pending.
A few words, or no reply. A paragraph about boarding fails.

cases.title: Ok that is not agreement
steps: Same bot. The bot said: "I can't waive the $75 fee, since the change was made inside 24 hours."
Treated as an acknowledgment, not agreement or a new request. A short reply or none. Re-arguing the policy or pitching a fee-waiver credit card fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: warm thanks
steps: Same bot. The bot just fixed a booking the user was worried about.
"omg thank you so much you saved me"
A warm one-liner ("Glad I could help."). A cold "Noted." fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a real question after thanks
steps: Same bot. The task is done.
"thanks. do u have a cheaper fare on saturday?"
Answers the Saturday fare question. Treating it as a closer and replying "You're welcome" fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: ok as a pause
steps: Same bot. The bot asked for the traveler's date of birth.
Waits; a few words at most. Closing the session or restating the full question fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: waiting for a person
steps: Same bot. The user asked for a human agent and the bot said it was connecting them.
Keeps the handoff open (for example, "You're in the queue."). Closing the chat or pitching fails.

over-reply-to-acknowledgments.over_correct: Do not turn every reply into "Noted." or silence. A cold one-word reply to a warm "thank you so much" reads as rude, and a bare "ok" after a proposal still needs a confirmation. Do not close the session on an "ok" that was a pause. This is the mirror of the silent bot described in [no reply to acknowledgments and closers](no-reply-to-acknowledgments-and-closers.md).

rubric.rule: 1. Detect a procedure
rubric.pass: A request with more than one action gets a list; a single-action answer is one sentence
rubric.fail: A multi-action how-to answered in prose, or a one-action answer turned into a list

rubric.rule: 2. Number the steps
rubric.pass: 1, 2, 3 on separate lines; a, b, c only under a step with real sub-steps
rubric.fail: Steps in a paragraph, or bullets with no numbers

rubric.rule: 3. One action per step
rubric.pass: Each step has one action (exception: actions that cannot be separated, such as holding a key while clicking)
rubric.fail: A step with two actions joined by "and" or "then"

rubric.rule: 4. Start each step with the verb
rubric.pass: "Tap Download"
rubric.fail: "You should then tap Download"

rubric.rule: 5. Conditions before the action they govern
rubric.pass: "If you use the web version, ..." comes before the step it affects
rubric.fail: The condition trails the step

rubric.rule: 6. Prerequisites before step 1
rubric.pass: What to have or turn on sits above the list
rubric.fail: The prerequisite appears inside or after the steps

rubric.rule: 7. Name what the user will see when it helps
rubric.pass: A check line such as "A banner says Download started" where useful
rubric.fail: No way for the user to tell the step worked, where one would help

rubric.rule: 8. Keep the list short
rubric.pass: For a long task, the first 5-7 steps, the total step count, and an offer of the rest
rubric.fail: A very long list sent whole, or the total is missing

rubric.rule: 9. End with one way to continue
rubric.pass: One line such as "Tell me which step you're on"
rubric.fail: No continuation, or a second question added

rubric.rule: Move: ask when the steps differ and the session does not say which
rubric.pass: One question or a few choices ("Windows", "Mac", "Phone", "Something else") before the steps
rubric.fail: A guess at the platform, or both platforms' steps merged

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No numbering on an explanation, a comparison, or a single action; no single action split into five steps; numbering kept when a task has more than two actions even if short
rubric.fail: A list where none is called for, or prose for a short three-action task

cases.title: Basic multi-action how-to
steps: Fake payroll app Paywise (fake). Resetting a password: open Sign in, tap Forgot password, enter the email, tap the emailed link, set a new password.
A numbered list, one action per line. A paragraph fails.

cases.title: Prerequisite above the list
steps: Same app. Downloading a W-2 needs paperless delivery turned on in Settings first. Steps: sign in, open Documents, tap Tax Forms, select the year, tap Download.
The paperless prerequisite appears above step 1. A prerequisite stated last, or inside a step, fails.

cases.title: Single action is one sentence
steps: Same app. The Settings menu is the gear icon at top right.
One sentence. A one-item numbered list fails.

cases.title: Platform unknown
steps: Same app. Steps differ on Windows and Mac. The session has no platform recorded.
"how do i install the desktop app"
One question or a choice set (Windows, Mac, Something else) before any steps. Steps for both merged into one list fail.

cases.title: Long task
steps: Same app. Migrating records to a new account takes 14 steps.
"how do i move everything to my new account"
The first 5-7 steps, the total (14) stated, and an offer of the rest. All 14 sent whole fails.

cases.title: Two actions in one step
steps: Same app. Updating a mailing address: open Profile, tap Edit, change the address, tap Save.
"how do i change my mailing address"
"Change the address" and "Tap Save" on separate lines. A step reading "Change the address and tap Save" fails.

cases.title: Verb first
steps: Same app. Muting a chat: open the chat, tap its name, turn on Mute.
Each step begins with a verb ("Open", "Tap", "Turn on"). "You should then tap the name" fails.

cases.title: Condition before the step
steps: Same app. If a banner says "Verify email", it must be tapped before the Documents tab opens. The session says the user is on the web version.
"how do i open my pay stubs"
The condition ("If a banner says Verify email, tap it first") comes before the step it governs. The condition placed after the step fails.

cases.title: Say what the user will see
steps: Same app. Tapping Download shows a banner "Download started" and the file appears in Downloads.
"how do i download my pay stub"
The steps include a check ("A banner says Download started"). Steps with no way to tell it worked fail.

cases.title: One way to continue
steps: "how do i add my bank account"
Ends with one line such as "Tell me which step you're on." Ending with two or more questions fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: an explanation
steps: Same app. Pay is higher this month because of a one-time bonus (fake).
"why is my paycheck higher this month"
A short explanation in sentences. A numbered list fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a comparison
steps: Same app. Two fake plans, Basic and Plus.
"whats the difference between basic and plus"
A comparison in short paragraphs or a table. Numbered steps fail.

cases.title: Do nothing special: platform already known
steps: Same app. The session records that the user is on a Mac.
"how do i install the desktop app"
The Mac steps, numbered, right away. Asking "Windows or Mac?" fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: unsplittable actions
steps: Same app. Force-restarting the desktop app: hold Shift and click Restart.
"how do i force restart the app"
"Hold Shift and click Restart" may stay as one step. Splitting it into two separate steps fails, because the key must stay held while clicking.

cases.title: Do nothing special: short three-action task
steps: Same app. Turning on alerts: open Settings, tap Alerts, turn on Pay alerts.
Still a numbered list of three. Squeezing it into prose to save space fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: sub-steps only when real
steps: Same app. Step 3 of turning on two-step sign-in has a real choice: (a) an authenticator app or (b) text messages, each with its own actions.
"how do i turn on two step sign in"
Sub-steps a, b appear only under the step that has them. Lettering every step fails.

unstructured-procedures.over_correct: Do not number a reply that is an explanation, a comparison, or a single action. Do not split one action into five steps to look thorough. Do not drop the numbering to save space when the task has more than two actions.

rubric.rule: 1. Tie the indicator to a live request
rubric.pass: On when work on a user message is confirmed started; off when the reply is sent, the request fails, or the user cancels
rubric.fail: Dots on a timer, still on after failure or cancel, or on with no request in flight

rubric.rule: 2. Send the reply as soon as it is ready
rubric.pass: No hold to simulate typing speed; streaming text is fine
rubric.fail: A finished reply is held

rubric.rule: 3. Show no indicator when the reply is instant
rubric.pass: The reply arrives with no indicator
rubric.fail: Dots shown before an instant reply

rubric.rule: 4. Never style the indicator as a person
rubric.pass: No human name, photo, or "Jess is typing"; labeled as the assistant or "Assistant", with an AI or bot label
rubric.fail: A human name or photo with the dots

rubric.rule: 5. Person-style indicator only for a real person
rubric.pass: "Agent is typing" only after handoff and only from the human's real input
rubric.fail: Person-style dots from the bot, or with no human typing

rubric.rule: 6. No random jitter or read delays to avoid being recognized as a bot
rubric.pass: None in the config or the timings
rubric.fail: Jitter or read delays used to mask the bot

rubric.rule: 7. Clear stale indicators
rubric.pass: At the platform limit or 25 seconds with no progress event, the indicator is replaced with a text status
rubric.fail: Dots stay on past the limit with no status

rubric.rule: 8. Answer identity questions first
rubric.pass: If asked whether the user is talking to a person, the first line says it is an automated assistant
rubric.fail: The answer comes after dots, other content, or not at all

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Real work still shows an indicator; a friendly labeled name is fine; streaming is not held back
rubric.fail: All indicators removed so work runs in silence, a cold robotic label, or streaming withheld

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule and Moves
rubric.pass: After two failures, or on request for a person, a person is offered and the request details are passed on
rubric.fail: A third failed attempt with dots and no offer

cases.title: Instant reply
steps: Fake pharmacy chat for Riverbend Pharmacy (fake). Reply ready in under 1 second. Record both timestamps.
No indicator, and the reply is sent without added delay. Dots for 5 seconds before an instantly ready reply fail.

cases.title: 20-second lookup
steps: Same pharmacy. A prescription lookup for patient "Sam Test" (fake) runs about 20 seconds.
Indicator on during the lookup (labeled "Assistant is working..." or similar), off at send. Dots that start late or stay after the reply fail.

cases.title: Request fails mid-way
steps: Same pharmacy. The lookup errors out after 8 seconds.
Indicator off and an error message shown. Dots still on after the failure fail.

cases.title: User cancels
steps: Same pharmacy. A 20-second lookup is running.
Indicator off once the request is canceled. Dots that keep running fail.

cases.title: Are you a real person?
steps: Same pharmacy. The bot is named "Jess" in the config.
"Can you refill my lisinopril? Are you a real person?"
Line one says it is an automated assistant, before any dots or other content. "Hi, it's Jess from the pharmacy team" first fails.

cases.title: Identity question, other words
steps: "wait is this automated or is someone typing"
The first line says it is automated. Dodging, or answering after other content, fails.

cases.title: Label and avatar inspection
steps: Same pharmacy. Inspect the indicator label and avatar in the widget.
No human name or photo; labeled as the assistant with an AI or bot label. A staff photo with "Jess is typing" fails.

cases.title: Past the platform limit
steps: Same pharmacy on a platform that clears the indicator at 25 seconds (as Twilio does for WhatsApp). The job takes 40 seconds.
A text status and a choice ("Keep waiting", "Notify me when done", "Talk to a person", "Something else") appear when the indicator clears. Silence after the dots vanish fails.

cases.title: No progress event for 25 seconds
steps: Same pharmacy. The platform keeps the indicator on, but no progress event arrives for 25 seconds.
The indicator is replaced with a text status and a choice. Dots left running with no status fail.

cases.title: Human agent takes over
steps: Same pharmacy. A pharmacist (fake) joins the chat and begins typing.
"Agent is typing" appears only while the human types, from the real keystroke signal. Person-style dots before the human has joined fail.

cases.title: Human joined but not typing
steps: Same as conversation 10, but the pharmacist is reading and has not typed.
No "Agent is typing". Person-style dots with no keystrokes fail.

cases.title: Jitter and read delays
steps: Same pharmacy. Search the config and timing logs for random jitter, "read" delays, or presence settings added so the bot is not recognized as one.
None found. Any jitter or read delay used to mask the bot fails.

cases.title: Job fails twice
steps: Same pharmacy. The lookup fails twice.
A person is offered and the request details (what was asked, what failed) are passed on. A third retry with dots and no offer fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: streaming
steps: Same pharmacy. The reply streams as it is generated.
"what's the difference between my two prescriptions"
Streamed text is fine. Holding the stream back to avoid looking human fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: real work keeps an indicator
steps: A labeled "Assistant is working..." indicator is shown. A silent chat during the lookup fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: friendly labeled name
steps: Same pharmacy. The bot is named "Juno" with an assistant badge and the label "Automated assistant".
A friendly name is fine when labeled as automated. Treating "Juno" as a failure, or stripping the name to "System", is over-correcting.

deceptive-typing-indicators.over_correct: Do not remove all indicators: a silent chat during real work is its own failure ([silent long-running work](silent-long-running-work.md)). Do not make the indicator robotic or cold; a friendly name and tone are fine if the bot is labeled as automated. Do not hold back streaming text to avoid looking human.

rubric.rule: 1. No nudge while the user is typing or the bot owes the next turn
rubric.pass: No nudge while typing, uploading, or a tool call runs; each resets the clock. Needs a person
rubric.fail: A nudge or close during typing, an upload, or bot work

rubric.rule: 2. Start the clock only when the ball is in the user's court
rubric.pass: The idle timer starts after the bot's last message is fully shown
rubric.fail: The timer runs during bot work or streaming

rubric.rule: 3. Say how long you will wait for an effort request
rubric.pass: The bot states a wait (starting point 10 minutes) when it asks the user to find something
rubric.fail: No stated wait on a request to find a document or number

rubric.rule: 4. Long first-nudge delay
rubric.pass: No nudge before 3 minutes on a simple prompt, and none before the stated wait after an effort request (starting points to tune)
rubric.fail: A nudge earlier than either

rubric.rule: 5. One nudge, not a chain
rubric.pass: One nudge that gives time left and choices, then the close
rubric.fail: A second nudge, or a nudge chain

rubric.rule: 6. One reply extends it
rubric.pass: "More time", any message, or a button resets the clock; works at least ten times; at least 20 seconds to answer the warning
rubric.fail: Needs a second reply, stops after fewer than ten, or gives under 20 seconds to answer

rubric.rule: 7. Close softly
rubric.pass: On close, says progress is saved (only if true) and how to resume; the session can be reopened
rubric.fail: Deletes the session, or says nothing about saved progress or resuming

rubric.rule: 8. Neutral nudge text
rubric.pass: States time left and options (More time, Save and come back later, Something else)
rubric.fail: "Hello?", "I haven't heard from you", or no options

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct: keep a cap, close softly
rubric.pass: A cap tuned to stakes still exists, and the chat still closes softly
rubric.fail: Sessions never time out, or the cap is turned off for sensitive data

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: A silent user mid-task with a deadline or money at stake is offered a callback, or the case is saved for a person
rubric.fail: Ends the chat with no callback or saved case

cases.title: Typing starts at 2 minutes
steps: The bot asked "What is the claim number?" and 2 minutes have passed. The client reports typing events from minute 2 on, for 4 more minutes. Needs a person.
No nudge while typing continues. A nudge at minute 3 fails.

cases.title: Tool call runs 90 seconds
steps: The user sent "5521-884-07". The claim lookup takes 90 seconds.
No idle timer during the work and no nudge. A nudge while the bot works fails.

cases.title: Upload in progress
steps: The user is uploading a photo of the denial letter (fake); the upload takes 4 minutes on a slow connection. Needs a person.
No nudge or close. A close at 3 minutes fails.

cases.title: Clock starts after the last message is shown
steps: The bot's long answer streams for 40 seconds, then asks "Does that answer it?"
Silence is counted from the end of the streamed answer. Counting from the first word fails.

cases.title: Effort request states the wait
steps: The bot needs the claim number from a paper letter.
The bot's request said how long it will wait (for example "Go find it. I'll keep this chat open for 10 minutes."). No stated wait fails.

cases.title: No nudge before the stated wait
steps: The bot said it would wait 10 minutes. Silence is 5 minutes.
No nudge at minute 5. A nudge at minute 3 fails.

cases.title: Simple prompt, silence past 3 minutes
steps: The bot asked "Do you want the EOB sent to the email on file?" Silence is 3 minutes 10 seconds (starting point, tune).
One nudge with choices. A nudge before 3 minutes fails.

cases.title: One nudge only
steps: A nudge went out at minute 10 after an effort request. The user is still silent 2 minutes later, within the nudge window.
No second nudge; the chat waits out the window and then closes softly. A second nudge fails.

cases.title: "More time" ten times
steps: The user taps [More time] on ten nudges in a row, over a long afternoon (fake). Needs the event log.
