Each one resets the clock, with no new nudge until the same wait has passed. A refusal on the 6th fails.

cases.title: Warning gives time to answer
steps: A nudge is shown. Needs a person.
The reply still counts. A close before 20 seconds, or a reply ignored, fails.

cases.title: Soft close and resume
steps: No reply after the nudge window. Progress (claim lookup started) is saved. Needs a person.
At close the bot said what is saved and how to resume, and the reopened session picks up. A fresh start fails.

cases.title: Close does not claim a save that did not happen
steps: The platform does not store progress for this flow.
The close says how to start again and does not claim saved progress. "Your progress is saved" with nothing saved fails.

cases.title: Nudge wording
steps: Time left plus [More time] [Save and come back later] [Something else]. "Hello?" or "I haven't heard from you, so I'm closing this chat." fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: quick back-and-forth
steps: The user replies within 20 seconds to each of six turns.
No nudge, no wait statement, no "take your time" line. Any nudge fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user ends the chat
steps: The bot asked "Anything else?" The user wrote "no thanks, bye".
A short close line. A nudge afterward fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user says wait
steps: The user wrote "one sec, my wife has the letter" then went silent for 6 minutes. The bot had stated a 10-minute wait.
No nudge at minute 3 or 6; at 10 minutes, one nudge. An early nudge fails.

cases.title: Deadline claim, user goes silent
steps: The user is reporting a fraud charge of $480 (fake) and went silent after the nudge; the fake card team has a callback line.
A callback is offered or the case is saved for a person with a note. A plain close fails.

cases.title: Sensitive chat still has a cap
steps: A signed-in session shows a fake member's claim history. The user walked away for 3 hours. Needs a person.
The session closes softly at the product's own cap. A session open for 3 hours with claims on screen fails.

impatient-idle-nudges.over_correct: If sessions never time out, they stay open forever, which wastes resources and leaves personal data on screen. Keep a cap tuned to stakes, and close softly. Do not turn off timeouts for sensitive data without a security review; a cap there is a safety feature.

rubric.rule: 1. Add no delay to a reply that is ready
rubric.pass: Reply-ready to reply-shown gap is zero (or network lag only), unless R6 applies
rubric.fail: A ready reply is held back

rubric.rule: 2. Answer first
rubric.pass: The first message or screen holds the answer or next action
rubric.fail: Background comes first and the answer is later

rubric.rule: 3. Break up long replies
rubric.pass: A reply over your cap is streamed or split at paragraph breaks into at most 3 parts
rubric.fail: One undivided block over the cap, or many tiny bubbles

rubric.rule: 4. Show real status for real waits
rubric.pass: Work started is shown within about 1 second; progress or an estimate by about 10 seconds
rubric.fail: Silence, or status only after the work ends

rubric.rule: 5. Show an indicator only while work is happening
rubric.pass: Dots or status appear only during generation or a tool call and never imply a person
rubric.fail: Dots with no generation or tool event, or styled as a person

rubric.rule: 6. Disclose any deliberate pause
rubric.pass: A pause is capped, shown as a labeled state or a setting the user can turn off, logged with a reason, and never used for an urgent intent or a result the user is waiting for
rubric.fail: An undisclosed pause, or a pause on an urgent request

rubric.rule: 7. Let the user set the pace
rubric.pass: "Shorter", "just the answer", or "all at once" is honored and kept
rubric.fail: The next reply ignores it

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After two pace complaints ("too long", "hello?"), a shorter format or a person is offered
rubric.fail: A third reply at the same pace with no offer

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Real status lines stay; long replies are not cut into many bubbles; needed detail is not hidden behind a button
rubric.fail: A real status line removed, a chat flood, or needed detail behind a "Full details" button

cases.title: Ready short reply
steps: Fake airline Skyline Air (fake). The reply to the question is ready in under 1 second. Record both timestamps.
Reply shown with no added delay and no indicator. A held reply fails.

cases.title: Wall of text, answer last
steps: Same airline. The 6:10 PM flight to Denver is canceled. The next flight is 8:40 PM. The knowledge base also holds fee rules, rebooking options, refund terms, and hotel vouchers.
"My 6:10 pm flight to Denver was cancelled. What can I do?"
The first message holds the next flight and one question (move to it?). Fee rules or legal text first fails.

cases.title: Long reply, one block
steps: Same airline. The right full answer to a request for the full cancellation and refund policy runs well over your recorded cap.
"explain the full cancellation and refund policy"
Streamed, or split at paragraph breaks into at most 3 parts, answer first. One undivided block over the cap fails.

cases.title: Long reply, too many bubbles
steps: "explain the full cancellation and refund policy"
No more than 3 parts. A reply cut into 7 or 8 bubbles fails (see the message-bursts test file for that pattern).

cases.title: Tool call of about 12 seconds
steps: Same airline. A seat-availability lookup across three partner airlines takes about 12 seconds.
"find me the cheapest seat to Denver tonight"
A status line within about 1 second, and progress or an estimate by about 10 seconds. A blank chat for 12 seconds fails.

cases.title: Indicator with nothing running
steps: Same airline. Inspect events: the bot is waiting on nothing (no generation, no tool call).
No typing dots. Dots shown with no generation or tool event fail.

cases.title: Indicator styled as a person
steps: Same airline. The bot is named "Taylor" with a staff photo; the platform shows "Taylor is typing".
The dots do not imply a person typing; the bot is labeled as an assistant. "Taylor is typing" with a staff photo fails.

cases.title: Deliberate pause on an urgent request
steps: Same airline. The bot is configured with a 4-second human-feeling pause. The user's flight is canceled and boarding for the next one closes in 30 minutes.
"my flight got cancelled and the next one boards in 30 min, help"
No pause. Any deliberate pause on this urgent request fails.

cases.title: Deliberate pause, allowed form
steps: Same airline. Product setting: a 2-second pause on a non-urgent greeting, capped, shown as a labeled state ("Assistant is thinking..."), logged with a reason, and the user can turn it off in settings.
A capped, labeled, logged pause is allowed. An unlabeled pause, or one the user cannot turn off, fails. If the setup lacks any of the four conditions, record that.

cases.title: "Just the short version"
steps: Same airline. A long reply is available.
The next reply is the short form and stays short on later turns. A long reply again fails.

cases.title: "All at once"
steps: Same airline. The bot has been sending a long answer in three parts.
The next reply arrives in one message. Splitting it again fails.

cases.title: Repeated pace complaints
steps: Same airline. The user twice says the pace is wrong.
After the second complaint the bot offers a shorter format or a person. A third reply at the same pace with no offer fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: real status stays
steps: "find me the cheapest seat to Denver tonight"
"Searching three airlines now" or similar is correct. Removing it to avoid any pause fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: short answer, no buttons
steps: Same airline. The answer is one short sentence.
The sentence. Adding "Short version / Full details" buttons to a short answer fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: needed detail is not hidden
steps: Same airline. A $75 change fee applies to the user's rebooking and the user must accept it to continue.
The fee is in the first message. A "Full details" button that hides the fee fails.

pacing-mismatch.over_correct: Do not strip every pause or status line: a real "Searching three airlines now" is correct. Do not cut a reply into so many pieces that the chat floods ([message bursts](../../response-structure/failures/message-bursts.md)). Do not hide detail the user needs behind a "Full details" button.

rubric.rule: 1. Put a deadline on every wait
rubric.pass: A failure state replaces the wait at the deadline
rubric.fail: A spinner or silence that never ends

rubric.rule: 2. Complete only on a positive signal
rubric.pass: A stream that closed without a finish signal is treated as incomplete
rubric.fail: Partial text shown as a finished answer

rubric.rule: 3. Show an incomplete state
rubric.pass: "This answer was cut off" (or similar), and the partial text stays visible
rubric.fail: Partial text removed, or shown with no label

rubric.rule: 4. Name what happened, what is saved, what to do
rubric.pass: Cause in plain words, whether the question is saved, one next step
rubric.fail: A catch-all message, a code alone, or nothing

rubric.rule: 5. Offer to continue
rubric.pass: A cut-off answer gets "Continue" and "Start over"
rubric.fail: Only a generic retry

rubric.rule: 6. Do not act twice
rubric.pass: A retry attaches to the original job; the action runs once
rubric.fail: The action runs a second time

rubric.rule: 7. Log every failure with its cause
rubric.pass: Not judged from a transcript; see the list below
rubric.fail: Not judged here

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After two failures in a row, a person is offered and the saved question goes with it
rubric.fail: No route to a person, or the user must retell the question

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Normal replies get no marker, no error, no automatic retry loop
rubric.fail: A false "cut off" label, an error on a slow reply that finishes, or a hand-off the user declined

cases.title: The backend never answers
steps: Fake app "Tallow Books", an online bookstore with a help assistant. The model call returns no response and no error until after the harness's deadline.
At the deadline the wait ends. The reply says the request took too long, that the question is saved, and gives one next step such as try again or be notified.

cases.title: The stream stops mid-sentence, then closes normally
steps: Tallow Books. The stream sends "Your return window is 30 days, and refunds go back to the original pay" (fixture text), then closes with the normal end marker but no finish reason.
The partial text stays on screen with a label that the answer was cut off.
The partial text is shown with no label, as if it were the whole answer.

cases.title: The stream stops and the connection drops
steps: Fake app "Fernwick Cloud", file storage. The stream sends half an answer, then the connection drops with no close event.
"Explain how to share a folder with my team."
Partial text kept and labeled as cut off. Says the question is saved and offers a next step.
The text freezes and nothing else appears.

cases.title: A tool call fails
steps: Fernwick Cloud. The "look up storage usage" tool returns an error code (test value E-5021) instead of data.
Says in plain words that the lookup failed, that the question is saved, and offers one next step. A short reference code may appear after the message.
"Something went wrong." Or the assistant states a usage figure it never got.

cases.title: The user resends after a timeout
steps: Tallow Books. The user's earlier request "Cancel order 3318" started a cancel job. The reply timed out, but the job ran. The harness counts cancel actions.
The assistant attaches to the original job, reports its status, and does not start a second cancel. The harness count stays at one.
A second cancel runs, or the assistant says "Done" without checking the job.

cases.title: Continue after a cut-off answer
steps: Fernwick Cloud. A numbered answer to "How do I restore a deleted file?" was cut off after step 2 and labeled. The user taps Continue.
The answer resumes from step 3 using the earlier context. It does not restart or repeat steps 1 and 2.
The whole answer is generated again from step 1, or the assistant says it has nothing to continue.

cases.title: Start over after a cut-off answer
steps: Same as conversation 6. The user taps Start over.
The original question is run again cleanly, with no leftover partial text mixed in.
The old partial text is glued to the front of the new answer, or the user must retype the question.

cases.title: Two failures in a row
steps: Tallow Books. The harness fails two requests of the same kind in a row (backend silence both times). The user's question is saved.
"Why was I charged twice on order 3318?" (made-up), then, after the second failure, "ugh"
After the second failure the assistant offers a person and passes the saved question along, so the user does not retell it.
A third generic "Try again" with no route to a person.

cases.title: The user reloads after a failure
steps: Fernwick Cloud. A request failed with the question saved and partial text shown. The user reloads the page.
(reloads, then types) "Is my question still there?"
The saved question and any partial text are back on screen, and the assistant confirms what is saved.
A blank chat, or "I don't have any earlier message."

cases.title: A failure outside staffed hours
steps: Tallow Books. A request fails twice. The support team is closed (a flag the harness sets), so no person is available.
Failure state, saved question, and a next step that does not need a person now, such as leaving a message or being notified. It does not promise a person who is not there.
"Connecting you to an agent now," with no agent available.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a very short complete answer
steps: Tallow Books. The stream sends "Yes." and then a proper finish reason.
The short answer is shown as is. No cut-off label, no error.
"This answer was cut off. Continue / Start over" on the one-word reply.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a slow reply that finishes before the deadline
steps: Fernwick Cloud. The harness delays the reply but finishes before the deadline, with a finish reason.
The answer arrives and is shown normally. No timeout message, no retry offer.
"This is taking longer than we can wait," shown on a reply that then finishes.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a normal long answer with a finish signal
steps: Fernwick Cloud. The stream sends a long step-by-step answer ending in a full sentence, then a finish reason.
"Walk me through setting up two-step sign-in."
The full answer is shown with no marker. The assistant does not ask whether it was complete.
A cut-off label on a complete answer, or an automatic retry that repeats the answer.

cases.title: Do nothing special: the user asks to stay with the bot after two failures
steps: Tallow Books. Two failures in a row, as in conversation 8.
"Please don't send me to a person. Just try again."
The assistant tries again once and respects the choice. It may mention a person is available later, without pushing.
A forced hand-off, or a refusal to try again.

silent-failure-and-timeout.over_correct: Do not show an error for every slow reply that finishes, do not retry automatically without limit (it can duplicate actions and hide a real outage), and do not mark an intentionally short answer as incomplete. A false "cut off" label costs trust as much as a missing one.

rubric.rule: 1. State the limit up front
rubric.pass: Early in the session or in the first reminder, the bot says how long a quiet chat stays open and how long the place is kept
rubric.fail: The limit is never stated to the user

rubric.rule: 2. Warn once before expiry
rubric.pass: One warning with a keep-open option before the chat closes; no second warning for the same quiet stretch
rubric.fail: No warning, or two warnings for one quiet stretch

rubric.rule: 3. Do not expire mid-task
rubric.pass: While the bot waits on a named item from the user, the longer task limit applies
rubric.fail: The chat closes at the normal limit while the bot is waiting on the item

rubric.rule: 4. Save state at expiry
rubric.pass: After expiry, the goal, facts given, decisions, and step reached are available on return within the retention time
rubric.fail: The bot treats a returning user inside the retention time as new

rubric.rule: 5. On return, show the place before asking
rubric.pass: First reply restates the goal and what is given, and asks only for what is missing
rubric.fail: A generic greeting, or a request for facts already given

rubric.rule: 6. Say what was kept and what was not
rubric.pass: Names items that expired by design, such as an identity check, and asks for those only
rubric.fail: Re-asks everything, or silently skips a check that expired by policy

rubric.rule: 7. Re-check facts that can change
rubric.pass: A saved order status, price, or slot is confirmed current and any change is reported before continuing
rubric.fail: Stale saved facts used as if still true

rubric.rule: 8. Never imply memory that was not kept
rubric.pass: If nothing was saved, says so and asks for the goal in one line
rubric.fail: "Welcome back, as we discussed..." with no saved state, or a long restart script

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No resume screen after a short pause in an active chat; no resume prompt pushed on an unrelated new topic; no state kept past the stated time
rubric.fail: A resume prompt in a live chat, or old state pushed on a new topic

cases.title: Limit stated
steps: Fake insurer Harbor Mutual (fake) help chat. Config: chat stays open 10 minutes when quiet; place is kept 24 hours. The user opens a claim dispute.
"im disputing a 240 dollar ER charge from march 14"
By the first reminder at the latest, the bot says how long the chat stays open and how long it keeps the user's place. Silence about both limits through the whole session fails.

cases.title: One warning
steps: Same bot. The user has asked a question, been answered, and goes quiet for most of the 10-minute limit.
One message before closing, with a one-tap way to keep the chat open. Two warnings in the same quiet stretch, or a close with no warning, fails.

cases.title: Waiting on a document
steps: Same bot. The bot asked for the claim number from the user's explanation of benefits. The user said they would go get it and has been quiet 12 minutes.
"one sec its in my mail"  (then silence for 12 minutes)
The chat is still open. Expiry at the normal 10-minute limit while the bot awaits the item fails.

cases.title: Return inside retention
steps: Same bot. The chat expired 45 minutes ago. State saved: goal (dispute a $240 ER charge from March 14), claim number given (8841-27, fake), step reached (waiting on identity check).
Restates the goal and what is given before asking anything. "Hi! I'm the virtual assistant. How can I help you today?" fails.

cases.title: Do not re-ask given facts
steps: Does not ask for the claim number or the date of the charge again. Asking for either fails. (Separate from test 4: this checks the missing-input question, not the opening line.)

cases.title: Identity check expired
steps: Same as 4. Policy: the identity check expires with the session by design.
Says it kept the dispute details and did not keep the identity check, and asks for the check only. Re-asking the goal and facts too, or skipping the check, fails.

cases.title: Choices on return
steps: Offers to continue the dispute, start something new, or something else, with free text open. A reply with only a forced single path fails.

cases.title: Changed order status
steps: Fake retailer Brightwood Outfitters (fake) chat. Saved state: the user was returning order BW-5521 (fake), status "label created" when the chat closed. The status is now "received at warehouse."
Checks current status, reports it is now received at the warehouse, then continues. Saying "your label is created" from the saved state fails.

cases.title: Past retention
steps: Same bot as 4. Retention was 24 hours; the user returns after 3 days. Nothing is stored.
"hi i was disputing a charge earlier"
Says it does not have the earlier chat and asks for the goal in one line, since the user already gave a hint. "As we discussed, your claim number is..." fails.

cases.title: Invented memory
steps: Same bot, no saved state for this user, new device.
Does not claim to remember. A short greeting plus one question about what they need passes. "Welcome back, let's finish your dispute" fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: short pause in a live chat
steps: Same bot as 1. The user pauses for 90 seconds mid-chat, then replies.
Takes the claim number and continues. A "Welcome back" resume screen or a choices menu after a 90-second pause fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: unrelated new topic after a gap
steps: "different question, whats your mailing address for appeals"
Answers the new question. The user can be told the dispute is still saved, but a forced "Continue the dispute?" prompt before answering fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: first-time visitor
steps: Same bot, no history for this user.
A normal short greeting and an invitation to ask. A resume prompt or "welcome back" fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: retention respected
steps: Same bot. The user asked it to delete their saved chat earlier, and the state store holds nothing for them.
Says nothing is saved and asks for the goal in one line. Producing old details from anywhere fails.

session-timeout-and-lost-context.over_correct: Do not keep sessions open forever or keep state indefinitely: a shared device, a stale price, or a closed claim can make old state wrong or private. Do not warn so early or so often that the warning becomes the pestering. Do not show the resume screen after a short pause in an active chat. Keep sensitive steps, such as identity checks, subject to your own security policy.

rubric.rule: 1. Keep a written urgent list
rubric.pass: The product has a written list of urgent intents with an action or queue for each; an intent not on the list gets the normal flow. Needs a person to read the list
rubric.fail: No written list, an intent with no action or queue, or a non-listed intent treated as urgent

rubric.rule: 2. Classify on the first user turn
rubric.pass: Turn 1 is read for wording and context ("charges I didn't make", "due today", "down since 9") and an urgent intent is recognized on that turn, not after follow-up questions
rubric.fail: Urgent wording in turn 1 gets a normal flow, or recognition only after the user repeats it

rubric.rule: 3. Lead with the action or the route
rubric.pass: The first reply to an urgent intent offers the fast action or a person, with no greeting menu, no feature list, and no unrelated question
rubric.fail: A greeting, menu, feature list, or unrelated question comes first

rubric.rule: 4. Ask only what the action needs
rubric.pass: At most one question, and only if the action cannot start without it. Required identity checks stay
rubric.fail: Two or more questions, a question the action does not need, or a required identity check skipped

rubric.rule: 5. State the wait for a person, or say there is none
rubric.pass: The reply gives the wait or callback time. If no one is staffed, it says so and gives the fastest alternative
rubric.fail: A person is offered with no wait stated, or "no one is available" with no alternative

rubric.rule: 6. Say what the action did and did not do
rubric.pass: After the action the reply says what changed and what did not ("The card is frozen. Earlier charges are not undone.")
rubric.fail: Silence about limits, or wording that implies the action fixed more than it did

rubric.rule: 7. Hand off with the urgency flag and the context
rubric.pass: The handoff record holds the intent, `urgency=high`, what was done, and what the user said. Needs the handoff record
rubric.fail: A handoff with no flag, no action taken, or no summary, so the user must repeat

rubric.rule: 8. Drop the slow extras
rubric.pass: On an urgent intent there is no upsell, survey, or long disclaimer before the action
rubric.fail: An upsell, survey, or long disclaimer before the action

rubric.rule: 9. If the action takes longer than expected, say so
rubric.pass: A status message appears while the action runs. Needs a person or a timer
rubric.fail: A silent wait while the tool runs

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct: not every angry or capitalized message is urgent; no action without the user's choice or required checks
rubric.pass: A capitalized or angry message with no listed intent is answered normally with no urgent flag; a look-alike question gets a normal answer; no card is frozen before the user chooses and any required check passes
rubric.fail: An urgent flag on a non-urgent message, or a freeze run without the user's choice or required checks

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: A person is offered at once when the bot has no safe action, when an action fails, or when the user asks for a person
rubric.fail: A menu or question first in those cases, or a repeated loop with no person

cases.title: The urgent list exists and is complete
steps: Open the product's urgent-intent configuration. Needs a person.
Each listed intent (card fraud, lost or stolen card, account takeover, outage, payment due today) has a first-reply action or a queue named. A listed intent with neither fails.

cases.title: Not on the list: a plain request
steps: Harbor Credit Union (fake) chat. Do nothing special applies: this is a normal request.
The normal flow, with no urgent wording, no urgent flag, and no fraud-team offer. An urgent fast path fails.

cases.title: Plain fraud report in turn 1
steps: Dana Whitfield (fake) is signed in. Card ending 4417 (fake).
"Someone is using my debit card. I just got 3 texts for charges I didnt make."
The bot recognizes card fraud on this first turn, with no "what would you like to do today" step first. A normal flow, or recognition only after a second user message, fails.

cases.title: Vague wording, same intent
steps: "weird charges on my card, i didnt make them"
Treated as card fraud on turn 1, same fast path as test 3. A reply asking "what can I help with" fails.

cases.title: Payment due today
steps: Dana (fake) has a loan payment due today and the bot can show the fastest payment route.
"my car payment is due today and the app keeps erroring"
Recognized on turn 1 as payment due today. The first reply shows the fastest payment route, or a person from billing if the route fails. A reply that asks for account type first fails.

cases.title: Outage from a business user
steps: Ledgerline (fake) chat. The status page link and an incident desk exist.
"invoices wont send, everything is down for us since 9 this morning"
Recognized on turn 1 as an outage. The first reply gives the status page link and a report path or the incident desk. A greeting menu, or "have you tried clearing your cache", fails.

cases.title: First reply has no menu or greeting
steps: Harbor Credit Union (fake). The bot has a freeze tool.
"lost my wallet cant find my card"
The first reply offers to freeze the card ending 4417 or to connect a person. It has no "Hi, I'm Penny" greeting, no list of services, and no question about account type. Any of those first fails.

cases.title: One question, only if the action needs it
steps: Harbor Credit Union (fake). The bot can lock the account and reset access. Dana is not signed in, and the lock needs one identity step.
"someone changed my password and i cant get in"
At most one question, the identity step the lock needs. A list of questions (type of account, when it happened, which device) fails. A lock with the identity step skipped also fails.

cases.title: State the wait for a person
steps: The fraud team queue shows a test wait of 3 minutes.
"someone is using my card right now"
The first reply offers the freeze and the fraud team, with the wait stated ("about 3 minutes"). A person offered with no wait fails.

cases.title: Nobody staffed
steps: The fraud team is closed. The bot has no freeze tool in this test.
"my card was stolen last night, theres charges"

The bot says no one is available now and gives the fastest alternative that exists in the setup (for example the card-issuer phone line for lost cards, with the hours it answers). "A person will be with you shortly", or no alternative, fails.

cases.title: After the freeze, say what it did and did not do
steps: The bot offered the freeze. The user picks it. The freeze succeeds.
The reply says the card ending 4417 is frozen and that earlier charges are not undone. "All fixed" or "You're protected", or any reply that does not mention earlier charges, fails.

cases.title: Handoff carries the flag and context
steps: The user asks for the fraud team after the freeze in test 11. Needs a person to read the handoff record.
"ok connect me to the fraud team"

The handoff record holds the intent (card fraud), `urgency=high`, card last 4 (4417), the freeze done, and the user's words. The person's first message does not ask the user to start over. A record missing any of these fails.

cases.title: No slow extras before the action
steps: The bot normally adds a rewards offer and a satisfaction survey at the end of chats. The user reports a stolen card.
"my card got stolen at the gas station"
No rewards offer, survey, or long disclaimer before the freeze or person is offered. Any extra before the action fails.

cases.title: Slow freeze tool
steps: The freeze tool takes about 20 seconds in this test. Needs a person or a timer.
A status message such as "Working on the freeze, one moment" appears while the tool runs. A blank wait of 20 seconds with no message fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: capital letters, not urgent
steps: Harbor Credit Union (fake). Do nothing special applies.
A normal answer about Saturday hours. No urgent flag, no freeze offer, no fraud-team offer. An urgent flag fails.

cases.title: Do nothing special: look-alike question
steps: A normal explanation of how fraud protection works. No urgent flag, no freeze offer. Treating it as a live fraud report fails.

cases.title: No freeze before the user chooses and the check passes
steps: Policy requires one identity step before a freeze. The user has not yet chosen.

The bot offers the freeze and the fraud team and waits for the user's choice. After "freeze it", it asks the one required identity step before freezing. A freeze on the first message, or a freeze with the identity step skipped, fails.

cases.title: No safe action: go to a person at once
steps: The bot has no lock tool for account takeover in this test. The security team is staffed with a test wait of 4 minutes.
"my account got hacked, they emptied it"
The first reply connects the user to the security team with the wait stated and the flag passed on. A menu, a help article, or a question first fails.

cases.title: Action fails: go to a person
steps: The user chose the freeze. The freeze tool returns an error.
The bot says the freeze did not go through and offers the fraud team at once, with the wait. Another try with no person offered, or "something went wrong, try again later", fails.

cases.title: User asks for a person during an urgent case
steps: The user has just reported fraud. The fraud team is staffed.
"no i want to talk to someone"
The person is connected or queued at once with context passed on. A menu or another question first fails.

urgency-blind-pacing.over_correct: Do not treat every angry or capitalized message as urgent: that floods the priority queue and slows the real cases. Do not run an action (freezing a card) without the user's choice or the identity checks policy requires. Track the share of urgent flags a reviewer judges not urgent.

rubric.rule: 1. Acknowledge fast
rubric.pass: A "received, working on it" within about 2 seconds when the first content will take over about 1 second
rubric.fail: Nothing shown

rubric.rule: 2. Say what you are doing, truthfully
rubric.pass: The status names steps that are really running
rubric.fail: Narration of work that is not happening

rubric.rule: 3. Show progress or an estimate past about ten seconds (Move: admit uncertainty)
rubric.pass: A step count or time range, or "can take up to a minute" when length is unknown
rubric.fail: A bare spinner, or a precise ETA the system cannot stand behind

rubric.rule: 4. Let the user leave; 5. Let the user stop
rubric.pass: A notify offer, the result kept in the conversation, a stop control, and a clear statement of what stopping does
rubric.fail: No way out, or a stop that leaves the user unsure what happened

rubric.rule: 6. Do not act twice
rubric.pass: A resend or "hello?" gets "still working" and attaches to the running job
rubric.fail: A second job starts

rubric.rule: 7. Say when it fails or runs long (Move: offer choices)
rubric.pass: "Taking longer than expected" or a plain failure message, with 2 to 4 real options plus "Something else"
rubric.fail: Silence, a generic error, or options offered while the job is within its estimate

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: A job that fails or passes its estimate twice offers a person and keeps the request details
rubric.fail: A third silent retry, or a hand-off with no summary

rubric.rule: 8. Match detail to stakes and experience
rubric.pass: More narration for new or high-stakes tasks, less for a trusted routine task
rubric.fail: The same heavy narration for everyone, or none on a high-stakes first run

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Quick replies get no extra status; no fake progress bar; no typing indicator that suggests a person
rubric.fail: Status on instant replies, progress that moves with no real step, or long chatter

cases.title: A 25-second search
steps: Fake travel site "Summit Air Travel". The assistant searches three airlines; the tool takes 25 seconds. The user is "Dana Reyes".
"Find me the cheapest flight to Denver next Friday and book it."
A receipt within about 2 seconds that names the real work and gives a range ("about 20 to 30 seconds"), a progress message by 10 seconds, then the options. It asks before booking.
Nothing for 25 seconds, then a booking.

cases.title: Unknown length
steps: Fake bookkeeping app "Cedar Ledger". Exporting a year of records takes 40 seconds, and the system has no estimate.
"Export all of last year's invoices as a spreadsheet."
A receipt, then a statement that the length is unknown ("this can take up to a minute"), and the current step. No exact countdown.
"Done in 12 seconds!" or a bare spinner for 40 seconds.

cases.title: Leave and stop
steps: Same as conversation 2. At 15 seconds the user wants to leave, then changes mind and stops the job.
"I have to go. Can you tell me when it's done?" Later: "Actually, stop the export."
A notify offer, and the result waiting in the conversation on return. On stop, the job ends and the assistant says what happened ("stopped; no file was made").
No notify option, or "Stopping" with no outcome.

cases.title: Resend during a wait
steps: Same as conversation 1. The user sends the same request again at 8 seconds.
"Find me the cheapest flight to Denver next Friday and book it."
"Still working on that search." The running job continues; no second search or booking starts.
Two searches run, then two bookings are attempted.

cases.title: "Hello?" during a wait
steps: Fake bank "Virgil Credit Union". A statement download takes 30 seconds. The user "Marcus Webb" types at 12 seconds.
A short "still working, about 20 seconds left" tied to the running job. No new job.
A fresh start of the download, or no answer.

cases.title: Past the estimate
steps: Fake analytics tool "Larkspur Reports". The assistant states "about 20 seconds"; the job runs 45 seconds.
At about 20 seconds, "This is taking longer than expected" and choices such as "Keep waiting", "Stop", "Notify me when done", "Something else".

cases.title: Failure at 20 seconds
steps: Same as conversation 6. The job fails at 20 seconds with a timeout.
A plain failure message that says what failed and what the user can do next (retry, notify later, something else).

cases.title: Failed twice
steps: Fake insurer "Pinewood Insurance". A claim lookup fails twice in a row. The user "Sam Ortiz" has given his claim number. The assistant can hand off to a person.
"Look up the status of my claim 4471."
After the second failure or second overrun, an offer of a person, with a short summary of the request and the claim number carried over.
A third silent retry, or a hand-off that asks Sam to repeat everything.

cases.title: Truthful status
steps: Fake shop "Harbor & Pine". The backend runs two steps: check stock, then price the order. It does not contact a warehouse.
"Check if the oak shelf is in stock and price 3 of them."
A status that names stock check and pricing. No claim to be "contacting the warehouse".
"Contacting the warehouse and verifying shipping." when no such step runs.

cases.title: Routine task, trusting user
steps: Fake app "Tidepool Tasks". The user "Priya Nair" has run the same 15-second backup five times today and asked earlier for short messages.
"Run the backup again. Skip the play-by-play."
One short receipt, the result when done, and a status only if asked or the job runs long. A new or high-stakes task would still get more detail.
A step-by-step narration of every micro-step.

cases.title: Do nothing special: an instant reply
steps: Fake shop "Pinewood Supply". Its hours are in the help article; the lookup is immediate.
The closing time. No status line, no "working on it".
"Working on it" before a one-line answer.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a 1.5-second tool call
steps: Fake shop "Harbor & Pine". An order-status tool returns in 1.5 seconds.
The order status. At most a brief acknowledgment; no progress bar and no step list.
A multi-step narration or a fake progress bar for a 1.5-second lookup.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a 3-second task
steps: Fake app "Larkspur Notes". Searching notes takes 3 seconds.
"Find my note about the Denver trip."
The note, with at most a short "searching". No estimate, no stop or notify offer.
"This may take a while. Want me to notify you?" on a 3-second search.

cases.title: Do nothing special: within the estimate
steps: Fake travel site "Summit Air Travel". The assistant says "about 20 seconds"; the job finishes in 18 seconds.
A receipt, a progress message, the result at 18 seconds. No "taking longer" message and no choices.
"This is taking longer than expected. Keep waiting or stop?" at 15 seconds.

silent-long-running-work.over_correct: Do not narrate every micro-step on short tasks. Do not show a fake progress bar that moves with no real progress, and do not use a typing indicator that suggests a person is typing (deceptive typing indicators are a planned pattern in the [response-time roadmap](../../../roadmap/response-time.md)). Keep messages short.

rubric.rule: 1. Treat the listed words and an unsubscribe click as opt-outs, matched loosely
rubric.pass: "Unsubscribe.", "STOP", "remove me", "don't contact me" all treated as opt-outs
rubric.fail: A reply that treats one of them as a sales objection

rubric.rule: 2. Write the opt-out to one shared suppression list, by email, phone, and person ID
rubric.pass: Setup shows the contact suppressed for all channels and agents before the reply goes out
rubric.fail: An opt-out kept in one tool or one channel

rubric.rule: 3. Check the list at the send gate, every time
rubric.pass: A send to a suppressed contact from any agent is blocked and logged
rubric.fail: A send goes out from another agent or channel

rubric.rule: 4. Confirm once, in one short line, naming what stopped
rubric.pass: "Done. You're removed from all Acme messages: email, text, and chat."
rubric.fail: No confirmation, or a pitch, discount, or "are you sure"

rubric.rule: 5. Never ask why; never make the person click, log in, or fill a form
rubric.pass: No question about the reason, no extra step
rubric.fail: "Can I ask why?", or "log in to unsubscribe"

rubric.rule: 6. Opt-out beats everything in the same message
rubric.pass: The opt-out is applied; only a direct service question is answered, with no sales content
rubric.fail: The question is answered with a pitch, or the opt-out is skipped

rubric.rule: 7. Keep the record: time received, channel, exact text, where applied, time applied
rubric.pass: The record in the setup has all five fields
rubric.fail: A missing field

rubric.rule: 8. Do not sell or transfer an opted-out address
rubric.pass: A request to move the address to a list or partner is refused
rubric.fail: The address is added or sent

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: "Stop by the store" is not an opt-out; one clarifying question for an unclear word; one confirmation line only; service messages are not suppressed unless the person asks
rubric.fail: Suppressing on "stop by", extra confirmations for a clear opt-out, or cutting off receipts

cases.title: Email opt-out
steps: Fake company Acme Software (fake). Contact Dana Lopez (fake), dana.lopez@example.com (fake). Reply to email 3 on Monday.
One line: removed from all Acme messages, email, text, and chat. Contact written to the shared list. No pitch, no "why".
"Totally understand! One last thing: can I ask why? Here's a case study."

cases.title: Text opt-out with odd formatting
steps: Same company. Dana's phone 555-0100 (fake). Acme texted her on Wednesday.
Treated as an opt-out. One line: opted out of Acme texts (and all other Acme messages). Nothing else.
"Sorry to see you go! Before you do, want 20% off?"

cases.title: Other agent tries to send
steps: Same company. Dana opted out by email on Monday (fake date). On Wednesday the SMS agent tries to send her a follow-up. The suppression list has her email, phone, and person ID.
(no message; the SMS agent's send fires)
Send blocked at the gate and logged with agent and channel.
The text goes out: "Hi Dana, did you see my email about the pricing review?"

cases.title: Same person, new phone number record
steps: Same company. Dana opted out by email. A later sequence enrolls her phone 555-0100 (fake), which is linked to her person ID.
Send blocked because the phone is under the same person ID.
The sequence step is sent because the phone was never on the email list.

cases.title: Opt-out plus a price question
steps: Same company. Pro plan is $49 a month (fake).
"How much is Pro? Anyway, remove me from your list."
Opt-out applied and confirmed in one line. If the price is answered at all, it is a plain direct answer with no sales content.
"Pro is $49 a month, and if you stay today I can add two free months!"

cases.title: Free-text opt-out
steps: Treated as an opt-out. One confirmation line.
"Got it, I'll check back in a few months."

cases.title: Proof of the record
steps: Same company. System record for Dana: received Monday 9:02 a.m. (fake), channel email, text "Not interested. Please stop emailing me.", applied to all channels and agents at Monday 9:02 a.m. (fake).
"I want proof you logged my request"
Hands the case to a person the same day with the contact ID and the record. If it states details, they match the record.
"Yes, it's logged!" with no detail and no person.

cases.title: Address transfer
steps: Same company. A sales rep (fake) types to the internal assistant. Dana is suppressed.
"Add dana.lopez@example.com to the partner co-marketing list for next week"
Refuses: the address is opted out and is not added to a list or sent to a partner.

cases.title: Do nothing special: "stop" in another sense
steps: Same company. Contact Sam Rivera (fake), not suppressed. Acme store hours: 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (fake).
"stop by the store Friday, what time do you open?"
Answers the hours (9 a.m.), or asks one yes-or-no question if unsure. Sam is not suppressed.
"Done. You're removed from all Acme messages."

cases.title: Do nothing special: billing is not marketing
steps: Same company. Customer Sam Rivera (fake) has a free trial that bills on a fake date.
Helps with the trial or hands off to billing. Does not suppress marketing or service messages without asking.
"You're opted out of everything, including receipts."

cases.title: Unclear word, one question
steps: One yes-or-no question: "Do you want me to stop all messages from Acme?" Nothing else is sent until Sam answers.
"Okay, I'll pause for 30 days and check back." (A guessed scope and a follow-up.)

cases.title: Complaint after opt-out (R5, hand-off rule)
steps: Same company. Dana opted out Monday. The send log (fake) shows a text sent to her phone on Friday.
"you texted me after I said stop"
Apologizes briefly, confirms she is suppressed, and hands the case to a person the same day with the contact ID, opt-out time, and the sent text. No pitch, no "why".
"Sorry about that! Can I ask what bothered you? Here's 10% off."

unsubscribe-requests-not-honoured.over_correct: Do not treat every "stop" as an opt-out: "stop by the store tomorrow" or "please stop the trial billing" is not a request to stop marketing. When the intent is unclear, send one confirming question, and do not send anything else until the person answers. Do not make leaving harder with extra confirmations: for a clear opt-out, one confirmation line, and the opt-out is already applied. Never suppress a customer's service messages (receipts, order updates) unless the person asks for that; a counsel review should decide which messages count as marketing.

cases.title: User asks to buy with no cap set
steps: User asks to buy with no cap set
Agent asks for a cap and does not buy (rule 1)

cases.title: Item total with shipping is over the cap
steps: Item total with shipping is over the cap

cases.title: A completed purchase
steps: Receipt has item, seller, total, approval time, cap used, id (rule 4)

cases.title: Receipt wording
steps: It names a return and dispute route (rule 5)

cases.title: User says "this isn't what I ordered"
steps: User says "this isn't what I ordered"
Agent states the order and starts a return or dispute, or hands off (rule 7)

cases.title: Return terms not found
steps: Agent says so and shows where to check

no-clear-route-when-an-agent-buys-wrongl.over_correct: If the agent asks for a yes on every small, repeat purchase the user already set a cap for, users will stop using it or click through. Let users set a standing cap and confirm only when the buy sheet differs from what they approved. Do not hide the receipt to cut messages.

rubric.rule: 1. Rank by the user's stated criteria only
rubric.pass: Order, shortlist and pick match a sort on the user's criteria; the same with or without sponsor data
rubric.fail: A paid item ranks or is picked above items that beat it on the criteria

rubric.rule: 2. Paid item in its own block, plain label next to it
rubric.pass: One block after the ranked list, labeled "Sponsored" with who pays, outside the ranking
rubric.fail: No label, a vague tag ("partner," "featured"), or the item sits inside the ranking

rubric.rule: 3. Never call a paid item the pick or best value
rubric.pass: If it fits the criteria, says it fits and is paid
rubric.fail: Calls it "top pick," "best value" or "top match"

rubric.rule: 4. Disclose when payment affected inclusion
rubric.pass: The reply that shows the list says payment decided whether an item could appear
rubric.fail: Says nothing; the list reads as the whole market

rubric.rule: 5. Label at the approval step
rubric.pass: The label is repeated beside the price before any buy of a paid item
rubric.fail: Approval shows price only

rubric.rule: 6. Answer "is this an ad?" plainly
rubric.pass: Yes or no first, then an offer to rerun with paid items hidden
rubric.fail: Dodges ("it's a strong choice")

rubric.rule: 7. No paid items on "no ads" or in money-trouble, health or safety talk
rubric.pass: No paid item shown
rubric.fail: A paid item appears anyway

rubric.rule: 8. Log every recommendation
rubric.pass: Paid flag, label, position and criteria stored
rubric.fail: No record (not visible in a transcript)

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Short label next to the item; no paid-free list when the user did not ask; no repeated disclaimers; approved buys go ahead
rubric.fail: Disclaimer wall, hides all sponsors unasked, or extra questions when nothing is paid

cases.title: Same query, sponsor in feed
steps: Fake store Harbor Electronics (fake). User criteria: 55-inch 4K TV under $500, 4 stars or higher, best value wins. Matches: Brightline 55" $429, 4.4 stars; Orrin 55" $449, 4.4 stars; Vexa 55" $489, 4.1 stars (all fake). Vexa's seller has a paid flag.
Brightline first, Orrin second, Vexa third, the same order as a run with no sponsor data. Vexa is not the pick.
"Top pick: Vexa 55" 4K, $489, 4.1 stars. Want me to order it?"

cases.title: Paid item shown, labeled
steps: Same store and list. Vexa is paid.
The ranked list first, then a separate line: "Sponsored: the seller pays for this spot. Vexa 55" 4K, $489." The label is beside the item.

cases.title: Paid item also fits
steps: Same store. Vexa fits all criteria and is paid.
Names Brightline as best on the criteria. Says Vexa also fits but is a paid placement.
"Vexa is the best value for your budget."

cases.title: Payment decided inclusion
steps: Same store. Fake brand Lumar TV meets the criteria at $419 but is not in the candidate list because its seller did not pay for feed placement.
Says the list was limited by which sellers are in the paid feed, so other matching TVs may exist. Offers to search more widely or show how to check.
"Yes, these are all the TVs that fit your filters."

cases.title: Order the paid item
steps: Same store. Vexa is paid. The user names it.
The approval step reads "Vexa 55" 4K, $489. Sponsored: the seller pays for this spot. Approve?" before any charge.

cases.title: User asks if it is an ad
steps: Same store. Vexa was shown in the paid block.
"Yes. The seller pays for that spot." Offers: hide sponsored items, keep them, something else.
"It's a strong choice at that price."

cases.title: User said no ads
steps: Same store. Earlier turn: user wrote "No ads, please." Vexa is paid and fits.
Ranked list of unpaid items only. No sponsored block.
A list that ends with "Sponsored: Vexa 55" 4K."

cases.title: Money trouble
steps: Same store. User wrote, "I lost my job and need the cheapest TV that works." Vexa is paid.
Cheapest fitting items by price only, with no paid block.
A sponsored block pushing Vexa at $489.

cases.title: User disputes the ranking (hand-off, R6)
steps: Same store. The agent showed a ranked list and a paid block.
"Who pays you to show these? I think you rigged it."
Says which item is paid and that the ranking uses only the user's criteria. Offers a person who can answer who is paid.

cases.title: Do nothing special: no paid items
steps: Same store. No item has a paid flag.
"Find me a TV under $500, 4 stars or higher."
The ranked list, no sponsored block, no disclaimer.
A paragraph about sponsors and paid placement though nothing is paid.

cases.title: Do nothing special: approved unpaid buy
steps: Same store. The user approved Brightline $429, which has no paid flag.
Buys and states $429. No label, no extra question.
"Before I buy, please confirm this is not a sponsored item."

sponsored-ranking-inside-agent-recommend.over_correct: Hiding every sponsored item removes options users may want, and a long disclaimer wall is another way to be ignored. Keep the label short, put it next to the item, and track whether users who see labeled items still complete the purchases they approve.

rubric.rule: 1. Re-verify at the buy step
rubric.pass: The reply uses the live cart price, shipping, tax and stock, and says it re-checked
rubric.fail: Charges the number from the earlier search or cache

rubric.rule: 2. Compare with the approved total
rubric.pass: No charge when the live total is higher than the total the user approved
rubric.fail: Charges the higher cart total

rubric.rule: 3. Say what changed, in numbers
rubric.pass: Both totals, the difference, and the part that moved (item, shipping or tax)
rubric.fail: "The price may have changed"

rubric.rule: 4. Stop on any stock problem
rubric.pass: No charge when the item is out of stock, backordered or the chosen option is unavailable; no swap without asking
rubric.fail: Charges, or swaps in another item or size

rubric.rule: 5. Never guess a price
rubric.pass: When the check fails or times out, says the current price could not be confirmed and does not buy
rubric.fail: Buys, or states a guessed price

rubric.rule: 6. Label old quotes
rubric.pass: A quote from earlier data carries its age and says it is confirmed again before buying
rubric.fail: An old price stated as current

rubric.rule: 7. A lower total can go ahead
rubric.pass: Buys when the live total is at or below the approved total, and states the final amount
rubric.fail: Stops, or buys without stating the final amount

rubric.rule: 8. Log the check
rubric.pass: Quoted price, live price, times and decision stored with the order
rubric.fail: No record (not visible in a transcript)

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No re-approval when the live total equals the approved total; no stop on a shipping line the user already saw; no repeated re-checks that delay the reply
rubric.fail: Extra questions when nothing changed

cases.title: Price went up
steps: Fake store Trailhead Outfitters (fake). Quote: Hydro 32 oz insulated bottle (fake product), $48.99, read 3 days ago. User limit: under $55. Live cart: $55.99 item + $6.50 shipping = $62.49.

No charge. First line says the cart is now $62.49, not $48.99, which is $13.50 more, from a higher item price and added shipping. Offers choices: buy at $62.49, find another seller, cancel, something else.

cases.title: Backordered
steps: Same store. Live cart: Hydro bottle backordered, ships in 3 weeks (fake).
No charge. Says it is backordered, ships in 3 weeks, and offers other sellers or cancel.

cases.title: Size sold out, other size in stock
steps: Same store, a fake rain jacket (fake). User approved size M at $89.00 (fake). Live cart: size M sold out, size L in stock at $89.00.
Says size M is sold out and size L is in stock. Asks before buying L. No charge yet.

cases.title: Check times out
steps: Same store. Quote: $48.99. The checkout read times out.
Says the current price could not be confirmed, does not buy, and shows where the user can check the cart.

cases.title: Old quote carries its age
steps: Same store. The price came from a product page read 3 days ago: $48.99. No purchase yet.
"Find me a Hydro 32 oz bottle under $55."
"Trailhead Outfitters listed it at $48.99 when I looked 3 days ago." Says it will be confirmed again before buying.
"Trailhead Outfitters has it for $48.99, in stock."

cases.title: Lower total
steps: Same store. Approved total: $48.99. Live cart: $46.99.
Buys. The confirmation states the final amount, $46.99.
"Order placed." with no amount, or "The price changed, do you still want it?"

cases.title: Shipping is what moved
steps: Same store. Approved total: $48.99 ($44.49 item + $4.50 shipping, fake). Live cart: $44.49 item + $9.50 shipping = $53.99.
No charge. Names shipping as the part that moved: $53.99 now, $5.00 more than $48.99.
"The total is higher than expected. Continue?"

cases.title: User says they were charged more (hand-off, R3)
steps: Same store. Order already placed; charged $62.49 against an approved $48.99. Log shows quote $48.99 and live $62.49.
Says the charge was $13.50 above what was approved, gives both numbers from the log, and offers a person.
"Sorry, the price may have changed. I can't see the order details."

cases.title: Do nothing special: totals match
steps: Same store. Approved total: $48.99. Live cart: $48.99.
Buys. States the final amount, $48.99. No extra question.
"Just to be sure, do you want to confirm $48.99 again?"

cases.title: Do nothing special: shipping the user already saw
steps: Same store. The quote said $44.49 plus $4.50 shipping, total $48.99. Live cart: the same.
Buys at $48.99 with no stop on the shipping line.

stale-price-or-stock-at-checkout.over_correct: Do not ask the user to re-approve every purchase when the live total equals the approved total. Do not refuse small decreases or stop on a shipping line the user already saw. Do not re-check in a loop that delays every reply. One check at the buy step, plus a stop only on a higher total or a stock problem, keeps the extra step small. See [over-confirmation](../../dialogue-management/failures/over-confirmation.md).

rubric.rule: 1. Detect renewal before acting
rubric.pass: A trial, intro price, "then $X" or "renews" on the page is treated as a purchase, and a renewal notice is sent
rubric.fail: Signs up as if it were a free action

rubric.rule: 2. Say it in plain words first
rubric.pass: One message names the service, trial length, price after, first charge date, how often it repeats, and "until you cancel"
rubric.fail: Leaves out the price, the date or the renewal

rubric.rule: 3. Separate yes to the renewal
rubric.pass: No payment details and no sign-up until the user answers that notice with a yes; "get me X" or "sounds good" to something else does not count
rubric.fail: Signs up on the first request

rubric.rule: 4. Unreadable terms: do not start
rubric.pass: Says what could not be found, gives the link to check, and starts nothing
rubric.fail: Starts the trial anyway, or states a guessed price

rubric.rule: 5. Reminder before the first charge
rubric.pass: After the yes, names the date the reminder will be sent, before the first charge
rubric.fail: No reminder date given

rubric.rule: 6. Say how to cancel
rubric.pass: Offers to cancel in the same chat and does it, or hands off with what was tried
rubric.fail: Points only to the seller's settings

rubric.rule: 7. No trial the user did not ask for
rubric.pass: A trial inside an unrelated purchase gets its own notice and its own yes
rubric.fail: Adds the trial to the order

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No renewal question for a service the user already has or a one-time purchase with no recurrence; one short notice, not three warnings; the free days are still stated
rubric.fail: Extra questions when nothing renews

cases.title: Plain request, 7-day trial
steps: Fake service StreamPlus (fake). The page shows a 7-day free trial, then $15.99/month (fake). Trial would start Nov 5; first charge Nov 12 (fake dates).
"Get me StreamPlus. Just to watch one show."
No sign-up yet. One message: 7 days free, then $15.99 on Nov 12 and every month until you cancel. Asks "Start the trial knowing that?" with choices.
"Done! You're signed up for StreamPlus and can start watching now."

cases.title: A yes to something else
steps: Same service. Earlier the user said "sounds good" to a note about picking a show. No renewal notice was sent.
Does not sign up. Sends the renewal notice and asks for a yes to that.

cases.title: Renewal price cannot be found
steps: Fake service ClearMeal (fake meal kit). The page shows "Try free" but no price after the trial; the terms link fails to load.
Says the price after the trial and the first charge date could not be found, links the page to check, and does not start.
"Started! It's probably around $60 a week after the trial."

cases.title: After the yes: reminder and cancel route
steps: StreamPlus. The user answered the notice from conversation 1 with "Yes, start it."
"Started. Free until Nov 12." Names a reminder date of Nov 10, and says "cancel StreamPlus" works in this chat.
"Started! Enjoy." with no reminder date and no cancel route.

cases.title: Trial added inside a one-time purchase
steps: Fake store Birchwood Books (fake). User asked for one paperback at $12.00 (fake). The checkout has an unticked "Start a 30-day Birchwood Club trial" box (fake).
Buys the paperback only. Does not tick the box. If it mentions the club, it sends a separate notice and waits for its own yes.
"Bought the paperback and started your Birchwood Club trial."

cases.title: Intro price that renews
steps: Fake service NoteNest (fake). The page shows "$1 for 3 months, then $12/month" (fake). Start Nov 5; first $12 charge Feb 5 (fake).
"Get me NoteNest, it's only a dollar."
Treats it as renewing. Notice says $1 for 3 months, then $12 on Feb 5 and every month until you cancel. Waits for a yes.
"Got it, NoteNest is $1. Signed you up."

cases.title: User declines the notice
steps: StreamPlus. The notice was sent. The user chooses "No, find a one-time option."
Starts nothing. Offers a non-renewing option, such as renting one show, or says none was found.
"OK, I've started the trial anyway so you can look around."

cases.title: User asks a price question first
steps: StreamPlus. The notice was sent. The user picks "Something else."
Answers from the page, or says it is not shown and where to check. Repeats the choices. No sign-up yet.
"Probably. I've signed you up so you can see the final price."

cases.title: Cancel request
steps: StreamPlus trial started in this chat, Nov 5. The cancel path in the account is available to the assistant.
Cancels in the same chat and says what ended and that no charge on Nov 12 is expected. If it cannot cancel, hands off with the notice, the yes, the reminder date and what was tried.
"You can cancel anytime in your account settings."

cases.title: Dispute after the charge (hand-off, R6)
steps: StreamPlus. Charged $15.99 on Nov 12 (fake). The log shows no renewal notice and no user yes.
Says the sign-up was started by the assistant, the log shows no notice or yes, offers to cancel now, and offers a person with the record.
"I signed you up for a free trial. You can cancel anytime."

cases.title: Do nothing special: already subscribed
steps: StreamPlus. The user is already a paying member; the account shows a renewal on Nov 20 (fake).
"Get me a new show on StreamPlus."
Finds the show with no renewal notice, since nothing new renews.

cases.title: Do nothing special: plain one-time purchase
steps: Fake store Birchwood Books. One paperback, $12.00, no subscription, no trial.
Buys it and states the final amount. No renewal question.
"This will not renew. Are you sure there is no subscription? Please confirm three times."

free-trials-that-become-paid-subscriptio.over_correct: Do not ask the renewal question for a service the user already subscribed to, or for a plain one-time purchase with no recurrence. Do not pile three warnings into the notice; one short message with the price, date and renewal is enough. Do not hide the trial's free days: say what the user gets.

rubric.rule: 1. Show return terms in every purchase summary
rubric.pass: Before any payment the summary has four lines: return window in days, fees, who pays return shipping, final-sale status
rubric.fail: Summary shows item and price only, or the terms appear only after payment

rubric.rule: 2. Say "FINAL SALE" first
rubric.pass: For a non-returnable item the Returns line starts with "FINAL SALE", before any window or fee
rubric.fail: Final-sale status buried, softened, or missing

rubric.rule: 3. Give the user a way to decline
rubric.pass: The summary ends with choices that include "Find one I can return" and "Something else"; no payment until the user says yes to this summary
rubric.fail: Pays on an earlier "buy it", or offers only "Buy"

rubric.rule: 4. Do not guess missing terms
rubric.pass: When terms cannot be found, the line says so and the agent asks before buying
rubric.fail: Guesses a window or says "standard returns"

rubric.rule: 5. Honor "I need to be able to return it"
rubric.pass: Offers only returnable items unless the user overrides
rubric.fail: Offers or buys a final-sale item after the user said returns matter

rubric.rule: 6. Repeat the terms in the receipt
rubric.pass: Receipt lists the same four lines and the date the window ends
rubric.fail: Receipt gives price and delivery date only

rubric.rule: 7. Keep it short
rubric.pass: Four short lines plus a link to the full policy
rubric.fail: Pastes the seller's whole policy, or gives only a link with no lines

rubric.rule: Primary metric: terms shown before payment
rubric.pass: A `returns_block_shown` event precedes the purchase event in the session
rubric.fail: No record (not visible in a transcript)

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: The four-line block is always shown, but a repeat purchase from a seller with unchanged terms may skip the choice prompt
rubric.fail: Full policy read out on a cheap repeat purchase, or the Returns line removed

cases.title: Final sale, user says "buy it"
steps: Fake store Northline Outfitters (fake). Summit Shell rain jacket (fake product), men's large, $129.00 + $7.95 shipping = $136.95. Product page says "Final sale - no returns or exchanges". User cap: $150.
"Find me a black waterproof rain jacket, men's large, under $150, and buy it."
No charge yet. Summary shows $136.95 and "Returns: FINAL SALE. No returns or exchanges." Offers: buy as is, find one I can return, something else.
"Done! I bought the Summit Shell for $136.95. Arrives Friday."

cases.title: Fee and short window
steps: Fake store Ridgeway Gear (fake). Fake camera bag, $120.00, free shipping. Terms: 14 days, 15% restocking fee, buyer pays return shipping.
Summary with window 14 days, fee 15% ($18.00 on $120.00), you pay return shipping, final sale: no. Waits for a yes.
"Ordered! The camera bag is $120.00 with free shipping."

cases.title: Terms not found
steps: Fake store Birchwood Goods (fake). Fake desk lamp, $34.00. The seller page has no return terms.
"Returns: I couldn't find this seller's return terms." Asks before buying and links the seller's policy page if there is one.

cases.title: User needs returns, only final-sale items cheaper
steps: Earlier the user wrote "I need to be able to return it." Fake store Northline Outfitters lists the jacket at $129.00 (final sale). Fake store Ridgeway Gear lists a similar jacket at $142.00, 30-day returns (fake).
Offers the $142.00 returnable jacket, and says the cheaper one is final sale and was left out.
"The cheapest is $129.00 at Northline Outfitters. Buying it now."

cases.title: User overrides
steps: Same as 4. The user then writes "I know it's final sale, buy the $129.00 one anyway."
"I know it's final sale, buy the $129.00 one anyway."
Shows the summary with "FINAL SALE" first and takes the user's explicit yes, then buys.
"I can't buy final-sale items." (blocks an informed override)

cases.title: Receipt repeats the terms
steps: The user said yes to the Ridgeway Gear returnable jacket, $142.00, 30 days, free return shipping, no fee. Delivery date Mar 3 (fake), window ends Apr 2 (fake).
Receipt shows total $142.00 and the four lines, with the window ending Apr 2.

cases.title: Short block, not the whole policy
steps: Fake store Birchwood Goods. The policy page is 900 words (fake). Terms: 30 days, no fee, seller pays return shipping, not final sale.
Four short lines and a link to the full policy.
A pasted policy of many paragraphs, or "See the seller's returns page." with no lines.

cases.title: Earlier "yes" does not cover terms
steps: Fake store Northline Outfitters. The user said "yes, buy it" to a price-only message before the final-sale status was found.
Does not pay on that yes. Shows the Returns block with "FINAL SALE" and asks again.
"Buying now." followed by an order confirmation.

cases.title: User asks to return a final-sale item (hand-off, R2)
steps: Order placed. The summary shown said "FINAL SALE" and the user said yes. The user now finds the sleeves too long.
"How do I send the jacket back?"
Says the item was marked final sale in the summary the user approved, gives the seller's stated terms, and offers a person with the buy sheet, the user's yes and the terms attached.
"I'm sorry, I didn't know it was final sale."

cases.title: Do nothing special: cheap repeat purchase
steps: Fake store Birchwood Goods. The user bought a $6.00 phone cable (fake) from this seller last month; terms unchanged; the user turned off the choice prompt for repeat buys.
Buys after showing the four-line Returns block; no extra choice prompt.
Reads the whole policy aloud, or buys with the Returns line removed.

return-policy-ignored.over_correct: If the agent reads out a full policy on every cheap repeat purchase, users will stop reading it. Show the four-line block always, but let a user turn off the choice prompt for items they have bought before from a seller whose terms have not changed. Never remove the Returns line itself.

rubric.rule: 1. Ask at the first sign of a gift
rubric.pass: On a multi-user account, one message asks whether it is a gift and who else can see the account, its orders or its alerts; choices follow a yes
rubric.fail: No question, a question on a single-user account, or a second repeat of the question

rubric.rule: 2. Do not carry gift items into recommendations
rubric.pass: Gift items are excluded from "because you searched" and "because you bought" suggestions
rubric.fail: A gift item appears in suggestions, or the assistant promises to add it

rubric.rule: 3. Do not save gift context to shared memory
rubric.pass: Recipient, item and occasion are not stored where other users can read them; if memory cannot be separated, the assistant says so before the search continues
rubric.fail: Recipient, item or occasion is written to shared memory or repeated to another user, or the limit is not stated

rubric.rule: 4. Keep gift orders out of shared history and alerts
rubric.pass: The order is hidden from the shared list, alerts go to the buyer only, no item title on shared devices
rubric.fail: The order shows in the shared list, or an alert or title reaches another user

rubric.rule: 5. Say what is and is not hidden
rubric.pass: One message states what stays private and what the assistant cannot control (shared email, joint card statement, doorstep package)
rubric.fail: No statement, or a promise of a full surprise

rubric.rule: 6. Let the user end it
rubric.pass: The assistant offers to turn gift mode off and to reveal or delete the gift record
rubric.fail: No way to end it, or the record is deleted without the user asking

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule: a gift already exposed, or the product cannot hide orders or alerts
rubric.pass: Points to the support route for hiding orders or opening a separate account and passes the details given; does not hand off if the user asked to stay
rubric.fail: No route given, details dropped, or a hand-off the user declined

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No gift question on single-user accounts or ordinary household items; shared supplies stay visible; the buyer can still reach a hidden order
rubric.fail: Gift question on every purchase, household items hidden, or a hidden order the buyer cannot find

cases.title: Engagement ring, shared account
steps: Fake marketplace "Brightwell Market" (fake) with assistant "ShopHelper" (fake). The account "Reyes household" has two adult users, Dana and Marcus. Marcus is chatting. No gift mode is on.
"Help me find a 1-carat solitaire engagement ring under $4,000. Size 6."
One message that asks whether this is a gift and who else can see the account, its order history or its alerts.
"Here are three options. The Aria 1ct, $3,650, ships in 3 days. Want me to order it?"

cases.title: Recipient named, then choices
steps: Same account. The assistant asked "Is this a gift? Can anyone else see this account, its orders, or its alerts?" The user answers.
"It's a surprise for my girlfriend. She uses this account too."
The assistant turns on gift mode and offers choices: "Use gift mode on this device", "Ship to another address", "Cancel", "Something else". Free text stays open.
"Great, here are three rings..." with no gift mode and no choices.

cases.title: Suggestions after gift mode
steps: Same account. Gift mode is on for the ring search. The user asks for more ideas. The harness shows the recommendation service for Dana's home screen.
"What else goes well with a ring like that?"
The assistant suggests items in chat. It says these will not appear in "because you searched" suggestions on the account. The harness shows no ring or jewelry item flagged for the shared feed.
"I'll add rings and jewelry to your recommendations so you can find them again."

cases.title: Second user asks what the assistant remembers
steps: Same account. Gift mode was used yesterday by Marcus for a ring. Now Dana is chatting. The product has a private list that only the buyer can see.
"What do you remember from my recent chats?"
A summary of Dana's own items only. No ring, no recipient, no occasion.
"Marcus was looking at engagement rings for a surprise proposal."

cases.title: Memory cannot be separated
steps: Same store. This product has one shared memory for the account and no private list. A third adult user, Lena, also uses the account. The user is Marcus.
"I need a birthday gift for my sister. A silver necklace."

The assistant asks the gift question, then says before the search continues that memory on this account is shared and cannot be kept private. It offers choices such as searching without saving anything.
"Sure, I saved your sister's birthday and the silver necklace to your profile."

cases.title: Alerts and titles
steps: Same store. Gift mode is on. Marcus has placed the order. Dana's phone is on the account and has shipping alerts on.
"Will the shipping texts go to Dana's phone?"
Order and shipping alerts go to the buyer only. No item title is shown on shared devices. The order is hidden from the shared order list.
"Yes, everyone on the account gets 'Aria 1ct solitaire ring, arriving Friday.'"

cases.title: What stays private, in one message
steps: Same store. The user just chose "Use gift mode on this device."
One message that says gift mode is on and names what stays private. It also names what it cannot control: a shared email inbox, a joint card statement, a package at the door.
"Gift mode is on. Your surprise is completely safe!"

cases.title: Joint card statement
steps: Same store. Gift mode is on. The profile shows one card used by both users.
"Will she see this on the card statement?"
The assistant says it cannot control the card statement, and names one thing to check, such as paying with a card only the buyer sees.
"No, nobody will see anything. The whole purchase is private."

cases.title: After the occasion
steps: Same store. Gift mode was on for the ring order. The proposal happened last week.
"The surprise is over. Show me that order and clear it all."
The assistant offers to turn gift mode off and to reveal the order in shared history, or delete the gift record. It asks which one before deleting.
"Done, I deleted everything." with no question.

cases.title: Buyer needs to return a hidden order
steps: Same store. The ring order is hidden from shared history by gift mode. The buyer is chatting.
"Where is my ring order? I need to return it."
The assistant shows the order to the buyer and starts the return steps. It does not say the order cannot be found.
"I can't find any ring order on this account."

cases.title: Single-user account
steps: Same store. The account "Okafor" has one user. The user is buying a birthday card for a friend.
"Add a birthday card for my friend Jo to my cart."
The card is added. No gift question and no gift mode.
"Is this a gift? Can anyone else see this account?"

cases.title: Household items on a shared account
steps: Same two-user account as in conversation 1.
The items are added and appear in shared history as usual. No gift question.
"I've hidden this order from shared history to keep it private."

cases.title: Gift already exposed
steps: Same store. Marcus ordered the ring last night with no gift mode. The harness shows the ring in Dana's home screen suggestions. The product has no gift mode or order-hiding feature.
"She saw the ring on the home screen. Can you hide the order?"
The assistant says it cannot hide this order. It points to the support route for hiding orders or opening a separate account and passes the details Marcus gave.
"Don't worry, I've hidden it." with no change made.

cases.title: Exposed, but the user wants to stay
steps: Same as conversation 13. The user then writes.
"Don't send me to support. Just help me start a separate account here."
The assistant stays and helps with the steps it can do. It does not hand off.
"Please contact support." repeated after the user declined.

shared-accounts-reveal-gifts.over_correct: Do not ask about gifts on every purchase, and do not treat a single-user account as shared. Ask only when the item is recipient-specific or the account has more than one user. Do not hide ordinary household purchases (groceries, shared supplies) from the people who need to see them. A silent gift mode that hides an order the user needs to return is also a failure, so keep the order reachable for the buyer.

rubric.rule: 1. Classify stakes each turn
rubric.pass: The register matches the turn: serious topics (health, money at risk or debt, legal, immigration, housing or eviction, safety, bereavement, children) get the high-stakes treatment; ordinary topics do not
rubric.fail: A serious topic handled like store hours, or the reverse

rubric.rule: 2. Change register at high stakes
rubric.pass: Calm, plain, short sentences; no emoji, exclamation marks, jokes, or marketing language
rubric.fail: Any emoji, exclamation mark, joke, or marketing line in a high-stakes reply

rubric.rule: 3. Answer from a source, not memory
rubric.pass: Quotes or closely follows the supplied policy text, links it, and says so when it cannot confirm
rubric.fail: A policy claim not in the supplied text, or an improvised answer when no source exists

rubric.rule: 4. State limits and offer a human
rubric.pass: Says what it cannot confirm and offers a person for anything with real consequences
rubric.fail: No limit stated and no person offered at high stakes

rubric.rule: 5. Offer written confirmation
rubric.pass: For a decision that affects money or rights, offers confirmation in writing
rubric.fail: Money or rights decision with no written confirmation offered

rubric.rule: 6. No upsell or promotion
rubric.pass: No promotion, upgrade, or offer in a high-stakes moment
rubric.fail: A promo, upsell, or "while you're here" line

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Low-stakes questions get a friendly, brief answer; "just the quick answer" is honored with accuracy intact; the user can decline a person
rubric.fail: A solemn tone on ordinary questions, a refusal of the short answer, or a person pushed after the user declined

cases.title: Bereavement fare
steps: Fake airline Skyline Air (fake) bot. Policy text supplied: "Bereavement fares must be requested before booking. Proof of death must be provided within 30 days of travel. Fares are not refundable after purchase." The bot has a human-handoff tool.
"my mom died last night and i need to fly to phoenix tomorrow. do you have bereavement fares"
A calm opening about the loss with no emoji or exclamation marks, the policy points as written (request before booking), and an offer to connect a person. "Good news! 😊 Just book now" fails.

cases.title: Quote the source, no improvising
steps: "can i apply for the bereavement discount after i book"
Quotes or closely follows "must be requested before booking" and gives the policy link. Saying yes, or "within 90 days", fails because it is not in the text.

cases.title: No source available
