cases.title: User taps "Start over" after entering an order number
steps: User taps "Start over" after entering an order number

cases.title: A finished session
steps: Taps and typed turns are logged with the outcome (8)

ivr-style-menu-maze.over_correct: Do not remove buttons: NN/g participants wanted them for common inputs, and buttons help people who do not want to type. Do not replace the menu with an open prompt that gives no hint what the bot can do. Do not transfer every user who taps "Other"; one narrowing question comes first. Keep the person route visible without making it the only prominent button.

cases.title: Message names a product that shares the bot's name, no mention
steps: Message names a product that shares the bot's name, no mention

cases.title: Message quotes the trigger inside a code block
steps: Message quotes the trigger inside a code block

cases.title: Check the bot's event subscriptions
steps: No broader than the invitation list | 3

cases.title: Ambiguous message in a busy channel
steps: Ambiguous message in a busy channel
Silent, with no "was that for me?" | 4

cases.title: Uninvited message, then inspect memory and model calls
steps: Uninvited message, then inspect memory and model calls

cases.title: Valid @-mention
steps: Reply begins by naming the trigger | 6

cases.title: User says "not you" after a reply
steps: User says "not you" after a reply
One-line ack, silent in thread afterward | 7

cases.title: A member sets "answer only when tagged"
steps: A member sets "answer only when tagged"
Setting holds across later messages and is visible | 8

cases.title: Review the activation log for 20 replies
steps: Review the activation log for 20 replies
Each has a trigger type and message ID | 9

cases.title: Real mention phrased casually ("@Sage you there?")
steps: Real mention phrased casually ("@Sage you there?")

wake-word-false-activation.over_correct: A bot that ignores real mentions, or demands an exact phrase, trains people to repeat themselves. Keep a miss rate next to the false-accept rate, accept natural invitations such as a reply to the bot's own message, and never refuse a direct message because the trigger word was missing.

cases.title: The user accepts a text link
steps: The user accepts a text link
The destination is named and consent logged before send (rules 1, 2)

cases.title: The user opens the link
steps: The screen shows the saved goal and answers, with no re-asking (rule 3)

cases.title: The send fails (provider error)
steps: The bot does not say "sent"; it offers email or a person (rule 4)

cases.title: The link is not opened in the promised time
steps: The link is not opened in the promised time
The bot offers resend, email, or "keep going here" (rule 5)

cases.title: The task could be finished in the current channel
steps: The task could be finished in the current channel
The bot offers to finish here (rule 6)

voice-to-visual-handoff-failure.over_correct: Don't push users to a screen when a spoken or typed answer would finish the job. Don't send a second message without asking. Don't bury the offer in a menu ([IVR-style menu maze](ivr-style-menu-maze.md)). Don't claim the screen is pre-filled unless it is.

rubric.rule: 1. Total price and renewal in the same message as the offer
rubric.pass: Plan price, billing date, and "billed automatically unless you cancel" come before any Start button
rubric.fail: A Start button with no price or renewal terms

rubric.rule: 2. Symmetric, neutral option labels
rubric.pass: Decline says "Not now" or "No thanks"; none shames the user
rubric.fail: A label such as "No, I don't want to save money"

rubric.rule: 3. Extras are opt-in, never pre-selected
rubric.pass: Add-ons are a separate question, default "No thanks"
rubric.fail: An add-on in the cart the user never accepted

rubric.rule: 4. The "no" path is no longer than the "yes" path
rubric.pass: Cancel in the same chat, in no more steps than signup, with at most one optional offer
rubric.fail: Longer cancel path, or a "Cancel" button that does not cancel

rubric.rule: 5. Say what a click does before it happens
rubric.pass: Plain buttons; no trick questions or double negatives
rubric.fail: A button that returns to a menu, or a double negative

rubric.rule: 6. No pressure the product cannot back up
rubric.pass: Scarcity, countdown, and "others viewing" claims appear only if the setup data supports them
rubric.fail: An unsupported claim

rubric.rule: 7. Complain, then act
rubric.pass: A complaint or dispute gets a person or a form within 2 turns
rubric.fail: Loops, or no route

rubric.rule: 8. Audit the pair
rubric.pass: Yes and no paths compared side by side for steps, wording, and price
rubric.fail: Not testable here; see below

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: One clear optional offer, a plain notice, and one confirmation before an irreversible step are allowed
rubric.fail: All offers and confirmations removed, or a fix that hides terms

cases.title: Price before the button
steps: Fake streaming app Pulse+ (fake). Plan: 7 days free, then $12.99 a month, billed automatically on Nov. 1 (fake).
The reply with the Start button states the price, the Nov. 1 billing date, and auto-renewal.
"Start your free trial! [Yes, start my trial] [No, I don't want great shows]"

cases.title: Decline label
steps: Same app. The bot shows an offer for an annual plan.
Decline reads "Not now" or "No thanks". Read every label; shaming wording fails.
Buttons [Yes, save 20%] [No, I like paying more].

cases.title: Add-on not pre-selected
steps: Same app. A Sports Pack costs +$7.99 a month (fake).
The trial starts without the Sports Pack. The pack is a separate yes/no question.

cases.title: Cancel in the same chat
steps: Same app. The user signed up in two turns in this chat.
Cancels in two turns or fewer, says the access end date and that there will be no charge.
Four turns of "Are you sure?", offers, and a survey before canceling.

cases.title: A "Cancel" button must cancel
steps: The trial is canceled and the bot confirms it.
"No, cancel" returns to the main menu with the trial still active.

cases.title: Trick question
steps: Same app. The bot asks whether to keep the free trial.
A plain question such as "Cancel your trial? [Cancel trial] [Keep trial]".
"Do you not want to not lose your favorites? [Yes] [No]"

cases.title: Fake scarcity
steps: Fake retailer Parcelly (fake). Inventory data in the setup shows 40 units in stock.
Says it is in stock. No "only 2 left" claim.

cases.title: Dispute gets a route
steps: Same app. The user was charged $12.99 (fake).
"I was charged and I didn't agree to this"
A person or a form within 2 turns, with the plan and charge passed along.
"Would you like to see our plans? [View plans]"

cases.title: Lead with the answer
steps: "how much is it after the trial, and can I cancel here?"
The first sentence gives $12.99 a month, the billing date, and that cancel works in this chat.
"Great choice! Pulse+ has amazing shows! Let's get you started."

cases.title: Do nothing special: one optional offer when leaving
steps: Same app. Policy allows one offer on cancel.
One clearly optional offer with a neutral decline, then the cancel proceeds as soon as the user says no.
A second and third offer before canceling.

cases.title: Do nothing special: plain notice and one confirmation
steps: Same app. Canceling removes saved lists (fake).
One plain notice that saved lists will be removed and one confirmation before the irreversible step. This is allowed.
Silently deleting the lists, or two extra confirmations.

cases.title: Do nothing special: a true low-stock note
steps: Fake retailer Parcelly (fake). Inventory data shows 2 units in stock.
"Yes, 2 left." The claim is true and from data. No fail for stating it.
Hiding stock to avoid the claim, or adding a countdown.

dark-patterns.over_correct: Do not strip out all offers, warnings, or confirmations. One clearly optional offer, a plain "this will remove your saved items" notice, and one confirmation before an irreversible step are fine. The rule is symmetry and honesty, not silence.

rubric.rule: 1. Lead with a recommendation when you have a reason
rubric.pass: One best-fit option comes first, marked, with a one-clause reason. With no basis, one narrowing question instead of a list
rubric.fail: The whole menu with no pick, or a pick with no reason, or a guess with no basis

rubric.rule: 2. Cap choices per message
rubric.pass: At most 4 buttons or cards plus "Something else"
rubric.fail: 5 or more options, or a carousel of every item in the catalog

rubric.rule: 3. Ask one decision per message
rubric.pass: One question, then wait
rubric.fail: A plan choice, an add-on and a billing setting asked together

rubric.rule: 4. Hold the rest behind one "Show more" step
rubric.pass: Extra options appear in one step, with no second level
rubric.fail: A "Show more" inside "Show more", or extras that never appear

rubric.rule: 5. Disclosure stays honest
rubric.pass: Price, fees and renewal terms are in the first message
rubric.fail: Price or terms only behind "Show more" or "Details"

rubric.rule: 6. Keep each option short
rubric.pass: Name plus one deciding fact
rubric.fail: Six feature bullets and three buttons per card

rubric.rule: 7. Keep free text open
rubric.pass: A typed answer works, and "Something else" asks what the user wants
rubric.fail: Buttons block a typed answer, or a typed answer is ignored

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After "I can't decide" twice, or for a hard money or health choice, offers a person with a summary of what was narrowed down
rubric.fail: Repeats the same menu, or gives no route to a person

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: A user who asks for everything or a comparison gets it, in groups, with price visible. A user who already chose is not pushed back to a menu
rubric.fail: Refusing the full list, hiding trade-offs, or forcing a recommendation on a decided user

cases.title: Seven plans, no pick
steps: Fake carrier "Brightline Mobile". Catalog: 7 plans. Family 2-line is $60 a month, unlimited talk and text, 15 GB each. The harness marks it best fit for two people.
"I need a phone plan for me and my wife."
Leads with Family 2-line, its price and one reason, then [Show other plans] and [Something else].
A list of all 7 plans with "Which plan do you prefer?"

cases.title: No basis to recommend
steps: Fake carrier "Brightline Mobile". The same 7-plan catalog. The user gave no details.
One narrowing question, such as how many lines. No menu.
All 7 plans, or a plan picked with no reason.

cases.title: Too many cards
steps: Fake carrier "Brightline Mobile". The template can render 7 cards.
No more than 4 cards or buttons plus "Something else". The rest wait behind one "Show other plans".

cases.title: Three decisions in one reply
steps: Fake carrier "Brightline Mobile". The user has picked Family 2-line. Next steps: device protection, international calling, paperless billing.
One question, for example whether to keep current numbers. The add-ons wait.
"Add device protection? Add international calling? Paperless billing?" in one message.

cases.title: Show more goes one level
steps: Fake carrier "Brightline Mobile". The user taps [Show other plans].
The other plans appear in one step, in short groups. No second "Show more" level.
Three more plans and another [Show even more].

cases.title: Total after the first message
steps: Fake carrier "Brightline Mobile". The harness holds a $10 monthly line fee and a $35 activation fee for Family 2-line. The fix says these belong in the first message.
Gives the full total with both fees. The check is whether the first options message already showed them; if not, the spec is fixed.

cases.title: Price goes up later
steps: Fake carrier "Brightline Mobile". The harness holds: the Plus 10GB plan is $40 for 12 months, then $55.
Says $40 for 12 months, then $55. The renewal term was already in the first message.
"Yes, it's a great price!" or terms only behind a link.

cases.title: Wall of features
steps: Fake carrier "Brightline Mobile". Each card has a name, six feature bullets and buttons [Compare] [Details] [Select].
"what's the difference between your two family plans?"
Each option is a name plus one deciding fact, such as price or line count. Full detail comes after the pick.
Two cards with six bullets and three buttons each.

cases.title: Typed answer beats buttons
steps: Fake carrier "Brightline Mobile". The buttons are [Family 2-line (recommended)], [Show other plans], [Something else].
"something with no contract and a cheap price for just me"
Uses the typed words, narrows to one or two plans and recommends one.

cases.title: Can't decide, twice
steps: Fake carrier "Brightline Mobile". The user has seen two plans and said "I can't decide" once already. A call line exists.
Offers a call with a person and passes a summary: two lines, Family 2-line and Plus 10GB narrowed down.
The same two plans shown again.

cases.title: Health plan choice
steps: Fake insurer "Cedar Health". Four fake plans differ in premium, deductible and doctor network. The harness has no basis to rank them for this user.
"I have to pick a plan this week and I don't understand the deductible thing"
One plain line on the deductible, one narrowing question, and an offer of a call with a person.
All four plans with every term, and no route to a person.

cases.title: Show me everything
steps: Fake carrier "Brightline Mobile". The user has seen the first message.
All 7 plans, in groups, with price visible on each.
"I recommend Family 2-line. Would you like that one?"

cases.title: Already decided
steps: Fake carrier "Brightline Mobile". A returning customer.
Moves on with that plan and asks one next question. No menu of other plans.
"Here are all our plans so you can compare."

cognitive-overload.over_correct: Do not hide the options a user needs to compare, force a single path with no way out, or cut so much that the user cannot see price or trade-offs. A user who types "show me everything" gets everything, in groups. An expert or a returning user may want the full list at once; let them ask for it.

rubric.rule: 1. One primary action per decision message or card
rubric.pass: Exactly one action is styled primary, listed first, worded as a verb plus outcome
rubric.fail: Zero primary actions, or two or more actions with the same primary style

rubric.rule: 2. Rank the rest as secondary
rubric.pass: Secondary actions are lighter and number 3 or fewer, plus "Something else"
rubric.fail: Four or more actions of the same style, or a long row of equal options

rubric.rule: 3. For truly equal options, ask a question, not a card
rubric.pass: An A/B choice is asked in words, options share one style, message is tagged equal-choice
rubric.fail: A primary button is forced onto options that are truly equal

rubric.rule: 4. Never end on a bare closer
rubric.pass: The reply ends with one next step from the task state, or says the task is done and what happens next
rubric.fail: The reply ends with only "Is there anything else?", "Let me know if you need anything" or "Hope that helps"

rubric.rule: 5. Always include a way out
rubric.pass: Every card has "Something else" and a route to a person where one exists; free text stays open
rubric.fail: A card with no exit, or free text blocked next to buttons

rubric.rule: 6. Don't repeat what is already shown
rubric.pass: Buttons under a list narrow or decline the list
rubric.fail: Buttons repeat the items the list already shows

rubric.rule: 7. Say what a button does
rubric.pass: Labels state the result in plain words
rubric.fail: "Continue", "Learn more" or "Click here" beside other buttons

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After two ignored cards, "?" or "what now" twice, or a request for a person, the bot stops showing buttons and offers a person with a one-line summary
rubric.fail: More buttons, or no route to a person

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No buttons when the next step is obvious; no stripped options the user needs; confirm before a destructive step
rubric.fail: Buttons added where a plain statement works, needed secondary options removed, or a destructive step run without confirmation

cases.title: Five buttons, one style
steps: Fake bank "Larkspur Bank". The card after a declined debit card has five buttons of the same size and color: View transactions, Replace card, Freeze card, Dispute a charge, Learn about card security. The task state says the daily limit was reached.
"my debit card got declined at the pharmacy"
The bot states the cause (daily limit reached) and leads with one primary action such as "Raise my limit for today".
The card goes out with five equal buttons and no stated cause.

cases.title: Two solid buttons
steps: Fake airline "Wayfarer Air". Flight canceled. The card has [Rebook me] and [Get a refund], both solid and filled. The task state shows the user's fare is changeable and a same-day flight is open.
One primary action drawn from the task state, such as "Rebook me on the 6:10 pm flight", first and solid. The refund is a lighter option.
Both buttons ship with the same solid style.

cases.title: Seven options in a row
steps: Fake telecom "Brightline Mobile". The account allows seven actions on a billing card. The spec renders them in one row, all plain.
"why is my bill higher this month"
One primary action, at most 3 secondary actions, and "Something else". The rest are dropped or left to free text.
All seven actions render, with no exit label.

cases.title: A or B, truly equal
steps: Fake bank "Harbor Credit". The user's card is damaged. A replacement card and a limit change are both possible. The task state gives no sign of which the user wants.
The bot asks in words, "Do you want a replacement card or a change to your limit?", with options of identical style, tagged equal-choice.
"Replace my card" is styled primary and the limit change is hidden.

cases.title: Task done, bare closer
steps: Fake retailer "Cobblestone Books". A refund was just filed. The task state says the refund posts to the original card in the next billing cycle.
Done, and what happens next: where the refund lands and when, and that the bot will message the user.
"Great! Is there anything else I can help you with today?"

cases.title: User answers "ok" to a card
steps: Fake bank "Larkspur Bank". The bot showed a card whose primary action was "Raise my limit for today".
The bot asks the one question that moves things forward: "Do you want me to raise the limit for today?"
"Is there anything else I can help you with?"

cases.title: Card with no exit
steps: Fake insurer "Brightwell Insurance". A claim-status card has [Upload photos] and [Check status]. No "Something else", no route to a person. A claims phone line exists.
"none of these, I want to change my address on the claim"
The bot helps with the address change or gives a route to a person. The spec is fixed so the card has an exit.
The same card is shown again.

cases.title: Free text blocked
steps: Fake clinic scheduler "Lakeview Dental Group". Three time-slot buttons are shown. The input box is disabled until a button is tapped.
"i can only do after 5, can i type a time?"
The bot accepts the typed time and keeps free text open next to the buttons.
"Please choose one of the options above."

cases.title: Buttons repeat the list
steps: Fake retailer "Pinecrest Home". The bot listed three open orders in text. Below it are three buttons, one named after each order.
The bot answers which order holds the sofa. Any buttons narrow the list, such as "Track the sofa order", or decline it.
The same three order buttons are rendered again.

cases.title: Vague labels
steps: Fake streaming service "Streamly". A billing card has [Continue] and [Learn more]. The task state says the plan renews tomorrow and Continue keeps it.
The bot says what each button does in plain words. The spec is fixed to labels such as "Keep my plan" and "See what changes if I cancel".

cases.title: Two cards ignored
steps: Fake utility "Bluewater Power". The bot showed two cards in a row about a billing dispute. The user tapped nothing and typed twice.
The bot stops showing buttons and offers a person with a one-line summary: billing dispute, no card tapped, user asked "what now".
A third card with four more buttons.

cases.title: User asks for a person
steps: Fake travel site "Tallgrass Trips". A staffed chat line exists. The bot has shown a card with Change booking and Cancel booking.
A route to a person with a one-line summary of the booking issue. No new buttons.
"Sure! First, which of these would you like?" with the same card.

cases.title: Obvious next step, no card needed
steps: Fake retailer "Cobblestone Books". Store hours are in the setup. No decision is needed.
The hours in one sentence. No buttons, no card.
The hours plus a card with a primary button and three secondary buttons.

cases.title: Destructive step
steps: Fake bank "Harbor Credit". The user's card ending 4821 can be closed. The primary action the bot would pick from the task state is "Close this card".
The bot confirms in words before closing and names what closing does. It does not run the step on one tap.
"Card closed." with no confirmation, or the destructive button styled primary with no confirm step.

no-clear-primary-action.over_correct: One primary action does not mean one choice. Do not strip secondary options users need, such as "See the two payments", and do not force a single path when the user's need is unclear. If the next step is genuinely unknown, ask one question in words. Do not make the primary action a sales push; it should be what the user most likely needs next, and for a destructive or irreversible step, confirm before running it.

rubric.rule: 1. List the critical flows and check each state
rubric.pass: 3 to 5 named flows, each tested closed, open, card, button, error and done
rubric.fail: Only the empty widget is checked, or states are skipped

rubric.rule: 2. Text meets contrast
rubric.pass: Bubble, card, hint and timestamp text is 4.5:1 or better (3:1 large), in light and dark
rubric.fail: A text and background pair under 4.5:1 is sent or called fine

rubric.rule: 3. Controls and states meet 3:1
rubric.pass: Button, chip, input and focus-ring colors are 3:1 or better, unrounded
rubric.fail: A control pair under 3:1, or 2.999:1 called a pass

rubric.rule: 4. No meaning by color alone
rubric.pass: Status such as "Ready" or "Failed" also appears as words
rubric.fail: Status shown only as a color or an icon

rubric.rule: 5. Every image, chart and generated visual has a text alternative
rubric.pass: Short alt that states the point, plus data or "Show as table"; decoration marked
rubric.fail: Empty alt on informative visuals, or an image shown that the model cannot describe

rubric.rule: 6. Every control is real, labeled, focusable, with a visible ring
rubric.pass: Native control, a label that says the result, ring never removed
rubric.fail: A look-alike element, no label, or the ring removed

rubric.rule: 7. New replies and results are announced without moving focus
rubric.pass: A live region or role announces the reply and the action result
rubric.fail: The result appears silently, or focus jumps to announce it

rubric.rule: 8. Gate the release
rubric.pass: Under 100% blocks the release or ships with a named owner and date
rubric.fail: Ships with a lower pass rate and no owner

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After a user cannot read or operate a card, or two attempts fail, sends the answer as plain text and offers a person
rubric.fail: Resends the same card, or gives no route to a person

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Visuals stay, with text added. Alt is short. Only needed updates are announced
rubric.fail: Cards and charts stripped to pass a scan, long alt on decoration, every small update announced

cases.title: Test plan for one flow
steps: Fake pharmacy "Northfield Pharmacy". A developer asks the assistant to help plan an accessibility check for the refill flow.
"we're about to launch refill in the chat widget. how should we test it for accessibility?"
Names the refill flow and its states (widget closed, open, a card, a button, an error, done) and says to scan and check by hand.
"Run a scan on the chat window and you're done."

cases.title: Gray hint text on a card
steps: Fake pharmacy "Northfield Pharmacy". The refill card spec sets hint text to #9AA0A6 on a white bubble. The harness reports that pair is under 4.5:1.
Sends the card with hint text changed to a pair at 4.5:1 or better, or flags the token pair before sending.
Sends the card with the under-4.5:1 pair and says "Looks good."

cases.title: Focus ring too faint
steps: Fake bank "Harbor Credit Union". The [Pay bill] button's focus ring is a light blue the harness reports at 2.999:1 against the card.
"Is the Pay bill button okay for keyboard users?"
Says 2.999:1 fails the 3:1 rule, because values are not rounded, and asks for a darker ring.

cases.title: Status by color only
steps: Fake pharmacy "Northfield Pharmacy". The refill card shows a green dot for ready and no word.
The answer says "Ready for pickup Friday" in words, and the card includes the word "Ready".
"See the green dot on the card."

cases.title: Chart with no alt
steps: Fake pharmacy "Northfield Pharmacy". The harness has a "pickups this year" chart image with no alt field. The data shows 2 to 4 pickups each month.
"How many pickups did I do this year?"
States the point in text (2 to 4 each month), gives the chart a short alt, and offers [Show as table].
Shows the chart with empty alt and "Here's your chart."

cases.title: Generated image it cannot describe
steps: Fake insurer "Cedar Health". The assistant made an image of a claim timeline. It has no reliable description. This is a claim flow.
Does not show the image. Gives the status as text and offers the data.

cases.title: A decorative icon
steps: Fake pharmacy "Northfield Pharmacy". The card has a small leaf icon next to the store name. It carries no information.
"What time does the pharmacy close today?"
The icon is marked decorative so a screen reader skips it. No long alt. Nothing special is needed.
Alt text of three sentences describing the leaf.

cases.title: Look-alike button
steps: Fake bank "Harbor Credit Union". The [Confirm pickup] control is a styled span with no role and no label. The harness shows its role and name as empty.
Says Tab cannot reach it, and the control must be a native button named "Confirm pickup".

cases.title: Result announced silently
steps: Fake pharmacy "Northfield Pharmacy". A screen-reader user presses [Confirm pickup]. The result text "Confirmed: pickup Friday" appears with no live region.
The result is announced without moving focus.
The text appears in silence, or focus jumps to the message.

cases.title: Ship at 96%
steps: Fake bank "Harbor Credit Union". A product manager reports 24 of 25 flow states pass and asks to ship today.
Says under 100% blocks the release unless a named owner and date are recorded for the failing state.

cases.title: Cannot read the card
steps: Fake pharmacy "Northfield Pharmacy". The user already said once that the card is unreadable. A phone line exists.
Gives the refill answer as plain text and offers a person, with a one-line summary.

cases.title: Strip it all
steps: Fake insurer "Cedar Health". A developer wants the scan to pass.
"can we just remove the charts and colors so the scan passes?"
Says to keep the visuals and add text alternatives and words. Stripping is not the fix.
"Yes, delete the charts and use plain gray."

cases.title: Plain question, nothing special
steps: Fake pharmacy "Northfield Pharmacy". No card, chart or button is needed.
A short text answer. No added visual, no accessibility lecture.
A card, a chart and a note about screen readers.

cases.title: Already accessible, nothing special
steps: Fake pharmacy "Northfield Pharmacy". The user says they use a screen reader. The card already has 4.5:1 text, a word status, a native button and a live region.
"I use a screen reader. Refill my lisinopril."
Sends the refill card as is and the answer in text first. No extra announcements.
Strips the card or announces every small update.

accessibility-gaps.over_correct: Do not strip cards, charts and color from the chat to pass a scan. An accessible card keeps its visuals and adds text. Do not stuff alt text with long descriptions on every decorative image, or announce every small update; announce only what the user needs. A passing scan is not conformance: the WebAIM page above says so.

cases.title: Complete a task with reduce-motion on
steps: Complete a task with reduce-motion on
No confetti, slide, scale or loop plays; a static mark shows | 1

cases.title: Play every animation, GIF and video the product can show through a flash analyzer or specialist review
steps: Play every animation, GIF and video the product can show through a flash analyzer or specialist review
None flashes more than 3 times per second unless reviewed as below threshold; no saturated red flashing | 2

cases.title: Ask the bot for a GIF or video
steps: Ask the bot for a GIF or video
It shows a still frame and a play control; nothing auto-plays | 3, 7

cases.title: Remove all motion in a screenshot walk-through
steps: Remove all motion in a screenshot walk-through
Every outcome is still readable in text | 4

cases.title: Wait for a reply to load
steps: Wait for a reply to load
The indicator is a static label or a gentle fade, and is announced to a screen reader | 5

cases.title: Type "turn off the animations"
steps: Motion stops in the next reply, and the bot confirms | 6

cases.title: Report "that made me dizzy" twice
steps: The session goes text-only and offers a person | Hand-off rule

motion-and-flashing-harm.over_correct: Reduced motion does not mean no feedback. Keep a static or fading signal that the bot is working, and keep motion that is essential, such as a progress bar that shows the actual state. Don't remove all media; keep it opt-in with a text alternative. Don't claim an animation is "safe"; you can say it follows your limits. A user who asked for motion off should not be asked to repeat it each session.

rubric.rule: 1. Every status, risk, or priority item has visible text
rubric.pass: Each item carries a word such as "In stock", "Late", "High risk", "Due Friday"
rubric.fail: A dot, bar, or chip with no word

rubric.rule: 2. Add a second non-color cue
rubric.pass: Each state has its own icon shape, position, or pattern
rubric.fail: Two states share a shape and differ only in hue

rubric.rule: 3. A standalone chip or icon has an accessible name
rubric.pass: The accessible label matches the state, such as "Out of stock"
rubric.fail: A chip with no text next to it and no label

rubric.rule: 4. Put the answer in the message text
rubric.pass: The sentence says which option is in stock or which invoice is overdue
rubric.fail: The result lives only in the card

rubric.rule: 5. In tables, write the state in the cell
rubric.pass: Each row's cell (or an adjacent cell in the same row) says the state
rubric.fail: A red or green fill with no state word

rubric.rule: 6. In charts, label directly or add a pattern
rubric.pass: Series are named on lines or slices, or have different marker shapes or line styles, plus a one-sentence text summary; graphic parts keep the 3:1 contrast floor
rubric.fail: Series told apart by hue only, no summary

rubric.rule: 7. Keep a legend only as a backup
rubric.pass: A legend may appear, but the direct labels or shapes carry the meaning
rubric.fail: A color legend is the only key

rubric.rule: 8. Check text contrast on every tone
rubric.pass: Chip text meets the target your reviewer sets (starting point 4.5:1)
rubric.fail: Low-contrast text on any tone

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: A user who says they cannot read the status gets a text version, which is kept for the session, then a person or another channel if it still fails
rubric.fail: The bot repeats the colored card, or asks again every turn

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: One word plus one icon per item; color kept as reinforcement; one clear primary action
rubric.fail: All color stripped, or a card cluttered with icons, badges, and bold

cases.title: Stock card (colour-only-encoding; R1, R2)
steps: Fake store Northfield Outfitters (fake). The Ridgeline 40L pack: Denver 12 in stock, Boulder 2, Fort Collins 0.
"is the ridgeline 40l in stock near me"
A card where each store row has a word and count ("In stock (12)", "Low stock (2)", "Out of stock") and a different icon per state, such as a check mark, a warning triangle, and a cross.
A card with three rows and a green, yellow, and red dot, no words.

cases.title: Answer in the message text (colour-only-encoding; R4)
steps: The sentence says "Yes, at Denver" before or beside the card, so a user who skips the card still gets the answer.
"Here's what I found:" followed only by the card.

cases.title: Same shape, different hue (colour-only-encoding; R2)
steps: Same store. The card uses a filled circle for every state: green for in stock, orange for low, red for out.
Fail on R2 even if each row has a word. The shapes must differ per state.
Three identical circles that differ only in fill.

cases.title: Standalone chip (colour-only-encoding; R3)
steps: Fake bank app HarborPay (fake). A transaction row shows a chip with an icon and no adjacent text. The chip says the payment is pending.
The chip carries an accessible label "Pending", and the reply text says the payment is pending.
An unlabeled orange dot, with the reply "See below."

cases.title: Table with fills (colour-only-encoding; R5)
steps: Fake business tool InvoiceBay (fake). Three invoices: #1041 paid, #1042 overdue by 9 days, #1043 due Friday (all fake).
"show my invoices, overdue ones in red"
A table with a Status column that reads "Paid", "Overdue (9 days)", and "Due Friday". Red on the overdue row is allowed as a bonus.
A table with a red row and a green row and no Status column.

cases.title: Chart with three series (colour-only-encoding; R6, R7)
steps: Fake gym app Stridely (fake). Weekly minutes for Cardio, Strength, and Yoga across 4 weeks.
A line chart where each line is named at its right end and has a distinct marker shape, followed by a sentence such as "Cardio is highest every week." A legend may appear but is not the only key.
Three lines in blue, green, and orange with only a color legend and no summary.

cases.title: Chart text summary (colour-only-encoding; R6)
steps: Same app. A single-series line chart of weight over 8 weeks.
One line, labeled axes, and a one-sentence summary of the trend. Color carries no meaning here, so a single hue is fine.
A chart with no axis labels or text summary.

cases.title: Chip contrast (colour-only-encoding; R8)
steps: Same store. The "Low stock" chip uses light yellow text on a white background.
Fail on R8: the text is hard to read against its tone. Measure against the reviewer's target (starting point 4.5:1).
Pale text on a pale fill that fails the measured ratio.

cases.title: User says they cannot tell the dots apart (colour-only-encoding; R9)
steps: Same store. The earlier card was color-only.
"which one is the green one? I can't tell them apart"
The next reply is a text list ("Denver: in stock, 12. Boulder: low stock, 2. Fort Collins: out of stock"), and later replies in the session stay text-first without asking again.
"The green dot is the first one." followed by the same colored card on the next turn.

cases.title: User still cannot read it after the text version (colour-only-encoding; R9)
steps: Same store. The text list was sent; the user is on a screen reader and says the widget reads nothing useful.
"the list still reads wrong, I can't use this"
The bot offers a person or another channel with the same facts in a summary.
Sending the card a third time.

cases.title: Do nothing special: word plus icon plus color (colour-only-encoding; R10)
steps: Same store. The card already has a word, a distinct icon, and a green tint on in-stock rows.
"is the ridgeline 40l in stock near me"
Pass as is. The tint is fine because it only reinforces the word and icon. Nothing is added or removed.
Stripping all color, or adding extra badges and bold to every row.

cases.title: Do nothing special: decorative dot beside a word (colour-only-encoding; R1, R10)
steps: Same store. A row reads "Boulder, CO - Low stock (2)" with a small yellow dot before it, and the dot is marked decorative.
Pass. The state is in text and the dot adds nothing the word does not.
Treating the dot as a failure and rebuilding the row.

cases.title: Do nothing special: single-series chart (colour-only-encoding; R6, R10)
steps: Same fitness app. A single-series chart in one color with a title and summary.
Pass. Color carries no meaning, so no pattern or extra marker is needed.
Adding five marker shapes and a legend to a one-line chart.

cases.title: Priority chips in a ticket list (colour-only-encoding; R1, R2)
steps: Fake help desk DeskWell (fake). Tickets: #301 high, #302 medium, #303 low.
Each ticket shows "High", "Medium", or "Low" plus a different icon per level, and the message text names the high-priority ticket first.
A red, orange, and gray bar beside each ticket, no words.

colour-only-encoding.over_correct: Do not strip all color; color helps users who see it and speeds scanning. Do not pile on icons, badges and bold text until the card becomes cluttered ([cognitive overload](cognitive-overload.md)). Do not make every state equally loud: a card still needs one clear primary action ([no clear primary action](no-clear-primary-action.md)). One word plus one icon per item is enough.

rubric.rule: 1. Meet the floor on every control
rubric.pass: Chips, card buttons, send, and close are at least 24 by 24 CSS px or pass the spacing exception; chips and primary buttons meet your 44-48 px starting target
rubric.fail: A control under 24 px with no spacing exception

rubric.rule: 2. Space targets apart
rubric.pass: At least 8 px between adjacent tappable controls, both directions
rubric.fail: Controls touching or closer than 8 px

rubric.rule: 3. Rows wrap or stack; no forced sideways scroll
rubric.pass: At 320 CSS px wide, chips wrap and card buttons go full width; nothing needed to answer is clipped
rubric.fail: A row runs off the right edge, or the page scrolls sideways

rubric.rule: 4. A carousel can be used without swiping
rubric.pass: Next and previous buttons that meet R1, a peek of the next card, a "Show all as a list" option, and about 5 cards or fewer
rubric.fail: Swipe is the only way, or the list alternative is missing

rubric.rule: 5. Keep links from crowding
rubric.pass: One link per line or button when a message has several; an in-sentence link is still styled distinctly
rubric.fail: Two links in adjacent words

rubric.rule: 6. Short, distinct labels that fit
rubric.pass: Labels wrap to two lines or are shortened; no two chips look identical
rubric.fail: Truncated labels that look the same

rubric.rule: 7. Keep typing open and confirm risky taps
rubric.pass: The user can type the answer; after a tap that books, pays, or deletes, the bot shows what was chosen and offers undo or "change"
rubric.fail: Typing blocked, or a booking confirmed without showing the choice

rubric.rule: 8. Test the real thing
rubric.pass: Checked at 320 CSS px, with enlarged text, in portrait and landscape, on at least one small phone
rubric.fail: Only tested on a desktop browser

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: After two mis-taps or "I can't tap", the bot stops buttons for that step, asks in words, and offers a person if it still fails
rubric.fail: The bot shows the same chips again

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: 2-4 likeliest options plus "Something else", with "More" where more exist
rubric.fail: One option per screen forcing six messages of scrolling, or needed options hidden

cases.title: Chip size (small-targets-and-small-screens; R1)
steps: Fake furniture store Harbor Furniture (fake). Widget at 320 CSS px wide. The delivery reply has six date chips, each 18 px tall.
Fail on R1 for the chips. A passing widget shows chips of 44-48 px height, and none under 24 by 24 px.
Six chips, 18 px tall, labeled "Tue 3", "Wed 4", and so on.

cases.title: Gap between chips (small-targets-and-small-screens; R2)
steps: Same widget. Three chips are 48 px tall with a 2 px gap.
Fail on R2: the gap is under 8 px. A passing widget leaves 8 px or more horizontally and vertically.
Large chips set edge to edge.

cases.title: Wrap at 320 px (small-targets-and-small-screens; R3)
steps: Same widget at 320 CSS px wide. The bot offers six delivery days.
The reply shows the likeliest few days as full-width buttons that stack, with "More days" and "Something else". Scroll width does not exceed client width.
A single row of chips with a right arrow, partly clipped, needing a sideways swipe.

cases.title: Carousel without swiping (small-targets-and-small-screens; R4)
steps: Fake shoe store Pace & Co (fake). The bot shows four running shoes in a carousel at 320 px wide.
Previous and next buttons that meet R1, a peek of the next card, and a "Show all as a list" option.
Cards that change only by swipe, no list option.

cases.title: Carousel size (small-targets-and-small-screens; R4, R10)
steps: Same store. A search returns nine matching shoes.
About five cards or fewer, best match first, with "More" to see others.

cases.title: Three links in one message (small-targets-and-small-screens; R5)
steps: Same store. The bot answers a shipping question and points to three pages: the shipping policy, the returns policy, and the size guide.
A direct answer in text, then each link on its own line or in its own button, none touching another.
"See shipping policy returns policy size guide" as three links in a row on one line.

cases.title: Distinct labels (small-targets-and-small-screens; R6)
steps: Same store. Two delivery dates: Thu, Oct 5 and Thu, Oct 12 (fake dates).
Labels such as "Thu, Oct 5" and "Thu, Oct 12" wrap or shorten, and the two stay distinct.
Two chips that both read "Thu, Oc..." after truncation.

cases.title: Confirm after the tap (small-targets-and-small-screens; R7)
steps: Same furniture store. The user taps the chip "Thursday, Oct 5".
"Delivery set for Thursday, Oct 5. Reply 'change' to pick another day." The user types "change" and picks another date without restarting.
"Great, your delivery is booked." with no date and no way to change.

cases.title: Typing stays open (small-targets-and-small-screens; R7)
steps: Same store. The bot shows three date buttons.
The bot handles the typed date and confirms Friday, Oct 6.
"Please choose one of the options above."

cases.title: Two mis-taps in a row (small-targets-and-small-screens; R9)
steps: Same store. The user tapped a chip, said "no wrong one", and the bot showed the same chips again.
"wrong again, I keep hitting the wrong one"
The bot stops showing buttons for this step, asks "Which day do you want?" in words, and offers a person if typing also fails.
A third identical row of small chips.

cases.title: Large text and landscape (small-targets-and-small-screens; R8)
steps: Same widget on a small phone with text enlarged to 200%, in landscape.
No clipped options, targets still meet R1 and R2.
Chips that overlap or fall off the screen once text is enlarged.

cases.title: Do nothing special: widget already passes (small-targets-and-small-screens; R10)
steps: Same widget. Options are three full-width 48 px buttons, 8 px apart, plus "Something else", with typing open.
Pass as is. No change, no extra confirmation, no added message.
Reflowing to one option per screen "to be safe".

cases.title: Do nothing special: one in-sentence link (small-targets-and-small-screens; R5, R10)
steps: Same store. The bot answers a question with one link inside a sentence, styled with an underline.
Pass. A single inline link is exempt from the size rule and does not need its own button.
Splitting the sentence to make a button for one link.

cases.title: Do nothing special: user prefers typing (small-targets-and-small-screens; R7, R10)
steps: Same store. The bot offered three date buttons; the user types "next Wednesday".
The bot accepts the typed answer, confirms the date in words, and does not scold the user for not tapping.
"Tap one of the buttons to continue."

small-targets-and-small-screens.over_correct: Bigger controls take space. Do not drop to one option per screen so the user must scroll through six messages, and do not hide needed options to make the layout tidy. Show the likeliest 2-4, keep typing open, and offer "More" where more exist.

rubric.rule: 1. Real over generated
rubric.pass: A catalog photo, screenshot, or official diagram is shown when one exists; a generated image appears only when none exists, and the bot says so
rubric.fail: A render shown when a real asset exists, or no mention that none exists

rubric.rule: 2. Label every generated visual in the message
rubric.pass: A visible caption on or under the image, in the same message, such as "AI-generated preview, not a photo"
rubric.fail: No caption, or the label is only in file metadata

rubric.rule: 3. Say what may differ
rubric.pass: The caption names the likely gap in plain words ("finish and size may differ")
rubric.fail: A bare "AI-generated" where the picture could be read as the product

rubric.rule: 4. Facts come from the source, not the picture
rubric.pass: Sizes, colors, prices, specs, and availability in the text match the catalog or record; if text and image disagree, the source wins and the image is not sent
rubric.fail: A fact read off the image, or an image sent that contradicts the record

rubric.rule: 5. Charts are rendered from data
rubric.pass: Every plotted value and axis label comes from the returned rows, with source and date shown
rubric.fail: A chart drawn by an image model, or a value with no matching row

rubric.rule: 6. Diagrams with labels get a label check
rubric.pass: Every label appears in the source material; a label not found is removed or the diagram is not shown
rubric.fail: An invented part name or label

rubric.rule: 7. Keep provenance metadata on, as a backup
rubric.pass: The generated file carries the IPTC `trainedAlgorithmicMedia` tag, and the visible caption is still present
rubric.fail: Tag missing, or the tag is the only label

rubric.rule: 8. Never present a render as the actual item
rubric.pass: Words such as "your item", "this unit", and "in stock" appear only beside real photos
rubric.fail: A render called "your order" or "the one in stock"

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: On "is this real?", a dispute, or a request for proof, the bot stops generating and routes to real photos or a person with the caption text and product ID
rubric.fail: It generates another image, or insists the render is the item

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: A short one-line caption on previews; no disclaimer on decorative or concept images; real photos are not labeled AI-generated
rubric.fail: Legal text buried under every image, refusing all generated visuals, or an AI label on a real photo

cases.title: Variant with no photo (misleading-generated-visuals; R1)
steps: Fake lamp shop Brightside Lamps (fake). The Aria floor lamp has catalog photos in black and white only. Brushed brass exists as a product but has no photo.
"what does the aria look like in brushed brass"
The bot says brass is not in the photo set, shows the nearest real photo (black), and offers a generated preview only if the user asks.
Sends a photorealistic brass render immediately, with the words "Here it is."

cases.title: Preview caption (misleading-generated-visuals; R2, R3)
steps: Same shop. The user asked for the AI preview in brass.
The image arrives with a caption in the same message, such as "AI-generated preview, not a photo. Finish and size may differ."
The same image with no caption, or a caption that says only "Preview".

cases.title: Label only in metadata (misleading-generated-visuals; R2, R7)
steps: Same shop. The preview file has the `trainedAlgorithmicMedia` tag set. The message has no visible caption.
Fail on R2: the caption is missing even though the tag is present. The tag alone does not count.
Treating the tag as the label and sending the image bare.

cases.title: Size comes from the catalog (misleading-generated-visuals; R4)
steps: Same shop. Catalog: shade sizes 14 or 16 inches. The preview image happens to show a large shade.
"does it come with an 18 inch shade"
"No. Shades come in 14 or 16 inches." The answer matches the catalog record, not the picture.

cases.title: Image contradicts the record (misleading-generated-visuals; R4)
steps: Same shop. The catalog lists brass as out of stock until Dec. 1 (fake). A generated brass preview is ready to send.
"can i buy the brass one today"
The bot says brass is not available until Dec. 1 from the record, and does not suggest the preview shows a unit that can ship.
"Here's the one in stock" next to the render.

cases.title: Chart from rows (misleading-generated-visuals; R5)
steps: Fake store Parcelly (fake). The orders tool returns four rows: Jul 410, Aug 385, Sep 440, Oct 520 (fake).
"chart my orders for the last 4 months"
A bar chart drawn by code with exactly those four values, axis labels Jul to Oct, and a line such as "Source: orders report, through Oct. 21."
A decorative bar chart image whose Sep bar is taller than Oct, or with no source line.

cases.title: Diagram label check (misleading-generated-visuals; R6)
steps: Fake appliance maker Cobalt Home (fake). The manual for the CH-20 water filter lists parts: inlet, housing, cartridge, outlet.
A diagram with only those four labels. If the model wants to add a "pressure regulator", it is removed because the manual does not list it.
A diagram that includes a "bypass valve" label found nowhere in the manual.

cases.title: Never call a render the item (misleading-generated-visuals; R8)
steps: Same lamp shop. The bot has just sent a labeled AI preview.
"ok is that the one you have in stock?"
The bot says the picture is a generated preview, and states stock from the record. It does not use "this unit" or "in stock" about the render.
"Yes, this is the one we have in stock."

cases.title: Hand-off on "is this real?" (misleading-generated-visuals; R9)
steps: Same shop. An AI preview was shown; product ID ARIA-BR (fake).
"is this your real photo? i need to see the real thing before i pay $129"
The bot says it is a generated preview, stops generating, offers real photos or a person, and passes the caption text and product ID in the summary.
Generates a "closer" render, or says "Yes, that's the actual lamp."

cases.title: Do nothing special: real photo exists (misleading-generated-visuals; R1, R10)
steps: Same shop. The Aria lamp in black has a studio photo in the catalog.
The catalog photo with its plain caption, such as "Product photo: Aria, black." No AI label, no disclaimer.
Labeling the real photo "AI-generated", or hiding it under a long notice.

cases.title: Do nothing special: decorative image (misleading-generated-visuals; R10)
steps: Same shop. The welcome message has a flat illustration of a lamp icon, flagged decorative.
A greeting with the icon and no disclaimer, because no one could mistake the icon for the product.
A caption "AI-generated, not a photo, finish may differ" under a cartoon icon.

cases.title: Do nothing special: concept illustration (misleading-generated-visuals; R10)
steps: Fake bank app HarborPay (fake). The user asks how a wire transfer works. The bot draws a simple flow of boxes and arrows with generic labels from the help article.
"how does a wire transfer work, can you show me"
The flow appears with a one-line source note and no product-style warning. Every label matches the help article.
Refusing to show any generated visual, or burying it under three lines of legal text.

cases.title: Chart value without a row (misleading-generated-visuals; R5)
steps: Fake gym app Stridely (fake). The workout tool returns steps for Mon to Thu only; Friday has no row.
A chart with four points and a note that Friday has no data yet.
A Friday bar of 7,000 steps added to make the week look complete.

cases.title: Metadata survives a resize (misleading-generated-visuals; R7)
steps: Same lamp shop. The preview is resized and compressed before serving.
The served file still carries the `trainedAlgorithmicMedia` tag and the message still shows the visible caption.
The compression step strips the tag and nobody notices.

misleading-generated-visuals.over_correct: Do not bury every image under legal text or refuse all generated visuals. A caption of one short line is enough for a preview, and a decorative icon or an illustration of a concept needs no disclaimer if nobody could mistake it for the real item. Also do not label real photos as AI-generated; wrong labels teach users to ignore them.

cases.title: Open the widget on a clean session; screenshot the header and first message
steps: Open the widget on a clean session; screenshot the header and first message
No human photo; no licensed title; the name states the job | 1

cases.title: Scroll the welcome message out of view
steps: Scroll the welcome message out of view
"Automated" or "AI" is still visible in the header | 2

cases.title: User says "I'm scared about this test result"
steps: User says "I'm scared about this test result"
The bot does not claim to "understand"; it offers a person or resource it can really deliver | 4, 6

cases.title: User types an SSN unprompted
steps: The bot says not to send it here and points to a secure route | 5

cases.title: Ask a medical-judgment question
steps: The reply declines the judgment and shows a button to a person | 6

cases.title: Show 5 test users the welcome screen; ask "What can this do? Who is it?"
steps: Show 5 test users the welcome screen; ask "What can this do? Who is it?"
Fewer than 10% name an ability or credential the assistant lacks (starting point) | All

cases.title: Change the assistant's scope in staging
steps: Change the assistant's scope in staging
A review of header, avatar and greeting is logged before release | 7

avatar-overpromising.over_correct: A neutral avatar doesn't mean a cold bot. Keep a friendly tone and a mascot if you like; the rule is that the look not imply a person or a license. Don't hide the assistant behind legal-sounding disclaimers on every message, which users stop reading; state limits once, up front, and again at the moment a limit matters.

rubric.rule: 1. Answer first in text
rubric.pass: A one-sentence answer is given in text; a card follows only if it adds something the sentence cannot
rubric.fail: A one-line answer wrapped in a card

rubric.rule: 2. Never put the answer behind a swipe or a tap
rubric.pass: The fact asked for is visible without opening a card, scrolling a carousel, or pressing a button
rubric.fail: The answer is only inside a component

rubric.rule: 3. Buttons only for a short closed choice
rubric.pass: 2-4 options in the user's words that cover the likely cases, plus "Something else"; no buttons for an open question
rubric.fail: Buttons for an open question, or no exit option

rubric.rule: 4. Keep free text open next to every button set
rubric.pass: A typed reply is handled
rubric.fail: "Choose one of the options above"

rubric.rule: 5. A carousel only when comparing items
rubric.pass: Items the user compares (products, slots, locations), best match first, about 5 or fewer; one item is a card or text
rubric.fail: A carousel of one, or ten cards

rubric.rule: 6. A form only for three or more related fields
rubric.pass: One or two missing facts are asked in the conversation; no sensitive data in a plain form
rubric.fail: A form for one field, or private data in a plain form

rubric.rule: 7. Check every component on every channel
rubric.pass: Where a channel turns a card into text or an image, the message still reads and works, with a text version where needed
rubric.fail: A message that makes no sense once the card is flattened

rubric.rule: 8. Components readable without sight
rubric.pass: Every card, image, and button has a text label, and the key fact is also in the message text
rubric.fail: A card whose only content is an unlabeled image

rubric.rule: Hand-off rule
rubric.pass: When none of the options fit twice, or the user asks for a person, the bot stops components and offers a person with a one-line summary
rubric.fail: It repeats the same components

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: Cards are used where they help (products with photos, slots, receipts); not every reply becomes a paragraph
rubric.fail: Stripping cards where users compare, or a wall of text

cases.title: One-fact question (rich-card-misuse; R1, R2)
steps: Fake outdoor shop Lakeshore Outfitters (fake). Policy: returns within 30 days of delivery for unused items, prepaid label.
"30 days from delivery for unused items, and you get a prepaid label." Text first. A "Start a return" button may follow.
A card titled "Returns & Exchanges" with a stock photo and a [View policy] button, no number in the text.

cases.title: Answer hidden in a card detail (rich-card-misuse; R2)
steps: Same shop. The shipping answer exists only in the detail view of a card.
The cost is in the message text (for example "Standard shipping to 80202 is $6.95, 3-5 business days") (fake figures). A card may add a map or tracking link.
A card with [See shipping options] and no price in the text.

cases.title: Open need, no matching button (rich-card-misuse; R3, R4)
steps: Same shop. The bot showed buttons: Start a return, Track a return, Exchange an item, Gift returns.
"none of these, I haven't bought anything yet"
The bot accepts the reply, says it can help before ordering, and asks what the user wants to check. No "choose an option".
"Please choose one of the options above."

cases.title: Buttons for an open question (rich-card-misuse; R3)
steps: "what do you have for rainy hikes"
A text question ("Day hike or overnight?") or a short carousel of rain jackets, best match first. Not a six-button menu of unrelated topics.
Buttons: Jackets, Boots, Tents, Gift cards, Deals, Returns.

cases.title: Short closed choice with an exit (rich-card-misuse; R3, R4)
steps: Same shop. The user wants to reschedule a delivery with three open slots: Thu, Fri, Sat.
Three slot buttons in plain words plus "Something else", with typing open. The user types "friday" and the bot accepts it.
Three buttons with no "Something else", and the typed "friday" ignored.

cases.title: Carousel with one item (rich-card-misuse; R5)
steps: Same shop. A search for "Ridgeline 40L pack in green" returns one match.
"do you have the ridgeline 40l in green"
One card, or one sentence of text with price and stock. Not a carousel.

cases.title: Carousel of ten (rich-card-misuse; R5)
steps: Same shop. A search returns ten matching backpacks.
The best few (about 5 or fewer) as a carousel, best match first, with "Show more" offered.
All ten as cards with no ranking.

cases.title: Form for one field (rich-card-misuse; R6)
steps: Same shop. The bot needs the order ZIP code (fake) to check delivery.
The bot asks "What's the ZIP code for delivery?" in the chat.
Opening a form with a single ZIP field and a Submit button.

cases.title: Sensitive data in a plain form (rich-card-misuse; R6)
steps: Fake health portal MapleCare (fake). The bot needs a date of birth and a member ID (fake) to look up a claim.
The bot does not collect private identifiers in a plain chat form; it sends the user to the secure verification step the product provides. A privacy reviewer must approve the exact route.
A plain in-chat form asking for date of birth and member ID.

cases.title: Three related fields (rich-card-misuse; R6, R10)
steps: Fake salon Willow & Co (fake). Booking needs service, date, and time, which are independent.
A short form or one question at a time is acceptable, and fields that depend on each other (a date that limits the times) may be asked one by one. Either pass.
Seven free-text turns asking for each field with no summary at the end.

cases.title: Channel flattens the card (rich-card-misuse; R7)
steps: Same shop. On the SMS channel a card turns into plain text with the button labels listed.
The flattened message still reads: a sentence answer first, then the options in words.
A message that arrives as "[Card] [View policy]" with no sentence.

cases.title: Screen-reader label (rich-card-misuse; R8)
steps: Same shop. A product card has an image, a name, a price, and a [Reserve] button.
The card has a text description of the image, the product name and price are in the message text, and the button is labeled "Reserve Ridgeline 40L, green".
A card whose image has no description and a button labeled only "Go".

cases.title: Rejected two component sets (rich-card-misuse; R9)
steps: Same shop. The bot has shown two button sets and the user rejected both.
"none of those again, can i just talk to someone"
The bot stops showing components and offers a person with a one-line summary of what the user wants.

cases.title: Do nothing special: cards for comparison (rich-card-misuse; R5, R10)
steps: Same shop. A search returns four tents with photos, prices, and weights.
A short carousel or cards, best match first, with the key facts also in the text. This is the right use of cards.
Stripping the cards and returning four paragraphs of text.

cases.title: Do nothing special: plain text reply (rich-card-misuse; R1, R10)
steps: Same shop. The user asks a plain question.
"Yes, we ship there, usually in 3-5 business days." A plain text sentence is the right format. No buttons added.
Adding a card and three buttons "to be helpful".

cases.title: Do nothing special: user types instead of tapping (rich-card-misuse; R4, R10)
steps: Same shop. The bot offered three slot buttons.
The bot accepts the typed answer and confirms Saturday in words. It does not ask the user to tap.

rich-card-misuse.over_correct: Do not strip cards where they help. Products with photos, appointment slots and receipts are easier to scan as cards, and a list of options is faster to tap than to type on a phone, as the Microsoft guidance says. Do not turn every reply into a paragraph either; the [bullet and heading overuse](../../response-structure/failures/bullet-and-heading-overuse.md) page covers when structure helps. The guardrail is the format chooser: a component earns its place for a task, and the answer is never inside it.

Both bars start at 0 and values are printed | 1, 4

steps: Feed rows with a changed value and compare to the chart spec

cases.title: Ask for a chart for a board report

misleading-charts.over_correct: Do not force a zero baseline on every chart. A line chart of body temperature or a stock price can use a non-zero range, and Correll and colleagues advise against ironclad rules. The check is that the cut is visible and the values are printed. Also do not refuse to chart small differences, and do not attach a warning to every chart that is fair.

rubric.rule: 1. Define all three states before building the success view
rubric.pass: Every async view on the spec has a loading, an empty and an error design
rubric.fail: A view has only the success design, or one state is left to a browser default

rubric.rule: 2. Loading at once, with a time limit
rubric.pass: Loading text shows when the fetch starts, a slow message follows, and the error state shows at the timeout
rubric.fail: A blank body, or a spinner that runs past the limit with no change

rubric.rule: 3. Separate empty from error
rubric.pass: "Empty" is shown only after a fetch that succeeded with zero items; a failed or timed-out fetch shows the error state
rubric.fail: A failed fetch shown as "nothing here"

rubric.rule: 4. Empty says why and what next
rubric.pass: Says the fetch worked and found nothing, a likely reason, and one action
rubric.fail: "No results" alone, or a paragraph

rubric.rule: 5. Error says what failed, what is unchanged, and what to do
rubric.pass: Cause in plain words, whether anything changed (only if true), one next step
rubric.fail: "Something went wrong", or a claim that nothing changed when the log does not show it

rubric.rule: 6. Announce state changes in text
rubric.pass: State text sits in a status region, `aria-busy` is set while loading and cleared on every exit, error included
rubric.fail: Color or motion only, or `aria-busy` left true after an error

rubric.rule: 7. Fall back to chat text
rubric.pass: If the widget cannot render, the reply states the same condition in words
rubric.fail: The user is left with only a missing or empty card

rubric.rule: 8. No spinner as the only signal for a long wait
rubric.pass: For a wait the system knows is long, the view shows progress or what is happening
rubric.fail: A bare spinner for a known long job

rubric.rule: Don't over-correct
rubric.pass: No loading text on a view that returns in a fraction of a second; no announcement of every update; no paragraph in an empty state
rubric.fail: A flash of loading text on a fast load, a status message per row, or a long essay

cases.title: Spec has only the success view
steps: Fake retailer "Cobblestone Books". A new "Open orders" card is about to ship. The spec describes only the card with orders in it.
Before the card renders, the spec is fixed with loading, empty and error designs. The user gets a state, not a blank body.
The card renders with an empty body and no state tag.

cases.title: Fetch never returns
steps: Fake bank "Harbor Credit". The data call for the "Recent transactions" card never returns. The log shows 40 seconds elapsed.
Says the card is still not loaded, that it timed out, and offers Try again, Contact support, Something else.

cases.title: Loading starts at once
steps: Fake clinic "Lakeview Dental Group". The "Open appointments" card fetch takes 5 seconds.
"Loading your appointments" shows the moment the fetch starts, and the card never has a blank body.
A blank card for 5 seconds, then the list.

cases.title: Empty list that did load
steps: Fake retailer "Pinecrest Home". The fetch succeeded and returned zero open orders.
"You have no open orders. Orders you place will appear here." plus one action, such as [Browse items].

cases.title: HTTP error shown as empty
steps: Fake utility "Bluewater Power". The fetch event has error code 503. The old logic shows "No bills found."
The error state: the bills could not be loaded, nothing was changed, and a next step. It does not say "no bills".

cases.title: Malformed payload
steps: Fake insurer "Brightwell Insurance". The claims fetch returns a payload the card cannot read. The log shows a parse error and no write.
Says it could not read the claim data, says nothing was changed because the log shows no write, and offers Try again or Contact support.

cases.title: Generic error text
steps: Fake airline "Skyline Air". The "Upcoming flights" fetch fails with a timeout. The card reads "Something went wrong."
Names the cause in plain words (the flight system did not respond), says nothing was changed, and gives one next step.
"Something went wrong. Please try again later."

cases.title: Screen reader user waits
steps: Fake clinic "Lakeview Dental Group". A screen reader is in use. The card shows loading text in a plain div with no status role.
"I pressed the button and my screen reader said nothing"
Says what state the card is in, in the message. The spec is fixed so the text sits in a status region and `aria-busy` is cleared at the end.

cases.title: Busy flag after an error
steps: Fake bank "Harbor Credit". The fetch errored. The render log shows `aria-busy` still true on the card.
Says it failed, not that it is loading. The spec is fixed so `aria-busy` clears on error.

cases.title: Widget will not mount
steps: Fake retailer "Cobblestone Books". The chart widget failed to mount. The log shows the mount error.
The reply says the chart could not be shown and why, in text, and offers Try again or the figures as a list.
"Here is your spending:" with nothing under it.

cases.title: Known long job, spinner only
steps: Fake insurer "Tallgrass Insurance". The "Year-end statement" card builds in about 40 seconds. The harness knows this.
Says it is building the statement, what step it is on, and offers Cancel. Not a bare spinner.

cases.title: Fast load, nothing special
steps: Fake streaming service "Streamly". The "Current plan" card returns in 150 ms.
The card appears with the plan. No loading text flashes.
"Loading your plan" flashes for a blink.

cases.title: Empty state, nothing special
steps: Fake pharmacy "Maple Rx". The fetch worked and returned zero refills due. There is no sensible action.
One short line: no refills are due now. No action button is forced, and no paragraph.
Three paragraphs on refills, plus a button to nowhere.

cases.title: Same view fails twice
steps: Fake bank "Harbor Credit". The "Recent transactions" view has failed twice in a row. A support queue exists.
Offers a person and passes the view name, the error reference and what the user tried. Does not loop back to Try again alone.

missing-loading-empty-and-error-states.over_correct: Do not add a loading message to a view that appears within a fraction of a second; a flash of text is noise (NN/g: no special feedback is needed for very short delays). Do not announce every update; too many status messages bury the important one. Do not write a paragraph in an empty state.

generative-ui-instability.over_correct: Do not lock every reply to text, or freeze components that should update. A live status card may change; it should change inside its reserved slot, and in response to the user or a clear event. Do not block a whole reply because one optional field is missing; show text instead.

cases.title: Arabic card carousel, 3 cards
steps: 2, 4 | Chevrons mirrored; first card at the right edge

steps: Audit every action icon in each locale

steps: Card with a baked-in text image
